articles.title: US bars Microsoft, Indian IT firms from green card programme; TCS Q2 net profit rises 15%
articles.text:
US bars Microsoft, Indian IT firms from green card programme; TCS Q2 net profit rises 15%
The United States government is suspending new applications for permanent residency of foreign workers at companies including Microsoft, Cognizant, Infosys, TCS, and HCLTech, citing abuse in the entire process.
Dear Reader,
The United States government is suspending new applications for permanent residency of foreign workers at companies including Microsoft, Cognizant, Infosys, TCS, and HCLTech, citing abuse in the entire process.
In a particular reference to Microsoft, US Vice President J D Vance said, “Our message to Microsoft is: You’re a great American company, but you’ve got to hire great American workers.”
In other news, Prime Minister Narendra Modi has called for a global framework to tackle cyber frauds and deepfakes. At the tenth edition of the India Mobile Congress, PM Modi said governments, technology companies, telecom operators, and financial institutions should create mechanisms to curb digital frauds.
Meanwhile, India aims to double its 5G user base from 550 million to 1 billion by 2030, and up its game with 6G. Though the country had been behind in 4G, it marched with the world in 5G, and is now determined to take the lead in 6G, said Communications Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia said, at the mobile congress.
In funding news, DailyObjects, a design-led lifestyle-tech brand, has raised Rs 332 crore in a Series C round of funding led by Xponentia Capital Partners, Anicut Capital, and Axiom Asia Private Capital.
There’s a lot of chatter around founder burnout and stress. But a new study points out that startup employees may need greater attention.
Nearly half (47.5%) of people working in India’s startup ecosystem report low wellbeing, with employees faring the worst, according to a ‘State of Mind: The Startup Ecosystem’ study. The survey found that 54.3% of employees scored at or below the wellbeing threshold, compared with 45.2% of investors, 44.2% of ecosystem supporters, and 42.9% of founders.
In today’s newsletter, we will talk about
- TCS Q2 net profit rises 15%
- Women’s ride safety: Not just another feature on the app
Here’s your trivia for today: What device was the first Sony-branded product, released in 1955? (Scroll down for the answer)
Corporate
TCS Q2 net profit rises 15%
Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), India’s largest IT services exporter, registered a 15% rise in net profit and an 11.2% growth in revenue for the second quarter of the fiscal. Its performance was in line with market expectations.
The company attributed this performance to its international growth and certain deal wins during the quarter. It also noted that its annualised revenues from artificial intelligence (AI) has exceeded $3 billion.
Key takeaways:
- TCS has reported a net profit of Rs 13,884 crore for the July to September period of FY27, against Rs 12,075 crore in the similar period a year ago. Revenue was Rs 73,188 crore, compared to Rs 65,799 crore a year ago.
- TCS CEO K Krithivasan said, “We are pleased with the broad-based growth in all our international markets and most industry segments. This quarter we announced two unique deals with Porsche and Best Buy which represent a new category of transformation partnerships. Together with our clients, we are building repeatable value platforms that will industrialise AI at scale.”
- The manufacturing and energy & utilities segments posted strong growth for TCS. The BFSI segment is showing signs of revival. In terms of geography, TCS’ growth came from the UK and Continental Europe, while the North America region posted a modest rise.
Insight
Women’s ride safety cannot be just another feature on the app
There are several crucial questions when it comes to the safety of women passengers using app-based rides. Should the responsibility for staying safe always begin and end with the woman in the back seat? What responsibility should the mobility system itself bear for keeping women safe?
The National Commission for Women’s (NCW) new guidelines for the safety of women passengers using digital transport services seek to make women’s safety a shared responsibility of platforms, authorities, and law enforcement.
Key takeaways:
- The NCW guidelines aim to strengthen preventive safeguards, improve coordination between key stakeholders, and establish stronger response mechanisms at different stages of a woman’s journey.
- The real test lies in implementation. Coordination will matter as much as the technology. A route-deviation alert is useful only if someone responds immediately. An SOS button matters only if a functioning response system backs it up. A complaint mechanism means little if a woman still has to repeatedly explain what happened.
- For women, safer mobility is about being able to travel with confidence when the systems designed to protect them work when they need them.
News & updates
- Govt responds to Musk: The government has condemned Elon Musk over his allegations that Starlink’s satcom services are being blocked. It has also clarified that every satcom licensee in the country must comply with security norms. The statement comes after Musk alleged that “certain oligarchs” have blocked his company’s satellite communication services in India to maintain their monopoly in the country.
- Content crackdown: Meta said it has deployed new AI tools to crack down on ads that covertly lead users to child abuse material, as it disclosed that it acted on 5.3 million pieces of child sexual exploitation content in India during the first half of 2026.
- Record quarter: TSMC, the world’s largest contract chipmaker, reported a record third-quarter revenue of $46.71 billion, beating market forecasts and rising 50% from the year-earlier period due to surging demand for AI applications.

articles.title: TP-Link Sued by Four More U.S. States Over Router Security and China Ties
articles.text:
Four more U.S. states sued router maker TP-Link Systems on October 6, bringing the total to five, with Texas filing a suit in February. Florida, Iowa, Montana and Nebraska allege the California company misled buyers about how secure its routers are and how separate it is from China. TP-Link denies the claims and says it will fight them in court.
TP-Link Systems is based in Irvine, California. Until a 2024 restructuring, it was affiliated with TP-Link Technologies, a Chinese company that the suits do not name as a defendant.
The complaints from Florida, Montana , and Nebraska do not allege that the Chinese government has obtained customers' data through TP-Link. They describe that as a risk under Chinese law. Separately, they say state-backed hackers have exploited flaws in TP-Link routers.
Iowa's announcement is worded more strongly in places. Attorney General Brenna Bird's office said TP-Link firmware gives the Chinese government access to Iowans' devices and data. The same release also describes that access as something that could happen.
The next day, 21 state attorneys general sent a letter to the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) about TP-Link's effort to win approval for new router models in the U.S.
Three of the complaints also cite five flaws in TP-Link devices supplied by internet service providers (ISPs) to customers. Researchers published technical details of those flaws on October 8. Fixes exist, and they reach users through their ISP.
What The States Allege
The suits were filed in state courts under consumer-protection laws. The Florida, Montana, and Nebraska complaints share section headings and passages and make the same main claims.
The first is that TP-Link advertised security it did not deliver. The complaints quote TP-Link's web page for HomeShield, its built-in network protection service, as saying it "covers all security scenarios." The U.S. HomeShield page still said so on October 9.
The complaints set that against routers that were hacked and models that no longer get fixes. One example is two versions of the Archer AX21. TP-Link no longer updates them and says they reached end of life in May 2024, according to the complaints.
The second claim is that TP-Link overstated its split from China. The complaints quote the company as saying that the restructuring left it with "entirely different ownership, management, and operations" from those of TP-Link Technologies.
TP-Link and TP-Link Technologies together employed about 11,000 people in China, according to an April 2025 Bloomberg News report the states cite.
TP-Link says routers for the U.S. market are made in Vietnam. Only 0.5% of the parts used at its Vietnamese factory, by value, are sourced in Vietnam, and the rest are sourced from or through China, according to the complaints.
The third claim is that TP-Link's privacy policies leave out a risk. Its Tether, Tapo, Deco and Kasa Smart apps collect email addresses, location and phone identifiers. A 2017 Chinese intelligence law could expose that data to Chinese intelligence agencies, according to the complaints.
Florida wants a permanent court order against the practices, the surrender of money made from them, and $10,000 for each willful violation. Montana seeks up to $10,000 per violation.
Nebraska also wants TP-Link ordered to tell buyers where its products and parts come from, about its ties to China, and about known vulnerabilities that have been exploited in its devices.
TP-Link's Response
"The coordinated lawsuits are built on false premises. They do nothing to advance national security while unfairly penalizing an industry-leading U.S. company," Steve Kovsky, the company's corporate affairs officer, said in a statement issued the day the suits were filed.
For months, the statement said, TP-Link has given state regulators documents showing that its U.S. devices are made in Vietnam. It described itself as "an independent, U.S. company that is not owned or controlled by any foreign government."
"We do not, and will not, share customer network data with foreign governments or unauthorized third parties," it said.
What The Cited Attacks Show
The complaints point to real attacks in which hackers took over TP-Link routers.
Microsoft reported in 2024 that a hacking group it believes is in China had built a network of hacked small-office and home routers. The network was used for password-spray attacks, which try common passwords across many accounts.
TP-Link routers "make up most of this network," Microsoft said, counting an average of 8,000 hacked devices active at any time.
The complaints themselves say devices from other brands were hacked as part of the same network.
The FBI said in April that Russian military intelligence hackers had compromised TP-Link routers through a flaw tracked as CVE-2023-50224. They changed the routers' DNS settings and collected passwords and login tokens. TP-Link said in May that, with one exception, the products affected by that flaw had reached end of life.
The claim that Chinese state hackers used TP-Link routers in the Volt Typhoon and Flax Typhoon campaigns rests on testimony given in 2025. Rob Joyce, a former National Security Agency cybersecurity director, told a House committee that TP-Link routers "were among the various brands" exploited. His written testimony cites no source for that.
TP-Link disputed the testimony the same day, saying those campaigns "have no discernible preference for using TP-Link routers as a vector."
None of the three complaints says TP-Link built a backdoor into its products. The one backdoor they name, Horse Shell, was placed on TP-Link routers by a Chinese state-backed hacking group, according to Check Point Research, which the complaints cite.
The complaints also note that the U.S. Department of Defense in June listed TP-Link Technologies as a Chinese military company. That is the Chinese firm. TP-Link Systems, the company being sued, is not on the list.
The FCC Letter
Since March 23, the FCC has barred new foreign-made consumer routers from the equipment authorization they need before they can be sold in the United States. The only exception is a router that wins a "Conditional Approval."
Those approvals are decided by the Department of Homeland Security or the Department of Defense, which the FCC's notice calls the Department of War.
The rule covers routers made in any foreign country, whatever the maker's nationality. It applies by place of production, not by company.
Routers authorized before the rule can continue to receive software and firmware updates "that mitigate harm to U.S. consumers" until at least March 1, 2027, under an FCC waiver.
TP-Link said in April that its existing routers "remain fully authorized" and that it was "actively pursuing Conditional Approval for new products."
The letter, led by Nebraska Attorney General Mike Hilgers and signed by 20 others, raises three concerns with the FCC. They are TP-Link's security claims, its claims about separating from China and building routers in Vietnam, and what its privacy disclosures leave out about Chinese intelligence law.
The letter offers to work with the FCC. It does not ask the agency to deny, delay, or attach conditions to an approval.
"Consumers should be aware of these risks and the FCC should address them before authorizing these new routers for sale in U.S. markets," Hilgers said in announcing the letter.
Montana Attorney General Austin Knudsen said he hoped the FCC would refuse the approval.
Flaws In ISP-Supplied Devices
Aginet is TP-Link's line of mesh systems, routers, and modems that ISPs install for customers and keep up to date.
The complaints from Florida, Montana, and Nebraska cite five flaws in those devices as evidence that TP-Link's security problems persist. TP-Link disclosed the flaws on August 10. On October 8, the SEC Consult researchers who found them published the technical details.
Together, the flaws "allowed an unauthenticated attacker on the same network to fully compromise the affected device," SEC Consult said, and to run commands as root, the highest privilege level.
The attacker must first be able to reach the device's web management interface. Neither SEC Consult nor TP-Link says whether that interface can be reached from the internet.
The main flaw, CVE-2025-30237, allows crafted web requests to bypass the login check. With it, an attacker without an account can create a "Superadmin" user and enable SSH remote access, according to SEC Consult.
| CVE | What It Allows | What An Attacker Needs | TP-Link Rating (CVSS 4.0, Out Of 10) | Models Listed, Of 65 | 
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CVE-2025-30237 | Privileged actions on the web interface without logging in | Network access to the web management interface | 8.7, High | 56 | 
| CVE-2025-30238 | A low-privileged account can create a high-privileged account and enable SSH | A valid low-privileged login | 8.6, High | 59 | 
| CVE-2025-30239 | Stored passwords can be decrypted because the keys are hardcoded per model. On some setups this includes the ISP's remote-management credentials | Access to the device's stored configuration | 8.5, High | 65 | 
| CVE-2025-30240 | Files on the device can be read through a crafted link on a USB stick | Physical access to the USB port | 5.1, Medium | 33 | 
| CVE-2025-30241 | Operating-system commands run with elevated privileges | A login to the web interface | 8.6, High | 31 | 
SEC Consult calls the set of flaws critical.
TP-Link lists 65 affected models in its HB, HX, and HC mesh series, its EB, EC, and EX router series, its XC and XX fiber devices, and its VX DSL modems. Only 27 of them are listed for all five flaws, according to the CVE records TP-Link published. Versions that ISPs have customized are also affected, and TP-Link does not list those.
Owners may not be able to download the fix themselves. The updates are delivered through each ISP, and firmware for ISP versions "may not be publicly available for direct download," TP-Link's advisory says.
TP-Link advises users to check the device's management interface or its app for a firmware update. If none is offered, they should contact their ISP.
SEC Consult lists no workaround. Neither advisory says how many devices have received the fix.
SEC Consult reported the flaws to TP-Link in December 2024, and TP-Link's advisory followed nearly 20 months later. Most of the fixed firmware had been released by February 2026, according to SEC Consult's timeline.
SEC Consult left the exploit commands out of its advisory. Neither advisory reports attacks that use the flaws. None of the five was in the U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency's catalog of known exploited vulnerabilities as of its October 8 release.
Neither the complaints nor the advisories tie these flaws to the attacks described above, or to the allegations about China.

articles.title: I just tested the sequel to my favorite open earbuds ever, and their higher-res sound, ultra-compact build, and personalized EQ won me over — here’s why I’d recommend them
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
The Anker Soundcore AeroClip 2 are a solid upgrade over their likeable predecessor, offering higher-res audio support, better waterproofing, clearer call quality, and a more customizable sound. The main catch? They’re pricier than the original AeroClip at launch. In addition, their open-ear, cuff-style design still has its limitations, and they do require a bit of tuning to sound exciting. Still, they’re a great option for fans of the clip-on design, even when you account for the bump in price.
Reasons to buy
- + Ultra-comfortable yet secure fit
- + Lightweight with a more compact case
- + Solid sound quality for open-ears
- + Great features with personalized EQ
Reasons to avoid
- - Pricier than their predecessors
- - Open-ear architecture has its sonic limitations
- - Sound a bit unexciting out of the box
Why you can trust TechRadar
We spend hours testing every product or service we review, so you can be sure you're buying the best. Find out more about how we test.
Anker Soundcore AeroClip 2 review
I was incredibly excited to try out the Anker Soundcore AeroClip 2. The original model is easily among my favorite pairs of clip-on open earbuds, delivering immersive audio, an exceptionally comfortable fit, and a solid feature-set to match. So can the sequel build upon the strengths of the original AeroClip? Here’s my verdict after testing them.
Let’s start by talking about the upgrades on the Anker Soundcore AeroClip 2. Perhaps the main event is the new 'AnkerThus' chip, which — according to the company — offers 150x more computing power than the previous model. The key feature of the new chip is that it powers "Crystal-Clear Calls" and, indeed, you do get very solid call quality on the AeroClip 2. AI helps to scoop out pesky external sounds, and whether I was making a call or taking a voice recording, I found that my speech never sounded obscured. I also enjoyed the Whisper mode, which made my voice clear even if I was talking quietly.
One of the changes I really appreciate is HearID. Here, a few soundbites play, and you select the signature that sounds the best to you, before being shown your result. Perhaps unsurprisingly, my result favored a bit more emphasis in the low-end, making up for the low-end limitations of open-ear design. This feature helps the Anker Soundcore AeroClip 2 to stand out, even among the best open earbuds, and I recommend every user try it before they start listening to their tunes.
Elsewhere, the earbuds receive a huge waterproofing upgrade, from IPX4 to the AeroClip 2's IP57. This sees the buds protected against dust ingress, and submersion in up to a meter of water for as long as 30 minutes.
Battery life has also been improved. While the buds still offer a respectable, albeit unremarkable, eight hours of playback, they will stay alive for 32 hours with the charging case — an eight-hour boost over the original AeroClip.
The case design also see some changes; it's far more compact than the charging cradle on the first AeroClip. The buds also now slip into the case back-to-back, making the AeroClip 2 more convenient to slide into your pocket than their predecessors. The buds themselves look very similar — and still have that comfortable, lightweight, and secure fit of the original model that I so loved. They’re also pretty stylish, arriving in a range of colors including Burgundy Red, Cloud White, Midnight Black, and Mist Blue.
So, now on to how the AeroClip 2 sound. Something that piqued my interest is that the new buds seem to favor bass a little less than their predecessors — at least out of the box. If anything, I’d argue that bass is a little recessed, not helped by the AeroClip 2’s open architecture, which naturally leaks low-frequencies more than standard in-ear buds. But fear not: these are still very solid performers overall.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
With my HearID tuning in use, I was able to get a bit more weight at the low-end, while still leaving plenty of room for instruments to breathe in the mid-range and treble. And while the sonic upgrade over the first AeroClip buds is more incremental than revolutionary, there are certainly a few enhancements worth covering.
For instance, the news buds include LDAC, enabling you to stream higher-res music over Bluetooth with a compatible device (such as a modern Android phone). In practice, LDAC did make a difference — finer details in vocal performances and subtle percussive elements came through more prominently, opening up a more intricate listening experience.
Into my listening notes now, and we’ll start with the jazz-funk track Pret-Á-Porter by Robson Jorge and Lincoln Olivetti. The AeroClip 2 offered a wide, expansive soundstage — something clip-on open ears often excel at. Bass was well weighted and didn’t overstep its remit, but it wasn’t the most punchy or impactful. Treble sounded more articulate than on the original AeroClip, with precise, controlled percussion, and I was impressed by instrument separation, with horns and guitars operating separately rather than getting in each other's way.
Next, I switched over to a house track, Foreva by Caleb Jackson. Again, bass didn’t have that full-sounding, rich quality I love from my in-ear buds and over-ear headphones, but it was still agile and rhythmic. Vocals were well defined in the mix, and treble, while expressive and responsive, didn’t sound overly forward or grating — even at higher volumes. The subtlety of synths in the mid-range was also handled tastefully.
I finished up with Michi by Yuta Orisaka, a more stripped-back, acoustic track. Acoustic guitars in the intro were delicate and emotive — with LDAC helping the AeroClip 2 to provide more insight than their predecessor. Vocals, while not the most textured, were clear in the mic, and subtle bass came through nicely. All in all, the AeroClip 2 are a bit more revealing than the original model, and while they have limitations due to their open architecture, they perform pretty admirably overall.
The AeroClip 2 also feature a spatial sound mode, which can make your tunes sound more immersive, but I tended to keep this off for the most precise, natural presentation. You can access settings such as this in the Anker Soundcore app, which is responsive, well-laid out, and has a flashy UI. From there you can also alter EQ, with HearID, presets, or access a multi-band custom option. There’s also a section that enables you to listen to relaxing sounds such as waves crashing or forest noises — a little gimmicky, sure, but fun all the same.
In addition, the AeroClip 2 introduce customizable button controls, whose functions you can swap out for each bud via the Anker Soundcore app. So, for example, you might make one press on the right earbud to pause playback, but one press on the left earbud to trigger the voice assistant.
There’s no noise cancelling on the AeroClip 2. This is the norm for open ears, but there are some rival models, such as the Edifier LolliClip, for example, that include it. But the draw of the open fit is that you’ll be able to stay highly aware of your surroundings, which was true for the AeroClip 2, even when I was using them at max volume. Personally, I prefer the option to switch between ANC and a transparency mode, so I’m still more likely to reach for the JBL Live Beam 4, say. Nevertheless, if you like the open style, then the AeroClip 2 are a strong option.
So, are the Anker Soundcore AeroClip 2 worth buying? Overall, I'd say yes…but there’s a "but".
Anker has ramped up the price of its flagship clip-on earbuds to $169.99 / £159.99 (about AU$240), marking a $40 / £30 (about AU$30) increase over the first model. But do the improvements justify the increase?
Well, I really like the HearID setting, and the inclusion of LDAC is a neat bonus — as is the more compact design. But the sonic jump or boost in battery life isn’t massive, and some of the new features such as the AI assistant / translation and spatial audio feel more like "nice-to-haves" rather than essential upgrades. So, it really depends on what you value as a user.
The AeroClip 2 are still priced relatively well overall, and deliver very solid sound quality, a fantastic fit, and plenty of customization options. And I still think that they’re some of the more functionally fleshed-out and better-sounding models you can buy right now. Having said that, I don’t think the original AeroClip buds should be overlooked — especially if you’re an iPhone user who can’t harness the powers of LDAC, or if you want to make a bit of a saving.
Anker Soundcore AeroClip 2 review: price & release date
- $169.99 / £159.99 (about AU$240)
- Released in September 2026
The Anker SoundCore AeroClip 2 were released in September 2026, around a year and a half after their predecessors, the Anker Soundcore AeroClip. The AeroClip 2 are priced at $169.99 / £159.99 (about AU$240), which is a significant jump up in price from the original AeroClip model, which cost $129.99 / £129.99 (about AU$210) at launch.
Of course, there are a number of improvements that help justify this price hike, including a more compact build, LDAC, enhanced waterproofing, and implementation of the AnkerThus chip. And while the AeroClip 2 are still cheaper than rivals such as the Shokz OpenDots 2 and Bose Ultra Open Earbuds, you can get impressive quality from cheaper models such as the Edifier LolliClip and budget-friendly Baseus Bowie MC2.
Anker Soundcore AeroClip 2 review: specs
| Waterproof rating | IP57 | 
| Drivers | 12mm dynamic | 
| Battery life | 8 hours (buds), 32 hours (with charging case) | 
| Connectivity | Bluetooth 6.0 | 
| Weight | 6.2g (per bud) | 
| Frequency range | 20Hz-20kHz | 
Should I buy the Anker Soundcore AeroClip 2?
| Attribute | Notes | Score | 
|---|---|---|
| Features | HearID works great, customizable controls, decent battery life, LDAC now here. | 4.5/5 | 
| Performance | Solid detail and balance, although open design limits bass output. | 4/5 | 
| Design | Ultra-comfortable and lightweight, more compact than before, neat color options, open design has its pros and cons. | 4.5/5 | 
| Value | A price hike that’s justified in many areas, but some improvements could be greater. | 4/5 | 
Buy them if…
You’re drawn to the clip-on design
If you like the look of cuff-type earbuds, you’ll almost certainly enjoy the AeroClip 2. They have a stylish aesthetic, they're comfortable, and their highly secure fit all combine to make them solid all-rounders.
You’re looking for highly customizable sound
HearID enables you to take a multi-choice test that optimizes the AeroClip 2’s audio to suit your specific tastes. But if that wasn’t enough, there are also a handful of EQ presets as well as a multi-band custom equalizer, giving you advanced control over the sound of your open earbuds. 
Don’t buy them if…
You want premium audio
If you’re looking for premium sound quality, you won’t get it here. That’s largely inherent to the open design that leaks sound, with the low-end especially weaker than in-ear buds.
You want noise cancelling
If you’re looking to shut out the outside world, then the AeroClip 2 aren’t for you. Some open earbuds include noise-cancelling technology, but it's pretty rare. Want ANC? I’d recommend the JBL Live Beam 4 or AirPods Pro 3 instead.
Anker Soundcore AeroClip 2 review: also consider
| Header Cell - Column 0 | Anker Soundcore AeroClip 2 | Shokz OpenDots 2 | AirPods 5 | 
|---|---|---|---|
| Price | $169.99 / £159.99 (about AU$240) | $199.95 / £179.99 / AU$339 | $129 / £129 / AU$219 | 
| Drivers | 12mm dynamic | Dual 11.8mm dynamic | Custom high-excursion | 
| Waterproof rating | IP57 | IP55 | IP57 | 
| Battery life | 8 hours (buds), 32 hours (with charging case) | 10 hours (buds), 40 hours (with charging case) | 4 hours (buds), 20 hours (with charging case) | 
| Connectivity | Bluetooth 6.0 | Bluetooth 6.1 | Bluetooth 5.3 | 
| Weight | 6.2g (per bud) | 6.4g (per bud) | 4.3g (per bud) | 
| Frequency range | 20Hz-20kHz | 100Hz-20kHz | 20Hz-20kHz | 
Shokz OpenDots 2
The Shokz OpenDots 2 are an excellent pair of clip-on buds that boast great sound quality with punchy bass, good battery life, a secure and comfortable fit, and plenty of customization options. They’re a little bit pricier than the AeroClip 2, but you get more playtime, intuitive controls, and premium build quality that makes the investment feel worthwhile. Read our full Shokz OpenDots 2 review.
AirPods 5
Time for something a little different. The AirPods 5 are open-fit earbuds rather than clip-ons, but they still let you hear plenty of the world around you while delivering great style and sound quality to match. There's ANC to block out the outside world, plus they’re also highly waterproof, rammed with features, and beautifully lightweight. Non Apple-users may find their functionality overly restricted, and their battery life is disappointing, but they’re still a great pair of open-fit buds overall. Read more about the AirPods 5.
How I tested the Anker Soundcore AeroClip 2
- Tested in the office and while out and about
- Mainly streamed music over Tidal
- Compared directly against predecessor
I spent countless hours testing the Anker Soundcore AeroClip 2, during which time I made full use of their features, spent countless hours listening to music, and assessed their performance in a range of environments.
As always, I started my testing by sifting through the TechRadar reference playlist, but I also tuned into a huge variety of tracks from my personal library. I made sure to test the AeroClip 2 directly against their predecessor, as well as a handful of rivals.
More generally, I’ve spent years testing audio gear here at TechRadar, where I serve as a Senior Reviews Writer. I’ve reviewed everything from party speakers such as the Marshall Bromley 750 through to premium wireless headphones such as the Sony 1000X The Collexion. I’ve also tested a number of clip-on open earbuds, such as the Edifier LolliClip and the Sony LinkBuds Open.

articles.title: Cuánto tiempo demora la revisión de WhatsApp cuando se suspende una cuenta
articles.text:
La revisión que WhatsApp realiza cuando bloquea una cuenta se completa en un plazo de 24 horas, explica la plataforma
WhatsApp indica que el plazo de 24 horas comienza cuando el usuario solicita la revisión. Además, aclara que solo puede revisar un número de teléfono por apelación. Si no aparece la opción para solicitar una revisión, el bloqueo es definitivo y no puede apelarse.
Para consultar el estado de la solicitud, hay que abrir WhatsApp. La plataforma advierte que contactarla fuera del proceso de revisión o desde la cuenta de otra persona no acelerará el trámite ni influirá en la decisión.
Por qué WhatsApp suspende o bloquea cuentas
WhatsApp puede bloquear una cuenta cuando detecta actividades que vulneran sus reglas o que pueden afectar a otros usuarios.
La plataforma señala que toma esta medida frente a casos de spam, fraude y conductas que comprometan la seguridad dentro del servicio. También prohíbe utilizar la aplicación con fines ilegales, no autorizados o inaceptables.
Entre las prácticas que pueden derivar en un bloqueo figuran el envío de mensajes masivos o automáticos, la suplantación de identidad y la difusión de información falsa o engañosa.
WhatsApp también contempla las amenazas, el acoso, los mensajes que incitan al odio y cualquier contenido que promueva delitos violentos, ponga en peligro a niños o coordine acciones dañinas.
La restricción alcanza, además, a quienes vulneren derechos de privacidad, propiedad intelectual o publicidad de la empresa, de otros usuarios o de terceros.
La compañía puede suspender cuentas que intenten acceder sin autorización a sus sistemas, enviar virus, interferir en la seguridad del servicio o crear perfiles mediante mecanismos automatizados.
Las normas incluyen la prohibición de recopilar datos de usuarios de forma indebida, revender el servicio, desarrollar herramientas similares sin permiso y presentar reportes fraudulentos o sin fundamento.
WhatsApp recuerda que cada persona es responsable de proteger su dispositivo y su cuenta, y debe informar de inmediato cualquier uso no autorizado o falla de seguridad.
Estas medidas buscan evitar daños a la plataforma y a la comunidad, según las condiciones de uso. Un bloqueo puede aplicarse cuando la actividad detectada incumple esas obligaciones o afecta la seguridad colectiva.
Cómo recuperar una cuenta de WhatsApp suspendida o en revisión
Si una cuenta de WhatsApp fue suspendida, el usuario debe abrir la aplicación y buscar la opción para solicitar una revisión. El proceso de apelación permite que WhatsApp evalúe el bloqueo y se aplica a un solo número de teléfono por solicitud.
La plataforma indica que la revisión se completa en un plazo de 24 horas desde que se presenta el pedido.
Para consultar su estado, hay que abrir WhatsApp. Si no aparece la opción de revisión, el bloqueo es definitivo y no se puede apelar. Contactar a WhatsApp por vías externas o desde otra cuenta no acelera ni modifica la decisión.
Qué nuevas funciones hay en WhatsApp
WhatsApp, la aplicación de mensajería de Meta, incorporó nuevas funciones para llamadas, herramientas de seguridad y opciones para usar el servicio en más dispositivos.
Entre las novedades, permite hacer y recibir llamadas de audio y video desde WhatsApp Web, transferir una llamada grupal entre dispositivos, activar una sala de espera mediante enlaces y reducir el ruido de fondo. Incorporó video en alta definición desde los primeros segundos de la comunicación.
Los grupos permiten fijar una hora de cierre para las encuestas, ocultar nombres de quienes votan y editar preguntas durante 15 minutos.
La mención @todos avisa; en grupos de más de 32 personas, queda para los administradores. WhatsApp permite crear grupos con participantes de un chat existente.
En seguridad, la verificación en dos pasos usa una contraseña extensa y las claves de acceso pueden configurarse en más de un dispositivo móvil. Las actualizaciones se implementan gradualmente y su disponibilidad varía según la región y el sistema operativo del usuario.

articles.title: Prix du gazole : la France parmi les pays les plus chers d'Europe. Devinez à quelle place !
articles.text:
Avec les crises au Moyen-Orient, le gazole est cher partout. Mais en Europe, la France est clairement parmi les plus mal lotis !
La guerre lancée par Donald Trump contre l'Iran le 28 février dernier a entraîné des effets qui n'ont pas plu aux Américains, et que doit même regretter le président américain, avec l'explosion du prix du gazole - ce qui devrait faire très mal aux prochaines élections des midterms. Mais avec des prix proches de 6,27 dollars le gallon, soit 1,48 € le litre, les Américains peuvent encore se sentir privilégiés par rapport à nous Français.
La France est le 4ème pays le plus cher d'Europe pour le gazole
Le gouvernement cherche à aider autant qu'il le peut les Français pour financer leur carburant. Et quand on regarde les chiffres qui nous sont donnés par le Bulletin pétrolier hebdomadaire de la Commission européenne, en date du 5 octobre, on peut comprendre qu'il y a de quoi se plaindre chez nous.
En effet, ces chiffres, dont Sud Ouest se fait l'écho, montrent que la France est l'un des pays les plus chers de l'Union européenne. En fait, notre pays est tout simplement le 4ème plus cher niveau gazole de tout le Vieux Continent !
Les différences de fiscalité en Europe entraînent des disparités dans les prix à la pompe
Dans l'ordre, voici le classement des pays les moins chanceux de l'UE, avec la moyenne des prix qui y sont pratiqués :
- Finlande (2,553 euros au litre) ;
- Pays-Bas (2,506 euros au litre) ;
- Danemark (2,488 euros au litre) ;
- France (2,355 euros au litre).
Ces prix historiquement hauts par rapport à nos voisins s'expliquent par une politique fiscale très lourde en France, contrairement à certains de nos voisins. Ainsi, en Espagne, un décret maintient en ce moment un rabais de 0,20 € par litre, quand l'Allemagne essaye de son côté de réduire la facture avec une baisse des taxes sur l'énergie décidée jusqu'à la fin de l'année (mais avec une portée relative).
L'Italie au contraire, qui avait jusque-là bénéficié d'un coup de pouce fiscal, a laissé expirer la réduction d'urgence sur les accises le 6 octobre dernier, ce qui a entraîné en renchérissement immédiat de 0,61 € par litre. La libération des stocks de diesel décidée cette semaine changera-t-elle la donne ?

articles.title: Researchers Publish Working Exploit for Pre-Auth AnyDesk Linux Flaw That Gives Root Access
articles.text:
Security researchers have published a full working exploit for a pre-authentication remote code execution flaw in AnyDesk Linux that gives attackers root access before anyone approves the connection.
AnyDesk patched the flaw in version 8.0.3 in June, but its changelog described the fix only as "fixed a bug that could lead to a crash," with no CVE assigned and no security advisory.
The exploit, called AnyPwn, targets a heap buffer overflow in AnyDesk's session protocol, a remote desktop tool. The code was released on GitHub on October 8.
Administrators should update AnyDesk Linux to at least version 8.0.3. The latest release is 8.1.0.
What the Exploit Demonstrates
The published exploit works only over direct TCP connections on port 7070.
The exploit is probabilistic: the heap layout must place a target object adjacent to the overflowed buffer; otherwise, the service crashes instead of executing the attacker's command. The offsets in the published code target a specific build of AnyDesk Linux, 8.0.2; other builds would require different values.
The researchers say the same vulnerable code path is also reachable via AnyDesk's relay servers, which the software uses when a direct connection is unavailable. They validated this with a Frida instrumentation trigger but did not demonstrate the full exploit chain over relays.
AnyDesk said in June that the vulnerability is "limited to direct connections on Linux (connections that do not go through our relays). Windows and macOS are not affected."
The exploit targets AnyDesk Linux 8.0.2. The researchers imply that earlier versions, such as 8.0.1, may share the vulnerable code path, but exploitation of those versions has not been confirmed.
The researchers announced the flaw on June 22. AnyDesk acknowledged it the next day and released version 8.0.3 with the fix.
No CVE has been assigned to the vulnerability as of October 9. AnyDesk has not issued a formal security advisory.
AnyDesk's download page no longer lists version 8.0.2, though it still appears in the changelog. "The vendor appears to have deleted (?) the 8.0.2 build of AnyDesk upon the release of our poc video," the researchers wrote.
Administrators who cannot update immediately can reduce exposure by restricting access to TCP port 7070. Whether the flaw is fully exploitable over relay connections remains unresolved.
How the Flaw Works
AnyDesk's session protocol uses mode-5 stream packets. The handler calculates the size of its backing allocation by adding a 16-byte header to the declared payload length, using 32-bit arithmetic without overflow checking.
The exploit declares a payload length of 0xFFFFFFF0. Adding 0x10 wraps the 32-bit result to zero, so the allocator reserves a tiny buffer while the object records the original large length. Even one byte of attacker data then writes past the end of the allocation.
The overflow corrupts fields in adjacent heap objects, and the exploit uses a ROP chain to run an arbitrary command as root.
The vulnerability was found by Rick de Jager of the V12 security team using V12, a security code review engine. V12's founders previously built security firm Zellic and led the competitive hacking team Perfect Blue.
A separate AnyDesk heap buffer overflow, CVE-2025-27918, was fixed in version 7.0.0 in April 2025. That vulnerability affected all AnyDesk platforms and involved an integer overflow in user image processing, a different mechanism from AnyPwn's session protocol flaw.
AnyDesk was hacked in early 2024 in a separate incident in which the company's production systems were breached, leading to certificate revocations and forced password resets.

articles.title: Sega vende una figura de Sonic por 21.000 dólares y promete que tiene su propio “ADN”
articles.text:
Una figura de Sonic que cuesta 21.000 dólares busca convertirse en uno de los objetos de colección más exclusivos de Sega. El fabricante japonés puso a disposición de los fanáticos una versión del erizo azul que contiene ADN sintético inspirado en el personaje, resguardado dentro de una Esmeralda del Caos verde ubicada en su pecho.
El artículo fue desarrollado en colaboración con LOM BABY, un equipo especializado en biotecnología y arte que combina ciencia y cultura popular. La pieza forma parte de las iniciativas vinculadas con el 35.º aniversario de Sonic the Hedgehog y se distingue por incorporar material genético artificial diseñado a partir de las características del personaje.
Según la página de la tienda de Sega, el precio es de 3.300.000 yenes, equivalentes a unos 20.845 dólares, aunque el costo final supera los 21.000 dólares al considerar los gastos adicionales de envío. La cifra la sitúa muy por encima de otros artículos de colección relacionados con el personaje y la convierte en una pieza dirigida a compradores dispuestos a pagar por una edición singular.
Por qué la figura de Sonic cuesta 21.000 dólares
El elevado precio no responde únicamente al tamaño o a los materiales empleados en su fabricación. La propuesta se basa en la creación de una secuencia de ADN sintético que representa, de manera conceptual, la identidad del personaje de Sega.
Para desarrollar ese código genético, el equipo de LOM BABY analizó distintos rasgos de Sonic, entre ellos su apariencia, personalidad, velocidad y hasta su conocida incapacidad para nadar. A partir de esas características, los creadores elaboraron una representación genética artificial que acompaña a la figura.
Es importante aclarar que no se trata de ADN extraído de un organismo real ni de material biológico perteneciente a Sonic. El personaje es ficticio y el ADN presentado en la pieza es una construcción sintética concebida como parte de un proyecto artístico y tecnológico.
El material utilizado es un ácido nucleico, una clase de molécula que también cumple funciones relacionadas con el almacenamiento de información genética en los seres vivos. En este caso, se emplea para materializar el concepto de un código genético asociado a un personaje de ficción.
Una Esmeralda del Caos permite ver el ADN
Uno de los elementos más llamativos del coleccionable es la Esmeralda del Caos verde que se encuentra en el pecho de Sonic. Dentro de ella está sellado el material sintético, que puede observarse a través de una lente translúcida incorporada al diseño.
El cuerpo de la figura, la esmeralda y los componentes que permiten visualizar su interior están fabricados con resina. El conjunto mide 25 centímetros de alto y se entrega con una base de 30 centímetros de ancho, 21 centímetros de profundidad y 1,5 centímetros de grosor.
Cada unidad cuenta, además, con un número de serie propio, un detalle que refuerza su carácter de objeto de colección. Aunque la pieza tiene dimensiones relativamente compactas, su precio la ubica en una categoría muy distinta de la de los juguetes convencionales inspirados en videojuegos.
Sega apuesta por coleccionables que mezclan ciencia y ficción
La figura de Sonic DNA fue concebida inicialmente como una pieza a tamaño real y se exhibió en la tienda de Sega en Shibuya, Tokio. Posteriormente, la compañía habilitó la posibilidad de adquirir el modelo mediante su tienda, con disponibilidad para compradores de otros países sujeta a las condiciones de venta y envío.
La colaboración con LOM BABY sigue una línea de proyectos que combinan elementos de la biotecnología con universos ficticios. El equipo también ha trabajado en propuestas inspiradas en Resident Evil, incluido un modelo artístico relacionado con el virus T, y en la creación de materiales que evocan conceptos de mundos fantásticos.
Con un precio cercano a los 21.000 dólares, la figura no apunta al público general, sino a coleccionistas interesados en piezas poco comunes. Su propuesta transforma un elemento de la ficción —el ADN de un personaje que no existe en el mundo real— en un objeto físico que combina diseño, ciencia sintética y cultura de videojuegos.

articles.title: [Weekly funding roundup Oct 3-9] Steep decline in VC inflow
articles.text:
[Weekly funding roundup Oct 3-9] Steep decline in VC inflow
Venture capital funding into Indian startups recorded a sharp decline in the second week of October and this was primarily due to absence of large deals.
Venture capital funding into Indian startups recorded a sharp decline and this was largely due to the absence of large deals during this week.
The total funding this week came in at $168 million across 28 deals. In comparison, the previous week saw a total amount raised at $418 million.
Last week, there were two deals with value above $100 million but this week, the highest funded deal was of TVS Automotive Solutions at $44 million.
This shows the uncertain nature of VC funding into the Indian startup ecosystem in the current environment as there are no definite trends that define the capital inflow.
In addition, when investors are focused on the artificial intelligence segment, there is no credible story from India as yet. This also explains the lower funding volume into the ecosystem.
Interestingly, this week there were a few deals which were focused on the consumer tech segment. These are ventures which have created distinct brands in a highly competitive market.
Key transactions
TVS Automobile Solutions owned myTVS raised Rs 425 crore ($44 million approx.) led by CE-Invests.
Lifestyle brand DailyObjects raised Rs 332 crore ($34.3 million approx.) from Xponentia Capital Partners, Anicut Capital, and Axiom Asia Private Capital.
Consumer tech brand Lumio raised $12 million from Blume Ventures, Stellaris Venture Partners and 3one4 Capital.
Kitchen appliances brand Beyond Appliances raised Rs 110 crore ($11.3 million approx.) from Fireside Ventures, Dharana Capital and others.
Deeptech startup Quanfluence raised $10 million from Chiratae Ventures, Pi Ventures and Rainmatter by Zerodha.
Edtech company byteXL raised $9 million from Elevar Equity, Kalaari Capital, and The Michael & Susan Dell Foundation.
MSME-focused digital lender NeoGrowth raised Rs 85 crore ($8.8 million approx.) from FMO and LeapFrog Investments.
Medtech company Sunfox Technologies raised $7 million from Ashish Kacholia, Lashit Sanghvi, Alchemy Capital and 3one4 Capital.
Deeptech startup QpiAI raised Rs 50 crore ($5.1 million) from InnoVen Capital India Fund II.

articles.title: Anthropic Launches Free AI Vulnerability Scanner for Open-Source Projects
articles.text:
Anthropic on Thursday unveiled OSS Scanner as an opt-in vulnerability scanner to help secure the open-source ecosystem using artificial intelligence (AI).
"It's an opt-in service informed by our experience using Claude to find vulnerabilities during Project Glasswing," Anthropic said. "Projects that join will receive thorough, periodic security scans by our strongest models at no cost."
Anthropic also noted that the outputs of the scanner will be fully model-generated and do not require human review or triage, thereby facilitating faster and more frequent scanning. These reports are expected to be generated by its strongest models, including Claude Mythos.
The company pointed out that it expects to use a set of criteria similar to Google's OSS-Fuzz to pick projects, while emphasizing that the process may evolve over time. Project maintainers are advised to provide a short description explaining the importance of their project in cases where "it is not already self-evident."
Core maintainers of a project can enroll by opening a pull request on the OSS Scanner's GitHub repository along with a YAML configuration file that provides the following information -
- Link to the git repository that should be cloned
- Email address of the primary contact
- A repository-relative path to the Dockerfile that sets up the environment, pre-installs all dependencies and builds the project so to help an offline agent conduct its security audit
"The Dockerfile configures the environment that the project will run in and installs all dependencies so that the agent can perform its security audit without any internet access," Anthropic said. "We recommend verifying that the test cases pass inside of the built container."
Other optional details that can be added to the YAML file are below -
- Additional email addresses that are to be CC'ed on all reports
- Project home page
- GPG public key to encrypt report emails
- A repository-relative path to a threat model file ("threat_model.md") that spells out what code should be tested, vulnerability classification, or report formats.
- Opt out of receiving bug reports by setting "disabled: true"
As of writing, a total of 116 pull requests have been submitted. Unlike other vulnerability reporting programs, Anthropic said it does not intend to impose a 90-day disclosure period on the findings, given the risk that they may contain false positives.
"If we later validate one of these reports manually through our existing CVD program, we may disclose it under our CVD policy starting 90 days from when you are notified that a human has validated this report," it added. "As we gain greater confidence in OSS Scanner's performance, we may in the future impose a disclosure period on some high-severity vulnerability reports."
The AI company said it has identified more than 29,000 candidate vulnerabilities in some of the world's most important software projects, out of which a little more than 6,000 flaws have been reported to maintainers. These have resulted in 584 advisories as of October 2, 2026.
The development comes as Anthropic also unveiled the Critical Infrastructure Defense Program to safeguard critical infrastructure and open-source software as part of its Cyber Mission.
With AI increasingly equipping bad actors to discover and exploit vulnerabilities, automate various stages of cyber operations, and conduct attacks faster and at scale, the idea behind the initiative is to arm defenders with the right tools to combat the threat, accelerate fixes, and explore new secure architectures and coding practices.
"Our forecast is that in two years, AI will favor defense: it will be easier to catch bugs before they ship, write fundamentally secure software from scratch, and actively defend systems with models," Anthropic said.

articles.title: La chute des ventes d'ordinateurs s'accélère violemment ces derniers mois
articles.text:
Le climat n'est pas au beau fixe pour le secteur des ordinateurs. Car les ventes reculent fortement ces derniers mois !
Le secteur de la tech est d'un côté dans une forme exceptionnelle, quand on regarde les activités liées à l'IA. Mais de l'autre, quand on jette un oeil cette fois aux ventes d'appareils électroniques, c'est clairement une autre chanson qui nous est jouée. Les ventes de smartphone sont ainsi en chute libre, tout comme celles des ordinateurs, ainsi que nous le rapportent les derniers chiffres de IDC.
Les ventes mondiales d'ordinateurs ont reculé de 20,1% lors du troisième trimestre 2026
Lors du second trimestre de l'année 2026, les fabricants d'ordinateurs avaient pu observer un léger recul de leurs ventes globales, de -3,8%. Mais le trimestre suivant est clairement d'une autre ampleur !
En effet, on peut observer cette fois durant le troisième trimestre une chute très lourde des ventes, cette fois de -20,1% sur un an. Durant cette période, ce sont 62,7 millions d'unités qui ont trouvé preneur. Mais cet effondrement global cache des disparités entre les différentes marques que l'on peut retrouver en magasin.
Apple s'en sort mieux que les géants du secteur
Car si tous les grands fabricants enregistrent un recul sur la période discutée, certains souffrent plus que d'autres. C'est le cas du numéro 2, HP (19,1% de part de marché), dont les ventes s'effondrent de 30,9%, mais aussi du numéro 3 Dell (12,9% de part de marché), qui affiche une baisse de 25%.
Le numéro 1 mondial Lenovo (24,6% de part de marché) doit aussi faire face à un recul de 22,6% de ses ventes lors du troisième trimestre 2026. En comparaison, Apple, qui n'est pourtant que le numéro 4 mondial (8,5% de part de marché) ne fait face qu'à une baisse de -11,3%.
Et ça ne devrait pas être la fin de la tendance. « Nous ne nous attendons pas à ce que les prix reviennent à leur niveau d’il y a un an. Les prix resteront élevés. Compte tenu de la détérioration de la conjoncture économique, le risque est que les perspectives pour les prochains trimestres s’assombrissent avant de s’améliorer » explique ainsi le directeur de recherche chez IDC, Jitesh Ubrani.

Le Galaxy S24 Ultra avait rempli tous les critères attendus d'un smartphone très haut de gamme, et Samsung fait aussi bien, sinon mieux, avec son Galaxy S25 Ultra. Le terminal est une réussite incontestable sur le plan technique et se paie le luxe de gagner en puissance comme en endurance, tout en conservant son talon d'Achille (minime, il faut bien le dire), à savoir sa charge pas vraiment rapide. Son seul véritable problème n'en est un que pour les plus férus de téléphonie : si l'on excepte son volet logiciel dopé à l'IA, il n'apporte pas de véritable nouveauté à son prédécesseur. Il se frotte dès lors à la même difficulté que ses concurrents ; alors que la téléphonie a atteint un plateau technique, comment se démarquer, si ce n'est par des fonctionnalités logicielles ? Pour résumer, il manque peut-être au Galaxy S25 Ultra ce que l'on pourrait qualifier de petit supplément d'âme pour non seulement convaincre (ce qu'il fait sans peine), mais aussi séduire. Mais tout cela n'est que chipotage, puisqu'à notre sens, c'est l'efficacité qui prime.

articles.title: 'Just silly enough to be perfect' — I’ve seen Rivian’s Ghostbusters Ecto-R1 in action, and it's packed with Halloween tricks
articles.text:
'Just silly enough to be perfect' — I’ve seen Rivian’s Ghostbusters Ecto-R1 in action and Slimer would definitely approve
Rivian’s EVs get a paranormal makeover
Rivian loves a seasonal update, especially its now-annual Halloween drop, which has become a treat for owners of its electric vehicles. But for 2026, Rivian has done its best — and succeeded — to beat previous themes like Knight Rider and Back to the Future, with a pretty perfect pairing.
With the Halloween update rolling out now — R2 is the 2026.36.40 version, and R1 is 2026.36.0 — owners of the R1S, R1T, and R2 can turn their Rivian into a modern-day Ecto-1 thanks to a Ghostbusters-themed software update.
Rivian even tagged in Bill Murray — ahem, Dr. Peter Venkman — for the spot teasing this year's update, and created a very special vehicle to celebrate: the Ecto-R1.
And if you happened to be in New York City last night and thought you spotted Mr. Murray taking a loop around the block in what looked like an Ecto-1, I can confirm that was indeed the case. At a special event, I saw Rivian's custom Ecto-R1 in person, with the R1S sporting a custom white paint job, Ghostbusters logos, and a full array of paranormal-fighting equipment up top. I also got to see Bill Murray take the passenger seat for a ride before spending a bit of time with the Halloween update itself in the R2.
For the custom Rivian that pays tribute to the classic Ecto-Mobile, the design team really paid attention to the details. Up top, you won't just find the paranormal-fighting gear, but also vintage-style police lights that do a good job of mirroring the original. There's even more equipment tucked into the rear of the vehicle, making this feel like a proper Ghostbusters conversion rather than simply an R1S with a fresh coat of paint and a few logos.
Of course, all that extra equipment comes at a cost to the R1S's silhouette, with the roof-mounted gear and lights adding some extra height. But that's part of the fun here: Rivian has taken its electric SUV and given it a treatment that feels right at home in the Ghostbusters universe.
Murray seemed to appreciate the attention to detail, too. Describing the Ecto-R1, he said it was "just technical enough, and just silly enough to be perfect; it's really perfect." After taking in the lights and all the sound effects, he summed it up as a 'cool car'. It's clear he enjoyed the commercial, too, even teasing the quick joyride at the end during his remarks at the event.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
While the custom Ecto-R1 is a one-off recreation, Rivian's Halloween update brings some Ghostbusters to owners' vehicles. I got to experience the update in the R2, where the main display transforms into a full-on paranormal-fighting control panel called Trick or Treat mode.
It's far from just a simple Halloween wrap as well. The screen takes on the look of a piece of Ghostbusters equipment, complete with switches, buttons, sound effects, games, and controls for the vehicle's interior ambient lighting and exterior lights.
And it's not just a static screen, either. The panel is packed with little touches that make it feel like you're operating the equipment on a real ghost-hunting mission. Try flipping the switch for the radar equipment, for instance, and a ghostly hand pops up to flip it back off. It's a small detail, but one that shows just how much thought Rivian has put into this update.
There are several preset light and sound shows to choose from, including Ecto-1, Proton Pack, Slimer, Ghost Trap, Peter Venkman, and Random. These let you quickly activate a combination of interior and exterior lighting effects and audio, while Manual and Motion modes give you a little more control over the experience.
Motion Mode seems particularly fun, letting the effects trigger when someone moves nearby. I'd absolutely want to try that one in a parking deck, if only to see the reaction of an unsuspecting passerby.
And yes, you can blast the Ghostbusters theme, too. Between the full siren, the other sound effects, and the coordinated lighting, there's plenty here to make your Rivian feel like it's ready to answer a call from the Ghostbusters.
The experience extends beyond the main display, too. Rivian carries the Ghostbusters theme over to the screen behind the steering wheel and its app on both Android and iOS, so the seasonal makeover isn't limited to one screen. It's a surprisingly comprehensive treatment, and one that makes the update feel like a proper event rather than a quick seasonal Easter egg.
Of course, not every paranormal investigation needs to happen on the road. For those moments when you're parked or charging, Rivian has also included an arcade with games to keep you occupied.
Mallow Mash challenges you to pop as many Mini-Puft marshmallow men as possible. Murray himself noted that the game was quite hard, so even Dr. Peter Venkman might need a little practice.
Between the preset effects, motion-triggered surprises, soundtrack, and arcade games, Rivian has given owners a whole paranormal playground to explore — no proton pack required.
Beyond Bill Murray, who stars in the ad, Gil Kenan — co-writer of Ghostbusters: Afterlife and director and co-writer of Ghostbusters: Frozen Empire — was brought in to help shape it.
It's a fitting pairing for an update that leans so heavily into the franchise's look, sound, and humor. The custom Ecto-R1 is the attention-grabbing centerpiece, but the software makes the experience accessible to Rivian owners who don't have a fully kitted-out paranormal investigation vehicle in their garage.
And that's what makes this year's Halloween drop particularly good. Rivian has taken something as ordinary as a seasonal software update and turned it into a playful tribute to a beloved franchise, complete with the lights, sounds, and interactive touches that make it feel special. It might even be enough to get a few Ghostbusters super-fans looking at a Rivian in a whole new light.

articles.title: Apple adelantaría el lanzamiento de su primera MacBook Pro con pantalla táctil al 27 de octubre
articles.text:
Apple presentaría el 27 de octubre su primera computadora Mac con pantalla táctil, según un reporte de la agencia Bloomberg. La fecha contradice versiones difundidas apenas unos días antes, que ubicaban ese lanzamiento recién para comienzos de 2027.
El nuevo equipo sería una MacBook Pro de 14 y 16 pulgadas con pantalla OLED táctil y, por primera vez en una Mac, con el recorte de cámara conocido como Dynamic Island. El diseño sería más liviano que el de los modelos actuales y usaría los chips M5 Pro y M5 Max.
Según Bloomberg, ese mismo evento incluiría además una iPad mini con pantalla OLED, una MacBook Pro de 14 pulgadas con chip M6 y diseño actual, y una nueva iMac con el mismo procesador. El periodista Mark Gurman describió la convocatoria como pensada para profesionales de video, fotografía y música.
El formato replicaría el que Apple usó en otros lanzamientos recientes: una presentación en video disponible en línea, sumada a una instancia presencial reducida para periodistas, dos semanas después del evento del 13 de octubre dedicado a sus productos para el hogar.
Ese evento del 13 de octubre, al que Apple llamó “Bienvenida a casa”, ya fue confirmado por la compañía mediante una invitación oficial e incluiría un nuevo centro para el hogar inteligente, una renovación del Apple TV 4K y un HomePod mini actualizado.
El formato con instancia presencial para la prensa recuerda al que Apple usó para presentar nuevas Mac en octubre de 2024, en Los Ángeles, cuando también combinó una presentación grabada con encuentros reducidos para periodistas.
El giro frente al cronograma esperado
A comienzos de octubre, el propio Gurman había dicho en su pódcast Power On que la MacBook Pro táctil podía llegar en octubre o noviembre, aunque advirtió que también podía demorarse hasta 2027. Esa última posibilidad fue la que circuló con más fuerza en los días siguientes.
Reportes basados en fuentes de la cadena de suministro describieron entonces un cronograma dividido en dos etapas: primero una MacBook Pro con chip M6 y diseño actual, y recién en 2027 el modelo con pantalla OLED táctil. Una de las razones citadas era evitar que ese lanzamiento compitiera por atención con el iPhone Duo, el teléfono plegable que Apple prepara.
El reporte de Bloomberg del jueves revierte ese escenario. En lugar de separar ambos lanzamientos por meses, ubica a la MacBook Pro táctil y a la actualización con chip M6 en el mismo evento de fin de mes.
Tanto la iMac como la MacBook Pro de 14 pulgadas con chip M6 mantendrían, según los reportes, un diseño exterior igual al de los modelos vigentes. El salto de diseño quedaría reservado de manera exclusiva para la MacBook Pro con pantalla táctil.
Qué cambia en el diseño de la computadora
El cambio más significativo es el táctil: sería la primera vez que una computadora Mac permite tocar la pantalla directamente con los dedos. Apple mantuvo durante más de una década una postura contraria a esa función en sus notebooks, a diferencia de fabricantes que usan Windows.
Los nuevos modelos tendrían los nombres en clave K114 y K116, de acuerdo con reportes del sitio especializado MacRumors. Según esas mismas fuentes, el uso táctil sería complementario al teclado y al panel táctil tradicional, y no reemplazaría la forma habitual de operar una Mac.
Una versión beta del sistema operativo macOS 27.2, ya disponible para desarrolladores, incluye animaciones de mantener presionado en el dock que varios sitios especializados interpretaron como una pista técnica de la llegada del táctil a la Mac.
Reportes de los últimos días también señalaron que Apple necesitaría reforzar la bisagra de la notebook para que la pantalla no se mueva al tocarla, y que el reconocimiento facial Face ID, ya presente en el iPhone y el iPad, seguiría sin llegar a las computadoras Mac.
Antes de este reporte, algunas versiones ubicaban el nombre comercial del equipo como MacBook Ultra, en lugar de sumarlo a la familia MacBook Pro. Bloomberg, sin embargo, lo ubica dentro de esta última línea, igual que los modelos con chip M6.
Lo que Apple todavía no confirmó
Apple no anunció de forma oficial ningún evento para el 27 de octubre ni confirmó características, precios o nombres comerciales de los equipos. La compañía declinó hacer comentarios ante la consulta de Bloomberg, que basó su reporte en fuentes que pidieron no ser identificadas.
Reportes previos anticiparon también que el precio de la MacBook Pro táctil sería varios cientos de dólares más alto que el de los modelos actuales, aunque esa cifra tampoco fue confirmada por la empresa.
Apple suele concentrar sus lanzamientos de otoño entre fines de octubre y noviembre, ya avanzado el nuevo año fiscal de la compañía, que arranca a comienzos de octubre.
Bloomberg describió la fecha como “el 27 de octubre o alrededor de esa fecha”, la misma formulación que la agencia usó semanas antes para anticipar el evento del 13 de octubre, que Apple terminó confirmando con una invitación oficial.

articles.title: Attackers Exploit AhsayCBS Flaws to Deploy XMRig Miners Disguised as Microsoft Edge
articles.text:
Threat actors have been observed exploiting two recently disclosed flaws in the AhsayCBS backup utility to seize control of affected devices and deploy web shells and XMRig cryptocurrency miners.
Details of the flaws are below -
- CVE-2026-105133 (CVSS v4 score: 5.5) - An improper authentication vulnerability in the checkSysPwd() function in the "com/ahsay/obs/api/ApiStructsAction.java" component.
- CVE-2026-105134 (CVSS v4 score: 9.3) - An operating system command injection vulnerability in the Replication Receiver component.
A remote attacker could chain the two vulnerabilities to bypass authentication and execute arbitrary commands on affected systems. It's worth noting that CVE identifiers for these flaws were not published until October 4, 2026.
According to Huntress, exploitation efforts aimed at the two flaws began on October 7, 2026, at 11:20 p.m. UTC, with unidentified threat actors weaponizing them to achieve remote code execution on impacted hosts. As of October 8, 2026, five organizations targeted are estimated to have been affected by these flaws.
"Post-exploitation, threat actors are conducting reconnaissance, dropping web shells, planting XMRig cryptominers masquerading as Microsoft Edge, and more," the cybersecurity company said. "They also dropped what appears to be an AI-assisted PowerShell script that monitors the Windows Task Manager and shuts it down if it remains open for too long in the middle of the night."
The cryptocurrency miners have been found to impersonate the Microsoft Edge browser by using the name "edge.exe" to fly under the radar. Also dropped is a PowerShell script ("Taskgmr.ps1") that facilitates cryptomining operations after it's launched via curl.
The script, which is suspected to be written with assistance from an artificial intelligence (AI) tool, packs in anti-analysis checks that stop the mining activity as soon as a victim opens the Windows Task Manager app. It's also configured to terminate the Task Manager at 6 p.m. if it has been left open for more than one hour overnight.
Although the advisories published in the National Vulnerability Database (NVD) state that the issues have been addressed in the latest version of the software (10.3.4), Huntress has since revealed that it's also impacted, essentially turning them to zero-days.
In at least one incident, the threat actors are said to have used the built-in "certutil.exe" binary to download a legitimate-but-vulnerable driver ("WinRing0x64.sys") to the TEMP folder, likely with the aim of gaining kernel-level access to the underlying hardware and optimizing the mining process.
In the absence of a patch, users are recommended to limit access to the management interface and hunt for signs of compromise.
"Organizations should restrict AhsayCBS management interface web access, as the exploit targets the externally accessible web app service on the host," Huntress said. "Access should be limited to trusted IP addresses only or require VPN."

articles.title: Clubic recrute trois lecteurs pour tester le TCL X11L chez eux
articles.text:
Clubic recherche 3 lecteurs pour évaluer le TCL X11L, le nouveau téléviseur haut de gamme SQD-Mini LED de la marque. Pendant 3 semaines, vous testerez la version 75 pouces chez vous avant de partager votre avis sur notre site.
Clubic lance une nouvelle opération de recrutement de lecteurs-testeurs pour évaluer le TCL X11L, le nouveau modèle haut de gamme des TV 2026 de TCL, numéro un mondial des ventes de téléviseurs Mini LED et de grande taille. Cette initiative vous permet de tester en conditions réelles, dans votre salon, un téléviseur premium.
Comment participer à notre opération lecteur-testeur ?
Le dispositif se déroule sur environ 3 semaines. Les candidats retenus recevront chez eux un TCL X11L en version 75 pouces pour un test grandeur nature : films, séries, sport, jeux vidéo…
Si vous souhaitez participer à ce lecteur-testeur, cliquez simplement sur les boutons présents dans cet article pour accéder à notre formulaire de recrutement Google Form. Vous avez jusqu’au lundi 12 octobre 23h59 pour soumettre votre candidature.
À l’issue de la phase de recrutement, seuls les candidats retenus seront contactés par e-mail. Au vu du nombre important de participations, il ne nous est malheureusement pas possible de répondre individuellement à chaque candidature. 
Les lecteurs sélectionnés recevront ensuite toutes les informations concernant les détails de l’opération (livraison, installation, protocole de test, etc.). Une fois la période d’évaluation terminée, il leur sera demandé de partager leur retour d’expérience à l’aide d’un contenu rédigé, que nous mettrons ensuite en forme dans un article reprenant tous les avis des participants.
Et si c’était le moment de passer au très grand écran ?
Pendant longtemps, le choix d’un téléviseur haut de gamme se résumait à un arbitrage : l’OLED pour ses noirs parfaits, le LCD pour sa luminosité. La technologie Mini LED a progressivement brouillé cette frontière. En remplaçant le rétroéclairage classique par des milliers de minuscules LED pilotées par zones, elle permet d’éteindre localement les parties sombres de l’image tout en poussant très haut les zones lumineuses. Qualité d’image, luminosité, contraste, immersion : c’est ce qui explique que le Mini LED soit de plus en plus plébiscitée par les consommateurs.
C'est un avantage concret dans un salon baigné de lumière, où un écran trop sombre perd vite de son impact, mais aussi pour les contenus HDR, de plus en plus nombreux sur les plateformes de streaming et dans les jeux vidéo. Reste un défi : plus l’écran est grand, plus la gestion des halos lumineux autour des objets clairs sur fond noir devient délicate.
C’est précisément sur ce terrain que TCL, pionnier du Mini LED, positionne son X11L, présenté comme le premier téléviseur SQD-Mini LED au monde. Issu des travaux de plus de 47 centres de R&D répartis à travers le monde, il promet un contrôle de la lumière bien plus fin que sur les Mini LED classiques, avec des couleurs plus pures et des halos réduits.
Une image taillée pour le HDR
Sur sa déclinaison 75 pouces, le X11L embarque 11 520 zones de local dimming et annonce une luminosité HDR pouvant atteindre 9 000 cd/m². Ses quantum dots de nouvelle génération (Super QLED) lui permettent, selon TCL, de couvrir la totalité de l’espace colorimétrique BT.2020, la référence la plus exigeante en matière de couleurs.
La dalle Ultra WHVA 2.0, conçue par CSOT (la filiale écrans du groupe TCL, qui maîtrise ainsi toute la chaîne, de la dalle au produit fini), vise de son côté un meilleur contraste natif et des angles de vision élargis. Elle est associée à un film antireflet limitant la réflexion à 0,5 %, un point non négligeable face à une baie vitrée. Le tout est piloté par le processeur TSR AiPQ, qui ajuste netteté, contraste, couleurs et fluidité en fonction du contenu affiché.
Un son signé Bang & Olufsen et une vraie fibre gaming
Côté audio, le X11L reçoit le label « Audio by Bang & Olufsen » : ses haut-parleurs ont été conçus et réglés en collaboration avec les ingénieurs du spécialiste danois.
Les joueurs ne sont pas oubliés. La dalle affiche un taux de rafraîchissement natif de 144 Hz en 4K, et peut monter jusqu’à 288 Hz avec une source compatible grâce au mode 288 VRR Game Accelerator. La Gamebar permet en outre d’ajuster rapidement les réglages selon la console utilisée.
Donc, si vous souhaitez mettre à l'épreuve au quotidien le téléviseur TCL X11L, c’est le moment où jamais de participer à notre dispositif Lecteurs-Testeurs. Remplissez notre questionnaire et, si vous êtes sélectionné.e.s, vous pourrez partager votre retour d’expérience sur Clubic dans quelques semaines.
À l’issue de la période de test, le téléviseur devra être restitué. Son enlèvement sera organisé directement avec les participants, sans frais de leur part.

articles.title: Netflix lui confie 55 millions de dollars pour réaliser une série ambitieuse, il en détourne une partie pour s'acheter une Ferrari, cinq Rolls-Royce et investir en bourse
articles.text:
Netflix lui confie 55 millions de dollars pour réaliser une série ambitieuse, il en détourne une partie pour s'acheter une Ferrari, cinq Rolls-Royce et investir en bourse
Carl Rinsch est un réalisateur hollywoodien qui a notamment dirigé Keanu Reeves. Netflix lui a donc fait confiance pour diriger une ambitieuse série de science-fiction en lui confiant 55 millions de dollars. Sauf que sur cette somme, 11 millions ont été utilisés pour des placements risqués, l’achat de cinq Rolls-Royce, d’une Ferrari et autres biens de luxe. Quant à la série, elle n’existe pas et le réalisateur fut condamné à 30 mois de prison.
Tout commence avec ce projet de série appelée White Horse avant d’être renommée Conquest. À ce moment, Carl Rinsch n’a qu’un seul long métrage à son actif, 47 Ronin, qui met notamment en scène Keanu Reeves et a coûté 175 millions de dollars à Universal.
Un projet Netflix qui termine en détournement de fonds
Carl Rinsch a alors tourné plusieurs très courts épisodes de sa série Conquest via ses propres fonds, mais aussi ceux de Keanu Reeves. Netflix a ensuite décroché l’exclusivité du projet et donné une grande liberté créative à Carl Rinsch. Entre 2018 et 2019, Netflix a versé environ 44 millions de dollars au projet.
Le tournage a eu lieu entre le Brésil, l’Uruguay et la Hongrie. Sauf qu’après ces prises de vue, le réalisateur n'a rien à rendre à la plateforme de streaming. Carl Rinsch réclame donc plus d’argent pour terminer la production. Netflix accepte en 2020 avec une rallonge de 11 millions de dollars.
Et c’est là que commence vraiment l’histoire. Sur ces 11 millions de dollars, Carl Rinsch en transfère 10,5 millions vers un compte de courtage personnel pour investir en bourse dans des opérations risquées. Il ne faut que quelques semaines pour qu’il perde la moitié de la somme.
Ensuite, le réalisateur a investi dans les cryptomonnaies. En mai 2021, il remonte à près de 27 millions de dollars après la vente de ses Dogecoin. Et ça ne s’arrête pas là puisque grâce à cet argent, le réalisateur s’achète cinq Rolls-Royce et une Ferrari pour environ 2,4 millions de dollars.
On trouve aussi une facture de près de 3,8 millions de dollars pour des meubles et des antiquités. Le réalisateur a également déboursé 650 000 $ et 638 000 $ respectivement dans des montres et des vêtements et deux matelas de luxe. Des factures de cartes bancaires ont été réglées à hauteur de 1,8 million dollars.
Keanu Reeves demande à la justice d'être "indulgente"
Pourtant, ce détournement n’empêche pas Carl Rinsch d’engager une bataille juridique contre Netflix et de demander 14 millions de dollars en plus. Finalement, c’est en mai 2024 qu’un arbitre donne gain de cause à Netflix. Carl Rinsch doit alors verser environ 8,8 millions de dollars à Netflix et la plateforme a récupéré les droits sur les images tournées même si Conquest n’a jamais vu le jour.
Puis en mars 2025, la justice fédérale étasunienne arrête Carl Rinsch. En décembre 2025, un jury de Manhattan le juge coupable de fraude électronique, de blanchiment d’argent et de transactions illégales. Selon le procès, les 11 millions de dollars de Netflix étaient pour terminer la série, mais ont été détournés vers des opérations financières et des dépenses personnelles.
Keanu Reeves a défendu son ami dans une lettre où il demande au tribunal "indulgence et miséricorde". L’acteur qualifie Carl Rinsch d’"artiste exceptionnel". Quant à la défense du réalisateur, elle évoque des problèmes de santé mentale, un traitement médical mal géré, une forte pression professionnelle et un divorce conflictuel. Carl Rinsch a admis une partie de ses erreurs.
Finalement, c’est cet été 2026 que Carl Rinsch a été condamné à 30 mois de prison, alors que le parquet en réclamait cinq ans. Le réalisateur a déclaré en réponse : "J’ai fait une erreur". Le tribunal lui impose également trois années de surveillance après la prison, 11 millions de dollars de confiscation et encore 11 millions de dollars à rembourser à Netflix, en plus de 700 $ de frais obligatoires.
Mais l’histoire n’est pas encore terminée puisque le 7 juillet 2026 très exactement, Carl Rinsch a fait appel. Une procédure toujours ouverte alors qu’à la fin du mois d’août, le tribunal a refusé de repousser sa mise en détention. C’est depuis le 1er septembre que le réalisateur est derrière les barreaux.
