articles.title: Windows 11 prépare un widget bien pratique pour garder un œil sur l’autonomie de vos périphériques sans fil
articles.text:
Microsoft teste un nouveau widget pour Windows 11, capable d'afficher au même endroit le niveau de batterie de votre PC et de vos périphériques connectés. Une petite nouveauté qui devrait faciliter le suivi de leur autonomie.
Un pourcentage dans la barre des tâches pour le PC, un détour par les paramètres Bluetooth pour la souris ou le casque… Windows 11 sait déjà afficher le niveau de charge de vos appareils, mais les informations sont encore dispersées dans son interface. Microsoft a pourtant multiplié les améliorations dans ce domaine, avec une refonte de l’indicateur de batterie de l’ordinateur l’an dernier. Aujourd’hui, l’éditeur cherche à tout réunir au même endroit avec Battery Status, un nouveau widget introduit dans la build 26340.9616, publiée le 7 octobre sur le canal Experimental du programme Windows Insider.
Un seul widget pour les surveiller tous
Battery Status prend place dans le panneau des Widgets de Windows 11, accessible depuis la barre des tâches ou à l'aide du raccourci Windows + W. Il suffit ensuite de cliquer sur « Ajouter des widgets », puis de sélectionner « Battery Status ». Les niveaux de charge du PC et des périphériques compatibles s'affichent alors dans un même espace.
Microsoft ne précise toutefois pas quels types d'accessoires sont pris en charge, ni si tous les périphériques capables de transmettre leur niveau de batterie à Windows pourront y figurer.
Pour le moment, cette nouveauté est réservée aux membres du programme Insider disposant d'une version récente du canal Experimental. Son déploiement est progressif et aucune date de disponibilité générale n'a été annoncée. Comme pour les autres fonctions expérimentales, Microsoft pourrait encore la modifier avant une éventuelle intégration à la version grand public de Windows 11.

articles.title: Juspay FY26 revenue rises 30% to Rs 664 Cr as international business and AI bets scale
articles.text:
Juspay FY26 revenue rises 30% to Rs 664 Cr as international business and AI bets scale
Juspay reported a 30% year-on-year increase in FY26 revenue to Rs 664 crore, driven by global expansion and scaling daily transaction volumes, while strategic investments in AI infrastructure widened its net loss.
Payments technology company Juspay reported a 30% year-on-year increase in revenue for the financial year ended March 31, 2026 (FY26), reaching Rs 664 crore, up from Rs 514 crore in FY25.
The top-line growth reflects sustained momentum across the company's core operations, with revenue more than tripling over a three-year period from Rs 213 crore in FY23, representing a compound annual growth rate of approximately 46%.
The Bengaluru-headquartered fintech firm remained Adjusted EBITDA positive at Rs 33 crore for FY26, excluding non-cash ESOP costs. However, increased capital allocation towards global market expansion and deep-tech artificial intelligence infrastructure widened its net loss to Rs 90 crore for the fiscal year.
Juspay’s platform scaled to process 400 million daily transactions during the year, driving an annualised Total Payment Volume past the $1 trillion milestone with a reported 99.999% uptime reliability. The platform currently powers payment orchestration for more than 500 enterprises and financial institutions globally, including Amazon, Swiggy, Flipkart, Google, IndiGo, Agoda, HSBC, IKEA, and Zurich Insurance.
During FY26, Juspay accelerated its international footprint across North America, Europe, Latin America, the Middle East, and the Asia-Pacific region, alongside continuous scaling and profitability within its domestic Indian payments division.
A substantial portion of the capital deployed throughout the year was directed into developing proprietary, open-source AI infrastructure tailored for enterprise workflows and agentic commerce. Key technological platforms developed during the period include Xyne, an open-source, model-agnostic, and data-sovereign enterprise AI framework built on Unix-like architecture.
The firm also rolled out Juspay Genius, an AI-native payment intelligence suite designed to automate enterprise payment management, routing logic, and analytics. Additional launches included Breeze Buddy, a no-code AI voice platform supporting automated customer support, and Breeze Universal, which facilitates brand discovery across third-party AI ecosystems.
Commenting on the financial performance, Sheetal Lalwani, Co-founder and Chief Operating Officer at Juspay, stated that FY26 marked a pivotal investment period geared towards laying infrastructure for the company’s next phase of global growth.
"FY26 was a year of investing in the capabilities that will support Juspay’s next phase of growth. Our international payments business is scaling, and we are beginning to see traction across markets. As we expand globally, we are also investing in AI as part of a broader strategy to build new solutions for enterprises," Lalwani said. "Xyne is one example of this investment, bringing our experience in building reliable, enterprise-grade infrastructure to an open-source AI platform."
Lalwani acknowledged the short-term impact of these capital deployments on near-term net earnings, noting that the strategy remains anchored in building long-term capabilities, expanding technical talent, and establishing sustainable value for enterprise clients.
Founded in 2012, Juspay currently operates with a global workforce of over 1,500 employees across key international hubs including Bengaluru, San Francisco, Dublin, São Paulo, Singapore, and Dubai.""

articles.title: Startup news and updates: daily roundup (October 9, 2026)
articles.text:
Startup news and updates: daily roundup (October 9, 2026)
YourStory presents the daily news roundup from the Indian startup ecosystem and beyond. Here's the roundup for Tuesday, October 9, 2026.
YourStory presents the daily news roundup from the Indian startup ecosystem and beyond. Here's the roundup for Thursday, October 8 , 2026.
Funding news
NeoGrowth raises Rs 85 crore led by FMO
MSME-focused digital lender NeoGrowth has raised Rs 85 crore in an investment round led by FMO, the Dutch entrepreneurial development bank, with participation from existing investor LeapFrog Investments.
The funding will support the company's next growth phase, including expanding access to credit for micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), strengthening its digital lending capabilities, and deepening its market presence.
Other news
EyeROV delivers two indigenous underwater robotic systems to Indian Navy
Kochi-based marine robotics company EyeROV has delivered two TROUT military-grade remotely operated underwater vehicles to the Indian Navy. The delivery forms part of an order for five systems and marks progress in India’s development of indigenous underwater robotic technology.
Developed under the Innovations for Defence Excellence (iDEX) programme, TROUT is designed for naval and subsea operations, including underwater inspection, surveillance, reconnaissance, search and recovery, and robotic intervention.
The system underwent field trials and qualification processes covering manoeuvrability, navigation, endurance and performance in challenging underwater conditions. It also completed type testing and quality assurance procedures aligned with applicable military standards.
Accenture and Dell expand partnership to scale enterprise AI
Accenture and Dell Technologies have expanded their more than 20-year collaboration by establishing the Accenture Dell Business Group. The initiative aims to help enterprises modernise infrastructure and deploy AI at scale, with greater control over data, costs, and performance.
The collaboration will focus on private AI infrastructure, hybrid and sovereign environments, agentic AI applications and integrated enterprise AI solutions. It will also support organisations operating in highly regulated industries that require stronger control over sensitive information.
BuyBuyCart launches B2B wholesale ordering platform
Retail supermarket chain BuyBuyCart has launched a business-to-business platform designed to streamline wholesale operations and digital ordering across its franchise network.
The platform is being developed as a centralised system for wholesale and franchise orders. Its features include state-wise order tracking, value- and quantity-based analysis, franchise-wise ordering, salesperson performance monitoring and product-level sales insights. As the platform evolves, the company plans to enable franchise partners to place routine and replenishment orders directly through the portal.
JSW MG Motor India selects eight startups for MG Developer Program
JSW MG Motor India has selected eight startups as winners of the sixth edition of its MG Developer Program, an initiative supporting innovation in mobility and emerging technologies. The selected companies are Nayan Technologies, Technod8.AI, LiveNSense, LW3, Smaartbrand by Acquink Solutions, Fitsol, Cautio and Meta Materials Circular Market.
Their solutions cover road intelligence, agentic AI, industrial intelligence, electric-vehicle battery supply-chain compliance, customer decision intelligence, supply-chain decarbonisation, mobility intelligence, and automotive circular-economy infrastructure. The winners will work with JSW MG Motor India and its partners to explore pilot projects and real-world deployments.
Zomato and Blinkit’s EV Bazaar attracts 2,500 delivery partners
Eternal’s Zomato and Blinkit have hosted the third edition of EV Bazaar in New Delhi to encourage electric vehicle adoption among delivery partners. The event attracted 2,500 delivery partners and ecosystem participants, including more than 20 electric vehicle manufacturers, which showcased over 30 electric two-wheeler models. The initiative enables delivery partners to compare vehicles, explore rental and ownership options, and understand charging and battery-swapping facilities.
Four India-linked startups feature in Y Combinator cohorts
Four startups founded by alumni of Indian educational institutions are developing AI-driven solutions across hardware procurement, enterprise software, pharmaceutical documentation and video editing. The document features Waybill, Ressl AI, Ritivel, and Cardboard.
Waybill, founded by Plaksha University alumni Rishi Laddha and Tushar Goyal, aims to simplify hardware procurement by combining supplier discovery, ordering, payments, shipping, customs and inventory management. Ressl AI, founded by IIT Bombay alumni Arushi Gandhi and Abhishek Eswaran, uses AI agents to automate repetitive maintenance tasks in enterprise software.
Ritivel, founded by IIT Bombay alumni Pavan Kalyan Tankala, Nirmit Arora and Gunin Gupta, develops AI tools to draft pharmaceutical regulatory documents while linking information to its sources. Cardboard, founded by BITS Pilani alumni Saksham Aggarwal and Ishan Sharma, is building a browser-based AI video editor that converts raw footage into initial cuts using natural-language instructions.
Aditya Birla World Academy hosts student-led mental health festival
Aditya Birla World Academy hosted The Happy Place, a student-led mental health festival supported by Mpower, bringing students together to explore emotional well-being through creative expression. The latest edition, themed ‘The Messy Middle’, focused on uncertainty, setbacks and self-doubt experienced during adolescence. The school said it integrates mental health education into its curriculum through Minds Matter, which covers students in Grades 1 to 12. The initiative aims to encourage open conversations about emotions, develop coping strategies and help students seek support when needed.
Harness acquires select Augment Code assets
Harness has acquired select assets from Augment Code, including Cosmos, the Auggie CLI products, the Code Context Engine and related technology. The acquisition aims to accelerate Harness’s efforts to automate software development across the software delivery lifecycle.
Cosmos will become the Harness Cosmos Software Factory Agent, designed to turn requirements, tickets and bug reports into code and tests before opening pull requests for review. The system uses AI agents to plan changes, write code and address reviewer feedback, with engineers involved where human judgement is required.
Harness plans to combine Augment’s codebase understanding capabilities with its Software Delivery Knowledge Graph, which provides information about builds, deployments, security and operational costs.
Cummins India appoints Gbile Adewunmi as managing director
Cummins India has appointed Gbile Adewunmi as Managing Director of Cummins India Limited and India Regional Leader, effective November 1, 2026. He will take on the expanded responsibilities alongside his current role leading Industrial Markets within the company’s Power Systems business. Adewunmi currently serves as Vice President of Power Systems Industrial Markets, working with customers and partners across industrial sectors, including mining.
Kore.ai launches Autoloop for continuous AI agent optimisation
Kore.ai has announced the general availability of Autoloop, an optimisation engine within its Agent Platform, Artemis edition. The capability is designed to build, evaluate and continuously improve enterprise AI agents against business-defined goals, reducing reliance on manual adjustments. Autoloop assesses agents across task completion, accuracy, adherence to business rules, safety, consistency, user experience and cost efficiency. Its continuous process covers building, evaluation, diagnosis, optimisation and verification, both before deployment and during production.
Atlassian unveils new AI collaboration capabilities
Atlassian has announced new AI collaboration capabilities at its Team ’26 Europe conference in Amsterdam, including the Agentic Multiplayer Protocol (AMP). The framework establishes guidelines for AI agents to work alongside human teams across digital tools and workflows.
AMP covers collaboration within existing work environments, clear agent identities and ownership, and governance controls governing access to organisational information. It also supports auditability, permissions and human checkpoints for important decisions. Atlassian said people and agents collaborate more than 10 million times each month across its platform, while the number of Rovo agent users has doubled in six months.
Scalefusion launches vulnerability management capability
Scalefusion has launched Veltar Vulnerability Management, a capability that connects vulnerability detection with remediation through its unified endpoint management platform. The offering enables IT and security teams to identify vulnerabilities across managed Windows and macOS devices, assess risks and deploy fixes through existing patch management workflows.
The system combines vulnerability severity, threat intelligence and endpoint information to help organisations prioritise remediation. Its signals include the Common Vulnerability Scoring System, Exploit Prediction Scoring System, CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities data and Device Risk Score.
Spardha School of Music launches technology-enabled training platform
Spardha School of Music has expanded its digital learning ecosystem with a training platform designed to support music and performing arts students beyond scheduled classes. The platform combines one-to-one teaching with practice tools, assignments, progress tracking and AI-powered feedback.
Students can access practice videos and sheet music and use tools such as metronomes, virtual keyboards, tabla, mridangam and tanpura. AI-powered session notes, monthly progress reports, and real-time practice feedback help learners track their progress. The platform also supports teacher performance monitoring and personalised professional development.
Mirror Security selected for Google for Startups cybersecurity programme
Mirror Security has been selected for the inaugural Google for Startups Gemini Startup Forum: Cybersecurity, joining 33 cybersecurity startups chosen globally. The company participated in the programme at Google’s London office on September 8 and 9, 2026, where founders engaged with experts from Google Cloud and Google DeepMind.
The company was selected under the AI Security and Governance category for its use of fully homomorphic encryption, which allows data to remain encrypted while AI models process it. Its technology aims to protect sensitive information contained in prompts, embeddings and agent messages as organisations deploy AI applications.
New Relic introduces AI evaluation capabilities
New Relic has announced AI Evaluation, a new capability within its AI Observability offering designed to assess generative AI performance across the application lifecycle. The platform evaluates response quality, behaviour, security risks and business impact, extending visibility beyond individual large language model interactions.
The capability uses automated evaluations to identify issues such as hallucinations, prompt injections, data leaks, toxicity and bias. It connects quality scores with application traces, helping engineering teams investigate problems across prompts, retrieval systems and backend infrastructure.
Rocket Learning convenes policymakers and experts at Udaan 2026
Rocket Learning hosted Udaan 2026 in New Delhi, bringing together policymakers, researchers, educators, civil society representatives and technology leaders to discuss early childhood care and education. The event, themed ‘From Surviving to Thriving’, focused on strengthening Anganwadis, increasing investment in early childhood development and using technology to support young children.
The conference also presented findings from an evaluation of a technology-based early childhood development model, examining its impact and cost-effectiveness.
NWWA and Mpower launch mental health initiative for NDRF families
The NDRF Wives Welfare Association (NWWA) has signed a memorandum of understanding with Mpower to launch Project Nirmal, a mental health and psychosocial support initiative for National Disaster Response Force personnel and their families.
The programme aims to address occupational stress associated with disaster response, demanding working conditions and sudden deployments. Services will include mental health awareness sessions, psychological screening, individual and group counselling, tele-counselling, crisis intervention and suicide prevention support. The initiative will also establish regional teams and operate a dedicated multilingual helpline round the clock.
Varun Dhawan invests in biofortified staples brand Better Nutrition
Actor Varun Dhawan has joined Better Nutrition, a biofortified staples brand featured on Shark Tank India, as an investor and brand ambassador. His association with the company began with his own farming journey, which sparked an interest in soil, seeds and nutrient-rich food. He joins existing brand ambassador PV Sindhu as Better Nutrition looks to expand awareness of biofortified food among Indian consumers.
Better Nutrition offers everyday staples, including atta, dal, rice and millets, made from crops developed to contain higher levels of essential micronutrients such as iron and zinc. The company uses biofortified seeds, soil science and farm-level testing, including X-ray fluorescence technology, to measure nutrient levels. As part of the association, Dhawan's farm will also be developed as a biofortified farm in partnership with the company.
Vivriti Asset Management returns over Rs 3,400 Cr to investors
Vivriti Asset Management (VAM) has completed the lifecycle and exit of its Vintage II funds within the stipulated period, returning more than Rs 3,400 crore to investors through capital repayments and income distributions across two fund vintages.
The Vintage II funds raised Rs 1,700 crore in investor commitments and invested over Rs 3,500 crore across more than 45 portfolio companies. Their investments spanned infrastructure, clean energy, manufacturing, logistics and enterprise software. The funds collectively returned over Rs 2,260 crore in capital and income. The moderate-risk scheme generated a gross internal rate of return (IRR) of approximately 15%, while the conservative scheme delivered around 12%. Net returns were approximately 13% and 10.5%, respectively. VAM has invested over Rs 12,500 crore across 125-plus portfolio companies since inception.
Mi Arcus partners Papa Don't Preach for festive kidswear
Kidswear brand Mi Arcus has partnered with designer label Papa Don't Preach to launch a premium festive collection for children on October 12. The collection will be available through Mi Arcus stores, its website and e-commerce platforms, including Nykaa Fashion and Myntra. The collaboration marks Papa Don't Preach’s first partnership with a kidswear brand and Mi Arcus’s entry into ethnic wear. The collection combines playful designs and bold colours with soft fabrics and comfortable silhouettes.
BUSY Infotech targets Rs 1,000 crore revenue in five years
BUSY Infotech, a subsidiary of IndiaMART, is targeting revenue of approximately Rs 1,000 crore over the next five years, aiming for five- to sixfold growth as Indian MSMEs increasingly adopt digital business management tools.
The accounting and GST compliance software provider reported revenue of Rs 170 crore in FY26. Its revenue from operations rose around 47% year-on-year to Rs 36 crore in Q1 FY27, while cash from operations more than doubled to Rs 44 crore in FY26 from Rs 21 crore in FY25.
More than six lakh companies use BUSY software. The company plans to accelerate customer acquisition, expand cloud and mobile offerings, introduce AI-powered features and strengthen its presence in western, southern and eastern India. It will also explore strategic acquisitions to expand its products and market reach.

articles.title: Three Teams Demonstrate Remote Hacks of Fully Patched Google Pixel 10 at Pwn2Own
articles.text:
Three research teams broke into Google's Pixel 10 on October 8 at Pwn2Own Ireland, a hacking contest in Cork whose rules require every target to be fully patched. The contest pays researchers to show working exploits and passes the flaws to the vendors. One of the three Pixel exploits earned Ikotas Labs $300,000, the contest's top prize, and made the team the overall winner.
Trend Micro's Zero Day Initiative (ZDI), which runs Pwn2Own, posted the results but had not published how the three exploits work as of October 9. The wins were demonstrations on contest phones, and at least two of the three used a bug that was already known before the attempt.
The contest rules require each entry to use bugs that are not already known to the vendor or to the organizer. An entry that uses an already-known bug, which ZDI calls a collision, can still be accepted at a lower prize.
The three Pixel 10 wins, in the order they happened:
| Team | ZDI's Description | Award | Points | 
|---|---|---|---|
| Xint (Tim Becker and Yves Bieri) | Used "a single bug collision" | $150,000 | 15 | 
| Ikotas Labs | "chained multiple issues together" (entry labeled a collision) | $300,000 | 30 | 
| Dimitrios Valsamaras, Ken Gannon and Tenia Valsamara | A chain of two bugs: one collision and one zero-day | $112,500 | 22.5 | 
Together, the three wins paid $562,500. All three teams were competing for the same listed prize of $300,000 and 30 points.
Xint went first. Its win was first announced with the full prize still to be confirmed, then set at $150,000 and 15 points, half the listed amounts.
Ikotas Labs went second and received the full $300,000 and 30 points. Its entry is also labeled a collision in the results, with no explanation of the label or of why the full prize was paid.
All three Pixel 10 entries were registered as remote exploits. Under the rules, that means breaking into the phone through web content opened in its default browser or over one of four radio links: NFC, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth or baseband.
A winning entry must run code of the attacker's choice on the phone or pull sensitive information from it. Which route each team used, and what each exploit did on the phone, has not been published.
Three of the four remote attempts on the Pixel 10 succeeded. The other, on the contest's first day, ran out of time.
What Happens Next
Under the rules, winning teams hand their exploits and write-ups to ZDI, and the bugs are passed to the affected vendors. Vendors then have 90 days to release patches before ZDI publishes the full technical details, according to a June article from TrendAI, Trend Micro's enterprise security business.
Google's October Pixel bulletin was published on October 6, two days before the Pixel 10 exploits were shown, and does not mention the contest. ZDI's results list no fix and no step for Pixel owners to take.
Galaxy S26 and Other Results
Samsung's Galaxy S26 was exploited in all seven attempts made on it during the contest. Six of the seven winning entries included at least one collision. ZDI said one bug in the Galaxy S26 chain Ikotas Labs used on the first day "was already known to the vendor (yet unpatched)" at the time.
Ikotas Labs also exploited OpenAI's Codex coding agent and, on the second day, Oracle's Autonomous AI Database. Its four wins add up to $361,000 and 42.5 points in ZDI's posted results. ZDI named it Master of Pwn, the title for the contestant with the most points.
Researchers also exploited Lexmark, Canon and Brother printers, three smart home devices (Sonos Era 300, Philips Hue Bridge Pro and Home Assistant Green) and the Garmin Index BPM, a wellness device.
Every product on the schedule was exploited at least once, and 51 of the 63 scheduled attempts succeeded. The schedule listed no attempt on Apple's iPhone 17 or on WhatsApp, each with a top prize of $300,000.
ZDI's posted awards for the three days add up to more than $1.2 million, above the $1,024,750 it awarded at last year's Ireland contest.
Separately, Google in September patched a Pixel modem flaw, CVE-2026-58704, that it said : "may be under limited, targeted exploitation." Pixel phones at patch level 2026-09-05 or later have that fix.

articles.title: Cryptomonnaies : la taxation lors du passage en stablecoin adoptée à l'Assemblée. Mais il reste de l'espoir
articles.text:
C'est un mauvaise nouvelle qui arrive de l'Assemblée nationale, avec l'adoption de la taxation lors du passage de cryptomonnaies à un stablecoin. Mais il reste du chemin à faire pour que ça devienne une règle en France !
Les négociations autour du Projet de loi de finances (PLF) 2027 ont débuté, dans une ambiance qui a rarement été aussi rude, au vu des difficultés financières de l'État. Et il semble que personne n'échappera aux envies de taxation des députés, et surtout pas la cible toujours facible des cryptomonnaies. Car un amendement qui vient juste d'être voté va faire parler !
La Comission des Finances adopte un amendement du PLF 2027 taxant les opérations crypto-stablecoin
Voilà un amendement qui na va pas plaire à tout le monde ! En effet, l'amendement déposé par le député communiste Nicolas Sansu et imposant la taxation lors d'un passage d'une cryptomonnaie à un stablecoin vient d'être adopté en Commission des finances.
Avec cet amendement, tout passage d'une cryptomonnaie à un stablecoin comme l'USDC déclenche le calcul d'une plus-value. Et si plus-value il y a, celle-ci devient soumise à la flat tax, ou au barème progressif de l'impôt sur le revenu. Aujourd'hui, seul le passage au fiat (comme l'euro) déclenche l'imposition.
Vers un budget à nouveau passé grâce au 49-3 ?
Fait intéressant, comme noté par nos collègues de Cryptoast, seuls les stablecoins régulés par le règlement MiCA sont concernés. Un stablecoin décentralisé comme DAI, le jeton adossé sur l'or physique PAXG ou même l'USDT ne sont pas concernés.
Reste que les jeux ne sont pas encore faits. Si l'on peut craindre qu'un tel amendement soit adopté dès le début des discussions du PLF 2027, il faut ensuite qu'il le soit en session à l'Assemblée nationale, puis ensuite au Sénat. De quoi donner le temps aux investisseurs de cryptomonnaies de se faire entendre.
Enfin, et surtout plus important, il y a des chances que ce Projet de loi de finances suive la même trajectoire que ceux de 2025 et 2026. Ces derniers n'avaient pas été votés par l'Assemblée nationale, mais adoptés sans vote à l'aide du 49-3. Une procédure, pour rappel, dans laquelle le gouvernement choisit les amendements votés par les députés qu'il souhaite garder dans le texte, avant d'engager sa responsabilité pour imposer le texte de son choix. Dans ce cadre, le gouvernement pourrait décider de rejeter cet amendement, même s'il était prochainement voté.

articles.title: Cuáles son las 10 de creadoras de contenido hechas con IA con millones de seguidores y campañas de miles de dólares
articles.text:
Las creadoras de contenido generadas por inteligencia artificial ganan cada vez más popularidad en las redes sociales. Tal es el caso de Lu do Magalu, la influencer virtual más seguida del mundo, creada por la empresa minorista brasileña Magazine Luiza (Magalu). Tiene 9,7 millones de seguidores y apareció en la portada de Vogue en febrero de 2022.
Sus publicaciones en Instagram, sin embargo, no registran la cantidad de Me gusta que podría esperarse de una cuenta con esa cantidad de seguidores. Entre sus publicaciones recientes, la que más interacciones recibió obtuvo 609 Me gusta y unos 142 comentarios.
Como referencia, la creadora de contenido humana y conductora del podcast Call Her Daddy, Alex Cooper, tiene 7,9 millones de seguidores en Instagram. Su publicación más reciente fue un video que ya acumuló 137 mil Me gusta y 957 comentarios.
Así como Lu do Magalu, hay diversas creadoras de contenido generadas por IA que también acumulan millones de seguidores.
Qué otras creadores de contenido de IA existen
Además de Lu do Magalu, estas son otras creadoras con muchos seguidores:
- Lil Miquela.
Lil Miquela, una influencer virtual creada mediante tecnología digital, se convirtió en una de las figuras más reconocidas de este fenómeno en las redes sociales. Bajo el nombre de Miquela Sousa, el personaje publica contenidos vinculados con la moda, la música y la cultura pop.
Su cuenta de Instagram reúne 2,2 millones de seguidores y registra más de 1.500 publicaciones.
Aunque muchas de sus publicaciones tienen desactivado el conteo público de “Me gusta”, una foto compartida recientemente permite dimensionar parte de su interacción: acumuló 1.048 Me gusta.
- Milla Sofia.
Milla Sofia se presenta como una artista virtual enfocada en la música y las imágenes cinematográficas asistidas por inteligencia artificial. Su perfil de Instagram, @millasofiain, reúne 686 mil seguidores, sigue a 58 cuentas y acumula 1.007 publicaciones.
La creadora comparte retratos, videos y contenidos en los que aparece interpretando canciones, con una estética vinculada a la moda y la producción audiovisual. En su biografía invita a escuchar su música y dirige a sus seguidores a plataformas como Spotify.
Una de sus publicaciones recientes, en la que intepreta una canción alcanzó 89,2 mil Me gusta y 1.857 comentarios.
- Noonoouri.
Noonoouri es una artista virtual que combina moda, música y contenido digital en su cuenta de Instagram, donde reúne 454 mil seguidores. El perfil, que acumula 2.249 publicaciones, la presenta como artista y exhibe vínculos con IMG Models y Warner Music.
La creadora comparte imágenes de campañas, sesiones de fotos y apariciones en escenarios construidos digitalmente. Al igual que Lil Miquela no tiene activado el conteo de Me gusta en todas las publicaciones.
- Aitana Lopez.
Aitana Lopez es una influencer virtual enfocada en contenidos de entrenamiento, estilo de vida y belleza. Su perfil de Instagram, @fit_aitana, se identifica como generado con inteligencia artificial y reúne 404 mil seguidores, con 375 publicaciones.
La cuenta combina imágenes de rutinas de ejercicio, retratos de maquillaje, videos de moda y fotografías. La estética del perfil está marcada por el cabello rosado del personaje, que aparece en gimnasios, calles y producciones vinculadas al cuidado personal.
- Imma.
Imma es una creadora digital virtual que combina moda, música, tecnología y cultura pop en su cuenta de Instagram, @imma.gram. El perfil reúne 377 mil seguidores, suma 968 publicaciones y se presenta como una figura digital nacida en Japón.
- Naina.
Naina Avtr se presenta como la primera superestrella de inteligencia artificial de India. Su cuenta de Instagram, @naina_avtr, reúne 343 mil seguidores, sigue a 190 perfiles y acumula 729 publicaciones.
El perfil se identifica como generado con IA y describe al personaje como actriz, influencer y diseñadora. Además, destaca reconocimientos como creadora de inteligencia artificial de NDTV WhosThat360 en 2024, influencer de IA de Midday Showbiz en 2024 e influencer de IA internacional en 2024.
No obstante, sus publicaciones (en la mayoría de casos) no superan los 80 Me gusta.
- Ana y Mia Zelu.
Ana Zelu y Mia Zelu son dos perfiles generados con inteligencia artificial que muestran estética de moda, música y estilo de vida en Instagram.
Ana Zelu, que se presenta como una creadora de contenido sobre moda y viajes, reúne 306 mil seguidores con apenas 40 publicaciones. Su perfil también promociona el lanzamiento de la canción Entre Ahora y Antes.
Mia Zelu, por su parte, tiene 283 mil seguidores y 154 publicaciones. Su biografía se identifica como un perfil generado con IA y anuncia el tema Endless Summer.
- Shudu.
Shudu se presenta como “la primera supermodelo digital del mundo” y reúne 235 mil seguidores en Instagram. Su cuenta, @shudu.gram, acumula 211 publicaciones y exhibe retratos, videos y producciones de moda protagonizados por un personaje digital de piel oscura.
El perfil combina imágenes de campañas de belleza, trajes de baño y editoriales con una estética inspirada en la fotografía de moda.
En una de sus publicaciones recientes, Shudu aparece con un vestido amarillo y obtuvo 610 Me gusta y 83 comentarios.

articles.title: Un écran de 218 cm pour vos films et vos matchs : ce téléviseur LG MiniLED est à 1 099,99 €
articles.text:
Le téléviseur LG QNED85 MiniLED 4K de 86 pouces est à 1 099,99 €
Avec sa diagonale de 86 pouces, son rétroéclairage MiniLED et sa dalle 120 Hz, le LG QNED85 s’adresse aux amateurs de très grands écrans.
Le LG QNED85 de 86 pouces est proposé à 1 099,99 € sur Amazon, dans sa version 2026. Le téléviseur est indiqué en stock, vendu et expédié par Amazon, avec une livraison gratuite sur la capture fournie. Ce modèle est habituellement proposé à 1790 €.
Un écran MiniLED de 86 pouces pour le salon
Avec une diagonale d’environ 218 cm et une définition de 3 840 × 2 160 pixels, ce QNED85 mise d’abord sur son grand format. Les films, les retransmissions sportives et les jeux occupent ainsi une surface d’affichage importante, à condition de disposer d’un emplacement adapté.
Son rétroéclairage MiniLED s’accompagne du système Precision Dimming, qui ajuste l’éclairage par zones pour travailler le contraste. Le téléviseur prend également en charge les formats HDR Dolby Vision, HDR10 et HLG. Ces caractéristiques ne suffisent toutefois pas, à elles seules, à préjuger de ses performances mesurées.
La partie connectée repose sur webOS 26, pour accéder aux applications et services compatibles directement depuis le téléviseur. Ce format impose aussi de vérifier la largeur du meuble et l’espace disponible avant de commander.
Une dalle 120 Hz et quatre entrées HDMI
Le QNED85 dispose d’une dalle à 120 Hz natifs et prend en charge le rafraîchissement variable, ainsi qu’AMD FreeSync. Ces fonctions permettent d’adapter l’affichage au rythme des images envoyées par une source compatible, notamment pour limiter les déchirures d’image dans les jeux.
Les quatre entrées HDMI prennent en charge la 4K à 120 Hz. Une connexion eARC permet également de transmettre le son à une barre de son ou à un amplificateur compatible. Quant au Motion Booster annoncé jusqu’à 288 Hz, LG précise qu’il fonctionne en Full HD : il ne s’agit donc pas d’un affichage 4K à cette fréquence.

articles.title: The festive sales playbook: How Amazon and Flipkart are winning India’s mega sales
articles.text:
The festive sales playbook: How Amazon and Flipkart are winning India’s mega sales
India’s festive sale showdown sees Amazon and Flipkart racing to dominate non-metro markets, relying on instant quick-commerce deliveries, no-cost financing, and targeted AI tools to turn record traffic into sales.
If you’ve been tracking the annual showdown between Amazon’s Great Indian Festival and Flipkart’s Big Billion Days, it’s easy to get bogged down in the hype. Every year brings promises of bigger discounts and flashier launch events. But looking past the standard headlines this season, the actual narrative on the ground has shifted. The real battle isn't just about who knocks a few extra rupees off a television; it’s about instant fulfillment, structural supply chain pivots, and an aggressive push in Tier II and III cities.
The Amazon Great Indian Festival started a day earlier on October 8 compared to Flipkart’s Big Billion Days. Flipkart started its sale on October 9, with early access to select members starting a day ahead. Preparing for the big sale days, Flipkart created 2.5 lakh new opportunities to support this year’s Big Billion Days.
The biggest change in strategy this year comes down to delivery speed. Quick commerce has officially crossed over from grocery apps into mainstream ecommerce. Amazon brought its 10-to-15-minute quick delivery setup, Amazon Now, directly into its main festival sale for the first time. Supported by 800 micro-procurement centers in 120 cities, they were delivering flagship iPhones within minutes of the sale opening at midnight, on 8 October. Beyond the ultra-fast tier, Amazon opened up 10 million products for same-day delivery and another 40 million for next-day delivery nationwide.
Flipkart has responded with a similar operational pivot, embedding Flipkart Minutes (internally known as Magenta) directly into its primary app. Rather than switching apps, shoppers can search once and choose quick delivery for fast-turnaround items. To keep up with the volume without breaking its logistics engine, Flipkart added 250,000 seasonal workers and expanded its Ekart network into 750 new pin codes.
While metro cities drive significant transaction values, smaller urban centers are setting the pace for volume. Amazon hit 100% pin code coverage across India within hours of launch, with Tier-II and III cities generating 60% to 65% of total orders. Flipkart recorded nearly identical geographic demand, with over 60% of its order volume coming from non-metro markets.
Digging into specific shopping categories reveals clear shifts in how consumers are spending their festive budgets.
Mobile phones have shown surprising strength despite widespread industry talk about a cooling smartphone market. Amazon reported a 70% year-on-year jump in Android phone sales, driven by strong momentum from brands like Samsung, Xiaomi, and OnePlus, while premium flagship models across both platforms saw rapid initial uptake.
Home upgrades are another major driver, with shoppers taking advantage of festive financing to upgrade core household electronics. Amazon said it logged a 90% year-on-year increase in large appliances like refrigerators, washing machines, and air conditioners, while overall TV sales doubled compared to last year. Within televisions, 55-inch models grew the fastest, showing a clear preference for larger screens and better display technology.
Health and personal wellness products saw some of the most dramatic growth rates. On Amazon, wearable health trackers jumped 1,400% year-on-year, led by Apple, Samsung, and Whoop—which alone grew 900%. Air purifiers climbed 300% year-on-year, while premium treadmills also saw strong order volume.
Niche lifestyle categories, specialty kitchenware, and gifting items posted notable numbers across both storefronts. Espresso machines, led by De'Longhi, grew 500% year-on-year on Amazon, while Korean beauty brands tripled their sales volume. Gifting-related categories saw dinnerware grow 500%, juicers rise 400%, Lego sets increase 212%, and handheld vacuums expand 200%. Over on Flipkart, high-volume unit orders in fashion, beauty, personal care, and home decor remained the backbone of daily order volume, driving up to 90% growth in non-metro regions.
Flexible financing was a key driver in getting shoppers to complete these purchases. Amazon saw its no-cost EMI adoption rate jump from 30–35% last year to 50% in the opening hours of this sale, meaning one out of every two eligible purchases used structured financing. Flipkart reported a 30% to 40% rise in no-cost EMI usage, with customers increasingly applying credit to lower-ticket items like fashion rather than keeping it strictly for high-end electronics.
Finally, both platforms leaned on tech and media to help shoppers navigate their massive catalogs. Amazon deployed its AI shopping assistant, Rufus, to handle millions of customer queries in English and regional languages—helping with product comparisons, deal discovery, and installation details. Flipkart focused heavily on creator-led social commerce, mobilising an ecosystem of 200,000 monthly creators on platforms like Meta to run targeted video content aimed at Gen Z and younger shoppers, who now account for nearly 40% of its customer base."

articles.title: Citrix Patches Critical NetScaler Flaw That Could Enable RCE in SAML Deployments
articles.text:
Citrix has released patches for yet another critical security flaw impacting NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway that could result in remote code execution or denial-of-service (DoS) under certain conditions.
"CVE-2026-107406 is a memory overflow vulnerability that may lead to remote code execution or denial-of-service under specific configuration conditions," Citrix said.
The vulnerability carries a CVSS score of 9.5 out of 10.0. There is no evidence that the issue has been exploited in the wild. Citrix has credited Michael Tucker, Chew Keong Tan, and Alex Bernier of the JPMorgan Chase XOR Team, along with Maxim Suhanov, for discovering and reporting the flaw.
Successful exploitation hinges on the NetScaler deployments being configured as a SAML identity provider (IdP) or service provider (SP). Customers can determine if their instances meet the criteria by checking the configuration for entries like below -
- SAML SP: add authentication samlAction
- SAML IdP: add authentication samlIdPProfile
The issue impacts the following versions -
- 
    When configured as a SAML IdP -
    
  - NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway between 14.1-73.37 and 14.1-73.41, inclusive
  - NetScaler ADC 14.1-FIPS between 14.1-73.37 FIPS and 14.1-73.41 FIPS, inclusive
  - NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway between 13.1-64.23 and 13.1-64.28, inclusive
  - NetScaler ADC 13.1-FIPS between 13.1-NDcPP 13.1-37.279 and 13.1- 37.282, inclusive
- 
    When configured as a SAML SP or SAML IdP:
    
  - NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway before 14.1-73.37
  - NetScaler ADC 14.1-FIPS before 14.1-73.37 FIPS
  - NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway before 13.1-64.23
  - NetScaler ADC 13.1-FIPS before 13.1-NDcPP 13.1-37.279
"Secure Private Access Hybrid deployments using NetScaler instances are also affected by the vulnerability," Citrix warned. "Customers need to upgrade these NetScaler instances to the recommended NetScaler versions to address the vulnerability."
The shortcoming has been addressed in the versions below -
- Citrix NetScaler ADC and Citrix NetScaler Gateway 14.1-73.46 and later releases
- Citrix NetScaler ADC and Citrix NetScaler Gateway 13.1-64.29 and later releases of 13.1
- Citrix NetScaler ADC 14.1-FIPS 14.1-73.46 FIPS and later releases of 14.1-FIPS
- Citrix NetScaler ADC 13.1-FIPS and 13.1-NDcPP 13.1.37.283 and later releases of 13.1-FIPS and 13.1-NDcPP
The development comes as three different flaws in NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway appliances (CVE 2026-88771, CVE 2026-88772, and CVE 2026-88779) have come under active exploitation in the wild.

articles.title: Why public capital isn’t enough to save India’s deeptech
articles.text:
Why public capital isn’t enough to save India’s deeptech
The most powerful derisker is not a fund at all. It is a customer. A Rs 200 crore procurement commitment from the defence, space or railways sectors does more for a series B round than a Rs 200 crore grant, because it validates revenue rather than science.
Can government funds derisk deeptech enough to make private capital comfortable in India? Partly. The state is well placed to absorb technology risk. It is far less able to remove the two risks that actually keep fund managers awake: time and exit. Unless policy addresses those, India will get plenty of capital without much conviction behind it.
Start with the momentum, which is real. India’s AI and deep tech investment reached $2.1 bn across 289 deals in 2025, and deep tech share of total VC – PE activity has climbed to roughly 15%, up from 4% in 2016. The 2026 numbers look even better at first glance through August, Indian deeptech companies raised $2.22 billion across 179 rounds against $861 million across 287 rounds in the same period last year.
Look closer, though. Funding rose about 2.6 times while the number of rounds fell by nearly 40%. The average cheque went from roughly $3 million to over $12 million, a four-fold jump. Private capital is getting comfortable with deeptech companies that are already derisked. It is not getting comfortable with the derisking itself. Money is crowding into proven AI and hardware winners, and fewer new bets are being placed. That gap is exactly what public funds should fill.
The state’s toolkit is now large. The Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) Scheme, envisages a Rs. 1 lakh crore corpus over 6 years with Rs. 20,000 crore allocated in FY 2025-26 Union budget. Alongside it sits the Startup India Fund of Funds 2.0. SIDBI is mandated to deploy Rs 10,000 crores through SEBI registered AIFs, with the government's stake alongside private investors, who comprise a majority of the Fund corpus. The first version worked as a multiplier in 145 AIFs, which together invested more than Rs. 25,500 crores in over 1,370 startups. That is a leverage ratio of about 2.5x.
Now the maths is what matters. Spread evenly, the RDI corpus works out to about Rs. 16700 crores a year, or roughly $1.7 bn. That is very close to the size of India’s entire annual deeptech VC haul. The state is no longer a marginal anchor. It is an almost co-equal capital provider, and that scale can crowd private money in or crowd it out. But this will depend on which risk the money absorbs.
Technology risk means asking whether the product will work. Grants and lab-to-market funding (debt / equity) handle this well, and then RDI design targets it directly. Time risk is the mismatch between 8–12 year development cycles and 10 year fund lives, and patient fund-of-funds capital helps only partly. Exit risk is the weakest link.
The IVCA Bharat Deeptech Report 2026 notes that gaps persist in growth-stage funding and exits. Tracxn counts 104 acquisitions and 46 IPOs in the sector, set against 1,821 funded companies. That’s about one exit for every twelve funded startups over a decade. No LP will underwrite a fund on those odds, however much first loss cushion the government provides.
The most powerful derisker is not a fund at all. It is a customer. A Rs 200 crore procurement commitment from the defence, space or railways sectors does more for a series B round than a Rs 200 crore grant, because it validates revenue rather than science. Advance market commitments, outcome-based public purchase contracts and faster IDEX-style procurement would turn government from a financier into an anchor buyer. That is what private capital actually prices.
Corporate India is also ready to co-invest. Private industry’s share of total R&D spending passed the government’s, reaching 51.8% in 2023-24, as GERD rose to 0.84% of GDP. Yet peers such as the US (3.45%), China (2.58%), and South Korea (4.94%) invest far more. Some government funding through corporate venture arms and strategic acquirers would create the exit buyers the ecosystem lacks.
Sceptics raise fair concerns. State capital at this scale may inflate valuations. It may encourage “policy-shaped” startups that chase allocations rather than markets. It may also displace the private investors it is meant to attract. Israel’s Yozma programme worked partly because the government exited quickly. India’s design, through second-level managers and stake caps, gestures in that direction but has yet to be tested.
So the answer is a qualified yes. Government funds can make private capital comfortable, but only if the state thinks like a first customer and an early exit buyer, not just a generous LP.
Padmaja Ruparel, Co-founder, IAN Group

articles.title: Bitdefender mise sur une protection complète sans faire grimper le prix trop haut
Alerte sur l'emploi des jeunes : l'IA a détruit 75 000 CDI par an en France
articles.text:
On commence déjà à bien sentir les effets de l'IA sur le marché du travail. Et ce, particulièrement du côté des jeunes !
En ces temps de colère lycéenne et étudiante, on parle beaucoup de l'avenir bouché au niveau emploi des jeunes générations. Celles-ci doivent en effet faire avec l'émergence de l'intelligence artificielle, qui peut remplacer l'humain sur un nombre assez conséquent de tâches. Et ce n'est plus seulement une vue de l'esprit, comme nous le montre cette étude assez inquiétante !
Une chute de 28,9% des embauches en CDI des 21-29 ans enregistrée depuis 2022
Une nouvelle étude signée HEC et la Banque de France vient confirmer ce que beaucoup craignaient. L'IA a déjà commencé son travail de sape dans le monde de l'emploi, et particulièrement du côté des plus fragiles : les jeunes.
Selon cette étude, dont La Croix se fait l'écho, depuis 2022 (moment où l'IA décolle, avec le lancement de ChatGPT en novembre de cette année) les embauches en CDI des 21-29 ans ont lourdement chuté, de 28,3%, dans les emplois les plus exposés. Un recul qui correspond tout simplement à près de 75 000 CDI en moins offerts chaque année à cette classe d'âge.
Un danger à long terme pour les entreprises ?
Et il s'agit de postes non crées, et non pas de basculements de CDI vers des CDD. En effet, tout contrats confondus, le recul reste de 22,1%. À noter que ce que l'étude appelle emplois les plus exposés va de journaliste, traducteur ou technicien d'opérations bancaires à développeur informatique. Ces derniers sont ceux qui souffrent clairement le plus, avec une chute du nombre de CDI pour les jeunes de tout simplement 42%. En comparaison, la catégorie de métiers les moins exposés, comme aide-soignante ou ouvrier qualifié, n'enregistre que 7,5% de recul sur cette tranche démographique.
Et pour être plus précis, les auteurs expliquent qu'il s'agit ici moins de postes détruits que d'emplois non créés, les entreprises ne pourvoyant plus à leurs nouveaux besoins en faisant appel aux jeunes, mais plutôt en usant de l'IA. Reste tout de même que, sur le long terme, il se pourrait que le pari soit dangereux. « Si vous avez arrêté de recruter pendant plusieurs années, vous avez arrêté de former certaines compétences et vous allez avoir des jeunes qui vont aussi changer de filière, et donc il va y avoir une sorte de pénurie » alerte Antonin Bergeaud, un des économistes à l'origine de l'étude.

articles.title: Anthropic ofrece escaneos gratis de seguridad con IA para proyectos de software libre
articles.text:
Anthropic lanzó OSS Scanner, un servicio gratuito que usa sus modelos de inteligencia artificial más potentes para buscar fallas de seguridad en proyectos de software libre. Los mantenedores que se suman reciben escaneos periódicos sin costo, según anunció la empresa el jueves en su sitio oficial.
La particularidad del servicio es que los reportes salen directo del modelo, sin que un humano los revise antes de enviarlos a los equipos de cada proyecto. Anthropic lo reconoce de forma explícita en su comunicado.
“Los resultados de este escáner de vulnerabilidades opcional serán generados íntegramente por el modelo, sin revisión ni clasificación humana”, escribió la empresa, y aclaró que eso implica que algunos reportes podrían ser incorrectos o inválidos.
El cuello de botella que motivó el cambio
Anthropic explicó que durante los últimos seis meses usó sus modelos para escanear software ampliamente utilizado y encontró más de 29.000 vulnerabilidades candidatas. De esa cifra, solo pudo revisar y confirmar manualmente alrededor de 6.000.
La compañía admitió que ese proceso de verificación humana se convirtió en una traba. Por eso, ante el pedido de varios mantenedores de recibir todo lo que el modelo detectaba sin esperar la validación, ya envió cerca de 5.000 reportes sin revisar a quienes lo solicitaron.
El servicio se inspiró en OSS-Fuzz, la herramienta que Google mantiene desde 2016 para escanear código abierto con técnicas de fuzzing, una forma de probar programas con datos aleatorios para forzar errores. Anthropic adoptó un criterio de elegibilidad similar: los proyectos deben tener un impacto crítico sobre infraestructura y seguridad de los usuarios, y la empresa evalúa cada solicitud caso por caso.
El nuevo servicio se apoya en la experiencia previa de Project Glasswing, una iniciativa de este año en la que Anthropic asoció un modelo todavía no publicado, llamado Claude Mythos, con Amazon Web Services, Google, Microsoft, Cisco, CrowdStrike, JPMorganChase y la Linux Foundation para rastrear fallas en infraestructura crítica de código abierto.
Cómo funciona la inscripción
Los mantenedores de un proyecto pueden anotarse enviando una solicitud de incorporación de código al repositorio público de OSS Scanner en GitHub, junto con un archivo de configuración que describe el proyecto y un entorno de prueba aislado sin acceso a internet.
Cada reporte incluye una explicación del error, los pasos para reproducirlo y, cuando es posible, una solución propuesta. Anthropic no exige un plazo de divulgación obligatorio sobre los hallazgos sin validar, algo habitual en otros programas de seguridad, porque reconoce que podrían contener errores.
Si un hallazgo pasa luego por el proceso tradicional de revisión humana y se confirma, ahí sí empieza a correr el plazo estándar de 90 días para hacerlo público. Según The Hacker News, hasta el momento del anuncio ya se habían presentado 116 solicitudes de incorporación al repositorio.
Un lanzamiento con reservas de fondo
El medio especializado SiliconANGLE señaló que OSS Scanner forma parte de un paquete más amplio, bautizado Anthropic Cyber Mission, que también incluye un programa dirigido a empresas de infraestructura crítica como redes eléctricas y sistemas de agua.
Ese mismo reporte indicó que Anthropic no precisó quién cubre el costo de cómputo del nuevo servicio ni qué pasa con el código que analiza, más allá de mencionar que un fondo interno llamado Defender Advantage Fund financia que el escaneo siga siendo gratuito para los mantenedores.
Según Help Net Security, en una prueba previa con penetradores externos sobre 97 hallazgos de severidad alta o crítica en 48 proyectos, Anthropic confirmó que 85 cumplían sus criterios de divulgación coordinada, once resultaron hallazgos genuinos pero duplicados y solo uno fue inválido.

articles.title: Apple’s 512GB local AI beast nears, but M5 Max gets $200 price drop
articles.text:
As Apple readies its 512GB M5 Ultra Mac Studio for local AI, the M5 Max workstation drops by $200
This is one for serious pros
Apple's most extreme Mac Studio, an M5 Ultra with 512GB of memory aimed at running huge AI models locally, is due to ship in late October. And that might be one reason why I'm seeing the - ahem - "cheaper" M5 Max model dropping $200 in price right now.
• Best for: Creative professionals and AI developers who want Mac Studio power without paying M5 Ultra prices.
• The deal: The Apple Mac Studio (M5 Max, 36GB, 512GB) is $2299 (was $2499) at B&H Photo.
• Why it matters: We're expecting to see more of the 512GB M5 Ultra at Apple's upcoming event next week. And I reckon we could be looking at prices starting well above $10,000. That makes the M5 Max Mac Studio the machine most people can realistically buy, and it's now cheaper as the new flagship approaches.
Today's best Mac Studio (M5 Max) deal
This is the base M5 Max configuration, with an 18-core CPU, 32-core GPU and 16-core Neural Engine. It has four Thunderbolt 5 ports, 10Gb Ethernet, HDMI 2.1, an SD card slot and Wi-Fi 7, and B&H notes that supply at this price is limited.
Why we recommend it
Our roundup of M5 Ultra Mac Studio reviews revealed the Ultra's real strength is local AI, while its multi-core lead over the M5 Max is only about 26% and single-core performance is about the same, which is why the roundup points most creative users to the M5 Max. The M5 Max is the best-suited model for most professionals, as 36GB of memory fits many workflows. However, 1TB is a more practical starting point for storage than 512GB, and that's currently discounted to $2579 (was $2799) on the site.
Price Context & Historical Value
At $2,299, this is $200 (8%) off Apple's $2,499 starting price. Now, Mac Studio discounts may improve in the months after launch, especially around Black Friday, so this may not be the lowest price it reaches - but it's the lowest I've seen right now. As with previous Macs, you can't upgrade the memory in this model later, so make sure 36GB is enough before you buy.
Should you buy it?
✅ Buy the Apple Mac Studio (M5 Max) if...
You want Mac Studio performance for creative work or local AI at around $2,300, and you don't need the M5 Ultra's 512GB memory ceiling.
❌ Skip the Apple Mac Studio (M5 Max) if...
You need the 512GB M5 Ultra for large local AI models, or you want more than 512GB of storage without an external drive.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Bryan M. Wolfe is a staff writer at TechRadar, iMore, and wherever Future can use him. Though his passion is Apple-based products, he doesn't have a problem using Windows and Android. Bryan's a single father of a 15-year-old daughter and a puppy, Isabelle. Thanks for reading!

articles.title: FBI Seizes 7 Domains, Disrupts Flax Typhoon Tools Used in Critical Infrastructure Intrusions
articles.text:
The U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) and Department of Justice (DoJ) have announced the disruption of malicious tools used by a China-linked advanced persistent threat group known as Flax Typhoon.
To that end, the agencies seized several domains and blocked access to platforms that were used to scan, and in some cases infiltrate, U.S. critical infrastructure. The list of seized domains is as follows -
- c0cc[.]cc
- 98aiblog[.]com
- 98aicai[.]com
- 98aicode[.]com
- outlook3650[.]com
- youtubecard[.]com
- linkedinns[.]net
Flax Typhoon, also tracked as Ethereal Panda and RedJuliett, is associated with Integrity Technology Group, a Beijing-based company that contracts with the Chinese government. It was previously attributed to a botnet called Raptor Train that comprised thousands of compromised small office/home office (SOHO) and IoT devices. It was taken down following a U.S. court-authorized operation in September 2024.
"These state-sponsored hackers continue to aggressively target and access networks and systems throughout the world in an effort to identify and steal files and otherwise exploit victims' vulnerabilities," said U.S. Attorney Troy Rivetti for the Western District of Pennsylvania.
Court documents allege that Integrity Tech created and operated an IoT botnet that leveraged a variant of the Mirai malware. According to the FBI, the botnet is said to have used a number of domains, including subdomains of w8510[.]com, for command-and-control (C2), enabling bidirectional communications between the operators and devices in the botnet. The botnet itself was controlled and managed by an application named Sparrow.
A database server hosted on the server ("202.182.109[.]151") contained records for more than 1.2 million infected devices as of June 5, 2024, including over 385,000 unique U.S. victim devices. In all, more than 260,000 devices, including approximately 126,000 U.S. devices, were actively infected as of June 5, 2024.
The botnet made use of a tool called Microscan to facilitate reconnaissance and computer vulnerability scanning, allowing the threat actors to identify targets of interest. The Python-based web tool, originally hosted on "198.13.53[.]226," was accessible via the domain "c0cc[.]cc" as recently as September 9, 2026, according to an FBI affidavit. The tool is believed to have been put to use as early as 2017.
MicroScan features over 1,300 penetration testing scripts to scan websites for specific vulnerabilities, including OpenSSL, Oracle WebLogic, Rejetto, WordPress, Juniper ScreenOS, Jenkins, and Apache Struts. The scanner is complemented by open-source tooling like BBScan, dirsearch, Fscan, ksubdomain, masscan, NMAP, OneForAll, ShuiZe, and wpscan that are used to find vulnerabilities in networks and web-based applications.
Some of the targeted companies include a U.S. power company based in South Carolina, a multi-national Non-Governmental Organization, Japanese and Polish airports, Taiwanese critical infrastructure companies in the natural gas and power sectors, and two Taiwanese universities.
A second Integrity Tech tool is FishHub, which allegedly enabled the exploitation of computer networks through spear-phishing attacks and the deployment of follow-on payloads. Confirmed victims of FishHub-related activity include 20 Taiwanese universities.
"This malware provided Integrity Tech's clients with unauthorized remote access to the victim network or searched for specific files and sent them to servers controlled by Integrity Tech," the DoJ said.
"Integrity Technology Group provided China-linked threat actors with capabilities used to conduct widespread vulnerability scanning and, in some cases, intrusions targeting U.S. and foreign critical infrastructure," said Assistant Director Brett Leatherman of the FBI's Cyber Division.
"The PRC relies on contractor and enabling companies to expand the reach and scale of its malicious cyber activity. By exposing and disrupting these enablers, we make it harder for the PRC to target American networks and infrastructure."
In tandem, a joint advisory issued by cybersecurity and intelligence agencies from the U.S., the U.K., Australia, Canada, Japan, New Zealand, and Spain has called out the for-profit company for enabling malicious cyber actors to target organizations worldwide by acquiring or building cyber tools for use and sale and compromising networks.
Since at least mid-January 2021, the threat actors have been observed breaking into victim networks and cloud-based services using Python- and Go-based command line utilities, while also relying on cross-site scripting (XSS) attacks to conduct user credential harvesting.
Besides installing SoftEther VPN software clients on victim devices for persistence, the threat actors have been found to use EBurst, an open-source Python-based brute-force tool, to target accounts in Microsoft 365 Cloud environments, and gain unauthorized access to mailbox data using a command-line utility known as office-cli.
"Malicious cyber actors, enabled by Integrity Tech, are uniquely using AI tools, such as automated scanning, alongside large-scale botnets and manual exploitation techniques to compromise and steal confidential data from companies around the world, including critical sectors," the U.K. National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) said.
The development comes as the U.S. State Department announced rewards of up to $10 million for information leading to the identification or location of Zhang Yu, a Chinese national charged in the U.S. in connection with the 2021 Microsoft Exchange Server attacks.
The activity is tracked under the moniker Silk Typhoon (formerly Hafnium). In April 2026, co-defendant Xu Zewei was extradited to the U.S. from Italy to face charges related to allegedly stealing COVID-19 research from U.S.-based universities, immunologists, and virologists.
