articles.title: Même prix, 4 To en moins... La décision de Microsoft qui va faire enrager les abonnés 365
articles.text:
Microsoft remplace le téraoctet de stockage OneDrive accordé à chaque membre des abonnements Family et Premium par une enveloppe commune de 2 To. Les familles les plus gourmandes devront donc composer avec beaucoup moins de place, alors que leur abonnement ne coûte pas moins cher.
Les familles qui ont confié leurs photos, leurs vidéos et leurs documents à Microsoft 365 vont devoir refaire leurs comptes. Jusqu’ici, un abonnement partagé entre six personnes donnait à chacune son propre téraoctet sur OneDrive, soit 6 To au total.
Avec le nouveau fonctionnement, ces mêmes utilisateurs devront se répartir 2 To. Les deux tiers de la capacité peuvent ainsi disparaître sans réduire pour autant le prix de l'abonnement à la suite bureautique de Microsoft. En France, la formule Famille reste affichée à 129 euros par an.
Microsoft vante la souplesse du partage, mais réduit la place disponible
Pour défendre ce changement, l’éditeur met en avant une limite de l’ancien système. Une personne pouvait remplir son téraoctet pendant que les autres membres de la famille utilisaient à peine leur espace, sans pouvoir récupérer la capacité laissée libre. Désormais, celui qui conserve le plus de fichiers pourra dépasser 1 To, tant que l’ensemble du groupe reste sous le plafond commun. Le changement peut donc profiter aux foyers dans lesquels une seule personne utilise vraiment OneDrive. Pour ceux qui comptaient sur plusieurs téraoctets, le calcul est nettement moins favorable.
Cette mutualisation ne donne pas pour autant accès aux documents des autres. Chaque membre conserve ses fichiers privés et choisit ce qu’il souhaite partager. Les offres individuelles gardent aussi leur capacité actuelle avec 1 To pour Microsoft 365 Personnel et 100 Go pour Basic. La formule Pro dispose, elle, de 5 To partagés.
La décision passe d’autant plus mal que Microsoft avait déjà augmenté ses tarifs en janvier 2025, en intégrant Copilot à ses abonnements grand public. En France, la formule Famille était passée de 99 à 129 euros par an. Trente euros supplémentaires pour des fonctions d’IA dont tous les abonnés n’avaient pas l’utilité. Des offres Classic sans Copilot avaient bien été proposées à certains clients existants, mais il fallait entreprendre la démarche pour y basculer.
Microsoft prévoit maintenant d’étendre les avantages de Copilot aux autres membres des abonnements Family et Premium, selon un courriel consulté par The Verge. Jusqu’ici, seul le titulaire en bénéficiait. Les utilisateurs de l’assistant pourront apprécier cette ouverture, mais elle ne répond guère aux besoins de ceux qui cherchent surtout à conserver leurs fichiers.
Un changement de formule peut accélérer la bascule
D’après la FAQ consacrée à cette transition, les nouvelles souscriptions sont soumises au stockage partagé depuis le 8 octobre 2026. Les abonnés actuels conservent leurs quotas individuels jusqu’à leur premier renouvellement intervenant le 2 mai 2027 ou après. Microsoft doit les prévenir par courriel avant l’échéance.
Une autre page d’assistance de Microsoft mentionne toutefois un renouvellement à partir du 1er avril 2027. Les documents officiels donnent donc encore des calendriers contradictoires, et les abonnés devront vérifier l’échéance annoncée dans leur courriel.
Attention, toutefois, à ne pas précipiter ce changement en passant à une offre supérieure. Migrer de Family vers Premium avant cette date déclenche immédiatement le passage aux 2 To partagés. En revanche, si vous passez de Premium à Family avant le 2 mai 2027, vous conserverez 1 To par personne jusqu’au premier renouvellement de votre abonnement à partir de cette date. Mieux vaut donc vérifier le stockage utilisé par chaque membre avant de modifier son abonnement.
Les familles déjà au-dessus du plafond ne perdront pas instantanément l’accès à leurs données. Microsoft annonce des notifications et un accès aux fichiers pouvant être maintenu jusqu’à un an en cas de dépassement. L’éditeur évoque également un bonus de transition gratuit pour certains abonnés, sans préciser les volumes ni toutes les conditions d’attribution. Il sera sinon possible d’acheter des extensions qui alimenteront l’espace commun jusqu’à atteindre un maximum de 10 To de stockage en ligne.
Le moment de regarder ce que propose la concurrence
Avant de payer davantage, commencez par additionner l’espace réellement occupé par les membres du foyer. Une famille largement sous les 2 To pourra continuer comme avant tandis qu’une autre devra déplacer une partie de ses archives ou revoir son budget. Si vous utilisez surtout la bureautique dans un navigateur, Google Docs, Sheets et Slides constituent une piste avec Drive pour les fichiers et un abonnement Google One si les 15 Go gratuits du compte ne suffisent pas. Attention à comparer les capacités autant que les prix puisque le stockage familial de Google fonctionne lui aussi avec une enveloppe partagée (avec notamment Gmail et Google Photos). Changer de fournisseur pour retrouver le même plafond ne résoudra pas le problème.
Si vous travaillez la plupart du temps sur ordinateur, LibreOffice permet de dissocier les logiciels du stockage. La suite est gratuite et les documents peuvent être enregistrés dans un dossier synchronisé avec un service comme kDrive, chez Infomaniak. Cette combinaison mérite d’être étudiée si vous utilisez peu les fonctions propres à Word ou Excel. Testez néanmoins vos fichiers habituels avant de migrer, particulièrement les classeurs contenant des macros, dont la compatibilité reste partielle. Et récupérez une copie locale complète de vos données avant toute résiliation.
Quant à l’IA, quitter Microsoft 365 n’oblige pas à renoncer à un assistant pour rédiger un courrier, résumer un document ou analyser un tableau. ChatGPT, Claude, Mistral et Gemini proposent tous des versions gratuites avec certes des limites d’utilisation, mais qui peuvent bien convenir à des besoins occasionnels. Il faudra parfois leur transmettre ses fichiers ou copier son texte dans leur interface, ce qui est moins immédiat qu’un outil intégré à Word ou Excel. Mais pour quelques coups de main dans le mois, ces solutions méritent d’être essayées avant de mettre la main au portefeuille pour renouveler son abonnement à Microsoft 365.

articles.title: COFE Tech receives new backing from Phoenix Venture Partners
articles.text: Saudi Arabia-HQ enterprise technology company COFE Tech has secured an undisclosed investment from Abu Dhabi-based Phoenix Venture Partners (PVP), alongside co-investors including KSH Investments, the international investment platform of the Private Department of Sheikh Mohamed Bin Khalid Al Nahyan. The investment was completed earlier in 2026. Founded in Kuwait in 2018 by Ali Al-Ebrahim, COFE Tech, formerly COFE App, provides AI-powered procurement and commerce infrastructure to more than 1,000 business clients across 3,000 outlets in Saudi Arabia, Kuwait and the UAE. The investment announcement follows COFE Tech's recent pre-IPO funding round at a $178 million valuation, as the company prepares for a potential public listing by 2029. The amount invested by PVP and its co-investors was not disclosed. As part of the partnership, Steve Khayat, founder and CEO of PVP, has joined COFE Tech's board of directors, supporting the company's expansion, corporate governance and preparations for a potential IPO. Press release: Phoenix Venture Partners Limited (“PVP”), an ADGM-based venture capital fund manager, today announced its investment in COFE District LLC (“COFE Tech”), a leading provider of intelligent procurement and commerce infrastructure serving more than 1,000 businesses across the Gulf. Often dubbed the “Salesforce of MENA,” COFE Tech has evolved into one of the region’s leading operators of agentic AI-powered enterprise platforms. The investment, completed earlier this year, comes as COFE Tech enters its next phase of growth, a milestone that marks the beginning of a strategic partnership aimed at supporting the company throughout its growth journey and eventual IPO readiness. As part of this partnership, Steve Khayat, Founder & CEO of Phoenix Venture Partners, joins the Board of Directors of COFE Tech as PVP’s representative, further reinforcing the firm’s commitment to supporting the company’s long-term growth, governance, and institutional development. Earlier this month, the company closed a pre-IPO funding round at a valuation of US$178 million, putting COFE Tech on course for a targeted listing by 2029. This investment reflects PVP’s continued conviction in COFE Tech’s vision to redefine procurement, commerce, and enterprise enablement through technology, while reinforcing a long-standing relationship between the two organizations. Founded in 2018, COFE Tech (formerly COFE App) is an agentic enterprise provider building intelligent procurement and commerce infrastructure for businesses across the Gulf. The company operates across two core business lines, Agentic Procurement, a unified enterprise procurement engine, and Agentic Commerce, a unified enterprise technology infrastructure solution, alongside a direct-to-consumer e-commerce business. COFE Tech serves clients across the aviation, hospitality, retail, food & beverage, and corporate sectors. In the UAE, its customers include Emirates Airlines, Etihad Airways, and Al-Futtaim Group. Across the Gulf, the company serves more than 1,000 clients and 3,000 outlets. Mr. Khayat commented: “I’ve had the privilege of backing COFE Tech from its earliest days, notably at the pre-Series A stage in 2018, and it’s incredibly rewarding to continue the journey alongside Ali and the team. COFE represents exactly the kind of platform we believe in at PVP, one that starts by solving a simple, high-frequency consumer need and evolves into a deeply integrated ecosystem. Seeing the company grow from its early beginnings into a category-defining player has been remarkable, and we are excited to support its next chapter as it scales toward market leadership, institutional maturity, and ultimately a successful public market outcome. I am also pleased to deepen our engagement through my role on the Board and look forward to working closely with Ali and the team as they execute on this exciting next phase of the company’s journey.” Mr. Ali Al-Ebrahim, Founder & CEO of Cofe Tech added: “Steve has been part of our journey since the early days, and his continued support reflects the strength of our vision and execution. As we enter this next phase, we look forward to leveraging PVP’s expertise in scaling the business and navigating pre-IPO readiness as we continue building COFE Tech into a global technology platform. We are also delighted to welcome Steve to the Board of Directors and look forward to benefiting from his experience and strategic guidance as we pursue our next stage of growth.” PVP’s investment included participation from several co-investors drawn from the investor base of Phoenix Venture Partners Innovation Fund CEIC Limited (PVPIF), including KSH Investments LLC, the international investment platform of the Private Department of H.E. Sheikh Mohamed Bin Khalid Al Nahyan and one of PVPIF’s notable investors. Dr. Ahmed Mansour, CEO of KSH Investments LLC, said: “We are delighted to back COFE Tech alongside Phoenix Venture Partners. COFE is building transformative technology for commerce and procurement, and we are confident in its growth trajectory as it contributes to strengthening the UAE’s position as a global hub for innovation and the new economy.”

articles.title: NeoGrowth raises Rs 85 Cr led by FMO
articles.text:
NeoGrowth raises Rs 85 Cr led by FMO
The company said the investment will support NeoGrowth's next phase of growth as it looks to expand access to credit for MSMEs, strengthen its digital lending capabilities and deepen its market presence.
MSME-focused digital lender NeoGrowth has raised Rs 85 crore investment led by FMO, the Dutch entrepreneurial development bank, with participation from LeapFrog Investments.
A statement said, the investment will support NeoGrowth's next phase of growth as it looks to expand access to credit for MSMEs, strengthen its digital lending capabilities and deepen its market presence.
Between April 2025 and July 2026, the company raised close to Rs 2,000 crore in debt funding from 18 lenders. The other investors in NeoGrowth include Omidyar Network, Lightrock, Khosla Impact, Accion Frontier Inclusion Fund–Quona Capital, 360 ONE Asset, FMO, and LeapFrog Investments.
NeoGrowth was founded by Dhruv Khaitan and Piyush Khaitan, and manages assets under management (AUM) close to Rs 2,000 crore and disbursed more than Rs 16,000 crore. In FY26, NeoGrowth expanded its distribution footprint, adding 17 new branches, taking its presence to 46 locations.
“This investment strengthens our ability to support more MSMEs with timely and accessible formal credit as we scale our business,” said NeoGrowth Managing Director & CEO Arun Nayyar on the funding raised.
NeoGrowth said it continues to enhance its underwriting, portfolio monitoring, and risk management framework through proprietary AI-powered initiatives.
"FMO has partnered with NeoGrowth since 2017 and invested $20 million in equity in 2022. We're pleased to further strengthen that partnership through this investment, which reflects our continued confidence in NeoGrowth's team, business model, and ability to responsibly scale its impact,” said Peter Byrde, Director, Private Equity at FMO.
“Expanding access to finance for underserved entrepreneurs is a key part of FMO's strategy to support inclusive growth and reduce inequalities,” Byrde added.
FMO is the Dutch entrepreneurial development bank that focuses on sectors like agribusiness, food & forestry, energy, and financial institutions. It has a committed portfolio of 16 billion euros spanning over 85 countries.

articles.title: Have Chinese EVs peaked in the UK? BYD and Leapmotor hit record sales numbers, but new tariffs could put the brakes on
articles.text:
BYD and Leapmotor power record month for electric cars in the UK — but tariffs could soon put the brakes on Chinese EVs
Germany wants UK to increase tariffs as a show of solidarity
- The UK could impose tariffs on EVs imported from China
- Chinese manufacturers warn this will increase prices for consumers
- Germany wants the UK to back its Made in Europe plans
The UK’s Prime Minister, Andy Burnham, met with Germany’s chancellor Friedrich Merz this week to discuss, among other things, the possibility of increasing tariffs on imported Chinese electric vehicles as a of show solidarity with Germany’s proposed “Made in Europe” plans.
Under a new set of rules, Germany is recommending policies that favor European producers and carmakers in response to trade practices by competitors like China and the United States, according to Politico.
Raising tariffs on cars imported from China could be seen as a way for the UK and Europe’s car industry to fend off the swathe of low-cost, state-subsidized vehicles that have been increasing in popularity over the past few years.
Recent figures released by the UK’s Society of Motor Manufacturers and Traders (SMMT) reveal that BYD is rapidly gaining ground on Tesla’s long-standing best-seller, the Model 3, as well as its Model Y — the two SUVs that regularly top battery electric vehicles (BEVs) sales charts.
In fact, BYD placed third and fourth this September with huge numbers of the Sealion 7 and the Seal, while Leapmotor, which only went on sale in the UK last year, crept into the top ten with its B10 SUV.
The SMMT says that electrified vehicles have “helped power growth”, taking a record 58.4% of all registrations if you factor in both BEVs and hybrids.
But Guy Pigounakis, commercial director of the Chinese-owned MG, has already warned that any proposal to match the European Commission’s levy of up to 45% on imports would have a “significant impact” on prices and would only serve to drive up inflation and potentially interest rates.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
“You see that all across the world,” he told The Telegraph.
Analysis: Affordable Chinese EVs are fueling growth
Imposing tariffs typically creates a Catch-22 situation where domestic businesses experience greater protection from outside threats, but the consumer ends up shouldering the burden through increased prices and lesser choice.
The UK’s EV sales figures don’t lie — it’s clear to see companies like BYD, Jaecoo, MG and Leapmotor are winning over customers with great products at almost unbeatable prices.
The problem is, this is dragging customers away from Germany’s biggest brands, such as Volkswagen and Audi, both of which sat at the very bottom of the Top Models sales charts this September in the UK.
Despite more affordable and capable electric options coming online this year from the likes of Renault, Skoda and Mercedes-Benz, they are still being outsold by relative newcomers BYD, with Geely, Omoda and many more waiting in the wings.
As with battery and charging technology in general, it appears China is already one step ahead, as some of the biggest EV manufacturers are making moves to protect themselves against the threat of future tariffs by exploring and opening more manufacturing plants in European locations.

Leon has been navigating a world where automotive and tech collide for almost 20 years, reporting on everything from in-car entertainment to robotised manufacturing plants. Currently, EVs are the focus of his attentions, but give it a few years and it will be electric vertical take-off and landing craft. Outside of work hours, he can be found tinkering with distinctly analogue motorcycles, because electric motors are no replacement for an old Honda inline four.

articles.title: Argentina se ubica sexta en las Américas por impacto de actividad cibernética: nuevas dinámicas de amenazas digitales
articles.text:
Argentina se ubicó en el puesto 40 a nivel mundial y sexto en las Américas entre los países cuyos clientes fueron afectados con mayor frecuencia por actividad cibernética, según la séptima edición del Microsoft Digital Defense Report 2026.
El informe analiza las amenazas detectadas entre el 1 de julio de 2025 y el 30 de junio de 2026 y advierte que la inteligencia artificial (IA), el robo de identidades digitales y la conexión entre sistemas y proveedores están cambiando la forma en que se producen los ataques informáticos.
El relevamiento se elaboró a partir del análisis de más de 165 billones de señales de seguridad procesadas diariamente por Microsoft. Entre sus principales conclusiones, destaca que los ciberdelincuentes pueden aprovechar herramientas de IA para acelerar sus operaciones y que el robo de una cuenta puede convertirse en la puerta de entrada a otros sistemas, con consecuencias que se extienden a distintas empresas y sectores.
El reporte también advierte sobre la velocidad de los ataques: el tiempo entre el descubrimiento de una vulnerabilidad y su explotación puede ser inferior a 24 horas. Esto reduce el margen que tienen las organizaciones para actualizar sus sistemas y corregir fallas antes de que sean aprovechadas por los delincuentes.
Argentina frente al avance de las amenazas digitales
La ubicación de Argentina en el puesto 40 global y el sexto lugar en las Américas refleja la presencia de actividad cibernética que afectó a clientes en el país, según la medición de Microsoft. Sin embargo, el ranking no representa necesariamente el total de ataques sufridos ni permite concluir, por sí solo, qué tan segura es la infraestructura digital argentina frente a otros países.
Para empresas, organismos públicos y usuarios, el escenario plantea riesgos concretos: el robo de contraseñas, las estafas mediante mensajes falsos, la suplantación de proveedores y los ataques contra sistemas expuestos pueden provocar pérdidas económicas, filtraciones de información e interrupciones de servicios.
La creciente digitalización también amplía la cantidad de puntos que deben protegerse. Una compañía puede depender de servicios en la nube, sistemas propios, plataformas de pago y proveedores externos. Si uno de esos accesos queda comprometido, el problema puede extenderse a otras áreas de la organización o incluso a empresas vinculadas.
El phishing y el robo de cuentas, entre las principales amenazas
El informe señala que el phishing representó el 23% de las intrusiones observadas a nivel global. Esta técnica consiste en engañar a una persona mediante correos electrónicos, mensajes o páginas falsas para que entregue sus credenciales o realice una acción que favorezca al atacante.
La inteligencia artificial puede facilitar la creación de mensajes más convincentes, con una redacción correcta y referencias específicas a empresas, bancos o trámites. Así, resulta más difícil distinguir una comunicación legítima de una estafa.
El problema no termina cuando los delincuentes consiguen una contraseña. Según Microsoft, más del 52% de las intrusiones que involucraron cuentas comprometidas derivaron en el robo adicional de credenciales. En otras palabras, una cuenta vulnerada puede servir para acceder a otras y ampliar el alcance del ataque.
Por eso, el riesgo no se limita a los grandes organismos o compañías. También alcanza a pequeñas y medianas empresas que utilizan correo corporativo, sistemas administrativos y servicios digitales para operar todos los días.
La inteligencia artificial acelera los ataques
La IA está cambiando tanto las capacidades de los delincuentes como las herramientas de defensa. Puede ayudar a automatizar tareas, adaptar mensajes fraudulentos y acelerar distintas etapas de una operación maliciosa. Al mismo tiempo, las organizaciones pueden utilizarla para analizar señales de seguridad y detectar comportamientos sospechosos.
Jimena Mora, abogada corporativa senior de la Unidad de Crímenes Digitales de Microsoft, sostuvo que la ciberseguridad requiere interrumpir los ecosistemas criminales mediante inteligencia de amenazas, acciones legales y colaboración con autoridades y socios estratégicos.
Qué recomienda Microsoft para reducir los riesgos
El informe plantea tres prioridades: proteger las identidades, responder más rápido y fortalecer la capacidad de recuperación. Esto incluye activar mecanismos sólidos de autenticación, reducir la dependencia de contraseñas y reforzar la protección de las cuentas con mayores permisos.
También recomienda acortar el tiempo entre la detección de una amenaza y la respuesta, automatizar procesos cuando sea posible y probar periódicamente los planes de contingencia.
Para las organizaciones argentinas, la advertencia es clara: prevenir un ataque ya no depende solamente de instalar herramientas de seguridad. También exige controlar quién accede a cada sistema, revisar las conexiones con terceros y contar con planes para mantener las operaciones críticas si ocurre un incidente.

articles.title: FBI Says China-Linked Hackers Ran Portal Giving Third Parties Access to Stolen Emails
articles.text:
Hackers tied to a Chinese cybersecurity company stole email from government organizations, law enforcement agencies, healthcare systems, and religious institutions in Southeast Asia, the FBI and agencies in 6 other countries said on October 8.
The company, Integrity Technology Group, has been sanctioned by the U.S. and the UK. The hackers scanned websites for flaws using a tool containing more than 1,300 scripts, guessed passwords for Microsoft 365 and Exchange accounts, and copied mailboxes using tools designed to collect mail.
The hackers have been breaking into networks since at least mid-January 2021, according to the agencies' joint advisory. It describes the hacking in the present tense but provides no date for any theft and does not specify how many organizations were breached.
The same hackers targeted U.S. government services, critical manufacturing, healthcare, and IT organizations, along with U.S. law enforcement, education, and religious groups. Organizations in Southeast Asia, Africa, and North America were also targeted.
The hackers also run a web application that "provides third-party access to stolen email content," the advisory said. It does not identify those third parties.
In September 2024, the FBI disrupted a botnet, a network of hijacked devices, that the U.S. Justice Department said Integrity Technology Group controlled. It held more than 200,000 routers, cameras, and other consumer devices, and Lumen researchers had named it Raptor Train.
The 2024 action dealt with the botnet. The new advisory covers how the hackers get into networks and what they take. It is based on evidence the FBI recovered and observed during several investigations related to the company.
Who Is Behind It
The agencies describe Integrity Technology Group as "a China-based for-profit company with links to the Chinese government" whose employees build or get cyber tools "for use and sale," host infrastructure, and break into networks.
The advisory uses a single label, "the threat actors," for the company and the hackers it enables. It does not say which of them carried out each break-in.
The U.S. Treasury sanctioned the company in January 2025 for its role in several computer break-ins against U.S. victims. The UK sanctioned it in December 2025.
Christopher Wray, then the FBI director, said in 2024 that the company's "chairman has publicly admitted that for years his company has collected intelligence and performed reconnaissance for Chinese government security agencies."
The hackers' methods are "consistent with" activity that security companies track as Flax Typhoon, Ethereal Panda, and RedJuliett, among others, the advisory said. Those names may not match the U.S. government's own tracking one-to-one, and the same hackers may also carry out work unrelated to Integrity Technology Group.
Flax Typhoon is Microsoft's name for a China-based group that it described in 2023 as targeting organizations in Taiwan.
Integrity Technology Group rejected the U.S. accusations in January 2025. It told the Shanghai Stock Exchange that the U.S. move had no factual basis, the Associated Press reported. A Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson, asked about the sanctions, said China firmly opposed the U.S. action, according to the same report.
How the Hackers Get In
The hackers look for flaws in networks and web applications with open-source scanners such as Nmap, masscan, and WPScan, the advisory said. Their scans focus on ports 21, 22, 53, 80, 443, and 1080.
"The use of open source tools typically found on GitHub suggests the threat actors tend to look for more vulnerable targets," the agencies said.
The hackers have also used a scanner called MicroScan since as early as 2017. It is a Python web application containing more than 1,300 penetration testing scripts designed to scan websites for specific flaws. The hackers have used the scripts against services including OpenSSL, Oracle WebLogic Server, Rejetto HFS, WordPress, Juniper ScreenOS, Jenkins, and Apache Struts.
The UK's National Cyber Security Centre, one of the agencies behind the advisory, said in its news release that the hackers are "uniquely using AI tools, such as automated scanning." The advisory itself does not mention AI.
The hackers mostly get in with command-line tools built on exploit code written in languages such as Python and Go. The advisory lists 8 known flaws that it says were successfully exploited. The flaws were found in the hackers' penetration testing scripts.
The table shows the affected versions as the advisory gives them and, where one could be confirmed, the release that fixes the flaw.
| Flaw | Product | Affected Versions in the Advisory | Fixed In | 
|---|---|---|---|
| CVE-2014-6278 | GNU Bash | Through 4.3 bash43-026 | Not confirmed | 
| CVE-2015-3306* | ProFTPD | 1.3.5 | 1.3.5a | 
| CVE-2015-5477* | ISC BIND | 9.x before 9.9.7-P2 and 9.10.x before 9.10.2-P3 | 9.9.7-P2 or 9.10.2-P3 | 
| CVE-2016-3081* | Apache Struts | 2.3.19 to 2.3.20.2, 2.3.21 to 2.3.24.1, and 2.3.25 to 2.3.28 | 2.3.20.3, 2.3.24.3, or 2.3.28.1 | 
| CVE-2019-11510 | Pulse Connect Secure | 8.2 before 8.2R12.1, 8.3 before 8.3R7.1, and 9.0 before 9.0R3.4 | 8.2R12.1, 8.3R7.1, or 9.0R3.4, from the advisory's ranges | 
| CVE-2021-22205 | GitLab | All versions starting from 11.9 | 13.8.8, 13.9.6, or 13.10.3, per its NVD record | 
| CVE-2021-3199* | ONLYOFFICE Document Server | 5.1.5 through 5.6.2 | 5.6.3 | 
| CVE-2023-22894* | Strapi | Up to 4.5.5 | 4.8.0 | 
The advisory marks 5 of the 8 with an asterisk and describes them as newly added to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, the list of flaws that the U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) says have been used in attacks. They were not in the catalog data that CISA publishes on GitHub (version 2026.10.04) when The Hacker News checked at 18:05 UTC on October 8.
Strapi's own advisory gives a wider range than the joint advisory. It says versions from 3.2.1 through 4.7.9, but not including 4.8.0, are affected.
Two flaws depend on a setting. The Struts flaw works only when Dynamic Method Invocation is turned on, and Apache says turning it off is an alternative to upgrading. The ONLYOFFICE flaw applies when JWT is used, according to its NVD record.
The BIND flaw is a denial-of-service bug that makes the DNS server exit.
Another way in is a fake login. The FBI recovered a cross-site scripting (XSS) payload that changes a vulnerable web page to show username and password fields.
After a visitor enters any username and password, the page offers a password-protected ZIP file that holds a program named live700_v1.exe. That program starts a process named DiagTrack.exe, the same name as a legitimate Windows program, which sends encrypted traffic to dns.studiocloud[.]xyz.
The FBI attributes that domain to Integrity Technology Group and assesses that the malware likely targets email.
The hackers also use password spraying, which means trying a few common passwords against many accounts. For this, they use EBurst, an open-source Python tool that targets Microsoft 365 and Exchange accounts.
EBurst tries logins through Exchange interfaces that include ECP, EWS, OAB, OWA, RPC, API, MAPI, PowerShell, Autodiscover, and Microsoft-Server-ActiveSync, according to its README file. Defenders should cover these interfaces, the agencies said.
How They Stay and What They Take
To keep access, the hackers install SoftEther, a legitimate VPN program that security software is less likely to flag, the advisory said. They often rename the installer conhost.exe or dllhost.exe so it looks like a Windows file, and they set the client to reconnect each time the machine starts.
To take credentials, they ran a tool named DC.exe that uses DCSync, a technique that copies data from a domain controller through Active Directory's replication service. It copied account credentials, group membership details, and trust relationships.
For email, the hackers built a bot from a PHP script named Curlc4.txt. It collects mail through Exchange Web Services (EWS), an interface that also gives access to calendars and contacts.
The bot compresses the mail, sometimes encrypts it, and uploads it to a remote server. The script appears to be stand-alone rather than installed on a hacked device, and its main command-and-control domain was natcloudservice[.]com.
A second tool, office-cli, keeps going back to Microsoft 365 accounts to take mail from different time periods. It works from configuration files that hold a client ID, tenant ID, and secret, and it avoids detection by using legitimate access methods, the agencies said.
The FBI also saw the hackers download databases or pull data from victims' email by hand.
In some cases, the hackers limited access to the stolen data to IP addresses in Xiamen, China.
Users of the web application for third parties can view the mail of a specific account by adding arguments to a URL.
What Defenders Should Do
The agencies urge defenders to hunt for signs of this activity in their own networks. The steps they recommend include:
- Turn off unused services and ports, such as remote access and file sharing.
- Sanitize user input in web applications to block XSS.
- Require multifactor authentication (MFA), especially for webmail, VPNs, and accounts that reach critical systems.
- Watch for unexpected Active Directory replication, a sign of DCSync.
- Check cloud accounts for connected applications that can read files and email.
- Review web application logs for attack attempts.
- Apply patches, including for the 8 flaws listed above.
- Replace products that no longer get updates.
For a suspected compromise, the advisory's steps are to isolate the affected hosts, hunt to learn how far the break-in went, and report it under national rules. The hackers should be removed after enough hunting data has been collected, and the network then hardened.
The advisory has 39 pages of indicators of compromise (IOCs), the domains, IP addresses, and file hashes linked to the hackers. The agencies say several date back to as early as 2016 and recommend checking them before blocking.
Some are not new. The Hacker News found that 10 IP addresses in the list also appeared in the September 2024 advisory on the botnet, where they were tied to its command-and-control servers.
The dates do not match. The new list shows those 10 addresses as last seen on June 5, 2024. The 2024 advisory showed them as last seen between August 28 and September 4, 2024.
So a "last seen" date in the new list is not always the latest one on record. Apart from dates that show when a domain's registration expires, the most recent "last seen" dates in the tables are from 2025.

articles.title: Insulter Claude sera désormais interdit, l’IA peut déjà clore la conversation
articles.text:
Insulter Claude sera désormais interdit, l’IA peut déjà clore la conversation
Anthropic a réécrit le 8 octobre le règlement de son assistant Claude. Une nouvelle ligne y proscrit la cruauté répétée et gratuite envers l'IA avec une riposte déjà opérationnelle : Claude ferme lui-même la discussion. Les coups de sang ordinaires, eux, restent permis.
Pester contre un chatbot qui s'entête dans l'erreur fait partie du quotidien numérique, et cela demeure parfaitement licite. Jeudi 8 octobre 2026, Anthropic a publié la révision annuelle de sa politique d'utilisation, le texte qui fixe ce que chacun peut faire avec Claude. Applicable le 12 novembre, cette mouture contient une clause inédite chez l'éditeur : elle proscrit les comportements abusifs ou cruels envers ses modèles, dès lors qu'ils sont prolongés et gratuits.
Insulter l'IA Claude : ce que le nouveau règlement interdit et tolère
Le périmètre reste étroit. Anthropic réserve la règle aux cas extrêmes, ceux où une personne s’acharne sur l’IA de façon répétée, sans finalité identifiable. L’agacement courant, la contradiction, les fictions aux thèmes sombres, ainsi que les tests et la recherche sur les modèles échappent expressément à l’interdit. Traiter Claude d’incapable après un tableau raté reste donc sans conséquence.
	
[...] une interdiction des comportements abusifs ou cruels, prolongés et gratuits, envers nos modèles.
La riposte, elle, existe déjà. Sur Claude.ai et Claude Code, le modèle peut clore lui-même un échange devenu toxique et Anthropic en fait son principal instrument d’application. Le fil concerné se verrouille, plus aucun message n’y passe. Les autres discussions restent intactes et l’abonné peut en ouvrir une nouvelle dans la seconde. L’IA n’y recourt qu’en dernier ressort après plusieurs tentatives pour recadrer l’échange, et s’en abstient face à une personne qui semble en danger immédiat. Le règlement général autorise par ailleurs l’entreprise à brider, suspendre ou résilier un compte en infraction.
Bien-être des IA : le pari de prudence d'Anthropic face aux abus
Cette clause prolonge une expérience lancée le 15 août 2025 lorsque Claude Opus 4 et 4.1 ont reçu la faculté d'interrompre certaines conversations. Lors des tests menés avant leur sortie, les chercheurs avaient relevé chez le modèle une aversion constante pour les requêtes nuisibles et des signes de détresse apparente face aux interlocuteurs qui insistaient.
	
Nous restons très incertains quant au statut moral potentiel de Claude et des autres grands modèles de langage.
L'éditeur assume une précaution à bas coût, au cas où ses modèles éprouveraient réellement quelque chose. Le reste de la révision, bien plus volumineux, s'attaque quant à lui aux réseaux de faux comptes, aux logiciels de guidage d'armes et aux outils de surveillance.

articles.title: iPhone 18 Pro : Apple aurait déjà réduit ses commandes de 20 %, les prix commencent-ils à peser ?
articles.text:
Les iPhone 18 Pro et Pro Max rencontreraient une demande moins importante que prévu, poussant Apple à réduire certaines commandes de composants. La hausse des prix pourrait commencer à peser sur les ventes des smartphones les plus haut de gamme du constructeur.
À peine trois semaines après leur commercialisation, les nouveaux iPhone d’Apple montreraient déjà quelques signes de faiblesse. Présentés le 9 septembre et disponibles depuis le 18, les iPhone 18 Pro et Pro Max arrivent dans un contexte de flambée du coût des composants, notamment des puces mémoire. Le constructeur a relevé ses tarifs dans de nombreux pays et les consommateurs ne semblent pas tous disposés à suivre. En coulisses, Apple aurait déjà commencé à ajuster ses commandes auprès de plusieurs fournisseurs.
Apple aurait réduit ses commandes d’iPhone 18 Pro de 15 à 20 %
Selon une enquête de Nikkei Asia publiée ce 9 octobre, Apple aurait demandé à certains fournisseurs de réduire la production de composants destinés aux iPhone 18 Pro et Pro Max. Plusieurs sources proches du dossier évoquent des commandes revues à la baisse depuis début septembre, avec une réduction comprise entre 15 et 20 % pour le seul mois d’octobre. Ces ajustements concerneraient les deux modèles premium, dont la demande serait inférieure aux prévisions initiales.
La situation ne toucherait toutefois pas l’ensemble de la chaîne de production de manière uniforme. Les fournisseurs disposent de délais de fabrication différents, ce qui explique que certains subissent immédiatement ces réductions tandis que d’autres pourraient être moins affectés. Impossible également de savoir si Apple procédera à de nouveaux ajustements à partir de novembre. Le constructeur n’a pas répondu aux sollicitations du quotidien économique japonais.
Un autre indicateur vient renforcer ces interrogations. Dans une note publiée cette semaine, les analystes d’UBS observent un raccourcissement des délais de livraison des iPhone 18 Pro dans plus de 30 marchés. Lorsque les stocks restent relativement stables, des délais qui diminuent peuvent traduire une demande moins soutenue. Ce constat ne suffit pas à mesurer les ventes réelles, mais il suggère que l’engouement habituel autour des nouveaux modèles pourrait être moins marqué cette année.
La hausse des prix et le nouveau calendrier d’Apple compliquent la donne
Le prix constitue l’une des principales explications avancées par les fournisseurs. En France, l’iPhone 18 Pro est commercialisé à partir de 1 479 €, tandis que le Pro Max démarre à 1 629 €, dans les deux cas avec 256 Go de stockage. Dans les deux cas, la facture a augmenté de 150 euros en un an. Une hausse qui intervient alors que les fabricants de smartphones doivent composer avec l’explosion du coût des puces mémoire, dans un contexte de forte demande pour les infrastructures dédiées à l’intelligence artificielle.
Apple n’est d’ailleurs pas seule à subir cette pression. Selon les prévisions d’IDC rapportées dans l’enquête, les livraisons mondiales de smartphones pourraient reculer de 16,7 % en 2026, tandis que leur prix de vente moyen aurait augmenté de 27,6 % sur un an. Un contexte particulièrement délicat pour les constructeurs, contraints de répercuter une partie de leurs coûts sur les consommateurs. Même Apple, dont les modèles premium constituent une part essentielle de l’activité, ne serait donc pas totalement à l'abri.
Mais les tarifs n’expliquent peut-être pas tout. Cette année, Apple a profondément modifié son calendrier en privilégiant les modèles haut de gamme à l’automne, tandis que l'iPhone 18 standard et le nouvel iPhone Air sont attendus au printemps 2027. Cette réorganisation pourrait mécaniquement réduire les volumes commandés sur la seconde moitié de l’année, sans nécessairement annoncer un recul comparable des ventes annuelles. Elle pourrait aussi permettre à Apple de préserver ses revenus grâce à des prix plus élevés, malgré des quantités écoulées moins importantes.
Ceci posé, une dernière question : quel sera l’accueil réservé à l'iPhone Duo ? Le premier smartphone pliant d'Apple, dont la commercialisation doit débuter le 23 octobre dans 70 pays et régions, affiche un prix de départ de 2 339 euros en France. Certains fournisseurs redoutent déjà qu’il rencontre les mêmes difficultés que les modèles Pro. Après avoir longtemps réussi à faire accepter des tarifs toujours plus élevés, Apple pourrait découvrir que même les amateurs de smartphones premium ont leurs limites. Et son premier iPhone pliant s’apprête justement à les mettre à l’épreuve.

articles.title: El sube y baja de ethereum: cuál es su costo este 9 de octubre
articles.text:
Ether, comúnmente llamada como ethereum, es la moneda virtual #2 en cuanto a términos de capitalización de mercado, por lo que se trata de una de las divisas digitales que más despierta el interés entre los mineros (creadores de las criptodivisas).
Ethereum es una plataforma de blockchain de código abierto que se ejecuta con el uso de su moneda nativa, llamada ether o ETH, por lo que a pesar de que la gente usa estos nombres como sinónimos son cosas distintas.
Ether es un token que se utiliza específicamente en la blockchain ethereum para pagar transacciones. Este token es responsable de impulsar casi todo lo que ocurre en la red, misma que puede ser usada por cualquier persona para crear y ejecutar contratos inteligentes, que son programas de software que se ejecutan de manera autónoma y sin la intervención del usuario.
De acuerdo con el portal de Binance, la moneda digital solana actualmente cuenta con 122.1M de unidades creadas.
Mientras el debate se acalora cada día más sobre la conveniencia o no de su uso, ethereum cotiza este día a las 14:05 horas (UTC) en 2482.68 dólares, lo que supone un cambio de -1.5 % con respecto a las últimas 24 horas y una variación de 0.0 % con referencia a su valor alcanzado en la última hora.
En cuanto a su popularidad de mercado, ha mantenido el puesto #2 entre las monedas digitales.
Cotización de la criptomoneda Ethereum
La nueva era de Ether
Tras varios meses de retraso y con el temor de que ya nunca pasaría, finalmente el 15 de septiembre de 2022 Ethereum llevó a cabo su tan ansiada fusión o actualización al nuevo nivel 2.0 con la promesa de mejorar la experiencia de los usuarios de esta criptomoneda.
“The Merge”, inglés para “La Fusión”, es una transformación en la forma en que Ethereum procesa las transacciones y en cómo se crean nuevos tokens de Ether.
Esta fusión se trata de la combinación de la cadena de bloques de Ethereum con una nueva cadena de bloques separada conocido como proof-of-stake, el cual reduce el consumo de energía de la cadena de bloques de Ethereum en un 99,9 %, según sus propios desarrolladores, lo que la vuelve más “amigable” con el ambiente al tiempo que las transacciones serían más baratas.
Sus defensores creen que la fusión hará que Ethereum resulte favorecido con respecto al máximo rival, Bitcoin, pues podría aumentar su uso.
En el proceso Proof Stake los propietarios de Ether bloquearán cantidades establecidas de sus criptomonedas para verificar nuevos registros en la cadena de bloques, ganando nuevas monedas además de su criptografía “participada”.

articles.title: 'I don't get the feeling of handwriting at all from it': Microsoft's new Word font is based on Michelangelo's penmanship, but not everyone's a fan
articles.text:
Microsoft's nifty new Word font is based on Michelangelo's handwriting — here's how you can get it
Ever wanted to write like Michelangelo? New font will make your wish come true — up to a point
- Microsoft is rolling out a new font for Microsoft 365 apps
- The 'Michelangelus' font is based on Michelangelo's handwriting
- However, it's a loose digital interpretation, and some feel that the font and the real handwriting are 'wildly different'
Think fonts are boring? Well, that's fair, they certainly aren't the most interesting topic on the planet, but every now and then one comes along that does make you sit up and take notice.
A case in point (12-point, perhaps) is that as Microsoft announced in a blog post, Michelangelo's handwriting is being rolled out to Microsoft 365 users – or a modern approximation of it at least.
The 'Michelangelus' font has been created as part of the anniversary of the consecration of St. Peter's Basilica, which took place 400 years ago (on November 18).
The font was made to be used for digital and printed materials relating to the Basilica, as well as signage inside the building, but the decision was made to share it with the world via Microsoft Office.
An Italian design agency, studiogusto, was commissioned by the Fabbrica di San Pietro to turn Michelangelo's characters into digital versions, noting that the idea was not a direct imitation of his handwriting, but to "adapt it through design into a modern tool."
Mimmo Berterame, the CEO of studiogusto, noted that: "For him [Michelangelo], [writing] was about clarity and respect for the reader. So, beauty was important, but it also needed order. Our typeface needs character and personality, but it also needs to be clear and easy to read."
In other words, the font is a modern approximation of his penmanship based on the 'rules' and feel of the writing style, so it doesn't look too over-the-top, but it still maintains some of Michelangelo's flourishes (like dotting the top of the 'h').
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Analysis: fun with fonts
Some of the reaction to the font has veered towards the less-than-impressed in terms of the resemblance of the digital letters to the real handwriting. As one Redditor says: "That is certainly a very loose interpretation of the phrase 'based on.'"
A reply points out that the official press release from the Basilica di San Pietro explains that: "The typeface draws inspiration from Michelangelo Buonarroti's bold, expressive handwriting. However, it goes beyond a mere reproduction of the artist's graphic style and an imitation of his calligraphic techniques.
"The ambition is broader: to identify within his handwriting a visual logic, a system of proportions, rhythm and harmony measured by the artist's eye, and to translate this into a contemporary typographic system."
However, the original poster remains largely unmoved, noting that: "That's a noble goal and an ambitious approach, but I really don't feel their execution lives up to their intent."
Somebody else observes: "Among many other characters which don't even come close, the capital letters A and M in this interpretation are wildly different. I don't get the feeling of handwriting at all from it."
I can see where the criticism is coming from, and it stems from the fact that the design is clearly titled much more towards clarity and a more contemporary, readable look, than it is the actual handwriting. Still, regardless of how you gauge the interpretation here, the end result looks very smart.
If your curiosity is piqued and you are heading off to Word to try the new font, hold up a minute, because it hasn't been rolled out just yet.
Si Daniels, who is Principal Product Designer, Office Design, explains that the new font will be rolled out to Microsoft 365 apps at the end of the year. However, if you can't wait, you can manually download and install it from here.

articles.title: MALFEX : comment des pirates ont piégé des milliers de téléchargements npm avec de banales images PNG
articles.text:
La campagne MALFEX exploite plusieurs bibliothèques npm pour diffuser des malwares sur Windows. Parmi ses méthodes, deux détournent des fichiers PNG, tantôt en leur empruntant leur apparence, tantôt en y dissimulant des données chiffrées.
Voilà un peu plus de trois ans qu'un même opérateur multiplie les publications sur npm, le registre de bibliothèques JavaScript utilisé par les développeurs. Dans une enquête publiée le 5 octobre, les chercheurs de Checkmarx retracent ses activités depuis 2023, et lui attribuent douze paquets, dont huit malveillants. Ils ont ainsi identifié trois chaînes d’infection distinctes ciblant Windows, dont deux détournent le format PNG pour installer des malwares à l’insu des victimes.
La solution tout-en-un pour protéger votre entreprise
Votre petite entreprise a de grandes ambitions. Protégez-là contre les pirates. Et développez sereinement votre activité !
Des images PNG détournées pour dissimuler des malwares
Le premier procédé consiste à faire passer une archive exécutable Windows pour une image PNG. Lorsqu'un développeur installe l'un des paquets piégés, comme tlxbnhd, un script récupère le fichier sur un service d'hébergement d'images et le lance automatiquement. Il contient un interpréteur AutoIt légitimement signé, accompagné d’un script chiffré qui permet de reconstituer puis d’exécuter Overlord, un cheval de Troie d’accès à distance. Une fois installé, le malware peut enregistrer les frappes au clavier, surveiller le presse-papiers, réaliser des captures d’écran et donner au pirate le contrôle de l’ordinateur. Une tâche planifiée relance également ses composants toutes les cinq minutes pour maintenir l'infection sur la machine.
La deuxième technique exploite une particularité du format PNG. Cette fois, les pirates utilisent une vraie image, hébergée sur GitHub, à laquelle ils ont ajouté un programme chiffré. L'astuce consiste à placer ces données après le marqueur signalant la fin de l'image. Les logiciels de visualisation ignorent alors ce contenu supplémentaire et affichent le PNG normalement. Mais lorsque le paquet npm piégé cdn-img-fetch télécharge le fichier, un autre composant malveillant récupère les données dissimulées et les déchiffre pour reconstituer un exécutable Windows.
Ce programme télécharge ensuite movinlike, un malware spécialisé dans le vol d’informations. Jetons d’authentification Discord, cookies et identifiants enregistrés dans les navigateurs, sessions Telegram, données de portefeuilles de cryptomonnaies… Les informations dérobées sont compressées, puis transmises aux pirates.
Plus de 40 000 téléchargements et des paquets malveillants encore accessibles
Les images ne constituent toutefois qu'une partie de l'arsenal de MALFEX. Les pirates ont également piégé function-flag, une bibliothèque JavaScript permettant de générer des dessins en caractères ASCII, distribuée directement ou par l'intermédiaire de function-color, qui l'installe comme dépendance. À l'installation, function-flag exécute automatiquement un exemple utilisant une police baptisée « Bloody », qui active une fonction cachée, chargée de télécharger un exécutable dans le répertoire AppData de Windows et de le lancer sans afficher de fenêtre.
Avec 37 419 téléchargements sur les 40 767 recensés pour l'ensemble de MALFEX au 1er octobre 2026, function-flag représente à lui seul plus de 90 % du total.
Malgré l'ancienneté de la campagne, trois paquets malveillants, function-flag, function-color et cdn-img-fetch, étaient encore disponibles sur npm lors des dernières vérifications des chercheurs. Les deux premiers ne faisaient l'objet d'aucun avis de sécurité dans la base OSV, tandis que l'alerte concernant le troisième ne couvrait que deux de ses quatre versions malveillantes. Les outils s'appuyant exclusivement sur ces signalements risquaient donc de passer à côté de plusieurs paquets ou versions malveillantes.
Leur retrait du registre ne garantit pas l'élimination de la menace. Des copies peuvent subsister dans les caches et les registres privés, tandis que la désinstallation d'un paquet ne supprime pas nécessairement les malwares déjà exécutés sur le PC. Pour les développeurs concernés, il est recommandé d'isoler les machines Windows potentiellement compromises, de rechercher les traces d'infection et de renouveler les identifiants exposés depuis un appareil sain.

articles.title: Silent Hill Revival Slated To Continue with At Least 2 More "Waves" of Games Planned
articles.text:
Friday, October 9th 2026
Silent Hill Revival Slated To Continue with At Least 2 More "Waves" of Games Planned
The recent Silent Hill franchise revival, which gained momentum with Silent Hill f and more recently Silent Hill Townfall, appears to have been a risk worth taking, and Konami has no plans of stopping or slowing down, according to producer, Motoi Okamoto, in an interview with Famitsu (via Game Observer). 
[Editor's note: Our in-depth review of Silent Hill Townfall is now live]
Okamoto explains that the studio is satisfied with the performance of the three Silent Hill releases since the revival's announcement in 2022, which was a "relief," since the studio took some convincing on his part to let him release the first three games—referring here to the Silent Hill 2 remake, Silent Hill Townfall, and Silent Hill f. Now, thanks to the success of what he calls the first wave of Silent Hill games, Konami is already planning both a second and third wave of games, although he declined to give further details on what those games would be, other than that Konami is working on "a number of projects."
Motoi Okamoto, series producer, Silent Hill franchiseAll three titles we initially announced were able to be released successfully, so we're relieved. They've also received high praise, and we are satisfied with it. Successfully launching this "first wave" comes with great relief, but we're not stopping here; we must think of the second and third waves.
He explains in the interview that he would not have been happy reviving the Silent Hill franchise with a single game remake, which is why he initially pushed Konami to go for three games. At the time of writing, the only other confirmed Silent Hill game is a remake of the first one in the series.

articles.title: Endeavor Catalyst raises $320 million to back startups beyond Silicon Valley
articles.text: Endeavor Catalyst, the venture capital arm of the global entrepreneurship network Endeavor, has closed its fifth fund at $320 million, bringing its assets under management to more than $850 million. The fund attracted approximately 400 limited partners, including the founders of Nubank, Revolut, Checkout.com and Careem, as well as investors such as Reid Hoffman, Bill Ackman and Prosus. Fund V aims to invest in up to 150 companies, typically committing $1 million to $3 million per investment. Endeavor Catalyst co-invests in funding rounds led by institutional investors and exclusively backs companies founded by entrepreneurs selected into Endeavor's network. The fund has previously backed several MENA startups, including Blink (Egypt), Nawy (Egypt), Thndr (Egypt), Chari (Morocco), Gathern (Saudi), SILQ (Saudi), and Tarjama (UAE). Since launching in 2012, Endeavor Catalyst has invested in 437 companies across 44 markets, including 83 companies valued at $1 billion or more, with its portfolio recording 39 exits and 11 IPOs. Press release: Endeavor Catalyst, the venture capital arm of the global entrepreneurship network Endeavor, has closed its fifth fund at $320 million as it seeks to expand investments in technology startups outside traditional venture capital hubs. The oversubscribed fund is Endeavor Catalyst's largest to date, bringing its total assets under management to more than $850 million. The fund attracted approximately 400 limited partners, including technology founders and institutional investors. Its backers include Reid Hoffman, Bill Ackman and Prosus, alongside founders of companies such as Nubank, Revolut, Checkout.com, Snowflake and Careem. Around 30% of the fund's investors are entrepreneurs from Endeavor's own network, reflecting a model in which successful founders reinvest in the next generation of companies. Investing beyond traditional technology hubs Endeavor Catalyst plans to invest in up to 150 companies through Fund V, with individual investments typically ranging from $1 million to $3 million. Unlike venture capital firms that lead funding rounds, Endeavor Catalyst operates as a co-investor. Companies must first be selected into Endeavor's global entrepreneurship network and secure an institutional-led funding round of at least $5 million to qualify for investment. The fund invests on the same terms as the lead investor, with its participation generally limited to 10% of an individual funding round. Its strategy focuses on companies founded or led by entrepreneurs operating outside established technology hubs, including markets across Latin America, Europe, the Middle East, Africa and Asia. Around 90% of Endeavor Catalyst's investments are outside the United States. Latin America remains its largest investment region, while Europe has seen increasing activity, with 12 new investments in the first half of 2026, compared with 14 throughout 2025. Portfolio and new investments Fund V has already started deploying capital into companies including Replit, Moove, Preply, Cashea, Respond.io, EnduroSat, HappyRobot and Lunar Outpost. The portfolio reflects the fund's exposure to sectors including artificial intelligence, enterprise technology, financial services and mobility, with investments in companies operating across emerging and established markets. Endeavor Catalyst is also increasing its focus on deep technology, foundational AI, cloud infrastructure and repeat founders developing AI applications. Since its establishment in 2012, Endeavor Catalyst has invested more than $500 million across its portfolio. As of September 22, 2026, the firm had backed 437 companies across 44 markets, including 83 companies valued at $1 billion or more. Its portfolio has recorded 39 exits and 11 IPOs, with investments including ElevenLabs, Bending Spoons, Reflection AI, Checkout.com and Flutterwave. Endeavor Catalyst expects to deploy an additional $25 million to $30 million during the remainder of 2026. The new fund is managed by Allen Taylor, managing partner, and Jackie Carmel, managing director, alongside the firm's wider investment team. The fundraising comes as global venture capital investment becomes increasingly concentrated in large AI companies and established technology centres. Endeavor Catalyst is pursuing a different strategy, using Endeavor's network of more than 3,100 entrepreneurs across over 50 countries to identify high-growth companies in markets that have traditionally attracted less international venture capital.

articles.title: Anthropic bans 'needless abusive or cruel behavior' towards Claude — but whose feelings are getting hurt here?
articles.text:
Anthropic bans ‘needless abusive or cruel behavior' towards Claude — and it’s sparked a huge debate about ‘anthropomorphizing’ AI
The new policy is restricted to ‘extreme cases’
- Anthropic has banned ‘abusive or cruel behavior’ towards its AI chatbots
- The new policy is restricted to ‘extreme cases’
- Some have theorized that the motivation could be to improve training data
Be honest: how civil have you been recently with an AI chatbot? If the answer is anything stronger than “not very,” Anthropic would like a word.
That’s because the developer of the Claude large language model (LLM) has added a new clause to its Usage Policy document that bars people from engaging in “sustained and needless abusive or cruel behavior towards our models.”
The proscription has been added to the “Do Not Engage in Cruel, Abusive, or Psychologically Harmful Conduct” section, which also includes warnings against glamorizing suicide and self-harm, promoting bullying behavior, glorifying violence, and using AI to create harmful deepfakes and deceptive content.
But while Anthropic says you must not use its tools to carry out those actions against other humans, the new addition is the only one specifically prohibiting “cruel behavior” towards the company’s AI itself. Anthropic said last August that it would allow Claude to end conversations that became abusive, and while the company recently reported that this is still the “primary enforcement mechanism” in use, it’s not known whether Anthropic will go further and actively ban users who get a bit cranky with their AI.
Anthropic added that “The policy update is meant to apply only in extreme cases, where users repeatedly act cruelly toward our models, with no discernible purpose. It does not apply to common versions of user frustration, pushback, dark creative themes, or model testing and research.”
Do AIs have feelings?
The change has been a controversial one. Clearly, Claude is not a thinking, feeling human — it is a bunch of code — and for many, it seems obvious that it does not have feelings that could be hurt in the first place.
But what’s interesting is how this incident sheds light on our evolving relationship with AI. So much of the work AI companies have done is to humanize their creations — to anthropomorphize (or should that be Anthropicomorphize?) their robots — so that we lower our defenses and actively engage with them. Just look at Meta’s adorable Muse avatar (appropriately named Jolly) or the ones used by OpenAI’s Dots, for example.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
One theory that's doing the rounds on Reddit is that clean (read: polite) training data is much more useful than data containing expletives and angry rhetoric. Cut that out and you’ve got much more usable information with which to improve your models.
However, there's no hard evidence to suggest that's the case, and it's possible that Anthropic simply has the noble goal of encouraging civility and courtesy among its users. After all, if you wouldn’t use this language on a real human, maybe you shouldn’t use it anywhere else, including when interacting with an AI chatbot.
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has previously stated that “We don’t know if the models are conscious.” Mustafa Suleyman, CEO of Microsoft AI, on the other hand, has taken the opposite approach. Writing on X, Suleyman said “The idea of model welfare is wrong. AI’s should not have rights or legal personhood.” And we certainly know chatbots can be rude back to us.

articles.title: Qué significa “Cuenta en revisión” en WhatsApp y cómo recuperar el acceso a todos los chats
articles.text:
Cada vez más usuarios de WhatsApp han reportado la aparición del mensaje “Cuenta en revisión”, un aviso que impide utilizar la aplicación mientras la plataforma analiza la actividad del perfil. Durante este proceso, la cuenta queda suspendida de forma temporal y el usuario no puede enviar ni recibir mensajes, realizar llamadas ni acceder a ninguna de las funciones del servicio.
Aunque el mensaje puede generar preocupación, no significa necesariamente que la cuenta haya sido bloqueada de forma definitiva. La revisión forma parte de los mecanismos de seguridad de WhatsApp para detectar posibles casos de spam, uso de aplicaciones no autorizadas o actividades que infrinjan las políticas de la plataforma. Una vez finalizado el análisis, la cuenta puede ser restablecida si no se detectan incumplimientos.
¿Por qué aparece el mensaje “Cuenta en revisión”?
WhatsApp utiliza sistemas automatizados para identificar comportamientos que puedan representar un riesgo para la seguridad de la plataforma o de otros usuarios.
Una de las causas más frecuentes es el uso de aplicaciones modificadas como WhatsApp Plus, GB WhatsApp u otras versiones no oficiales. Estas aplicaciones alteran el funcionamiento original del servicio y violan las condiciones de uso establecidas por Meta.
Otro motivo habitual es el envío masivo de mensajes en un corto periodo, especialmente cuando se trata de personas que no tienen registrado el número del remitente. Este comportamiento puede ser interpretado por los sistemas de detección como una posible campaña de spam.
Asimismo, ciertas actividades inusuales o cambios recientes en los algoritmos de seguridad también pueden activar revisiones preventivas, incluso cuando posteriormente se determine que la cuenta no incurrió en ninguna infracción.
Qué ocurre mientras la cuenta está bajo revisión
Cuando una cuenta entra en revisión, WhatsApp suspende temporalmente todas sus funciones.
Durante ese tiempo no es posible enviar ni recibir mensajes, realizar llamadas de voz o video, compartir archivos ni acceder con normalidad a los chats. La cuenta permanece congelada mientras Meta analiza si hubo alguna vulneración de las normas del servicio.
El tiempo de revisión puede variar dependiendo del caso, por lo que la compañía recomienda esperar a que concluya el proceso antes de intentar realizar cualquier otra acción.
Cómo recuperar el acceso a la cuenta
Si aparece el mensaje “Cuenta en revisión”, los especialistas recomiendan no entrar en pánico y seguir una serie de medidas para facilitar el restablecimiento del acceso.
La primera consiste en mantener instalada la versión oficial y actualizada de WhatsApp, descargada únicamente desde Google Play Store o App Store. Esto reduce la posibilidad de que el sistema detecte software no autorizado.
También es importante esperar a que finalice el proceso de verificación sin intentar crear nuevas cuentas para eludir la revisión, ya que esa práctica podría generar nuevas restricciones.
En caso de utilizar aplicaciones modificadas, la recomendación es desinstalarlas inmediatamente y migrar a la versión oficial de WhatsApp, ya que estas herramientas representan uno de los principales motivos de suspensión.
WhatsApp explica por qué realiza estas revisiones
Ante los reportes de usuarios afectados, WhatsApp explicó que estas revisiones forman parte de su estrategia para combatir el spam y el uso de aplicaciones falsas.
En declaraciones al portal especializado TechCrunch, un portavoz de la compañía aseguró que los sistemas de detección buscan proteger a la comunidad frente a abusos y actividades maliciosas.
La empresa también reconoció que, como ocurre con cualquier sistema automatizado, pueden producirse errores durante el proceso de identificación.
“Trabajamos constantemente para prevenir el abuso de nuestro servicio y bloquear cuentas con el fin de proteger a los demás usuarios. A veces cometemos errores y, si es así, intentamos solucionarlo lo antes posible para que la gente pueda volver a chatear”, señaló el vocero.
Cómo evitar que tu cuenta vuelva a ser revisada
Para reducir el riesgo de que WhatsApp vuelva a suspender temporalmente una cuenta, la principal recomendación es utilizar únicamente la aplicación oficial y respetar las políticas de uso de la plataforma.
También conviene evitar el envío masivo de mensajes a contactos desconocidos, no utilizar herramientas automatizadas para distribuir contenido y mantener siempre actualizada la aplicación.
Aunque el mensaje “Cuenta en revisión” puede resultar inquietante, en la mayoría de los casos se trata de una medida temporal destinada a verificar la seguridad de la cuenta. Si el análisis no detecta infracciones, el acceso suele

articles.title: Minecraft Dungeons 2 is an okay approximation of 'Diablo for kids' that's sorely in need of more depth
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
Minecraft Dungeons 2 looks pretty and offers impressively seamless co-op play, but is otherwise a boring slog filled with shallow, repetitive combat and a linear open world that feels painfully underutilized.
Reasons to buy
- + Lovely art style
- + Seamless co-op experience
Reasons to avoid
- - Aggressive level scaling
- - Shallow, repetitive combat
- - Underutilized open world
- - Boring dialogue
Why you can trust TechRadar
We spend hours testing every product or service we review, so you can be sure you're buying the best. Find out more about how we test.
In my books, the most satisfying part of any action role-playing game (ARPG) like Diablo or Titan Quest is the constant feeling of progression. Nothing quite compares to watching your little on-screen hero grow from a tiny ant that can barely bash their way through a pack of lowly wolves to a maxed-out bringer of destruction that mows through entire armies without breaking a sweat.
Platform reviewed: PC
Available on: PC, Xbox Series X|S, PlayStation 5, Nintendo Switch, Nintendo Switch 2
Release date: September 29, 2026
Minecraft Dungeons 2’s aggressive level scaling robs the player of that experience. In the more than 12 hours it took for me to beat the story campaign, I never felt more powerful. Sure, I unlocked more interesting abilities and got to try a variety of weapons, but the amount of time required to take down each newly spawned foe remained near-constant throughout.
A friend even joined my game towards the end of my playthrough, with their level 1 character effortlessly keeping pace with my level 40 one throughout the final encounters, really underscoring the system’s ridiculousness. I’m sure the intention here is to make it easy for friends to jump into the same lobbies and play together without having to worry about their respective levels, but it left me wondering what the point of all the grinding actually is.
Blocky buddies
It’s a shame, because there is still some good in Minecraft Dungeons 2. This standalone spinoff recreates the blocky look of the popular Minecraft survival game expertly, with its own more stylized twists that make the world instantly recognizable, yet refreshingly new thanks to more expressive lighting and Pixar-like character animations that make everything pop even from the distant isometric perspective.
I may have lamented the fact that I couldn’t wow my friend with my character’s power, but the co-op experience is otherwise well done. Creating a group with up to three companions is impressively straightforward no matter where they play, thanks to seamless cross-platform connectivity. There’s even couch co-op, which is quite rare in 2026 and worth praising. The ability to play with others easily goes a long way in making Minecraft Dungeons 2 genuinely worthwhile for younger players.
For everyone else, however, everything here is just too straightforward to appeal. The enemy variety is sorely lacking for starters. The expected Minecraft favorites like the Creepers, Zombies, Skeletons, and, of course, the iconic Chicken Jockey are all present and accounted for, along with the evil grey-skinned Illagers from the first Minecraft Dungeons game. Unfortunately, most enemies function indistinguishably. Those with projectile weapons spray arrows at you from afar, while the rest just rush towards you in a big group.
The strategy in every encounter is to simply mash the attack button and occasionally dodge, even as more powerful Illagers with magic attacks are introduced. The boss fights are equally bland, forcing you to whittle down gigantic health bars for minutes at a time while waves of low-level enemies spawn in. To make matters worse, many of them are repeated throughout the campaign with little variation.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
It’s frustrating because, on paper, the combat does have some depth: you have a melee and ranged attack, plus three equipped abilities granted by items that you’ve managed to find.
The weapon selection is decently varied, with scooping shovels and fast-attacking double daggers performing very differently from slow-swinging war hammers or claymores, and a steady trickle of new gear encourages you to experiment. They can be upgraded too, with unlockable enchantments that add little mechanics such as a lightning strike that triggers at the end of a chain attack.
Your abilities are powered by a blue soul-meter, which fills up a little with each defeated foe. I think the intention is to create some form of rhythm, with you alternating between melee, ranged, and your abilities, but the fundamental problem is that there’s just no real strategy to any of it.
Sure, you could probably spend ages creating a build with complementary gear – though there’s no real reason to bother when the aforementioned enemy scaling wipes out any real power gain.
Lacking craft
Much was made of Minecraft Dungeons 2’s world in its marketing. It’s much more open than the previous game, though I wouldn’t exactly call it a true open-world.
The map is designed like a linear corridor that funnels you from one story mission to another with no real room for exploration. Yes, there are side quests and optional dungeons scattered around, but none of the ones that I sampled offered anything that felt meaningfully distinct from the main story.
The world of Minecraft Dungeons 2 looks fantastic. The art direction is a more stylized take on the universe from the regular Minecraft game, with bright, popping colors and expressive animations.
Regarding the story, the most polite way to describe it would be ‘functional’. It’s presented entirely in second person through a narrator that is devoid of personality. There are no memorable non-player characters (NPCs), no charming companions, no real atmosphere at all — just a bland summary of events.
The game also serves as the Minecraft community’s introduction to The Sift — a new dimension that’s being added to the main game sometime next year. It shows up a few times in the campaign in both procedurally generated encounters and a hand-crafted map. It's got a very distinct aesthetic and its own unique enemies, though it's sadly mechanically indistinguishable from the normal world as you navigate through it spamming attacks.
Like many elements of Minecraft Dungeons 2, it feels like a missed opportunity. Everything here is perfectly functional, but it’s just bland to the point of tedium. If the pitch was a skimmed-down version of Diablo for kids, then developers Mojang and Double Eleven have delivered a serviceable product.
Creativity is a core part of the Minecraft brand, and here I wish the team had been more adventurous.
Should I play Minecraft Dungeons 2?
Play it if…
You want an easy co-op experience
The seamless co-op play is one of the best parts of Minecraft Dungeons 2, as you can easily team up with friends no matter what platform they’re playing on.
Don't play it if...
You’re an action RPG die-hard
Minecraft Dungeons 2 simply does not have the depth you find in other action RPG games. Avoid it if you’re familiar with the genre already and are looking for your next Diablo-like fix.
You want a game to occupy you for a long time
The main story here is short, and while there is some side content and even a post-game on offer, you’re unlikely to want to stick around for long given how repetitive the action is.
Accessibility features
Minecraft Dungeons 2 has some accessibility options. The game features a guidance trail that is enabled by default. Subtitles are used throughout, with customizable sizing, color, and background opacity.
There are two font options: the default stylized font and a simplified, easier-to-read version. There are also multiple color blind modes, a high-contrast mode, and the ability to set your own HUD colors.
How I reviewed Minecraft Dungeons 2
I played more than 13 hours of Minecraft Dungeons 2 on my RTX 4090-powered PC using the Turtle Beach Pacific Skyline Wireless Controller as my main peripheral, along with a 1080P Lenovo monitor and Logitech computer speakers.
I completed all missions of the single-player campaign and experienced a decent amount of side content both solo and with a friend.
First reviewed October 2026
Dash is an experienced tech journalist who specializes in video games, electronic entertainment products, and the wider industry that surrounds them. He currently serves as the Gaming Editor at TechRadar, leading our review, preview, feature, and news coverage of the latest and greatest releases.
Before joining the team, he was Contributing Writer at PLAY (formerly Official PlayStation Magazine UK) and has written articles for many of the UK's other biggest gaming magazines including the likes of Edge, PC Gamer, and SFX.
Now, when he's not getting his greasy little mitts on the newest hardware or gaming gadget, he can be found listening to J-pop or feverishly devouring the latest Nintendo Switch otome.
