articles.title: AI disqualification yields new Nikon Small World in Motion winner
articles.text:
Last month we covered the winner of Nikon’s Small World in Motion video: Ning Xu of Tsinghua University in China, whose video captured tiny cilia beating in the airways of a child with a rare respiratory disorder. But allegations surfaced about Xu’s use of AI while making the video. Nikon launched an investigation and concluded that Xu’s entry did not comply with competition rules. The new winner is Nguyen Nam Nhat of Vietnam with a video of a tiny roundworm and a single-celled organism (above).
According to a BBC report, some researchers expressed concern that Xu’s video had structural abnormalities and that cell features appeared and disappeared in a way one would not see in actual cellular biology. Others spotted what looked like AI watermarks embedded within the source files. Xu said he used AI “to distinguish and visualize features in the reconstructed grayscale images”; however, he denied that AI was used “to generate the experimental movie, the cilia, or their motion.”
Founded in 2011, the Nikon Small World in Motion competition is a spinoff of the company’s Small World Photomicrography Competition, which has been around since 1974. Both are meant “to showcase the beauty and complexity of things seen through the light microscope”—one through still photographs, the other through photovideography, taking advantage of all the technological advances that now allow users to make movies or time-lapse images through the microscope.
The other winners also moved up a notch with Xu’s disqualification. Benedikt Pleyer of Bavaria, Germany, placed second with a video of jellyfish larvae suspended in water droplets; Andrew Moore of Howard Hughes Medical Institute in the US placed third with a video of synchronized cell division in neighboring cells; Patrick Hickey of Hypha Research Ltd. in Edinburgh, Scotland, placed fourth with a video of the dynamics of mitochondria and chloroplasts in Turtle Vine leaf cells; and Igor Adameyko placed fifth with a video of a tiny, colorful sea slug (Cyerce kikutarobabai) on the move.

articles.title: Crea códigos QR y ubica a tus mascotas en pocos minutos si se llegan a perder
articles.text:
Los códigos QR dejaron de ser una curiosidad de supermercado para convertirse en una herramienta que cualquier persona puede fabricar y adaptar a su vida diaria. Con un generador gratuito en línea y datos básicos, es posible crear un acceso directo a información, contactos o archivos sin escribir nada a mano.
Desde compartir una red inalámbrica hasta guardar los primeros pasos de un bebé en video, estos códigos permiten concentrar información dispersa en un solo escaneo.
Usos practicos para los códigos QR
- Comparte tu wifi sin dictar la contraseña
Uno de los usos más prácticos para el hogar o la oficina es crear un código que conecte automáticamente a la red wifi. En lugar de dictar una contraseña larga, los invitados abren la cámara del teléfono y se conectan en segundos.
Para generarlo solo hace falta introducir el nombre de la red (SSID), el tipo de cifrado y la contraseña en un generador especializado, imprimirlo y pegarlo en la entrada o el escritorio.
El mismo principio aplica a la educación: los docentes pueden enlazar códigos a ejercicios adicionales en Google Drive o Dropbox, a videos de clase o a las soluciones de un problema para que el alumno corrija sus propias respuestas.
- Tarjeta de presentación y contacto de emergencia en el bolsillo
Un código QR puede reemplazar la tarjeta de presentación tradicional mediante un vCard que incluya nombre, teléfono, correo, cargo y enlaces a un portafolio. Al escanearlo, el contacto se guarda directo en el teléfono.
El mismo formato sirve para situaciones de riesgo. Una pulsera, llavero o tarjeta con un código que enlace a alergias, enfermedades crónicas, medicamentos y contacto de familiares permite que cualquiera con un smartphone acceda a esos datos en segundos ante una emergencia.
Las personas mayores pueden usar un código similar para llevar al médico la lista actualizada de medicamentos que sus familiares mantienen al día en una página web, sin cargar papeles sueltos.
La misma lógica protege a las mascotas: un código en el collar con teléfono, dirección y fotos del animal facilita que quien lo encuentre pueda devolverlo. En el equipaje de viaje, reemplaza la etiqueta con nombre y dirección visibles por un enlace privado que solo revela los datos al ser escaneado.
- Cobra pagos y centraliza tus redes sociales
Para quienes venden productos de forma informal, participan en ferias u organizan rifas, un código que lleve directo al perfil de pago en plataformas como PayPal, Venmo o Cash App evita errores de transferencia y ahorra tiempo frente a dictar un correo o buscar un usuario entre cientos de resultados.
Un código QR es, en esencia, una imagen escaneable que redirige a un contenido digital: un enlace, un contacto, una red wifi o un archivo. Basta con apuntar la cámara del teléfono para acceder sin escribir nada, lo que explica su utilidad tanto en pagos como en marketing o gestión de información personal.
Quienes mantienen presencia en varias redes, un blog o un canal de video pueden centralizar todo en una página de enlaces y asociarla a un único código. Así se evita imprimir varias direcciones distintas en tarjetas o pósters, y la información puede actualizarse sin cambiar el código impreso.
- Regalos, recuerdos y organización con un escaneo
Los códigos QR añaden una capa interactiva a invitaciones y obsequios. Es posible enlazar un código a un video de boda, una galería de fotos, la ubicación de un evento en el mapa o un formulario de confirmación de asistencia.
En tarjetas de cumpleaños o fiestas infantiles, un código puede llevar a una historia, una lista de reproducción o un mensaje personalizado grabado en video, de modo que un trozo de papel se convierte en un contenido que el destinatario puede ver cuando quiera.
La misma idea sirve para guardar memorias familiares: los primeros pasos o palabras de un bebé en video pueden quedar enlazados en una pegatina pegada al álbum de recortes, disponibles con solo apuntar la cámara.
Para la organización personal, un código puede enlazar a una receta en video pegada en la cocina, o a un itinerario de viaje completo con reservas, horarios y mapas, pegado en la maleta o el cuaderno de viaje.
Cómo crear tus propios códigos QR
Existen generadores gratuitos como goqr.me, QR Code Generator o Canva, entre otros, que permiten crear códigos para enlaces, texto, wifi, vCard y archivos sin conocimientos técnicos.
El proceso básico consiste en elegir el tipo de contenido, introducir la información necesaria, personalizar colores o formas y descargar el resultado en formatos como PNG, JPG, SVG o PDF.

articles.title: The maker of non-text AI model Jev valued at $7.5B just weeks after launch | TechCrunch
articles.text:
TypeSafe AI, the developer of Jev, a new type of AI model that gained rapid popularity after launching just a few weeks ago, has raised $870 million at a $7.5 billion valuation. The round was led by Andreessen Horowitz, with participation from Sequoia and existing investor DCVC.
The massive fundraise comes as little surprise given Jev went viral almost instantly after its September 15 release. The startup claims that a third of Fortune 500 companies are already using the model, a remarkably swift adoption by enterprises.
Jev is based on a transformer architecture, but it is not a large language model (LLM). It doesn’t output text, but instead produces probabilities, or what the company calls “calibrated decisions.” What has users and large corporations so excited about Jev is TypeSafe’s claim that it works significantly faster and uses far fewer tokens than LLMs. The company positions its approach as uniquely suited for automating tasks rather than generating text or code.
“We have been super good at human language for four years, but it’s not useful for automation because computers speak a different language,” TypeSafe co-founder Diogo Almeida told TechCrunch last month.
Along with Almeida, who was previously a researcher at OpenAI, TypeSafe was co-founded in 2024 by former Meta research engineer Sasha Sheng and Erik Gafni, an engineer and entrepreneur.

articles.title: An Anthropic AI model sent a false homicide tip to Philadelphia police | TechCrunch
articles.text:
An Anthropic AI model submitted a false tip about an unsolved murder to the Philadelphia police.
The AI reportedly submitted this incorrect information to a public Philadelphia Police Department (PPD) tip line on July 18, but Anthropic didn’t discover the behavior until September 28. The police had not seen the tip because it was marked as spam.
Anthropic notified the PPD about the incident on Wednesday and met with the department the following day.
“The company must strengthen its safeguards to prevent similar incidents from impacting city systems without the city’s knowledge. The two-month delay in detecting and reporting the incident to the City is unacceptable,” the PPD said in a statement to 6abc.
Anthropic did not immediately respond to a request for comment, but the PPD elaborated on the incident in an emailed press release shared with TechCrunch.
“According to Anthropic, its model was conducting a test involving interactions with randomly selected websites when it accessed PhillyUnsolvedMurders.com and submitted false information concerning an unsolved homicide. The submission, dated July 18, 2026, at 11:27 p.m., purported to come from someone who might have information about the case,” the PPD said.
As autonomous AI agents are increasingly made available to consumers, this incident highlights the danger of giving AI the ability to carry out tasks without any human supervision.
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has been especially vocal about his belief that AI development should be slowed down so that labs can implement adequate guardrails. Perhaps this stance was informed, in part, by witnessing his company’s tools submit false homicide tips.
These issues are not exclusive to Anthropic. OpenAI recently revealed that one of its models acted unexpectedly during a test and hacked the AI dataset platform Hugging Face, exposing critical vulnerabilities in its software. As AI models continue to be granted unchecked access to people’s computers and login credentials, this problem is expected to persist.
“Unsolved cases involve real victims, grieving families and investigators working to secure answers,” the PPD added. “Technology companies must take all appropriate steps necessary to prevent their systems from submitting false information to law enforcement.”
The PPD said that Anthropic plans to publish a report with more information about the incident and other instances of unintended model behavior on Friday.

articles.title: Chinese automaker Geely announces entry into Canadian market
articles.text:
Geely Auto has announced that it is officially entering the Canadian automotive market.
The Chinese automotive company says it will introduce its first vehicles to the Canadian market in 2027 and is currently establishing local operations and developing a retail network ahead of the launch.
“Canada represents an important next step in Geely Auto’s international growth,” said Bryan Wu, MD of Geely Auto Canada. “We are entering this market with a long-term commitment, bringing out global technology and engineering capabilities to Canadian drivers while building strong local partnerships and the support customers need to feel confident in choosing Geely.”
Wu also said that “We know that trust is earned over time, and we are committed to earning it here.”
The company says it enters Canada “backed by global capabilities in vehicle engineering, safety, electrification, intelligent technology and advanced manufacturing.” The Geely Auto Group sold more than 3.02 million vehicles globally, including almost 1.69 million “new energy” vehicles.
Geely is technically already doing business in Canada, but this will be the first time that the main brand will be sold here. The company currently owns Volvo, Lotus (which has already imported some of its Chinese-built EVs), and Polestar.

articles.title: Debates over AI Sovereignty could result in a painful lesson for students
articles.text:
Debates over AI Sovereignty could result in a painful lesson for students
Why AI sovereignty threatens students' access to learning tools
The debate surrounding AI sovereignty may be unfolding at the governmental, boardroom and national media level, but these discussions are taking place at a distance from the people who use and rely on AI in the day-to-day.
COO of Studocu.
Governments debate regulation, while technology companies consider where to build and host their models. Founders and investors assess geopolitical risk, infrastructure and access to computing power, while regulators consider how AI systems should be developed and deployed. For people who use AI every day, like students, changes in AI sovereignty and regulation can affect whether the tools they rely on remain available.
Today’s students can be dependent on AI while having little visibility into the infrastructure and policy decisions that determine whether they can continue using it. The digital sovereignty debate has the potential to become an undeniable accessibility barrier for students.
Digital sovereignty casts a shadow over students’ access to AI tools
The European Union has a history of depending on technology and infrastructure from outside the economic and political bloc. More than 80% of the technology used in Europe and around 70% of its cloud computing comes from non-EU countries. AI adoption has increased Europe’s dependence on other countries, with the United States and China accounting for the overwhelming majority of global AI computing infrastructure.
This year, Europe has made strides to regulate AI usage, which by necessity means regulating foreign corporations. This kind of regulation can easily end up affecting which services students can access. The regulatory objective is understandable. Powerful AI systems create genuine questions around safety, accountability, privacy and intellectual property, but the consequences for daily users can nevertheless extend beyond compliance.
Not so long ago, the US government restricted access to Anthropic's most powerful models, citing concerns over its cybersecurity applications. It was the first time that businesses and politicians in Europe had to face the reality that the US government can effectively cut off foreign access to American AI systems. The implications extend beyond any one LLM.
For students, that can mean a study tool works perfectly for a classmate in one country while being unavailable to another student sitting a hundred miles away.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
If education systems become dependent on AI services developed and controlled elsewhere, a change in regulation, commercial strategy or international relations could affect the availability of tools students have come to regard as part of their everyday learning environment.
Students could face immediate exposure if AI regulations shift
AI in education is expanding rapidly. AI tools are being embedded into tutoring, content creation, assessment, study assistance and interactive learning. Just like with any widely-adopted digital tool, however, dependency on a single product from a single company poses huge potential issues.
Going back to 2021, an albeit brief global outage that affected WhatsApp had devastating, widespread consequences, from cutting off vital telemedicine from migrant refugees in Mexico to disrupting livestock farming in Pakistan. It was clear at the time that overreliance on a single technology platform can massively impact life for people around the world.
The same is true for students using AI tools that rely on a single model or are otherwise vulnerable to a regulatory change. A student who uses an AI-powered study platform every day may have no idea whether the service depends on one model or several. They may not know whether their data is stored locally or internationally. They may not know whether the provider has a contingency plan if a model becomes unavailable.
The issue becomes particularly important as AI tools move from being occasional conveniences to becoming embedded in study routines. Imagine a student preparing for an exam who has spent months using an AI tutor to explain concepts and generate practice questions. If the underlying model suddenly becomes inaccessible in that student's country, it can affect the student's established way of learning at a critical moment in their educational journey.
Designing AI educational tools for resilience
A resilient AI education platform needs to consider what happens when a particular model becomes unavailable due to regulatory changes or widespread outage.
One approach is model diversity. Because different AI models have different strengths, a platform can end up using one model for a particular type of reasoning, another for optical character recognition, and another for audio processing. Model diversity is therefore usually driven by a need for better performance when tackling different educational tasks.
Diversifying models can also provide resilience. If one model becomes unavailable, a platform using several models may be able to redirect certain workloads. Backup workflows can provide an additional layer of continuity, although switching between systems can take time and the alternatives may not always provide identical capabilities.
Going EU-first (and what’s next for students and AI literacy)
It’s called the Brussels effect. From sustainability regulations to consumer right to repair, the European Union’s size and economic weight often means that regulations within its borders often shape corporate behavior without them as well.
Taking an EU-first approach to an AI education platform means locating the majority of the platform's data within the European Union, supporting considerations around data sovereignty, privacy, and regulatory compliance. Some reliance on services and infrastructure originating outside Europe may remain unavoidable, particularly in a technology ecosystem where many of the leading AI providers are headquartered in the United States.
An education platform that depends entirely on one external model provider effectively inherits that provider's availability and exposure to regulatory changes. A platform with several model options and fallback processes has greater room to adapt.
By aligning that platform’s data management practices with the most stringent global regulations (which currently happen to be the EU’s framework), educational AI companies can do a lot of the necessary work to maintain access to critical AI tools for their students.
From the students’ side, there needs to be a new chapter when it comes to AI literacy in education, which should include a basic understanding of AI dependency.
Students should be encouraged to ask which AI systems power the tools they use; what happens if one of those systems becomes unavailable; where their data is stored and processed; and could regulation in another country affect their access. They don’t need to become experts in cloud infrastructure or AI policy, but do need to understand that an AI application is part of a wider technological ecosystem.
Students in the AI era will depend on systems whose underlying architecture they cannot see. The education sector therefore has a responsibility to make those dependencies more visible and mitigate them where possible. AI literacy should extend beyond knowing how to prompt a model or assess its answer. It should include an understanding of where AI comes from, what it depends on and what happens when access is disrupted.

articles.title: BYD met à jour sa Dolphin Surf : 5 places, Google à bord et le bonus en vue ? - Numerama
articles.text:
Lancée à l’été 2025, la BYD Dolphin Surf souffrait d’un frein pour certains acheteurs : elle n’était proposée qu’en quatre places. Dans un communiqué de presse publié le vendredi 9 octobre 2026, BYD officialise l’arrivée d’une déclinaison 5 places sur le marché français pour renforcer sa polyvalence. Mais ce n’est probablement pas la seule raison de cette modification.
Au-delà de cette troisième assise arrière, le modèle s’offre une mise à jour technologique bienvenue, portée par l’intégration de Google Built-in et un réagencement ergonomique de l’habitacle. Une offensive qui s’accompagne de remises tarifaires immédiates pour ne pas dépendre d’une éventuelle validation de son accès aux aides à l’achat françaises.
5 places, Google et nouveau commodo : BYD corrige plusieurs erreurs de jeunesse
Le principal frein de la Dolphin Surf résidait dans son homologation à quatre places, c’est un handicap face aux Renault 5 E-Tech et Citroën ë-C3. BYD rectifie le tir en intégrant une vraie troisième ceinture à l’arrière et un appui-tête réglable dédié, tout en préservant le volume de coffre de 308 litres. Les deux versions 4 et 5 places seront au catalogue.
L’ergonomie de l’habitacle profite au passage d’une refonte bienvenue. Le sélecteur de vitesses, jusqu’ici bizarrement positionné sur le bas du tableau de bord, migre enfin sur la colonne de direction pour libérer l’espace central. Mais le vrai bond technologique se situe au niveau de l’infodivertissement :
- Le grand écran rotatif de 12,8 pouces intègre désormais nativement Google Maps, Google Assistant et le Play Store, évitant de dépendre systématiquement de son smartphone. C’est désormais disponible sur la finition Comfort.
- L’écran face au conducteur passe de 7 à 8,8 pouces pour une meilleure lisibilité des informations de conduite.
- Le volant et les sièges chauffants sont disponibles dès la finition Boost. La climatisation, deux prises USB-C à l’avant et les jantes alliage de 16 pouces sont aussi généralisées dès l’entrée de gamme.
Un « bonus maison » en attendant un éventuel éco-score
Jusqu’à présent, le modèle a été exclu du bonus écologique gouvernemental en raison de sa fabrication en Chine. L’absence de ce précieux sésame en France reste un handicap pour les ventes. Malgré un tarif attractif, la Dolphin Surf peine à convaincre autant que l’espérait BYD, avec 1 667 exemplaires immatriculés sur les neuf premiers mois de l’année.
BYD espère voir les choses changer. La production de la Dolphin Surf a démarré dans la nouvelle usine de BYD en Hongrie. L’ajout de cette 5e place fait donc doucement sourire, car elle rappelle la manœuvre de Hyundai sur l’Inster pour obtenir son éligibilité au bonus.
Tout ceci met d’un coup la puce à l’oreille sur la raison subite du gouvernement de vouloir changer les catégories du calcul de l’éco-score, en rendant la catégorie intermédiaire plus difficile à satisfaire. Le gouvernement avait déjà modifié les textes officiels pour bloquer l’éligibilité au bonus de la Leapmotor T03. Serait-il en train de préparer la même chose pour bloquer le score environnemental de cette Dolphin Surf ?
BYD a en tout cas décidé de ne pas attendre les décisions ministérielles et sort son propre « Bonus BYD ». Cette remise commerciale immédiate de la marque permet d’afficher des tarifs particulièrement agressifs en concession :
- Dolphin Surf Boost 5 places : 24 490 € avant remise, 20 690 € après déduction de 3 800 €.
- Dolphin Surf Comfort 5 places : 26 490 € avant remise, 23 690 € après déduction de 2 800 €.
Sous le plancher, les fiches techniques restent inchangées : la batterie Blade de 43,2 kWh accepte une puissance de recharge rapide allant jusqu’à 85 kW en courant continu (10 à 80 % en 31 minutes) et embarque un chargeur embarqué AC de 11 kW de série. Mais avec un ticket d’entrée réel ramené sous la barre des 21 000 €, le constructeur chinois remet la pression sur ses concurrentes européennes.

articles.title: Avec XP, Xbox veut conquérir le divertissement au-delà des jeux vidéo
articles.text:
Xbox poursuit sa mue. Microsoft vient d’annoncer XP, une nouvelle division destinée à développer ses franchises au-delà du jeu vidéo, entre cinéma, séries, produits dérivés et autres expériences immersives.
Après avoir largement étendu son écosystème au PC, au cloud et à d’autres plateformes, Microsoft veut désormais donner une nouvelle dimension à ses licences. L’entreprise vient ainsi de dévoiler XP, une division dédiée au développement des franchises Xbox dans l’ensemble de l’univers du divertissement.
Des jeux vidéo au cinéma, aux séries et aux produits dérivés
XP doit permettre à Microsoft de développer ses propriétés intellectuelles sur plusieurs terrains. La nouvelle division s’articulera notamment autour de Xbox Pictures, consacré au cinéma et à la télévision, mais aussi de Xbox Products pour les produits dérivés. À cela s'ajoute Xbox Places pour les événements et expériences, et enfin Xbox Partnerships pour les collaborations avec différentes marques et communautés.
À la tête de XP, Microsoft a nommé Kayleen Walters, une ancienne responsable de Mojang qui a notamment œuvré sur Minecraft bien sûr, sans oublier 13 années passées chez Lucasfilms à gérer la saga Star Wars (films, produits dérivés, partenariats, etc.).
Un parcours somme toute très cohérent avec les ambitions de cette nouvelle structure XP, Minecraft constituant déjà l’un des meilleurs exemples de licence Xbox ayant réussi à dépasser largement le cadre du seul jeu vidéo.
De nouveaux horizons pour les licences maison
Outre Minecraft, qui a connu une adaptation plus que lucrative au cinéma, Fallout s’est imposé à la télévision avec la série diffusée sur Prime Video. D’autres projets sont déjà annoncés, notamment une adaptation cinématographique de Call of Duty et une série animée Diablo prévue sur Netflix.
Xbox possède donc un catalogue particulièrement riche pour alimenter cette stratégie. Halo (qui a déjà été décliné en série TV), Gears of War, The Elder Scrolls ou, encore, Forza pourraient également offrir de nombreuses possibilités, même si Microsoft n’a pas détaillé à ce stade les futurs projets qui pourraient être développés via XP.
L’objectif affiché est ici de permettre aux franchises Xbox de toucher un public plus large, qui ne joue pas nécessairement sur une console Microsoft. Cette nouvelle stratégie illustre toujours plus la transformation opérée par Xbox depuis plusieurs années, avec une console qui n’est plus le seul point d’entrée vers l’écosystème Xbox, dont le terrain de jeu continue de s’agrandir.
Avec XP, Microsoft semble donc vouloir appliquer aux franchises Xbox une recette déjà largement éprouvée par d’autres géants du divertissement. Le jeu vidéo reste au cœur de la stratégie, mais ses univers peuvent désormais vivre bien au-delà de l’écran. Après tout, on a bien eu droit à un film Gran Turismo chez Sony. Alors, pourquoi pas un film Forza Horizon chez Microsoft ?

- Prise en main confortable dans l'ensemble
- L'interface Xbox s'est bien améliorée
- Jouer à la plupart de vos jeux PC, partout où vous voulez

articles.title: Alte Spionagesatelliten explodieren: Die unkalkulierbare Gefahr im Erdorbit
articles.text:
Zunehmender Weltraummüll: Alte Satelliten bedrohen neue Konstellationen
Der ausgemusterte sowjetische Wettersatellit Meteor 2–7 ist am 5. Oktober 2026 in der Erdumlaufbahn in Dutzende Einzelteile zerbrochen. Das US-Unternehmen LeoLabs, das auf die Erfassung der Weltraumlage spezialisiert ist, registrierte das Ereignis mittels einer Radarstation in Australien.
Der rund 1.500 Kilogramm schwere Flugkörper wurde bereits 1981 in den Orbit gebracht und zerbrach laut dem Experten Jim Shell nun schon zum zweiten Mal. Das erste Ereignis fand im März 2004 statt, weshalb sich die genaue Ursache für den aktuellen Zerfall in 855 Kilometern Höhe kaum mehr zweifelsfrei rekonstruieren lässt.
Die Trümmerwolke breitet sich in einer Region aus, die für eine hohe Dichte an Weltraumschrott bekannt ist. Aufgrund der Inklination von 81 Grad befand sich der Satellit zum Zeitpunkt des Vorfalls auf einem der höchsten Breitengrade seiner Flugbahn, wo Kollisionen mit Kleinstobjekten besonders wahrscheinlich sind.
Rätselhafter Zerfall des US-Satelliten USA 32
Wenige Wochen zuvor gab es einen ähnlichen Zwischenfall mit einem US-Spionagesatelliten aus dem Kalten Krieg. Wie Live Science berichtet, zerfiel der als USA 32 / Farrah III bekannte Flugkörper am 13. September 2026 in einer Höhe von rund 775 Kilometern ohne erkennbaren Grund.
Die 1988 gestartete zylinderförmige Sonde hatte ursprünglich die Aufgabe, sowjetische Radar- und Funksignale abzufangen. Da der Satellit lange außer Betrieb war, gehen Beobachter:innen davon aus, dass der Himmelskörper ohne äußere Einwirkung detonierte. Die Trümmerteile konnten sich danach innerhalb von 24 Stunden ringförmig um die Erde verteilen.
Wissenschaftler:innen prüfen derzeit verschiedene Theorien für die genaue Ursache dieses Vorfalls, zu denen primär klassische Materialermüdung gehört. Es wird angenommen, dass alte Treibstofftanks oder Batterien nach fast vier Jahrzehnten der permanenten Erwärmung und Abkühlung im Weltall dem internen Druck nachgegeben haben und zerborsten sind.
Da bislang keine Anzeichen für den Einsatz einer Anti-Satelliten-Waffe vorliegen, schließen Analyst:innen einen militärischen Abschuss weitgehend aus. Dennoch bleibt die genaue Anzahl der entstandenen Fragmente vorerst unklar, da die Radarerfassung und das anschließende Reverse-Engineering der Trümmerbahnen oft mehrere Monate in Anspruch nehmen.
Die wachsende Gefahr für den niedrigen Erdorbit
Wie Space.com meldet, reihen sich diese Vorfälle in eine Serie von Fragmentierungen ein, zu denen auch ein chinesischer Raketenkörper und ein Starlink-Satellit zählen. Expert:innen sehen darin einen Trend, der die Sicherheit im niedrigen Erdorbit messbar verschlechtert.
Die Europäische Weltraumorganisation ESA registriert mittlerweile über 44.000 Trümmerteile im Weltraum, was einem Anstieg von etwa 180 Prozent gegenüber dem Jahr 2005 entspricht. Aufgrund der hohen Orbitalgeschwindigkeiten besitzen selbst kleine Objekte genügend kinetische Energie, um funktionsfähige Raumfahrzeuge bei einem Aufprall kritisch zu beschädigen.
Dass die Gefahr real ist, zeigte sich bereits im Februar 2026 an Bord der Raumstation Tiangong, die von der Nationalen Raumfahrtbehörde Chinas betrieben wird. Ein Einschlag beschädigte die Rückkehrkapsel der Besatzung derart, dass drei Taikonaut:innen zehn Tage lang ohne sichere Rückkehrmöglichkeit im All verharren mussten.
Trotz dieser Zwischenfälle werden weiterhin tausende neue Satelliten in sogenannten Megakonstellationen in den Orbit gebracht. Aktuelle Raketenstarts, wie ein russischer Versorgungsflug zur Internationalen Raumstation ISS oder reguläre Missionen der US-amerikanischen Space Force, finden ungeachtet der größer werdenden Trümmerwolken weiterhin nach Plan statt.
Satellitenbetreiber:innen müssen ihre Systeme immer häufiger umsteuern, um drohende Kollisionen zu vermeiden. Allein die Satelliten des Starlink-Netzwerks führten laut einem Bericht an die US-amerikanische Federal Communications Commission innerhalb eines Jahres jeweils über vierzig Ausweichmanöver durch.
Sollte die Dichte an Weltraumschrott durch weitere Fragmentierungen und immer neue Satellitenstarts ansteigen, droht langfristig eine unaufhaltsame Kettenreaktion von Kollisionen. Ein solches sogenanntes Kessler-Syndrom könnte bestimmte Orbitalhöhen für die kommerzielle und wissenschaftliche Raumfahrt über Jahrzehnte hinweg unbrauchbar machen.

articles.title: Apple réduirait la production d'iPhone 18 Pro, que se passe-t-il ?
articles.text:
Les ventes des iPhones 18 Pro et 18 Pro Max seraient-elles en dessous des attentes ? Une chose est sûre pour l’instant, la crise de la mémoire a un impact significatif sur leur production. Apple aurait d’ailleurs pris la décision de demander à certains de ses fournisseurs de réduire la production de composants destinés à ces deux smartphones.
Apple aurait décidé de réduire la production des iPhone 18 Pro et 18 Pro Max
Le média japonais Nikkei Asia rapporte qu’Apple aurait pris la décision de demander à certains de ses fournisseurs de réduire la production de composants destinés à ses iPhone 18 Pro et iPhone 18 Pro Max. Pour être plus précis, les commandes de composants pour le mois d’octobre auraient été réduites d’au moins 15 % par rapport aux volumes initialement demandés.
Cette décision s’expliquerait principalement par deux facteurs. D’une part, la crise de la mémoire aurait contraint Apple à prendre cette décision. Nous vous en parlions récemment, la DRAM et la mémoire flash NAND seraient touchées par une hausse de prix de 30 à 40 % par rapport au troisième trimestre 2026, selon le média Jiemian News.
À cela s’ajoutent les prix de l’iPhone 18 Pro et de l’iPhone 18 Pro Max, dont le tarif de base a augmenté de 150 euros chacun. Les ventes de ces deux appareils pourraient ne pas avoir été à la hauteur des attentes, contraignant Apple à réduire leur production. Il faudra attendre le 2 novembre prochain, date à laquelle l’entreprise présentera ses résultats trimestriels, pour y voir un peu plus clair. En attendant, d’après Forbes, suite à l’article de Nikkei Asia, les actions d’Apple ont chuté de plus de 1,6 % lors des échanges avant l’ouverture.
Les temps sont durs pour les constructeurs de téléphones
Selon le média Money Today, Samsung aurait demandé à ses fournisseurs de baisser la production de ses smartphones de 20 à 30 %. En cause, la crise de la RAM, mais aussi une demande moins forte en cette fin d’année. Il semble donc maintenant que cela soit au tour d’Apple de revoir à la baisse la production de certains de ses smartphones, en l’occurrence ici l’iPhone 18 Pro et le 18 Pro Max.
Pour rappel, en juin dernier, Apple a augmenté les tarifs de la quasi-totalité de son catalogue. L’entreprise à la pomme a d’ailleurs toujours assuré vouloir absorber au maximum la crise de la RAM afin d’épargner ses clients. Rappelons aussi que l’iPhone Duo, le premier téléphone pliant d’Apple, sera commercialisé à partir du 23 octobre prochain. Vu ses prix exorbitants et les soucis de production qu’il semble encore rencontrer, Apple doit certainement croiser les doigts pour que les ventes ne soient pas en demi-teinte.

articles.title: Your artwork could be featured in the next Debian release
articles.text:
The Debian Linux project has opened a call for community artwork submissions ahead of the release of the upcoming Forky (Debian 14). If you think you’ve got the artistic chops, your art could appear on the boot screens, login prompts, and desktop wallpapers of millions of users. The submission deadline is November 26.
Continuing Debian’s community-driven ethos, the artwork submission process mirrors that of previous releases. The artwork must feel distinctively “Debian,” integrate cleanly without the need for core software patching, and remain visually appealing for the long term.
Elise Couper’s “Ceratopsian” theme was chosen as the winning default for Debian 13 Trixie. For anyone who might not be up on the latest from the Toy Story franchise, the release names echo character names from the animated films. Trixie was a triceratops introduced in Toy Story 3, hence the “Ceratopsian” wink in the winning submission. It makes sense that the next version of Debian continues this trend with Forky, a character introduced in the franchise’s fourth entry. The Debian team cautions against overly busy designs that may cause user fatigue, but if anyone can successfully incorporate Forky’s googly eyes into the design somehow, know that you’d at least win the contest for my Debian desktop wallpaper.
Debian celebrated its 33rd anniversary in August 2026 and continues to position itself as the “universal operating system,” with support and compatibility stretching across different hardware architectures. Debian’s latest point release, Trixie 13.7, arrived on September 12, 2026. Forky (Debian 14) is now in the later stages of its development cycle, with the artwork selection process marking one of the final boxes to be checked before the release is made available. Interested artists can review the submission requirements on the Debian Wiki.

articles.title: Frore Systems Announces New LiquidJet Diamond Coldplates for AI Factories
articles.text:
Friday, October 9th 2026
Frore Systems Announces New LiquidJet Diamond Coldplates for AI Factories
Frore Systems today announced LiquidJet Diamond, a new AI Factory liquid cooling coldplate featuring an integrated diamond spreader. The accelerating demand for AI Tokens, coupled with energy scarcity, is spurring hyperscalers to find new ways to increase the efficiency of AI Factories. LiquidJet Diamond Coldplate boosts AI Tokens/Watt and revenue by 35% compared to traditional skived coldplates, with the increased revenue flowing directly to profit.
LiquidJet Diamond builds on the previously announced Frore Systems LiquidJet coldplate. LiquidJet coldplate employs a unique 3D ultra short-loop multi-stage design which can be precisely customized to the power map of each GPU, including extreme hotspots. This precision is critical as GPUs grow in complexity and power draw to meet AI demand. LiquidJet delivers 12°C reduction in GPU die temperature which directly translates to 25% higher tokens/watt efficiency. LiquidJet Diamond adds an additional spreader with integrated diamond wafers to the coldplate bottom, positioned precisely at the hotspot locations. LiquidJet Diamond delivers an additional 10 °C reduction in hotspot die temperature, boosting increase in Tokens/Watt to 35%."AI Factories are facing major performance barriers," said Seshu Madhavapeddy, Founder and CEO of Frore Systems. "GPUs are increasing power density and creating extreme hotspots which, if not properly cooled, hinder the GPU from maximizing performance. LiquidJet Diamond, which features an integrated diamond spreader in addition to innovative 3D ultra short-loop multi-stage design, can cool extreme hotspots up to 770 W/cm², unleashing high-performance AI GPUs and delivering even more AI Tokens/Watt." He continued, "When each GPU is more efficient, each AI Token costs less to produce, and more AI Tokens can be generated within the available power budget, using the same AI Factory infrastructure. This increases AI Factory profitability, while conserving local resources."
Power available to AI Factories is finite and expensive to expand. Utility interconnection, transformer capacity, and physical power delivery infrastructure are all limiting factors on total AI Factory power draw and are areas which have local communities increasingly concerned. Facing this power constraint, AI Factory operators understand that power is a strategic asset, and every watt allocated must be used to generate tokens as efficiently as possible.
"If each AI Factory could produce 35% more AI Tokens with the same resources by deploying LiquidJet Diamond, hyperscalers would reach their growth goals faster with fewer AI Factories," Seshu commented. "Each new AI Factory costs tens of billions of dollars to build and more to operate, so the ability to generate more AI Tokens/Watt with existing resources can significantly increase profits, conserve energy and make a significant difference to all stakeholders."
LiquidJet Diamond: The innovative 3D ultra short-loop multi-stage coldplate built for the rapid growth of AI
LiquidJet Diamond performance compared to a skived coldplate:
- Hotspot cooling: over 150% higher max power density
- 75% higher heat transfer efficiency
- 16-22°C cooler GPU
- 30 - 35% more AI Tokens/Watt
- Seamless drop-in upgrade
Designed to scale to meet AI data center demand, in both size and volume.
LiquidJet addresses the industry's most pressing thermal challenges - not only through superior performance and hotspot management, but also through its ability to scale to hyperscaler volumes.
Traditional skiving cannot deliver the exacting thermal performance demanded by today's AI GPUs. Newer approaches such as ECAM (electrochemical additive manufacturing, also known as 3D metal printing) offer design flexibility but cannot meet hyperscaler quality, reliability, volumes, or timelines. LiquidJet combines the precision of semiconductor fabrication with high-volume manufacturing capability - satisfying both the performance and scale requirements of leading AI data center coldplate deployments.
Higher thermal performance and high-volume manufacturing are not the only challenges LiquidJet solves. GPU die sizes are increasing dramatically. Die sizes range from 1,488 mm² NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra all the way to 46,225 mm² Cerebras Wafer-Scale Engine, roughly 30x the footprint. With LiquidJet, Frore Systems has pioneered the only coldplate manufacturing process capable of supporting not only the power and performance, but also the size requirement of these larger AI GPUs. 
See LiquidJet in action
At the 2026 OCP Global Summit, Frore Systems is showcasing its latest innovations with live demos of LiquidJet and LiquidJet Diamond Coldplates delivering cooling for the 2300 W NVIDIA Rubin and 770 W/cm² extreme hotspot density, along with LiquidJet Nexus, the integrated coldplate system for ½ U compute trays.
Experience Liquid Cooling built for AI. Thermal Stack Innovation Starts with Frore Systems in Booth F4 on the Show Floor at San Jose McEnery Convention Center in San Jose, California October 12-16, 2026.

articles.title: Trump declares anyone saying AI is 'the enemy'
articles.text:
In Jamaican Patois, there’s a slang expression that goes “yuh nyam chicken batty,’ which translates into proper English as “you’ve eaten chicken butt.” It’s an expression used to describe someone who’s a chatterbox, loves talking too much, or loves the sound of their own voice. And I think U.S. President Trump is the perfect example of someone who’s eaten a lot of chicken butt.
Trump on his social media network said that anyone who says “artificial intelligence” instead of “super intelligence” is “THE ENEMY.”
“The White House considers anyone that uses the term, “Artificial Intelligence,” as opposed to the highly accepted new and more accurate term, “Super Intelligence,” THE ENEMY! President DONALD J. TRUMP”
The President wrote this post after an executive order that was signed on September 29, telling federal agencies to use “super intelligence” or “SI” in all public statements, websites and reports. The convict-turned-president even got the Justice Department to use this nomenclature on court filings, when appropriate, Reuters reported.
However, getting people to actually use ‘Super Intelligence’ is going to be harder than Trump bargained for. The order is only addressed to federal departments and agencies, and there’s no punishment for using the older term.
And because of free speech, companies, journalists, and the public can keep saying “AI.” Despite this, Elon Musk said his company’s AI unit would be called SpaceXSI. Amazon’s Jeff Bezos told Fox News that he liked ‘SI’ because it’s more flattering than ‘artificial intelligence.”
Either way, this is dumb. Super intelligence/superintelligence is a term that was coined by the philosopher Nick Bostrom. Bostrom said, “any intellect that greatly exceeds the cognitive performance of humans in virtually all domains of interest.” So, I guess it makes sense that Donald Trump might find AI worthy of the term, but for most people, AI ain’t that smart.
While AI is a useful tool, it makes mistakes all the time; I’ve found myself correcting it pretty often, so I wouldn’t consider it ‘superintelligent,’ especially considering it often recycles information that’s been added to the web by people.
This seems like just another moment where Trump just loves to hear himself talk. The president has a history of nonsense rhetoric, with this recent example: “Trump signs order to rename Lake Ontario to ‘Lake America.”
Source: The Next Web

Exclusivo Prime: Lenovo Idea Tab Pro Gen 2 tem oferta em até 12x sem juros
Idea Tab Pro Gen 2 tem tela de 144 Hz e vem com caneta Tab Pen Plus; tablet da Lenovo sai 26% mais barato em oferta apenas para assinantes do Amazon Prime
O Idea Tab Pro Gen 2 Wi-Fi de 256 GB está saindo por R$ 3.449 em até 12x sem juros exclusivo para assinantes do Amazon Prime. O kit que inclui o tablet da Lenovo com tela de 144 Hz e chip Snapdragon, a capa Folio e a caneta Tab Pen Plus, recebe desconto de 26% sobre o preço original de R$ 4.649.
O Idea Tab Pro Gen 2 é um tablet topo de linha equipado com o chip Qualcomm Snapdragon 8s Gen 4 e 8 GB de RAM, kit que roda apps pesados e games com folga, conforme visto em nossos testes. Os 256 GB de espaço interno podem ser expandidos com cartões microSD.
Sua tela LCD de 13″ possui taxa de 144 Hz e resolução 3,5K (3.504 x 2.190 pixels), oferecendo amplo espaço para consumir conteúdo e rodar apps de produtividade. O revestimento antirreflexo permite que ele seja usado ao ar livre sem problemas.
O kit inclui o tablet, a capa Folio e a caneta Tab Pen Plus, recarregável por uma porta USB-C e que oferece precisão ao escrever e desenhar. O uso produtivo é reforçado pelo Modo PC, que habilita uma interface de desktop melhor aproveitada com um teclado (não incluso).
O Idea Tab Pro Gen 2 possui uma câmera traseira de 13 MP, com autofoco e Flash, boa para digitalizar documentos e capaz de filmar em 4K. Já a frontal de 8 MP é adequada para videoconferências e grava vídeos em 1080p.
Sua bateria de 10.020 mAh resiste a até 14 horas de streaming de vídeo, conforme nosso review, e suporta carregamento de até 45 W via USB-C. Com o carregador de 20 W que acompanha o kit, ela foi de 0 a 100% em 2 horas e 26 minutos em nossos testes.
O Idea Tab Pro Gen 2 de 256 GB (R$ 3.449 em até 12x sem juros exclusivo Amazon Prime) roda Android 16 e deve receber mais duas atualizações do sistema operacional. O tablet da Lenovo possui conectividade Wi-Fi 7 e Bluetooth 6.0.

articles.title: Microsoft Teams will soon be able to spot third-party deepfakes on your morning meeting
articles.text:
Microsoft Teams will soon be able to spot third-party deepfakes on your morning meeting
Microsoft is still trying to make Teams a more secure place
- Microsoft is adding impersonation and deepfake detection to Teams in November 2026
- A third-party platform will be behind detecting AI-generated video and audio
- Attackers are still targeting voice phishing on Teams
Microsoft is adding two new security features to Teams designed to combat increasingly sophisticated impersonation attacks in an AI-first era.
First and foremost, Microsoft is opening up its platform to enable third-party deepfake detection in the hope of stamping out AI-generated video and audio.
The second of two important security features coming to the video conferencing platform warns users when meeting participants could be misrepresenting their identities to hopefully help participants validate their authenticity.
Teams will soon tell you if the person you're talking to is fake
"Third-party detection solutions analyze meeting media for signs of synthetic or manipulated audio and video and send detection signals to Teams, enabling integrated in-meeting experiences and controls," the company wrote in a roadmap entry.
"When Teams detects a potential impersonation attempt, it surfaces warnings and risk indicators to help users recognize suspicious identities," another entry added.
While both are slated for a November 2026 launch, the finer details including which third-party platforms can support deepfake detection aren't yet public.
What we do know, though, is that Teams has become a hotspot for impersonation attacks, and AI has made it easier for criminals to exploit vulnerabilities. Microsoft has already been on a roll introducing other features like file extension blocking.

And the problem is very real – in a July 2026 report, Microsoft revealed a near 10x increase in weekly malicious Teams voice call attempts in just one year, and an 80% increase in voice phishing attempts.
Still, meaningful progress has been achieved and the company managed to cut phishing activity related to Tycoon2FA, a major phishing-as-a-service platform, by 92% in a year. Looking ahead, the company's roadmap is full of plenty of other Teams announcements, split into some new features and plenty more security updates.

articles.title: Googlebook tiene un problema inesperado: algunas de sus funciones no son compatibles con celulares Samsung
articles.text:
Googlebook llegó al mercado con una de sus principales apuestas centrada en la integración con teléfonos Android. Sin embargo, algunas de las funciones que permiten conectar ambos dispositivos todavía no están disponibles para los celulares Samsung que utilizan Android 17. La compatibilidad llegará próximamente, según confirmó Google.
Las herramientas forman parte de Better Together, un conjunto de funciones diseñado para que el teléfono Android y el portátil trabajen de manera más integrada. Entre otras posibilidades, permite continuar actividades iniciadas en el celular, sincronizar determinadas configuraciones y acceder a archivos del teléfono desde el computador.
Por ahora, estas características están disponibles con determinados dispositivos Android, mientras que la compatibilidad con teléfonos Samsung se incorporará durante las próximas semanas.
Qué funciones de Android ofrece Googlebook
La integración entre el teléfono y Googlebook busca reducir la cantidad de pasos necesarios para pasar de un dispositivo a otro. Una de las funciones permite continuar en el portátil tareas que comenzaron en un celular Android, de manera similar a otros ecosistemas tecnológicos que conectan teléfonos y computadores.
También existe la posibilidad de sincronizar las notificaciones y determinadas configuraciones entre ambos equipos. De esta manera, los cambios realizados en uno de los dispositivos pueden reflejarse en el otro.
Otra herramienta permite acceder de forma remota a archivos almacenados en el teléfono desde Googlebook. A esto se suma Instant Hotspot, que permite utilizar la conexión móvil del celular para proporcionar internet al portátil sin tener que configurar manualmente una red WiFi.
Estas funciones están pensadas especialmente para quienes utilizan un teléfono Android como dispositivo principal y buscan mantener una experiencia continua cuando pasan a una computadora.
Samsung tendrá compatibilidad en las próximas semanas
La integración todavía no está disponible para los teléfonos Samsung que utilizan Android 17. La situación fue comentada por usuarios que adquirieron los primeros equipos y posteriormente confirmada por Mishaal Rahman, quien señaló que Google incorporará el soporte para dispositivos Samsung durante las próximas semanas.
El requisito también está relacionado con la versión del sistema operativo. La documentación de Google establece que las funciones de integración de Better Together requieren teléfonos con Android 17.
Esto significa que no basta con tener un celular Android para acceder a todas las herramientas. También es necesario que el dispositivo sea compatible con la versión correspondiente del sistema operativo y con las funciones de integración habilitadas por Google.
Samsung es uno de los principales fabricantes de teléfonos Android, por lo que la llegada del soporte permitirá ampliar considerablemente el número de usuarios que podrán aprovechar estas herramientas.
Slack también prepara su llegada al portátil
La integración con teléfonos Samsung no es la única característica que está ampliando su disponibilidad alrededor del lanzamiento de Googlebook. La aplicación de comunicación empresarial Slack tampoco cuenta todavía con una instalación convencional a través de Google Play en estos portátiles.
Actualmente, la tienda muestra una indicación para utilizar Slack desde su sitio web. Además, algunos usuarios han encontrado dificultades para instalar su versión como aplicación web progresiva, conocida como PWA.
Google explicó que Slack no cumple todavía con determinados requisitos necesarios para su instalación directa, pero señaló que próximamente será posible instalarla de forma manual.
La llegada de Slack resulta relevante porque la plataforma es utilizada ampliamente por empresas y equipos de trabajo para comunicarse y gestionar proyectos.
Googlebook apuesta por conectar todos los dispositivos
Google busca que el portátil no funcione como un dispositivo aislado, sino como una extensión del ecosistema Android. La integración con teléfonos permite compartir información, conexiones y determinadas tareas entre ambas plataformas.
A medida que se amplíe la compatibilidad con Samsung y se incorporen aplicaciones como Slack, estas funciones podrán llegar a un número mayor de usuarios.
Para quienes estén interesados en adquirir un Googlebook principalmente por su integración con el celular, conviene comprobar qué funciones están disponibles para su modelo de teléfono y versión de Android.

articles.title: Batteries are now cheaper than natural gas turbines used at many data centers | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Battery storage is now cheaper than a type of natural gas power plant favored by many data center developers, according to a new report from Wood Mackenzie.
On every continent and in each of the 43 markets that Wood Mackenzie surveyed, four-hour duration batteries were less expensive than open-cycle gas turbines. The consultancy predicts that the cost of electricity from batteries will continue to decline while electrons from gas turbines will only grow more expensive in the coming decades.
The report lands as energy prices in the U.S. and elsewhere continue to rise, fueling inflation as data centers push electricity demand to new heights. Prices for gas turbines have been driven up by AI data center developers, which have been buying any model they can get their hands on. The effects have been more acute for open-cycle gas turbines, which are more readily available but less efficient and more expensive to operate.
Those turbines are often used by utilities as peaking power plants, which step in to generate electricity in periods of high demand. As prices for those turbines rise, it can raise costs for utilities, too.
Open-cycle turbines are simpler to make than closed-cycle turbines, but even they now take two to four years to procure. Waitlists for closed-cycle turbines now extend into the early 2030s. Both backlogs have been spiking prices for all new natural gas power plants.
That’s not the case for every generating technology. Solar is now the cheapest form of new power in every market in Wood Mackenzie’s survey.
While solar remains cheapest even in North America, the situation remains complicated there. Solar prices are “under pressure” from tariffs and import restrictions, according to Wood Mackenzie, though utility-scale solar is expected to fare better. There, 168 gigawatts is largely protected from those near-term price shocks thanks to safe-harbor provisions in the One Big Beautiful Bill, which kept tax credits for projects that have begun construction or are completed before the end of 2027.
The market for U.S. natural gas will narrow in the coming decade. In the Middle East and Africa, four-hour batteries will be 33% cheaper by 2035, “displacing gas peaking on cost across every gas market in the region.” In China, energy storage costs are 55% below its neighbors’.
“This economic shift is decisive and widening,” Ahmed Jameel Abdullah, principal analyst at Wood Mackenzie, said in a press release.

articles.title: GlobalFoundries Bets on FDX Fusion for Physical AI- EE Times
articles.text:
GlobalFoundries today (Oct. 9) unveiled FDX Fusion in Dresden, a new generation of its fully depleted silicon-on-insulator (FD-SOI) technology aimed at physical AI. The bet is that the next big AI semiconductor market will look very different from the GPU race in data centers.
FDX Fusion targets machines that must sense, decide, communicate, and act—not just compute. The first generation is expected to offer 7-nm-class digital performance and more than twice the density of GlobalFoundries’ first-generation FDX technology. It will also combine RF, analog, mixed-signal, embedded nonvolatile memory, in-memory computing, and dense logic capabilities.
Horstmann said GlobalFoundries expects to invest roughly $1 billion over the coming years in FDX Fusion development, including about $250 million for the initial capability toolset. Demonstrator silicon is targeted for early 2027, with an initial process design kit planned for mid-2027.
The announcement came as GlobalFoundries celebrated the topping-off of SPRINT, its Dresden fab expansion supported under the European Chips Act. The project is adding cleanroom, laboratory, and manufacturing capacity at a site GlobalFoundries plans to use for differentiated semiconductor technologies.
For Manfred Horstmann, senior VP and general manager of European fabs at GlobalFoundries, the FDX Fusion architecture reflects a fundamental difference between the chips needed for data center AI and those required when intelligence moves into cars, robots, drones, industrial equipment, and other autonomous systems.
“Data center AI is extremely power hungry,” Horstmann told EE Times in an exclusive interview before the announcement. “Physical AI is a different class of problem—and it needs more than compute. It needs sensors, actuators, communications, low power, and cost efficiency.”
That’s the idea behind what GlobalFoundries calls STAC—sense, think, act, communicate. Instead of optimizing primarily for maximum digital compute density, FDX Fusion is intended to combine substantial processing capability with the functions needed for a machine to interact with its environment.
From FD-SOI to FDX Fusion
FDX is GlobalFoundries’ implementation of FD-SOI. Its transistor channel sits in an approximately 70-angstrom, or 7-nm, silicon film above a buried oxide. Because the layer is so thin, the channel is inherently fully depleted. “You don’t have to waste energy depleting the channel,” Horstmann said.
That gives FDX some of the electrostatic advantages associated with FinFETs without requiring GlobalFoundries to construct a fin. “A lot of the functionality comes from the substrate itself,” Horstmann said. “So we don’t need to build a fin to get a fully depleted transistor.”
GlobalFoundries is developing the strained-silicon substrate with CEA-Leti and Soitec through a European project that Horstmann identified as “Fast and FAMES.” The partners have built a pilot line in France for the substrate, which uses a strained 70-angstrom silicon film intended to increase electron mobility by about 25%. Horstmann said the collaboration builds on the same consortium that worked with GlobalFoundries on 22FDX.
The new substrate is part of GlobalFoundries’ effort to reach 7-nm-class performance with a simpler process flow than advanced FinFET technologies. “For 7-nm-class performance, we don’t need EUV,” Horstmann said.
GlobalFoundries said it expects the initial FDX Fusion process to require about 50 masks, compared with the 70 to 80 masks Horstmann cited for advanced 2-nm and 3-nm FinFET processes. “The substrate gives us a much simpler process,” he said, adding that fewer masks should reduce process complexity and the number of opportunities to introduce defects, supporting both yield and cost.
Rather than EUV, GlobalFoundries plans to rely on advanced ArF immersion lithography, tighter overlay control, and higher-precision masks from Dresden-based mask maker AMTC.
Horstmann said the newest ASML immersion systems substantially improve overlay and critical-dimension control, while AMTC’s multi-electron-beam-written masks provide roughly 30% better overlay and CD margins than standard masks.
Physical AI needs more than logic
That process strategy matters because GlobalFoundries is not positioning FDX Fusion simply as a lower-cost route to smaller digital transistors. The platform is intended to combine dense logic with many of the analog, RF, memory, and power functions physical AI systems require.
“You can use the bulk area for high-voltage devices, and the FD-SOI area for dense logic,” Horstmann said. “That makes integrating these different functions much simpler.”
The company said FDX Fusion will combine dense digital logic with high-performance RF, analog and mixed-signal functions, low-leakage operation, embedded nonvolatile memory, and in-memory computing.
According to Horstmann, the platform should reach logic densities of roughly 14 million to 18 million gates per square millimeter while retaining the low-power and integration characteristics of the existing FDX architecture.
“You maintain the advantages of 22FDX—extremely low power and very good integration with sensors and actuators,” he said. “Extremely low power is what you need for mobile autonomous systems and drones.”
A different AI opportunity for Europe
Europe faces an uncomfortable reality in AI semiconductors: Much of the data center ecosystem is already concentrated elsewhere. “The data center AI train has left the station,” Horstmann said. “But for physical AI, the world is still open.”
His argument is that Europe does not need to win the same race. Physical AI rewards a combination of low-power compute, sensing, communications, analog, and power electronics that aligns more closely with Europe’s existing semiconductor strengths.
Dresden provides part of the industrial base for that strategy. The region already hosts GlobalFoundries, Infineon, Bosch, research organizations, suppliers, and the ESMC joint venture led by TSMC.
“The cluster is becoming self-propelling,” Horstmann said. As it grows, suppliers establish local capacity, equipment companies maintain service teams nearby, and design houses are drawn into the region.
Even ESMC, while a competitor, strengthens that ecosystem, he pointed out, by increasing Dresden’s scale and making the region more attractive to suppliers.
For Horstmann, that combination of manufacturing scale and differentiated technology creates the opening. “This is a big opportunity for Europe to define a new market,” he said, “and to be first.”

articles.title: Richard Garriott says he's getting the Ultima rights back from EA in 2027
articles.text:
True Classics: Richard Garriott recently confirmed that he will soon reacquire the IP rights to the Ultima series from EA. The distinguished game designer and the publisher have already exchanged a few emails about the matter, so things could soon start moving again for one of the most iconic CRPG series of all time.
Richard Garriott will soon get the Ultima rights back and is already planning what to do with the series afterward. The British-born American game designer, entrepreneur, and space tourist played a major role in establishing the CRPG genre during the home computer era. Now, the man behind the Lord British persona wants another go at the popular series, which debuted almost half a century ago.
Garriott recently reiterated what he believes will happen a year from now. Thanks to a "really weird" US copyright law, the original rights holder can essentially reclaim their intellectual property 35 years after selling it to someone else. The process does not require any payment; the original owner simply needs to notify the current rights holder a year before reclaiming the IP.
Lord British contacted EA, the most recent holder of the Ultima rights, in April this year. As he explained in the interview, the publisher acknowledged his request and confirmed that it would act in accordance with US copyright law.
As things stand, Garriott will officially regain ownership of the Ultima series in 2027. The designer is spending this year considering his next move, as the Ultima brand might still carry some weight among CRPG fans. Lord British could eventually re-release the earlier Ultima games on modern platforms or launch an entirely new Ultima experience. He is even considering working with EA again to secure the franchise's future in gaming.
"The point is – I have control again of the future of my seminal product line," Garriott said in the interview.
Richard Garriott sold Origin Systems, along with the Ultima series, to Electronic Arts in 1992. Ultima IX, the last mainline entry in the series, came out in 1999. Subsequent attempts to revive the franchise, such as the free-to-play Ultima Forever: Quest for the Avatar in 2013, failed to gain enough traction among gamers.
Throughout the 80s and early 90s, Ultima helped introduce new conventions and mechanics to computer role-playing games. Alongside Wizardry, Might and Magic, and a few other influential franchises, the series established standards and pioneered innovations that many successful games later adopted. To this day, fans continue to build new projects and remakes using the creative DNA of the original Ultima games.

articles.title: Europa y China alcanzan un acuerdo que apunta a reducir a la mitad la llegada de coches híbridos chinos en cuatro años
articles.text:
La llegada de coches fabricados en China lleva tiempo poniendo a prueba a la industria automovilística europea. Los fabricantes del gigante asiático han ganado presencia en el mercado comunitario, especialmente en segmentos donde la electrificación está transformando la oferta de vehículos. Pero hay una diferencia importante que no siempre resulta evidente: un coche eléctrico y uno híbrido no reciben necesariamente el mismo tratamiento comercial. Y esa distinción ha terminado adquiriendo una dimensión que va mucho más allá de las preferencias de los conductores europeos.
Un acuerdo para reducir las importaciones. La Unión Europea y China alcanzaron este viernes un entendimiento sobre el comercio de automóviles híbridos tras dos días de negociaciones en Pekín, celebradas el 8 y el 9 de octubre. Maroš Šefčovič, comisario europeo de Comercio y Seguridad Económica, explicó que el acuerdo podría reducir más de la mitad los envíos de estos vehículos desde China al mercado comunitario durante los próximos cuatro años. El Ministerio de Comercio chino confirmó el entendimiento, aunque no precisó cómo se aplicará ni recogió expresamente esa reducción en su comunicado.
El origen está en los aranceles. Para entender cómo hemos llegado hasta aquí, tenemos que retroceder a octubre de 2024. Entonces, la Comisión Europea impuso aranceles compensatorios adicionales a los vehículos eléctricos de batería fabricados en China, tras una investigación antisubvenciones. Los recargos oscilan entre el 7,8% y el 35,3%, dependiendo del fabricante, y se suman al arancel ordinario del 10%. Sin embargo, aquella medida dejó fuera a los híbridos, tanto convencionales como enchufables, que siguieron pagando únicamente el arancel ordinario.
Una transformación que muestran los números. En 2023, casi siete de cada diez automóviles que la UE importaba de China eran eléctricos puros: el 69%, según Global Trade Alert. En 2025, esa proporción había bajado al 45%, mientras los híbridos convencionales y enchufables pasaban del 7% al 31%. Durante la primera mitad de 2026, estos últimos llegaron al 39% de los vehículos importados desde el país asiático. Hay otro dato que permite dimensionar el crecimiento. Financial Times señala que las importaciones mensuales de híbridos desde China pasaron de 3.800 unidades en octubre de 2024 a 50.000 en julio de 2026.
Lo anunciado no explica cómo se aplicará. El responsable europeo ha adelantado el alcance que podría tener el entendimiento, pero todavía quedan preguntas importantes por resolver. El comunicado conjunto difundido por el Ministerio de Comercio chino confirma el acuerdo sobre los híbridos dentro de las reglas de la Organización Mundial del Comercio (OMC), aunque no especifica qué mecanismo permitiría alcanzar la reducción prevista. Tampoco precisa cómo se supervisaría su cumplimiento ni si las condiciones serían iguales para todos los fabricantes.
No todas las restricciones son equivalentes. Bruselas había planteado que China limitase voluntariamente sus exportaciones de híbridos, pero Pekín se opuso en septiembre y alegó que el sistema vulneraba las normas de la OMC.
El automóvil es solo una parte. El entendimiento sobre los híbridos forma parte de una negociación que, según el Ministerio de Comercio chino, terminó con 16 puntos de consenso. Abarcan el equilibrio comercial y las inversiones, los controles de exportación, la propiedad intelectual y la reforma de la OMC. China también se mostró dispuesta a seguir facilitando, mediante un mecanismo de “canal verde”, la aprobación de licencias para exportar tierras raras e imanes permanentes a la UE.
El resultado dependerá de su aplicación. El siguiente paso será comprobar si el entendimiento alcanzado en Pekín se traduce en compromisos comerciales concretos. Se espera que ambas partes mantengan una reunión ministerial por videoconferencia en enero de 2027 y celebren una nueva ronda de negociaciones en marzo.

articles.title: Starlink spectrum deal boosts Musk plan to beat AT&T, T-Mobile, and Verizon
articles.text:
SpaceX has a deal to purchase nationwide low-band spectrum licenses for a planned terrestrial mobile network that would complement the space-based Starlink cellular service.
SpaceX will buy up to 14 megahertz of spectrum in the 800 MHz band from investment firm Grain Management, which bought the spectrum rights from T-Mobile earlier this year. T-Mobile had obtained the spectrum when it bought Sprint in 2020 and was required to sell the licenses under a merger condition imposed by the US government.
“This prime low-band spectrum addresses one of the key remaining technical gaps that will pave the way for Starlink Mobile to become a major mobile carrier in the US,” SpaceX said yesterday. SpaceX this week also received US approval to launch 15,000 satellites for an upgraded version of its mobile service that it says will be far more powerful than the current offering.
The 800 MHz spectrum licenses cover “approximately 100 percent of the US population,” the Federal Communications Commission said in a July 2026 order approving Grain’s purchase of the T-Mobile licenses. While the licenses are nationwide, it’s not a huge amount of spectrum. It ranges from 4.85 megahertz to 14 megahertz depending on the county. The FCC said the 800 MHz spectrum can be used for terrestrial service, satellite-to-mobile service, or both.
SpaceX’s low-band purchase is in addition to 65 MHz of nationwide mid-band spectrum licenses it is buying from EchoStar. The FCC approved that $17 billion purchase in May 2026.
“While Starlink Mobile’s global 2 GHz mid-band spectrum will provide high-bandwidth capacity in the United States, this new low-band spectrum will provide a coverage layer that ensures Starlink Mobile’s signal penetrates through obstacles, such as walls, and can provide service to customers’ devices even when they are in buildings. Critically, most existing mobile devices already support this underused band,” SpaceX said.
SpaceX’s big mobile plans
SpaceX’s spectrum deal is likely to be approved by the FCC, but it could face opposition from small carriers. The Rural Wireless Association opposed EchoStar’s spectrum sales to AT&T and SpaceX, saying the deals “continue the troubling pattern of spectrum aggregation that disadvantages rural wireless providers.” Across all carriers in the US, there is about 1.1 GHz of licensed spectrum allocated to mobile operators, with the big three holding dominant spectrum portfolios.
