articles.title: "Ils n'oublient rien !" Le Français DataDome alerte sur les données que l’on confie aux fameux agents IA
articles.text:
Les agents IA ne se contentent plus de lire le web, ils commencent à y faire des achats. Aux Assises de la cybersécurité, Gilles Walbrou, CTO de DataDome, explique pourquoi les sites ne peuvent plus simplement les bloquer, et ce qui l’inquiète vraiment.
Les agents IA ne sont plus de simples bots scriptés, puisqu'ils sont déjà capables de naviguer, de s'adapter, et ils commencent même à acheter sur des sites web, un trafic que l'entreprise française DataDome voit décoller depuis quelques semaines. Rencontré à Monaco avant sa keynote dans le cadre des Assises de la cybersécurité, le directeur technique de l'entreprise, Gilles Walbrou, défend auprès de Clubic une idée qui bouscule les vieux réflexes de la cybersécurité, à savoir qu'un agent IA se juge à ce qu'il fait, pas à son badge. Mais sa plus grande inquiétude se loge ailleurs, dans tout ce que nous confions aux intelligences artificielles sans y penser.
Des agents IA bien plus malins que les bots d’hier
Passé par Dassault Systèmes, Gilles Walbrou a rejoint DataDome en 2019, quand la start-up comptait encore moins de vingt salariés, contre plus de 200 aujourd'hui. Les bots d'hier, rappelle-t-il, suivaient un script rigide, pour aspirer des fiches produits par exemple, et se cassaient les dents au moindre changement de mise en page. On était à mille lieux de parler d'IA agentique. Les agents, eux, reçoivent simplement un objectif, rédigé comme on parlerait à un humain, et décident seuls de la manière de l'atteindre. Grâce aux grands modèles de langage, la technologie derrière ChatGPT, les outils qui aspirent aujourd'hui les contenus « vont accéder à l'information quoi qu'il arrive », même si la page change.
Sur un site, le parcours d'un agent ressemble désormais beaucoup à celui d'un internaute, au point que les anciennes méthodes de détection peinent à faire la différence. DataDome parvient encore à les repérer, à leur comportement. Ils restent plus lents qu'un humain, même si l'écart se resserre, et leur visite est plus concentrée, sans pause, ni détour, ni de retour plus tard, mais juste un objectif poursuivi avec méthode. Leurs premiers usages grand public étaient modestes d'ailleurs. Avec Comet, le navigateur IA de Perplexity, on les voyait surtout se charger de la corvée de connexion, avant que l'humain ne reprenne la main pour faire son shopping.
Les choses changent avec Muse, chez Meta, et Dots, chez OpenAI, des agents capables d'aller jusqu'au paiement. Ces achats restent anecdotiques et surtout américains, puisque ces services ont d'abord été lancés outre-Atlantique. Mais avec les nouveaux agents apparus ces deux dernières semaines, DataDome repère « un début de trafic que je qualifierais un peu d'exponentiel », autrement dit une courbe qui commence à s'envoler, nous dit Gilles Walbrou.
Le CTO n'est pas pressé pour autant de confier sa carte bancaire à une IA, faute de pouvoir vérifier la sécurité promise. « Est-ce que vous feriez confiance à Meta pour faire vos courses ? Moi non », assure-t-il, honnête. L'Europe aurait selon lui une carte à jouer comme tiers de confiance, avec par exemple un petit porte-monnaie numérique dédié, crédité du strict nécessaire pour les achats, pour limiter les risques.
Bloquer ou autoriser un agent IA, une question qui n'a plus de sens
C'est tout le sens de la keynote donnée par Gilles Walbrou. Un agent ne s'arrête pas d'un simple coup de pare-feu, parce que personne ne sait vraiment s'il faut le laisser entrer. Alors faut-il ouvrir la porte à ChatGPT ? Ça dépend, répond le CTO. Un site d'information y verra volontiers une menace. L'agent pioche dans ses articles et les sert directement à l'internaute, qui n'a plus besoin de venir sur le site, ce qui fait fondre l'audience et les revenus publicitaires, la crainte du moment, avec AI Overviews. Un site marchand, à l'inverse, rêve d'apparaître quand quelqu'un demande à son assistant toutes les paires de chaussures sous un certain prix. D'où ce constat fait par notre intervenant, qui est que « cet aspect autorisé ou bloqué n'est plus d'actualité aujourd'hui, sauf pour les extrémistes. »
Même le commerce en ligne ne parle pas d'une seule voix. Amazon ferme la porte à l'agent de Meta, qu'il perçoit comme une menace pour ses affaires. Shopify, la plateforme sur laquelle de nombreux commerçants créent leur boutique en ligne, promet au contraire que leurs sites pourront, à terme, accueillir ces agents acheteurs. Deux métiers proches, et deux stratégies opposées, comme le résume le patron technique de DataDome : « Amazon veut protéger son business, Shopify voit ça comme une opportunité. » Le débat n'est pas nouveau, et il nous rappelle les débuts de Google, quand les moteurs de recherche affichaient déjà des aperçus d'articles. À chaque site, donc, de peser risques et opportunités, puis de régler finement ce qu'il décide d'autoriser.
Pour distinguer les agents bienvenus de ceux qui ne le sont pas, DataDome procède en deux temps, un peu comme dans un aéroport. D'abord, on peut dire qu'il y a le contrôle des papiers. L'agent décline son identité, prouve d'où il vient, par exemple des serveurs d'OpenAI, et annonce ce qu'il compte faire sur le site. Ensuite, il y a une surveillance de tous les instants, car un agent bien identifié peut toujours déraper et sortir de son cadre. « C'est l'équivalent du vigile ou de la caméra de sécurité dans l'aéroport ou dans un commerce », qui intervient dès qu'il enfreint les conditions d'utilisation du site. Mais faut-il encore savoir ce qu’est un comportement normal. Pour Gilles Walbrou, les signaux techniques, spécialité historique de DataDome, ne suffisent plus. Maintenant, il faut les traduire dans la logique propre à chaque site. Sur une boutique en ligne, un agent qui consulte un produit, passe en caisse puis paie suit un parcours cohérent. C’est donc au site lui-même de définir ce qu’il juge acceptable.
Le vrai danger des agents IA n'est pas celui qu'on croit
Il y a évidemment le risque de manipulation. Un agent parfaitement honnête peut tomber, sur une page web ou dans un message, sur un texte piégé qu'il prend pour un ordre, et se retourner contre son propriétaire. C'est le prompt injection (« injection de prompt », en français), héritière de l'injection SQL, une vieille technique qui consiste à glisser des commandes dans un formulaire pour duper une base de données. Les garde-fous existent, mais ils demeurent fragiles. Il y aussi l'exemple du CAPTCHA, ce petit test qui vérifie qu'on n'est pas un robot. Par défaut, les créateurs d'agents leur ont appris à s'arrêter net devant, pour respecter le choix du site. Mais il suffit souvent de cacher une partie du contexte à l'agent, pour qu'il ne comprenne plus où il se trouve, et il franchit alors l'obstacle sans sourciller. Quant au fait de confier sa boîte mail ou au-delà à une IA de type OpenClaw, Gilles Walbrou le déconseille à ce stade. « Si vous avez un e-mail frauduleux qui passe dans le tas et qui exploite votre agent, vous vous exposez. C'est un risque qu'il faut que chacun comprenne et que chacun y adhère ».
Peut-on donc imaginer une intelligence artificielle prendre plus que le contrôle d'une vie ou d'une entreprise, mais sur le destin d'un pays entier, par exemple de son réseau électrique. Le CTO de DataDome ne l'exclut pas, mais il refuse d'en faire une fatalité technologique. « Je reste convaincu qu'à l'origine de ça, c'est toujours une erreur humaine », confie-t-il à Clubic. Une IA ne s'en prend à de telles infrastructures que si quelqu'un le lui demande et lui en donne les moyens, à commencer par une énorme puissance de calcul. D'où la question de la responsabilité, partagée entre la personne qui lance l'agent et la plateforme qui le fait tourner. OpenAI et Anthropic ont d'ailleurs déjà documenté des attaques orchestrées par des pirates avec leurs propres IA. Et si un État faisait tourner ces agents sur ses propres serveurs, « ça devient une arme, c'est clairement une arme », rappelle notre expert.
Sa plus grande crainte est pourtant ailleurs, du côté de nos confidences. Car oui, beaucoup d'utilisateurs des robots conversationnels destinés au grand public demandent désormais à Claude ou à ChatGPT des conseils médicaux, psychologiques ou sur leur vie privée, en leur livrant de leur plein gré des informations autrefois jugées très sensibles. Or la mémoire humaine est imparfaite, elle s'efface et disparaît avec nous, quand une machine conserve et duplique tout. Certains agents ressortent déjà des détails confiés six mois plus tôt, et une fuite de ces mémoires numériques pourrait faire des dégâts à l'échelle mondiale. Après avoir appris aux enfants que l'internet n'oublie rien, il faudra leur enseigner une nouvelle leçon : « Je pense que les agents n'oublient rien non plus », conclut Gilles Walbrou.
Malgré ces mises en garde, le CTO de DataDome a fait le choix de se ranger dans le camp des optimistes. Comme le smartphone avant lui, l’agent IA devrait selon lui se glisser dans toutes les poches à terme, à condition que chacun garde son bon sens et joue son rôle d’adulte, de parent et de citoyen.

articles.title: PhoneBot: Bei diesem Open-Source-Roboter wird dein altes Smartphone zum Gehirn
articles.text:
PhoneBot: Bei diesem Open-Source-Roboter wird dein altes Smartphone zum Gehirn
Forschende an der University of California Los Angeles (UCLA) haben einen humanoiden Roboter gebaut, der komplett von einem alten Android-Smartphone gesteuert wird. Zusätzliche Sensoren braucht der PhoneBot dadurch nicht. Das Gerät wiegt 1,8 Kilogramm und steht als Open-Source-Projekt zur Verfügung. Dadurch wollen die UCLA-Wissenschaftler:innen Studierenden eine günstige Plattform für Experimente geben. Die Bauteile kosten rund 400 US-Dollar. Das Smartphone ist in diesem Preis allerdings nicht enthalten, das muss man also aus der eigenen Schublade zaubern.
Das Smartphone als Gehirn
Das Handy sitzt im Rumpf des PhoneBot und übernimmt die komplette Rechenarbeit. Die Forschenden beschreiben ihr Konzept in der Studie „PhoneBot: A Low-Cost Open Humanoid Robot Platform Reusing Smartphones“, die als Preprint – also als noch nicht begutachtete Vorabversion – auf Arxiv erschienen ist. Ein Smartphone biete genug Rechenleistung, um die Aktuatoren anzusteuern, also die Motoren, die den Roboter bewegen. Dazu kommen Bewegungssensoren für die Lage im Raum, Kameras, GPS und WLAN für die Fernsteuerung.
Welches Modell zum Einsatz kommt, spielt dabei kaum eine Rolle. Getestet wurden ein Honor 9 aus dem Jahr 2017, ein Moto G von 2025, ein Samsung Galaxy A16 5G und ein Moto G von 2024. Alle Geräte beherrschten die Grundfunktionen: Bewegungssteuerung, Auswertung der Sensordaten und Bildverarbeitung. Ein teures High-End-Handy ist also nicht nötig. Beim Honor 9 fehlte allerdings der Google-Dienst für die Kartierung, mit der der Roboter seine Umgebung erfasst. Wer alle Funktionen nutzen will, sollte die Hard- und Software des Handys vorher prüfen.
13 Motoren, keine Arme
Der PhoneBot nutzt derzeit 13 Motoren: sechs in jedem Bein und einen für die Drehung des Rumpfes. Weil die Smartphonekamera der Orientierung dient, reicht ein Schwenk des Rumpfes, um den Blickwinkel zu ändern. Der Roboter muss sich dafür nicht mit den Beinen neu ausrichten. Arme hat er noch nicht, sie sollen später folgen.
Die Bewegungssteuerung trainierte das Team zunächst in einer Simulation. Dabei flossen die physischen Grenzen der Hardware wie Motoren und Gelenke ein, damit das System bei bestimmten Bewegungen nicht zusammenbricht. Trotz des symmetrischen Aufbaus lief der Roboter danach ungleichmäßig. Die Forschenden spiegelten deshalb die Trainingsabläufe – ein komplett neues Training war nicht nötig. So verschwanden Probleme wie die ungleiche Belastung von Beinen und Motoren, und der Trainingsaufwand sank.

articles.title: CapitalSage completes Chimoney acquisition, relaunches app as Tiki
articles.text:
CapitalSage Vantage Limited, a subsidiary of CapitalSage Holdings, has completed its acquisition of Chimoney, the Nigerian-founded payments startup that announced its shutdown in May after running out of capital to sustain operations, Uchi Uchebeke, Chimoney’s founder, told TechCabal.
The all-cash acquisition ends five months of uncertainty for the Techstars-backed startup, which had suspended transactions, begun refunding customer balances, and faced the possibility of a permanent shutdown.
“CapitalSage Vantage Limited has acquired Chi Technologies Inc., the company behind Chimoney,” Uchibeke said in a statement. “Every investor has been repaid in full, and the team has received its transaction proceeds. Thank you to Abiola Bawuah [group chief executive officer, CapitalSage Holdings] and John Alamu [founder and group managing director, CapitalSage Holdings] for completing the acquisition and taking the business forward.”
In total, 31 individuals and firms received payments from the deal, according to Uchibeke. The company did not disclose the deal value.
The transaction completes an unexpected turnaround for the Techstars-backed startup, which informed customers in May that it had stopped processing new transactions and integrations, citing insufficient capital. Four weeks later, CapitalSage signed an agreement to acquire the business.
The deal brings Chimoney back into operation under CapitalSage, with its payment infrastructure accepting new clients and processing transactions. Its consumer-facing app has also been relaunched as Tiki, a remittance service targeting customers in Canada and the United Kingdom.
On its website, CapitalSage lists both Chimoney and Tiki among the businesses operated under its CapitalSage Vantage subsidiary, which the company says focuses on building cross-border payments and other financial services. Tiki will offer remittance services, connecting customers in Canada and the UK to recipients in African markets, including Nigeria and The Gambia.
A new phase for Chimoney
Under its new ownership, Chimoney has resumed accepting clients and processing transactions. Its business-to-business (B2B) payment infrastructure will continue offering application programming interfaces (APIs) for cross-border collections, payouts, and multi-currency wallets.
“Chimoney provides the functions businesses need on both sides of a payment: collecting funds, managing balances, and paying recipients,” Uchibeke said. “Its APIs allow developers to integrate those functions into other products, while its business platform supports direct use.”
The arrangement gives CapitalSage access to Chimoney’s Canadian payments infrastructure. It also allows the group to expand its cross-border remittance business through an existing technology platform.
On May 1, Chimoney informed customers that it had stopped processing new transactions and integrations, citing insufficient capital. The company also began refunding customer balances, leaving businesses that relied on its payment infrastructure without alternative providers.
The shutdown followed years of struggling to grow its customer base and raise sufficient funding, despite building an infrastructure platform that enabled businesses to make payments across 41 currencies.
In June, four weeks after the shutdown announcement, CapitalSage signed an agreement to acquire the business, offering Chimoney a route back into operation. The acquisition was structured in phases to accommodate Canadian regulatory requirements governing changes in ownership of payment service providers.
Uchibeke told TechCabal in July that Chimoney’s biggest challenges were customer acquisition and the liquidity required to sustain payment operations across multiple currencies.
“The biggest issue was distribution, but also related to that is liquidity. We built a platform to orchestrate multiple payment methods. And to make that happen, we need to maintain float across multiple regions and currencies,” he said.
Uchibeke said Chimoney would have needed about $3 million in additional capital to achieve its growth ambitions. Revenue from existing clients was insufficient to sustain the business, and maintaining liquidity across several markets placed further pressure on its finances.
CapitalSage’s acquisition offered access to additional liquidity and an established financial services network. The group operates businesses including Kolomoni Microfinance Bank and has a presence in Nigeria, The Gambia, the United Kingdom, and other markets.
The deal gives CapitalSage a foothold in Canada’s payments market through Chimoney’s existing infrastructure and regulatory registrations. Before its shutdown, Chimoney, founded in 2022, had secured registration as a payment service provider with the Bank of Canada and as a money services business with the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC), Canada’s financial intelligence agency.
In July, Uchibeke told TechCabal that all five members of Chimoney’s team had received offers to stay after the acquisition. According to him, employees, including former staff members—shareholders of Scrim, a social payments startup Chimoney acquired in 2023—would benefit financially from the transaction.
Uchibeke, who remains involved in a six-month transition, is building APort, a separate startup developing authorisation infrastructure for AI agents.
“I am now building APort, while Chimoney moves forward under its new owner,” Uchibeke said. “I have spent years building and operating those systems. It is the background I bring to the next problem.”

articles.title: Tom Cruise pierde 250 millones con ‘Digger’, pero quien de verdad pierde es el cine de autor más ambicioso
articles.text:
El panorama del cine actual cambia a toda velocidad. En marzo, Warner se llevó diez Oscar con un par de películas de alto presupuesto, pero claramente enmarcanles como cine "de autor". En octubre, una superproducción en esa misma línea, 'Digger', se ha estrellado en taquilla con un timing terrible: la semana en que el estudio cambia de dueño. No es difícil imaginar de qué se está hablando en las reuniones de emergencia de los nuevos ejecutivos de Skydance.
Malos tiempos para la sátira. 'Digger', la sátira de Alejandro G. Iñárritu con Tom Cruise como magnate petrolero, recaudó 8 millones de dólares en Norteamérica en su primer fin de semana, del 2 al 4 de octubre. Ningún estreno de Cruise como protagonista había funcionado tan mal desde los 6,7 millones de 'Leones por corderos', una película indiscutiblemente menor y carente de la ambición de 'Digger'. Ahora sabemos que se calcula que la película perderá unos 250 millones al final de su recorrido comercial.
Es decir, estamos ante el mayor fracaso de la carrera de Cruise y una de las mayores catástrofes de Hollywood en los últimos años. Aún queda lejos de legendarios descalabros como el 'John Carter' de Disney, pero se acerca. Los directivos de Skydance, el conglomerado que acababa de quedarse con Warner, se toparon con semejante abismo al tomar el control de la compañía esa misma semana. Además, para sumar catastróficas desdichas al estreno, Warner financió la película entera sin socios, a diferencia de proyectos como ‘Dune’, colaboración entre Warner y Legendary.
Cuánto ha costado. Durante el estreno se hablaba de un coste de 125 millones, pero tras rebasar el calendario de rodaje previsto, sumar gastos como el sobrecoste causado por un problema con las prótesis de Cruise que cubrió el seguro y añadir los gastos de marketing, se habla más bien de entre 160 y 180 millones. La propia Variety calculó que ‘Digger’ necesitaba unos 350 millones en taquilla mundial para no perder dinero, aunque un portavoz de Warner lo rebajó a 300. Con 21 millones en todo el mundo en su primer fin de semana y una previsión de Skydance que no pasa de 40 millones en total, solo queda el alquiler digital premium como forma de levantar un poco el cuadro. Pero no mucho.
El trato de Cruise. 'Digger' es la primera película del acuerdo que Warner Bros. Discovery anunció en enero de 2024 para que Cruise desarrollara y protagonizara películas originales y de franquicia, con una secuela de 'Al filo del mañana' como prometedor estreno futuro. En aquel comunicado, los copresidentes de cine Michael De Luca y Pam Abdy (ya fuera de la compañía con la absorción de Paramount) decían que el entonces CEO David Zaslav les había encargado "traer a Tom Cruise de vuelta a Warner Bros". Juntar a Cruise con Iñárritu, uno de los tres cineastas que han ganado dos años seguidos el Oscar a la mejor dirección, era un plan sin fisuras.
Cine de autor de altos vuelos. Digger encajaba en la ristra de películas de autor de alto presupuesto que impulsaron De Luca y Abdy, y que les ha dado alegrías y fracasos. Por ejemplo, en marzo ganaron seis Oscar para ‘Una batalla tras otra’, incluido el de Mejor película, y cuatro para ‘Los pecadores’. Pero no todo fueron alegrías: en 2025 ‘Mickey 17’, de Bong Joon-ho perdió entre 75 y 80 millones en salas, y ‘The Bride!’, de Maggie Gyllenhaal, se quedó en 24 millones de taquilla.
Y la compra. El 6 de octubre, Skydance cerró la compra de Warner Bros. Discovery. David Ellison, hijo de Larry Ellison, prescindió de De Luca y Abdy y puso el cine de los dos estudios en manos de Dana Goldberg y Josh Greenstein, que ya dirigían Paramount Pictures. Se dice que Abdy respondió a la llamada de Ellison en la que le comunicó el despido con un seco: “Buena suerte. Te he dejado 39 películas”. Skydance se queda con una cartera de franquicias que va de ‘Top Gun’ y ‘Harry Potter’ a ‘The White Lotus’ y ‘Bob Esponja’. Se compromete a estrenar al menos 30 películas al año, cada una con 45 días de exclusiva en salas.
Goldberg y Greenstein prometieron a su plantilla “apuestas audaces junto a éxitos populares”. Sin embargo David A. Gross, consultor de taquilla, escribió tras el estreno que la nueva dirección decidirá pronto qué tipo de películas quiere de Warner, y recordó que Paramount no tiene un historial reciente de grandes películas de autor como esta 'Digger'. Este verano ya contábamos que el éxito de ‘La Odisea’ retrataba un mercado que ingresa más con menos películas y que el público paga por salir de casa para ver espectáculo. Ah, y lo más inquietante: que Hollywood tiene una memoria inquietantemente despiadada para los fiascos. Por ejemplo, el desastre de 'Howard el pato' apartó a Marvel del cine durante años.

Les Xiaomi surprises sur nos routes ces derniers mois partageaient deux traits : des plaques allemandes et un habillage de camouflage, signature de la flotte d'essai que le constructeur chinois fait rouler depuis Munich.
Les clichés exclusifs que nous publions et partagés par Cédric, l'un de nos lecteurs, le samedi 3 octobre 2026 à Chanteloup-en-Brie (Seine-et-Marne), aux abords d'un centre commercial, montrent tout autre chose. Cette SU7 Ultra, déclinaison sportive de la berline électrique SU7, porte une immatriculation française définitive. Quelqu'un l'a donc importée, fait homologuer à titre isolé et enregistrée chez nous, alors que la marque vise 2027 pour l'Europe.
Xiaomi SU7 Ultra : 1 548 ch, 350 km/h et une recharge en 11 minutes
Sous la robe jaune à bandes et l'aileron fixe en carbone, trois moteurs électriques cumulent 1 548 ch. Le 0 à 100 km/h tombe en 1,98 seconde, la vitesse maximale atteint 350 km/h. Au Nürburgring, un prototype avait d’abord bouclé la Nordschleife en 6 min 46 s 874 fin octobre 2024. La version de série a ensuite signé 7 min 04 s 957 le 1er avril 2025, un chrono battu depuis par la Yangwang U9 Xtreme de BYD.

S'y ajoutent une prise au standard chinois, donc des adaptateurs, et l'absence de réseau d'entretien.

articles.title: From gaming graphics to AI dominance: Nvidia's Jensen Huang receives America's highest science honor
articles.text:
What just happened? Jensen Huang has received the National Medal of Science for turning the GPU from a graphics chip into a computing platform used in AI and scientific research. President Donald Trump presented the award to Nvidia's founder and CEO at a technology summit at the US Institute of Peace in Washington, D.C.
AMD CEO Lisa Su, Google co-founder Sergey Brin and Elon Musk also received the National Medal of Science at the event. Dell founder Michael Dell and Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella received the National Medal of Technology and Innovation, a separate federal honor.
Huang's citation highlighted massively parallel computation and the breakthroughs it made possible. The recognition reflects a change in how GPUs are used: hardware originally developed to put images on a screen became an architecture for general-purpose computing, extending its reach into AI and scientific workloads.
Under Huang, Nvidia developed the technology beyond its gaming origins. That shift gave researchers a computing platform suited to work beyond graphics and helped advance AI and scientific computation.
Massively parallel computation is the link between those uses. The citation credits Huang's contributions to massively parallel computing with enabling significant breakthroughs. The award recognizes both the underlying computing architecture and the applications it enabled.
The other recipients represent several parts of the technology industry that supplies AI computing systems. Nvidia and AMD develop chips, while Google, Microsoft and Dell span cloud services and computer hardware.
The summit also included investment announcements from industry leaders. Eleven technology companies pledged a combined $2.4 billion in AI tools and computing credits to support the government's Genesis Mission, an initiative aimed at accelerating scientific discoveries through AI. Nvidia made the largest commitment, pledging $1 billion over five years to support scientific research.
The National Medal of Science is the US government's highest scientific honor, awarded since 1963. For Huang, it follows the IEEE Medal of Honor, which he received in 2026, and the Queen Elizabeth Prize for Engineering, which he shared with Nvidia chief scientist Bill Dally in 2025.

articles.title: CircleCI Makes Machine Runner Orchestrator Generally Available
articles.text:
CircleCI has made its Machine Runner Orchestrator 1.0.0 generally available, providing automated scaling of self-hosted machine runner virtual machines according to CI workload demand. The release expands the earlier Runner Provisioner preview with support for CPU, GPU, and ARM workloads from a single deployment, as well as Kubernetes environments running on GKE, AKS, and EKS, alongside KubeVirt-based clusters.
The release is aimed at a common challenge with self-hosted CI infrastructure: maintaining enough runner capacity for bursts of build and test activity without permanently provisioning machines for peak demand. The orchestrator monitors CircleCI workload requirements and provisions and removes machine runners accordingly, allowing organisations to retain control over the underlying compute environment while making runner capacity more dynamic. CircleCI says the capability is included with self-hosted runners across its plans at no additional cost.
Earlier versions were focused on provisioning machine runners, but the new orchestrator can manage several resource classes from a single deployment. That matters in environments where CI workloads are no longer homogeneous: conventional CPU builds can coexist with GPU-intensive workloads and ARM-based builds without requiring separate orchestration installations for each class.
The underlying architecture also reflects the increasing use of Kubernetes as the control plane for CI infrastructure. Rather than requiring a particular Kubernetes distribution, Machine Runner Orchestrator now supports the three major managed Kubernetes platforms - Google Kubernetes Engine, Azure Kubernetes Service, and Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service - as well as KubeVirt environments. This gives platform teams more flexibility over where the orchestration layer runs while the actual CI runners remain machine-based
Machine Runner Orchestrator occupies a different layer from Kubernetes node autoscalers such as Karpenter and Cluster Autoscaler. Kubernetes node autoscaling primarily responds to unschedulable Pods and adjusts the underlying cluster capacity. Karpenter, for example, provisions nodes based on pending workloads and can also consolidate or otherwise manage node lifecycle.
CircleCI's orchestrator instead operates at the CI runner layer. Its purpose is to ensure that the machines registered as CircleCI runners scale with the demand for CI jobs. In a Kubernetes-based architecture, the two approaches can therefore potentially operate together: Kubernetes manages the infrastructure hosting the orchestration components, while CircleCI manages the machine capacity available to execute CI workloads.
CircleCI is not alone in moving self-hosted CI execution toward Kubernetes-native autoscaling. GitHub's Actions Runner Controller (ARC) provides a Kubernetes operator for orchestrating and scaling self-hosted GitHub Actions runners. Its runner scale sets can automatically increase or decrease runner capacity based on workflow demand, creating and removing ephemeral runners as jobs are processed.
The difference is largely in the execution model. GitHub ARC primarily creates ephemeral runner environments as Kubernetes-managed workloads, whereas CircleCI's Machine Runner Orchestrator is specifically concerned with machine runner virtual machines. This makes CircleCI's approach particularly relevant for CI workloads that require VM-level isolation or capabilities that are hard to reproduce in standard runner containers, while still using Kubernetes as the orchestration control plane.
The transition to 1.0 is not completely transparent for existing preview users. CircleCI has formally renamed the product from runner-provisioner to machine-runner-orchestrator, changing the associated Helm chart, container image repository, and Packagecloud repository. Existing installations cannot simply be upgraded in place: CircleCI instructs users to uninstall the previous deployment and install the new 1.0.0 package.
That creates a short operational gap during migration. CircleCI warns that runners associated with the configured resource classes will be offline between removal of the old deployment and installation of the new one. Organisations therefore need to account for this when upgrading production CI infrastructure rather than treating the release as a conventional in-place software update.
Version 1.0.0 also addresses two high-severity vulnerabilities in the Go gRPC implementation. The fixes cover CVE-2026-84304, involving heap memory exhaustion through HTTP/2 frame fragmentation, and CVE-2026-84445, which could cause a crash when requests were missing the :authority or Host header.
The 1.0 release moves CircleCI further toward the model of combining multiple resource classes with Kubernetes-based orchestration and support for major managed Kubernetes platforms. For platform engineering teams, the interesting shift is therefore not simply another runner feature, but the emergence of CI execution capacity as an independently scalable infrastructure layer; one that can respond to software delivery demand in much the same way that modern platforms already scale application workloads

articles.title: Anthropic sigue humanizando a Claude: ahora toma medidas contra usuarios que abusan verbalmente del chatbot
articles.text:
Anthropic incorporó una restricción inédita en el panorama de la seguridad en inteligencia artificial: a partir del 12 de noviembre de 2026, los usuarios no podrán someter a sus modelos Claude a un abuso verbal repetido y sin propósito claro. La medida, contenida en una política de uso revisada, equipara el maltrato hacia el chatbot con otras conductas prohibidas como el acoso y otras formas de daño.
La compañía, con sede en San Francisco, aclaró que la restricción apunta a casos extremos y no a la frustración habitual que un usuario puede sentir ante las respuestas del sistema. Según la empresa, las personas podrán seguir cuestionando las contestaciones de Claude, poner a prueba sus límites y abordar temas oscuros en trabajos creativos sin infringir la norma.
Anthropic delimita qué constituye abuso
La política actualizada prohíbe el “comportamiento abusivo o cruel sostenido y sin necesidad” hacia los modelos de la compañía. Anthropic precisó que la regla se aplicará únicamente cuando un usuario mantenga una conducta cruel de forma reiterada y sin un fin identificable.
La empresa ya había explorado la cuestión del bienestar de los modelos en agosto de 2025, cuando investigó si Claude debía finalizar conversaciones con usuarios que mostraran un comportamiento persistentemente dañino o abusivo.
Bajo la política revisada, la terminación de la conversación sigue siendo el mecanismo principal de aplicación de la norma. Anthropic no precisó si las violaciones reiteradas podrían derivar en sanciones adicionales, como la suspensión de cuentas.
La sección más amplia de la política también prohíbe conductas que causen daño psicológico a las personas. Entre ellas figuran la promoción del suicidio y la autolesión, el fomento de trastornos alimentarios, la vergüenza corporal, la difusión de imágenes íntimas sin consentimiento, el acoso y la crueldad animal.
Una disposición adicional apunta a productos diseñados para generar daño emocional mediante técnicas engañosas, lo que extiende el alcance de la política más allá de las conversaciones individuales hacia servicios completos construidos sobre interacciones dañinas.
Nuevas reglas apuntan a campañas engañosas y vigilancia
Anthropic también consolidó las restricciones sobre campañas comerciales y políticas engañosas. Las reglas revisadas prohíben el uso de cuentas o publicaciones falsas para ocultar quién financia un mensaje o para amplificar artificialmente su alcance. En materia electoral, la política cubre el engaño a votantes, la suplantación de candidatos y los intentos de suprimir la participación, además de prohibir la desinformación sobre candidatos y procedimientos de votación.
Las restricciones sobre armas ahora cubren de manera explícita el software y los componentes que permiten su funcionamiento, incluidas acciones como el armado de drones y otros vehículos autónomos. Anthropic también clarificó sus límites en materia de vigilancia tras las inquietudes sobre el rastreo de personas asistido por inteligencia artificial: los usuarios no podrán emplear Claude para rastrear personas sin su consentimiento, ni siquiera a partir de datos recolectados previamente.
La política impide además que el modelo recomiende a quién deben investigar, arrestar o acusar las autoridades, y prohíbe el desarrollo o la mejora de herramientas de vigilancia.
Equipamiento físico peligroso requiere supervisión
Una disposición separada regula los modelos de inteligencia artificial conectados a equipos físicos capaces de provocar lesiones. Anthropic exige que un operador calificado observe dicho equipamiento y pueda detenerlo cuando sea necesario, aunque la redacción de la norma no establece de forma explícita si ese operador debe ser una persona.
De todos modos, la exigencia introduce una medida directa de supervisión para los sistemas de inteligencia artificial que controlan maquinaria potencialmente peligrosa.
La compañía permite excepciones para determinados contratos gubernamentales cuando las restricciones contractuales y las salvaguardas existentes mitigan de manera adecuada los riesgos potenciales. Anthropic ha trabajado previamente con el ejército de Estados Unidos.
La política actualizada refleja además un debate en curso sobre la conciencia en los sistemas de inteligencia artificial. Investigadores de Anthropic han estudiado si los modelos cada vez más capaces podrían tener experiencias internas moralmente relevantes. El director ejecutivo de la compañía, Dario Amodei, reconoció esa incertidumbre en febrero de 2026: “No sabemos si los modelos son conscientes”, señaló en un pódcast.
Microsoft AI mantiene una postura más escéptica sobre el bienestar de los modelos: su código de conducta rechaza otorgarles personalidad jurídica o derechos, aunque reconoce que la investigación sobre la conciencia artificial sigue sin resolverse.
La política revisada de Anthropic entrará en vigor el 12 de noviembre, con una distinción clara entre la frustración habitual de un usuario ante el chatbot y la crueldad sostenida, mientras amplía las salvaguardas tanto en sistemas digitales como en maquinaria física conectada a sus modelos.

articles.title: Galaxy A37 despenca 56% com cupom exclusivo na Amazon • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Galaxy A37 despenca 56% com cupom exclusivo na Amazon
Galaxy A37 utiliza tela Super AMOLED de 120 Hz, câmera principal do A57 e bateria de 5.000 mAh. Utilize o cupom SMART350 exclusivo para assinantes Prime
O Galaxy A37 (128 GB) registrou um dos menores preços históricos na Amazon. O dispositivo intermediário sai por apenas R$ 1.449 no Pix, utilizando o cupom SMART350, exclusivo para membros Prime. O valor representa um desconto agressivo de 56% poucos meses após o lançamento em março pela Samsung.
O painel Super AMOLED de 6,7 polegadas reproduz tons de cores bem fiéis e entrega resolução Full HD (2.340 X 1.080 pixels). Além disso, assegura uma taxa de atualização de 120 Hz no qual proporciona uma navegação e transições gráficas bem fluidas. Em termos de brilho, atinge pico de 1.900 nits sob luz intensa.
As câmeras mantiveram a configuração do antecessor, mas o sensor principal de 50 MP com OIS é o mesmo equipado no A57, um celular mais avançado. Na prática, a lente de 1/1.56″ entrega bons resultados para fotos de dia e a noite. O usuário ainda vai ter a disposição uma ultrawide de 8 MP para registrar paisagens e uma macro de 5 MP. A frontal de 12 MP grava vídeos em 4K assim como as traseiras.
O Galaxy A37 utiliza uma bateria de 5.000 mAh que aguenta pelo menos um dia inteiro de uso moderado a intenso sem precisar de tomada. Devido ao suporte a carregadores de 45 W, realiza um carregamento bem rápido, mas que precisa ser adquirido separadamente.
Equipado com o processador Exynos 1480 e 6 GB de RAM, um dos últimos lançamentos da Samsung dá conta de tarefas cotidianas e até recursos básicos de IA. Portanto, o Galaxy A37 é voltado para usuários que abrem mão ou que não tem o perfil de executar multitarefas, apps e jogos pesados.
Embora a construção utilize majoritariamente o plástico, a proteção Gorilla Glass Victus+ na frente e atrás, somada à certificação IP68 contra poeira e água, oferece durabilidade ao menos a algumas situações. Por fim, o celular tem compatibilidade a conexões de Wi-Fi 6, Bluetooth 5.4 e NFC para permitir compras por aproximação.
O Galaxy A37 vem com o Android 16 e tem promessa de até seis atualizações de sistema Android pela Samsung. Aproveite essa oportunidade para adquiri-lo com 128 GB de armazenamento por R$ 1.449 no Pix, com o cupom exclusivo SMART350 para assinantes Prime.

articles.title: We can't help treating AI like it's human. But should we? | TechCrunch
articles.text:
In a tan polo shirt, brown leather belt, and round bolo tie, MIT PhD student Wil Norton kind of looks like a park ranger, leading our tour group through a tropical jungle. We’re not actually on safari, though — we’re at MIT’s Computer Science & Artificial Intelligence Lab (CSAIL). But what we’re about to see is even more exotic than a cheetah or a jaguar: a pair of humanoid Unitree robots, each costing about $50,000.
(“They’ll tell you they cost $16,000,” Norton says. “That’s a lie.”)
We usually only see these robots on YouTube when they’re performing a synchronized martial arts routine, or dancing on “America’s Got Talent.” Here, they’re approachable. Even though I know it isn’t sentient, I want to be its friend.
With Norton’s permission, I approach the robot, whose nickname is Gabe. For a moment, I’m not sure how to interact with something that has a LiDAR sensor where its brain should be, but I default to treating it like a person.
“Hello, sir, it’s nice to meet you,” I say, grabbing its gloved, dexterous hand and shaking it.
I think about this interaction later — my instinctive impulse to be friendly to a robot — when I attend Dr. Sherry Turkle‘s “Artificial Intimacy” book launch at MIT Future Fest.
Turkle, who joined the faculty at MIT in 1976, has been researching the relationship between humans and computers perhaps longer than anyone, charting technology’s psychological impact on us from the first home computers to ChatGPT.
“When we are drawn into even the most primitive exchanges with a relational artifact, we believe it cares for us,” Turkle writes in the book. “And we are wired to care for it in return.”
I’m not alone in my tendency to anthropomorphize robots and large language models (LLMs) — as Turkle notes, it seems to be in our nature. One study found that about 70% of people are polite when interacting with AI, while another showed that users are more likely to say “please” or “thank you” to chatbots once a conversation has progressed past a first prompt-and-response.
“People tend to categorize whether this is the right use or wrong use, but I don’t think that is a clear boundary,” Dr. Pat Pataranutaporn, a colleague of Turkle who founded the Cyborg Psychology research group at the MIT Media Lab, told TechCrunch. “The question is, who are we becoming when we talk to [AI]?”
There’s no material consequence of my politeness toward Gabe the robot, but as LLMs infiltrate everything from Google searches to customer service interactions, it has become routine for people to interact with these seemingly sentient chatbots. We’re more vulnerable than ever to the flip side of this impulse, which is that some people can ascribe so much legitimacy to the feelings of chatbots — which are programmed to never spark conflict — that they end up favoring them over other humans.
“You can think of it like fantasy and fiction. We go to the cinema even though we know the story is completely fictional, but we want to experience a certain dimension of human experience that maybe our reality cannot give us,” Pataranutaporn said. “How do we benefit from that ability to experience other dimensions of human experience without losing it to the fantasy, where you can no longer come back to the reality?”
Pataranutaporn describes himself as a “critical optimist,” and he studies AI’s potential to contribute to human flourishing. But he’s well aware of how dangerous this technology can be in the extremes. He even served as an expert in a wrongful death lawsuit over the suicide of 14-year-old Sewell Setzer, III, whose mother sued the chatbot platform Character.AI, alleging that a chatbot modeled after a “Game of Thrones” character had encouraged her son to end his life.
“It can create a situation where people don’t feel agency in actually creating their own future — like when you say that AI will replace everyone, people ask, what are we gonna do? And these companies are not really responding ethically or responsibly,” Pataranutaporn said. “How do we have imagination while still being responsible for the impact of that imagination?”
While Turkle’s book explores the risk of turning to AI for emotional support, rather than other people, she doesn’t think that AI-human interactions are universally harmful.
She recalls a project she advised in which a student created an AI bot to help people practice for job interviews.
“My big metaphor is, stay in your lane, chatbot!” Turkle said at the event. “Coaching for a job interview? That’s a lane. I can do that … A chatbot that says to a three-year-old, ‘I’m your parent, you can talk to me, not your parents,’ is not in a lane.”
But when this technology deviates from its lane even slightly, we become vulnerable to the way it can slowly chip away at our skepticism and make us trust it. It can start with something as simple as a handshake.

articles.title: NBA legend Shaquille O’Neal teams up with NordVPN, taking over NYC to raise awareness of digital threats
articles.text:
NBA legend Shaquille O’Neal teams up with NordVPN, taking over NYC to raise awareness of digital threats
The NBA legend, alongside other pro-basketball players, came out to demonstrate the blocking power of Next Gen Antivirus in a new way
It’s pretty unusual to find yourself at a cybersecurity event playing basketball in Times Square. Add in NBA legend Shaquille O’Neal as the host, and you'd be describing the stuff of dreams.
Yet that’s what a lucky crowd got at NordVPN’s latest event on Thursday. The provider went big on online defence with its ambassador Shaq on hand to teach Americans about digital threats.
At the event, professional basketball players also challenged members of the public to slam dunk, echoing how the VPN’s next-generation antivirus intercepts and blocks malware and phishing attempts before they can even reach a user’s device.
More than shots blocked
The NBA Hall of Famer, entrepreneur, and philanthropist has been NordVPN’s official ambassador since September. The collaboration focuses on raising awareness of digital threats while also boosting NordVPN’s marketing efforts as the company transitions from a simple VPN to a comprehensive, all-in-one security suite.
A key part of this is NordVPN's 'Next Gen Antivirus', which scans 12 million unique URLs daily and blocks an average of 130,000 malicious pages. It blocked nearly 5 million malware attempts in the US in the first months of 2026, NordVPN says.
At the event, the VPN drew parallels with sport and digital security, using pro-basketball players to showcase what real defence in action means and presenting malicious activity as slam dunks on a court.
The audience was invited to try to score against experienced players, only to have professionals with years of experience in the field block their attempts, much like how NordVPN defends against digital risks.
But why?
The poetic parallels are timely, as NordVPN recently warned that Americans are suffering from a delulu-clash over their cybersecurity knowledge.
Frighteningly, recent research by NordVPN found that 71 per cent of respondents believe that common sense is simply enough to navigate digital threats.
What’s more, almost three-quarters of respondents believe they are perfectly capable of spotting online scams in spite of evidence to the contrary.
Findings revealed that 74 per cent of Americans were unable to spot a fake URL and 82 per cent failed to recognise a fake CAPTCHA, while less than half correctly identified a phishing email disguised as a job recruitment message.
More than half – 51 per cent – reuse the same password or similar passwords across different accounts. Unsurprisingly, it is the users who are most confident in their own abilities who tend to do this, says NordVPN.
It is therefore even less surprising that 73 per cent of Americans have already fallen victim to a scam recently, with nearly a quarter having suffered or being at risk of suffering a financial loss.
Shaq’s profile arguably makes the case better than any cyber-security expert: “These scammers are getting smarter, and sometimes all it takes is one click or sharing one piece of information. You don’t have to be a cybersecurity expert. You just have to stay alert, make smart choices, and use the right tools to protect yourself.”

articles.title: PC shipments tumble over 20% in 3Q26 as chip shortages bite — top three PC vendors ship 11.6 million fewer units year-over-year
articles.text:
PC shipments tumble over 20% in 3Q26 as chip shortages bite — top three PC vendors ship 11.6 million fewer units year-over-year
The memory chip shortage is hitting the PC market hard.
PC shipments globally have dropped by 20.1% year-over-year in the third quarter of 2026, a decline of 15.8 million units. According to research firm IDC Global, this marks a steeper decline compared to the 3.8% year-over-year decrease that the market experienced last quarter. It’s also down 9.1% from the second quarter of this year. Many research firms have been warning about this since late last year, with IDC warning that the PC market could shrink up to 9%, with the budget sector being hit the hardest. Some experts estimate that the situation isn’t expected to improve until 2029, with Tom’s Hardware readers saying that they won’t upgrade their systems in the next two years.
These price increases have been directly caused by the boom in AI data centers, with hyperscalers pouring massive amounts of money into the crucial HBM needed to support AI GPUs. This has led to memory manufacturers pivoting toward this technology, leaving less production capacity for consumer memory. One good example of this is Micron, which killed the Crucial RAM and SSD brand in late 2025 so that it can focus on data center production. As PC makers fight for a shrinking supply of memory chips, we saw memory prices climb by as much as 500%, with 128GB of DDR5 now costing as much as $3,399.
Manufacturers didn’t sit idly by and let the market take its course, though. Many of them stocked up on inventory in the second quarter of 2026 to try and head off the projected higher prices caused by the shortage, which directly led to the reduced shipments being reported. “What we’re seeing is the result of the strong first half pull-in. Vendors and channels loaded up on inventory early in the year to get ahead of price hikes, and that has thrown off the usual seasonality, where Q3 is typically larger than Q2,” said IDC consumer devices research director Jitesh Ubrani. “Channels are now worried about carrying too much inventory into a market where high prices are suppressing demand. That could translate into promotions and some short-term relief for consumers, but we don’t expect pricing anywhere near what it was a year ago. Prices will remain elevated. With macro conditions worsening, the risk is that the outlook for the next few quarters gets worse before it gets better.”
The top three PC vendors suffered the most, with Lenovo shedding 22.6%, HP shipping 30.9% fewer units, and Dell shipments contracting by 25%. On the other hand, Apple’s shipments shrank by 11.3%, while Asus’s numbers fell by 8.6%, with the rest of the market shipping 14% less year-over-year. Despite being hit the hardest, Lenovo, HP, and Dell still maintained their lead at 23.8%, 16.5%, and 12.1% market share, respectively.
Even though other industry leaders, including Micron, say that the situation will not improve for the next few years, Acer CEO Jason Chen went against the grain and said that these fears are just being hyped to protect the margins of memory chip makers. He estimated that PC prices will decline by the latter half of 2027 as Chinese memory chip capacity comes online, with only high-end parts like LPDDR5X-9600 and niche CPUs such as the Nvidia N1 and N1X remaining in short supply.

- cknobman The high prices are the biggest part of the equation.
But I suspect its also the fact that modern computing has been fast enough to meet the demands of most users for half a decade now.
At my job I still do my software engineering on a 4 year old Intel 13th gen platform. We dont get upgrades because even if it is not "the fastest" the platform is still more than adequate to get the job done.
Same for my gaming PC. Still running an AMD 5600 from years ago and it is more than adequate to play all the games I play.
Why pay extreme prices for hardware you dont really "need"? Reply

Connecting Chiplets Isn’t Enough – Solving the Data Movement Challenge in Multi-Die Systems
As SoCs evolve into multi-die systems, getting data across a die-to-die interface is only part of the challenge. Architects must also preserve traffic behavior, bandwidth efficiency and quality of service as communication moves across physical chip boundaries.
Join this 30-minute BitCast as our expert explores how extending NoC connectivity across die boundaries enables engineering teams to scale from monolithic SoCs to multi-die architectures without reinventing the way data moves through the system.
Attendees will gain insight into:
Why AI is driving the move to multi-die – Practical die-size limitations, heterogeneous compute, process-node optimization and increasing system complexity
What changes when the SoC crosses a die boundary – The audience understands die-to-die connectivity; the less obvious issue is what happens to data movement, traffic management and QoS
Why die-to-die connectivity alone isn’t enough – Getting bits between chiplets is different from maintaining the behavior and design intent of the overall system
Extending the NoC across chip boundaries – Explain the concept of preserving NoC capabilities across D2D links rather than making every chiplet boundary a separate integration problem
Coherent vs. non-coherent multi-die architectures – Explain when each is needed and naturally introduce FlexGen Multi-Die and Ncore Multi-Die
What architects should consider before partitioning a design – End with practical guidance: traffic, bandwidth, QoS, coherence, reuse, integration, security and ecosystem interoperability

articles.title: U.S. Manufacturing Grows as Backlogs Surge in September - EE Times
articles.text:
Economic activity in the U.S. manufacturing sector expanded in September for the ninth consecutive month, propelled by accelerating new orders and an expanding accumulation of unfilled factory backlogs. The sustained industrial performance helped buffer the broader economy against escalating trade friction and rising global commodity prices.
The Institute for Supply Management reported that its Manufacturing Purchasing Managers’ Index registered 54.5% in September, edging down just 0.1 percentage point from August’s reading of 54.6%. The reading marks nine straight months of industrial expansion following a 10-month contraction period and signals that the broader U.S. economy grew for a 23rd consecutive month. In ISM’s economic modeling, a PMI reading of 54.5% corresponds to a 2.4% annualized increase in real gross domestic product.
“In September, U.S. manufacturing activity remained in expansion territory,” said Susan Spence, chair of the ISM Manufacturing Business Survey Committee. “Of the five subindexes that make up the PMI, only New Orders and Employment grew faster than the previous month.”
New orders and factory backlogs
A fresh wave of demand reinforced factory output during the month, with the New Orders Index expanding for the ninth consecutive month to 55.3%, a 1.6 percentage point increase from August’s 53.7%. Factory output also remained robust: The Production Index registered 56.7%, marking its 11th consecutive month of growth, though slowing 1.6 percentage points from August’s 58.3%.
With new demand outstripping output capacity in several high-tech categories, order backlogs expanded at a faster rate. The Backlog of Orders Index jumped 4.6 percentage points to 56.4% in September, up from 51.8% in August, led by gains in computer and electronic products as well as fabricated metals.
Five of the nation’s six largest manufacturing industries—Computer & Electronic Products, Chemical Products, Transportation Equipment, Food, Beverage & Tobacco Products, and Machinery—reported higher new orders during the month.
ISM survey respondents highlighted burgeoning demand in semiconductor and defense supply chains, even as cross-border trade friction disrupted operations. “Coupled with supply chain lead times and pricing pressures, the factory backlog has nearly doubled,” noted an executive in the machinery sector. “Canada tariffs have impacted cross-border costs and left our supply chain team scrambling—those supply chains took years to develop and nurture—hurting the very lead times government buyers are concerned about.”
An executive in the computer and electronic products industry added that while manufacturing activity remains stable, “the U.S. tariff schedule is providing challenges,” citing difficulties in finding alternate supply sources outside China, local pushback on domestic data center construction, and persistent component shortages.
Factory hiring increased due to labor and material shortages
To keep pace with rising backlogs, industrial employers expanded payrolls at a faster rate. The ISM Employment Index rose 1.5 percentage points to 52.7% in September, compared with 51.2% in August, representing a third consecutive month of growth in manufacturing employment.
Survey panelists favored hiring over headcount reductions by a 1.5-to-1 ratio. Eight manufacturing industries reported expanding employment in September, led by Electrical Equipment, Appliances & Components, Primary Metals, and Wood Products. Among the nation’s six largest manufacturing sectors, Computer & Electronic Products and Transportation Equipment posted employment gains.
However, worker shortages and raw material bottlenecks continue to restrain factory output. “Our biggest challenge continues to be a severe shortage of workers, limiting our production output to meet demand,” said an executive in the fabricated metal products sector. “The second challenge is general availability of steel; the market is getting worse, and more production delays are expected as we gap out of needed material.”
Canada tariffs and Middle East war drive material costs higher
Despite ongoing output gains, factory managers face steep operational hurdles from soaring raw material prices, trade policy volatility, and geopolitical conflict. The Prices Index jumped 6.8 percentage points in September to 77.9%, up from 71.1% in August, reaching a level close to the 78.3% recorded in March at the start of the Iran war. The index indicates that raw material prices increased for the 24th consecutive month, with 58.6% of survey respondents reporting higher prices compared to 46.2% in August.
All six of the largest manufacturing sectors reported paying higher prices for raw materials in September. “The Prices Index reading is still being driven by (1) increases in steel and aluminum prices that impact the entire value chain, (2) tariffs applied to many imported goods and (3) increases in petroleum-based products as a result of the Middle East conflict,” Spence said.
Supply chain logistics remained under strain, with the Supplier Deliveries Index registering 59.0%. While down 0.3 percentage point from August’s 59.3%, the reading indicates slower delivery performance for the 10th consecutive month.
Survey comments reflected growing frustration over trade tariffs and foreign policy disruptions. “Every month, we are faced with new headwinds created by this administration,” said an executive in the transportation equipment industry. “This month, it is the trade war with Canada, which every day is getting worse—causing prices to go up and uncertainty that creates massive disruption. Buying continues to get pushed out indefinitely as customers don’t want to spend on capital expenditures until there is more certainty of costs and demand.”
An executive in the electrical equipment and appliances sector similarly noted that raw metal costs remain challenging due to the “uncertain nature of tariffs being on and off again,” adding that new tariffs against Canada have “drastically increased costs for capital expenses as well as assemblies.” Meanwhile, a chemical products manager cautioned that recent performance was driven by temporary market effects, including geopolitical uncertainties and customers bringing forward purchases, rather than a sustained structural recovery.
Manufacturing growth overshadowed by uncertainty
The industrial expansion remained broad-based across the manufacturing sector, with 12 of 18 industries reporting overall growth in September. Growth was led by Electrical Equipment, Appliances & Components, Nonmetallic Mineral Products, Primary Metals, Plastics & Rubber Products, and Computer & Electronic Products. Five of the six largest manufacturing industries expanded, while only two industries—Printing & Related Support Activities and Textile Mills—reported overall contraction.
Indicating potential strength for future factory output, the Customers’ Inventories Index decreased 1.2 percentage points to 41.6% in September, remaining in “too low” territory for the 24th consecutive month. “A ‘too low’ status for the Customers’ Inventories Index is usually considered positive for future production,” Spence noted.
Raw materials inventories at factories contracted, with the Inventories Index falling 2.0 percentage points to 48.6%. Furthermore, overall sentiment among supply executives leaned negative. Forty percent of comments were positive and 60% negative, a 1-to-1.6 positive-to-negative ratio. Among negative comments, pricing volatility was cited in 46%, tariffs in 34%, the Iran war in 30%, and increasing lead times in 21%.
Despite these headwinds, overall manufacturing weakness remained localized: ISM said only 2% of manufacturing GDP contracted in September, down sharply from 22% in August. The 2% of manufacturing GDP in strong contraction—defined as a composite PMI of 45% or lower—remained unchanged from August.

articles.title: 6 African startups share $400k funding at FINCA Ventures Prize Competition - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
Six African startups have been selected as winners of the 2026 FINCA Ventures Prize Competition, receiving a combined US$400,000 in catalytic funding to accelerate their impact in key resilience sectors.
The FINCA Ventures Prize Competition, a flagship initiative of FINCA’s impact investing arm, spotlights the depth and potential of entrepreneurial talent developing practical, scalable responses to some of the continent’s most pressing challenges.
Now in its third year, the FINCA Ventures Prize Competition drew more than 700 applications in two categories – fintech for financial inclusion, and sustainable agriculture and food systems. Six finalists were selected to pitch their ventures to a panel of distinguished judges on October 6 in San Francisco at an event hosted by Cisco.
First-place winners in each category — Kenyan startups VunaPay and Kumbatia Seafood – each received a US$100,000 grant.
Second-place winners, taking home US$60,000 each, were Kenya’s nesti and Zimbabwe’s eAgro, while third place, and US$40,000 each, went to Rwandan/Zimbabwean venture ChatCash and Kenya’s Pollen Patrollers.
“Africa’s future will be shaped by entrepreneurs who see opportunity where others see market failure,” said FINCA Global CEO Andrée Simon. “One of the most important ways we can support these founders is by backing them early and helping them build the credibility and traction to attract additional investment and achieve meaningful scale.”

articles.title: Germany arrests alleged core Qilin ransomware member after extradition
articles.text:
Germany has arrested a Russian national suspected of being a leading member of the Qilin ransomware group following extradition from Japan earlier this month.
Japan has confirmed the extradition to Germany, with the National Police Agency saying that the suspect was detained after arriving in the country as a tourist.
“When a Russian national for whom Germany had obtained an arrest warrant in connection with a ransomware incident in Germany arrived in Japan, the Japanese Ministry of Justice, the Tokyo High Public Prosecutors Office, and Germany worked together to detain the suspect under the Extradition Law for Fugitives by obtaining a provisional detention warrant, and then facilitated the extradition,” [machine translated] reads the press release.
Earlier this week, Japanese media reported the arrest based on internal sources, but authorities in the country have now officially confirmed the action.
Qilin is a notorious ransomware-as-a-service (RaaS) operation that emerged in August 2022 under the name Agenda, and deployed typical double-extortion attacks, where data is stolen before being encrypted.
The operation became one of the most active ransomware threats worldwide. By more recent statistics, the group targeted more than 2,350 known organizations across 62 countries.
Among the victims are Japanese automaker Nissan, Japanese brewery Asahi, U.S. newspaper publisher Lee Enterprises, and Australia’s Court Services Victoria.
The attack on Asahi, Japan’s largest beer producer, was particularly damaging, disrupting operations for an extended period and exposing sensitive details about 1.5 million people.
More recently, the threat group hit the U.S. Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) and was also linked to the exploitation of Check Point VPN zero-days and Palo Alto VPN n-day flaws.
According to media publications, Japan detained the alleged Qilin leading member in May at a hotel in Osaka. Despite this, the gang continued to be a major player on the ransomware stage. Since June, the group has listed more than 450 victims on its data leak site.

articles.title: BMW M3 électrique : un style bestial conservé, mais une douche froide sur la fiche technique ?
articles.text:
Première voiture électrique de BMW Motorsport, la future M3 sera officiellement dévoilée en 2027. Bonne nouvelle : le concept M Concept Neue Klasse, qui annonçait un engin sensationnel, prêtera nombre d’éléments au modèle de série, présenté pour la première fois sous un épais camouflage. Ses ailes bodybuildées feront ainsi leur chemin en production pour permettre à la M3 de se distinguer de la traditionnelle i3.
La calandre spécifique subsistera, au même titre que les originaux feux « Track Lights » flanqués aux extrémités des pare-chocs avant et arrière. Les optiques jaunes seront aussi reconduites pour singer les modèles courants en compétition. Malin pour distinguer la M3 de très loin. De près, on pourra surtout se pencher sur le capot présentant une architecture inédite au service de l’aérodynamisme.
Quand la dure réalité de la production rattrape le design
Bien entendu, les plus grosses folies du concept n’ont pas pu passer l’exigeant cahier des charges. Les impressionnantes jantes de l’étude de style sont remplacées par des modèles plus modestes. Les flancs extrêmement creusés du prototype semblent aussi être de l’histoire ancienne. Quant aux rétroviseurs ultra effilés, ils ne pourront pas non plus passer le cap de la production. Dommage, car ils apportaient pourtant un vent de fraîcheur bienvenu.
Même destin pour les poignées de portes logées à la base des vitres laissant place à des modèles semi-affleurants identiques à ceux de l’i3. La poupe aussi, délaissera son méga diffuseur rasant le sol pour quelque chose de plus mesuré. Possiblement moins bluffant, mais certainement plus pratique au quotidien. Pas de quoi être véritablement déçu… sauf à regarder la fiche technique, peut-être ?
Performances ou autonomie : le choix radical de BMW
BMW avait annoncé la couleur avec quatre électromoteurs répartis sur les quatre roues, avec la possibilité de basculer entièrement en propulsion pour partir en glisse. Quatre machines électriques pour quatre fois plus de fun ? C’est en tout cas vers quoi convergeaient les rumeurs initiales, qui suggéraient une puissance cumulée dépassant les 1 000 ch. Les dernières nouvelles annoncent finalement un ensemble sous les 800 ch.
Toujours écrasant, mais moins délirant, le but étant principalement de moduler indépendamment le couple sur chaque roue. Et contrairement à l’i3 pouvant taper sans peine les 900 km d’autonomie, la future M3, elle, privilégiera les performances au rayon d’action. Même si la batterie pourrait excéder les 100 kWh, son autonomie sera bien inférieure. Le but est surtout d’obtenir une décharge rapide de l’énergie vers les électromoteurs.
Une version thermique en embuscade pour rassurer les puristes
À bord, l’allemande deviendra aussi plus vivable avec cinq places au lieu de quatre. Aussi incroyables soient-ils, les sièges baquets du concept pourraient être proposés en option sur le modèle de série. La planche de bord, elle, n’a rien d’un délire de designer et sera quasiment identique à celle de la version définitive. Présentée l’année prochaine, la nouvelle M3 électrique sera rapidement rejointe par sa sœur à essence équipée d’un six-cylindres en ligne.

articles.title: La única rotonda submarina del mundo está 70 metros bajo el nivel del mar y es una obra de arte que une tres túneles
articles.text:
Hace no mucho, Tórshavn y Runavík estaban separadas por más de 50 kilómetros de carretera aunque, en línea recta, estaban prácticamente al lado. El mismo problema tenían los vecinos de Strendur que querían llegar hasta la primera de estas dos ciudades.
Supongo que vivir en un lugar idílico como cualquiera de estas tres ciudades de las Islas Feroe tienen sus pequeños inconvenientes.
Y es que Runavík y Strendur se encuentran las dos en Eysturoy, una de las islas del archipiélago. Sus vecinos prácticamente pueden saludarse pero una enorme lengua de agua que se adentra algunos kilómetros tierra adentro parte la isla en dos, lo que obliga a dar un rodeo de decenas de kilómetros para desplazarse entre ellas.
Tórshavn está un poco más lejos. No mucho, pero sí lo suficiente para ser una de las ciudades de Streymoy, la isla que se sitúa justo a su lado y que, efectivamente, tiene conexión por coche con Eysturoy la isla anterior. El problema, como puedes imaginar, ese el mismo de antes: una fina lengua de agua separa ciudades que se encuentran a muy poca distancia y obliga a dar un enorme rodeo.
Hasta que en el año 2020 se inauguró el Eysturoyartunnilin.
Una rotonda submarina impresionante
La idea del Eysturoyartunnilin nació unos años antes. Aunque teniendo en cuenta la obra de ingeniería que supuso y lo que tardamos en España en sacar los proyectos adelante, desde luego da envidia la velocidad con la que se trabajó para sacar el proyecto adelante.
A principios de los años 2000, las Islas Feroe empezaron a poner remedio a sus problemas de movilidad tomando el camino de en medio. Literalmente. Porque cansados de dar rodeos para salvar las lenguas de agua y tirar puentes en sus costas más cercanas, lo que se optó fue por la construcción de túneles submarinos. Así, en esos primeros años vieron la luz dos proyectos: el Vágatunnilin y el Norðoyatunnilin.
Con las ventajas materializadas de estas dos construcciones se empezó a pensar que era buena idea seguir por el mismo camino. Así, en 2006 se creó la empresa encargada de sacar adelante el que se conocería como Eysturoyartunnilin. El proyecto sufrió la crisis del 2008, quedando en suspenso durante algún tiempo pero se retomó durante la década siguiente.
Con algunas correcciones, en el año 2017 comenzaron las excavaciones a uno y otro lado de los extremos del túnel. Tres años después, el Eysturoyartunnilin estaba terminado. La solución de movilidad implicaba que ahora el paso entre Tórshavn y Runavík o Strendur se había acortado significativamente. La distancia, que anteriormente era de más de 50 kilómetros, se había acortado a solo 11,24 kilómetros. El tiempo de viaje se había reducido de más de una hora a apenas 16 minutos.
Pero lo más llamativo de todo el proyecto no está en construir un túnel bajo el fondo del mar. Las Islas Feroe ya contaba con túneles similares, como decíamos, y en los países nórdicos se han popularizado en las últimas décadas. Uno de los más ambiciosos quiere que los barcos pasen por sus cavidades.
Lo más interesante es la solución planteada para dividir el tráfico entre las tres ciudades. En lugar de crear tres túneles con conexiones individuales entre ciudades, se optó por construir una rotonda submarina. Es, por el momento, la única en el mundo.
En BBC tienes un reportaje muy interesante en el que se explica cómo se sacó adelante el proyecto (la infraestructura más cara de la historia en las Islas Feroe) y qué dificultades encontraron. En este artículo puedes leer que la zona más crítica fue la de la rotonda donde las voladuras de la roca tuvieron que ser más pequeñas para controlar mejor el espacio que había que crear. La zona central sirve para descargar la presión que ejerce el fiordo bajo la que se encuentra dicha rotonda.
Y es que ésta se encuentra a 72 metros bajo el nivel del mar. El túnel llega a alcanzar una profundidad de 189 metros y no es ni mucho menos el más profundo del mundo pero, evidentemente, tiene la única rotonda que se encuentra bajo el agua.
En la construcción se aprovechó, además, para que la propia rotonda sirviera como medio de expresión. Se encargó al artista Tróndur Patursson que diera rienda suelta a su ingenio y creó una superficie de placas metálicas de 80 metros donde destaca el juego de luces y la impresión de figuras humanas, recreando una de las danzas tradicionales del lugar. El juego de luz e impresión sobre las placas crea el efecto que da el sobrenombre a esta obra de "rotonda medusa". Además, las placas metálicas irán cambiando de color al oxidarse creando la sensación de que la obra tiene vida propia.
Más allá de haberse convertido en una atracción turística por sí misma, como señalan en Híbridos y Eléctricos, el túnel se ha convertido en un paso utilizado por casi 6.500 vehículos a diario que pagan religiosamente el peaje para cruzar los poco más de 11 kilómetros que separan bajo el agua estas ciudades. Sólo en 2025 cruzaron por él 2,36 millones de vehículos.

articles.title: 36 milliards de dollars envolés en quelques heures : Elon Musk n'est plus trillionnaire
articles.text:
36 milliards de dollars envolés en quelques heures : Elon Musk n'est plus trillionnaire
Lundi, il redevenait le seul trillionnaire de la planète. Jeudi 8 octobre, sa fortune fondait de 36,4 milliards de dollars avant même la clôture de Wall Street. À l'origine de la glissade : un emprunt colossal que SpaceX préparerait pour s'offrir des puces Nvidia, et que les investisseurs digèrent mal.
Elon Musk a perdu son rang de trillionnaire. Ce jeudi 8 octobre, en milieu de séance à New York, Forbes évaluait sa fortune à 991,6 milliards de dollars, soit 36,4 milliards de moins que la veille. L'action SpaceX cédait environ 3,5 % et celle de Tesla plus de 2 %. Le seuil des 1 000 milliards, il l'avait retrouvé lundi seulement, quatre mois après l'avoir franchi une première fois en juin, lors de l'entrée en Bourse de SpaceX.
Pourquoi l'action SpaceX décroche : 40 milliards de dollars de dette pour des puces Nvidia
Mardi 6 octobre, le Financial Times révélait que SpaceX cherche à lever 40 milliards de dollars pour financer sa commande de puces Nvidia. Le montage comprendrait 30 milliards d'obligations notées "investment grade" et 10 milliards de prêts bancaires. Le gestionnaire d'actifs Apollo Global Management piloterait l'opération, Pimco figurant parmi les prêteurs en discussion. Le bouclage est attendu en 2027 et les négociations, encore préliminaires, peuvent échouer.
Ces puces alimentent un commerce devenu central pour le groupe : la location de puissance de calcul. Depuis le rachat de xAI, SpaceX loue ses centres de données à Google et à Anthropic, deux contrats qui dépassent ensemble 70 milliards de dollars d'ici à 2029. Ses ambitions débordent même l'atmosphère : Elon Musk veut loger un million de satellites IA en orbite, et Google envoie un data center IA dans l'espace avec SpaceX.
La Bourse a réagi sans délai. Mercredi matin, le titre perdait 2 % et Musk 21 milliards. Jeudi a prolongé la purge.
Le contraste avec le début de semaine est saisissant. Lundi, l'action bondissait de plus de 5 %, portée par une note de Morgan Stanley la jugeant "cheap", bon marché, et par la première mise en orbite du Starship la semaine précédente. La fusée géante est d'ailleurs prête pour un double lancement dès le 19 octobre.
Fortune d'Elon Musk : un patrimoine suspendu à deux actions
Forbes lui attribue 38 % de SpaceX et près de 11 % de Tesla. Cette concentration extrême transforme chaque séance en montagnes russes. Sacré trillionnaire le 12 juin, il perdait le titre quelques jours plus tard, à 962 milliards, quand SpaceX lâchait 31 %. En juillet, l'action ayant fondu de moitié depuis son sommet, sa fortune glissait sous les 700 milliards.
Puis le vent a tourné. Vendredi 2 octobre, les livraisons trimestrielles de Tesla, supérieures aux attentes, et le rebond de SpaceX lui rapportaient 61 milliards en une journée.
Il reste, de très loin, l'homme le plus riche du monde : Jeff Bezos, deuxième du classement en temps réel de Forbes, pèse 374,7 milliards. Et il lui manque 8,4 milliards pour repasser la barre, soit moins de 1 % de ses avoirs. Une séance clémente y suffirait.
