articles.title: How Developers Can Add Personalized BaZi Readings to Astrology and Wellness Apps - Tech Guide
articles.text:
BaZi is moving from printed charts and private consultations into mobile astrology and wellness products. A BaZi calculator API lets developers generate the underlying chart without rebuilding every calendar rule, while a BaZi API can deliver the result to a phone, web app, or content platform in a structured format.
Also called the Four Pillars of Destiny, BaZi uses a person’s birth year, month, day, and hour to create an eight-character chart. Apps often place it beside Western natal charts, journaling, meditation, or habit tracking. The attraction is depth. Instead of a single zodiac sign, users receive a layered model of elements, timing cycles, and relationships between chart components. Frame this as a traditional interpretive practice, not medical evidence. When the product makes that boundary clear, BaZi can support reflection without making unsupported health claims.
Understanding the Core Components of BaZi
A BaZi engine starts with four pillars: year, month, day, and hour. Each pillar combines one Heavenly Stem with one Earthly Branch, producing the eight characters behind the Chinese name BaZi. The Hong Kong Observatory lists 10 Heavenly Stems and 12 Earthly Branches. Their compatible pairings form a 60-step sexagenary cycle, because the two sequences realign after 60 combinations. Each stem and branch maps to yin or yang and to one of five elements: Wood, Fire, Earth, Metal, or Water. The Day Stem is commonly treated as the Day Master, a reference point for interpreting the rest of the chart. Software must calculate the chart first, then interpret it. If those layers are mixed, content rules become hard to test and calendar errors can quietly change a reading.
How BaZi API Logic Connects Calendar Data and Interpretation
The calculation layer should return stable facts: pillar identifiers, stems, branches, hidden stems, element mappings, polarity, and calendar boundaries. A separate interpretation layer can then apply a chosen school or editorial model. This distinction matters because BaZi isn’t a single universal scoring formula. Practitioners may weigh season, roots, combinations, clashes, and transformations differently. Developers should therefore record the calculation method and content version with each saved chart. The API response can include both raw fields and display-ready labels, but the raw values must remain available for audits. It also helps to return confidence or rule notes when a birth time is missing, a location is approximate, or a chart falls close to a solar-term boundary.
Technical Architecture for Implementing BaZi Engines
A reliable engine needs a calendar service, geolocation and time-zone handling, a chart calculator, an interpretation rules layer, and a content delivery layer. These parts should be testable on their own. Fixed reference charts help regression tests, especially around year changes, solar terms, midnight boundaries, and daylight-saving transitions.
Solar Calendar Conversion and Timezone Normalization
Birth input usually arrives as a Gregorian date, local clock time, and place. The server first resolves the historical time-zone offset for that location. Current offsets are not enough because governments have changed time-zone and daylight-saving rules. Next, the calculator determines the relevant solar-term boundaries. BaZi month pillars follow solar divisions rather than ordinary Gregorian months, and many implementations use Li Chun, or Start of Spring, when assigning the astrological year. UNESCO recognizes the Twenty-Four Solar Terms as a knowledge system based on observation of the sun’s annual motion. That means the engine must store or compute 24 precise transitions for each year. Some schools also adjust clock time to true solar time using longitude and the equation of time. Because methods differ, the app should state its convention and show the normalized time used for the chart.
Algorithmic Element Analysis and Day Master Scoring
After the pillars are set, the engine maps visible and hidden components to the Five Elements. A basic count is easy, but a useful analysis usually needs weights. Season can strengthen one element and weaken another. Roots in the branches may support the Day Master, while producing, controlling, or draining relationships change the interpretation. Developers should avoid presenting the result as an objective biometric score. Element percentages are model outputs, not measured properties of a person. The scoring rules should be deterministic, versioned, and explainable. An online bazi calculator api might return raw element totals, normalized percentages, Day Master strength bands, and the rules that contributed to each result. Unit tests should cover balanced charts, dominant elements, missing elements, transformations, and threshold cases where a small weighting change alters the category.
Dynamic Daily Readings and Luck Pillar Engine
Long-term readings add another time layer. Luck Pillars are commonly represented as 10-year cycles, but their starting age and direction depend on the calculation convention. The engine must derive those values consistently and keep them separate from the natal chart. Daily content then compares the active year, month, and day stem-branch pairs with the stored pillars. Since the sexagenary sequence repeats every 60 steps, date indexing can be efficient, but boundary tests remain essential. An api bazi calculator JSON response can package the natal chart, active Luck Pillar, current solar term, interactions, and content keys in one object. The client should request only the needed period rather than downloading years of readings. Caching daily results by chart version, time zone, and date reduces repeated work while keeping notifications aligned with the user’s local day.
Key Features and UX Best Practices for BaZi App Integration
BaZi contains dense symbolic data, so the interface should reveal it in stages. Start with a plain summary, then let users open the pillars, elements, and timing details. Keep traditional terms available, but explain them in ordinary language. Four product choices make the result easier to use:
- Element balance visualizations. Show the Five Elements with restrained color, clear labels, and accessible patterns. Percentages should state which scoring model produced them.
- Personalized daily guidance. Translate interactions into optional prompts for planning or reflection. Avoid prescribing food, exercise, treatment, or mental-health action as if the chart were clinical evidence.
- Relationship and compatibility tools. Compare charts only with consent, explain how the score is constructed, and avoid deterministic claims about whether a relationship will succeed.
- Notifications for calendar shifts. Allow users to choose solar-term, monthly, or daily alerts. Frequency controls and quiet hours are more useful than manufactured urgency.
Data Privacy Localization and Content Strategy
Birth date, exact time, and birthplace can identify or profile a person when combined with account data. Products serving people in the European Union should therefore treat these inputs as personal data and apply GDPR principles such as purpose limitation, data minimization, accuracy, storage limits, and security. Collect only what the selected calculation requires. Encrypt records in transit and at rest, restrict staff access, define retention periods, and give users practical export and deletion controls. Third-party processors should receive the minimum fields needed. Localization needs similar care. A Bazi API JSON schema should separate stable identifiers from translated display names so language changes don’t alter calculations. Editors should explain terms such as Day Master, Luck Pillar, clash, and combination without flattening the tradition into generic wellness copy. Local experts can review terminology, tone, and culturally sensitive claims.
Conclusion
Personalized BaZi can give astrology and wellness apps a deeper structure than a short daily horoscope. The value comes from combining accurate calendar conversion, transparent chart logic, modular interpretation content, and an interface that does not overwhelm the user. Teams should test solar boundaries, historical time zones, the 60-step stem-branch cycle, and the rules behind Day Master scoring. They should also state where traditions differ. Privacy matters as much because birth details can be identifying, especially when stored with location and profile information. Good localization keeps the system understandable without erasing its Chinese context. And responsible wellness framing treats readings as prompts for reflection rather than diagnosis or guaranteed prediction. With those foundations in place, developers can add daily content, compatibility tools, and long-term timing views without turning the product into a black box. That is the practical role of a bazi api: consistent calculation, controlled content, and a clearer experience from input to reading.

articles.title: Man admits to running network of 15,000 money mules for cybercriminals
articles.text:
A Ukrainian-Russian dual citizen has pleaded guilty to running a massive money laundering operation that laundered millions for cybercriminals worldwide.
42-year-old Oleg Korniev was one of the leaders of Your Mule Cashout (YMCO), a criminal organization that has operated since September 2007 and used more than 15,000 money mules from the United States.
Four other individuals who were involved with YMCO were arrested overseas more than a decade ago, extradited to the Western District of North Carolina, and pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit money laundering. They received prison sentences ranging from 37 to 63 months and were also ordered to each pay more than $9.1 million in restitution to U.S. victims.
Korniev managed, hired, and fired YMCO employees; rewarded or punished them based on performance; and helped develop policies and procedures for the money laundering operation.
According to court documents, YMCO recruited U.S. residents as money mules through spam emails from fake companies, with each mule going through what appeared to be a legitimate hiring process and being told they would process payments for legitimate businesses.
Cybercriminals sent stolen money to the mules' bank accounts, and the mules allegedly wired the illicit funds through Western Union and MoneyGram to "cash-out contractors" in Moldova, Ukraine, Russia, or Latvia.
YMCO also allegedly ran similar schemes in Germany, Italy, the United Kingdom, and Australia, processing more than $10 million stolen by cybercrime gangs from over 750 U.S. bank accounts at more than 35 banks.
"Money mules play crucial roles in cybercrime, so the Justice Department pursues mules and their recruiters wherever they operate and however long it takes," said Assistant Attorney General A. Tysen Duva.
On Thursday, Korniev pleaded guilty to money laundering, aggravated identity theft, conspiracy to commit money laundering, conspiracy to commit computer fraud, and conspiracy to commit access device theft.
Korniev now faces a minimum penalty of two years in prison and a maximum penalty of 50 years after admitting that the money laundering operation he ran with multiple accomplices was behind over $14.7 million in actual and intended losses to confirmed victims.
He also confirmed that he laundered at least $7 million of the $9.7 million received from cybercriminals.
Five years ago, Europol also announced that law enforcement authorities from 27 countries arrested 1,803 money mules out of 18,351 identified as part of an international money-laundering crackdown operation codenamed EMMA (European Money Mule Action).
Money mules play a vital role in online fraud and often sign up out of desperation, or fraudsters force them into this role by threatening them.
"The organized crime groups do this (recruit mules) by preying on groups such as students, immigrants, and those in economic distress, offering easy money through legitimate-looking job adverts and social media posts," Europol warned at the time.
"Ignorance is not an excuse when it comes to the law and money muling; they are breaking the law by laundering the illicit proceeds of crime."

articles.title: SpaceX s'attaque frontalement aux opérateurs mobiles en rachetant pour 8 milliards de dollars de fréquences
articles.text:
Les marchés américains n’ont pas tardé à réagir à cette manœuvre menée par l’entreprise d’Elon Musk. En décrochant de précieux sésames hertziens auprès du fonds d’investissement Grain Management, SpaceX s’arme pour contourner les antennes-relais terrestres. Derrière cette transaction colossale, on retrouve la promesse d’une connexion directe entre les satellites et les smartphones qui prend forme, au grand dam des opérateurs en place.
Le pari des basses fréquences pour s’affranchir des obstacles
L’utilisation de bandes basses change techniquement beaucoup de choses pour un réseau satellitaire. Contrairement aux fréquences intermédiaires déjà exploitées par la constellation Starlink, ces ondes possèdent la capacité physique de parcourir de longues distances tout en traversant sans encombre les obstacles (murs, arbres, etc.). Les utilisateurs n’auront donc pas besoin de s’équiper de téléphones spécifiques, puisque la quasi-totalité des appareils du marché américain gèrent déjà la bande des 800 MHz.
 We announced an agreement to acquire a nationwide low-band spectrum license portfolio that will pave the way for @Starlink to become a major mobile carrier in the US.
With this new spectrum and our Gen2 constellation, Starlink Mobile can ensure Americans have access to high-speed mobile broadband no matter where they are → https://t.co/1Uaf48v5pm
— SpaceX (@SpaceX) October 8, 2026
Cette brique technique supplémentaire vient compléter l’approbation récente par la FCC (la Commission Fédérale des Communications aux États-Unis) de la demande concernant la seconde génération de satellites Starlink. Quinze mille nouveaux satellites, optimisés pour les fréquences de 2 GHz et positionnés en orbite terrestre basse, viendront alimenter un service. Du côté de la concurrence, les réactions ne se font pas attendre, les actions de T-Mobile, Verizon et AT&T ayant chuté d’environ 6 % après l’annonce.
Découvrez : Starlink en France : quel abonnement choisir et à quel prix pour l’internet par satellite ?
Vers un bouleversement complet du marché des télécoms
Les analystes estiment d’ailleurs que SpaceX ne se contentera pas d’une offre de base, prévoyant l’arrivée d’un pack combinant l’accès haut débit Starlink, la téléphonie mobile et pourquoi pas l’intelligence artificielle de Grok. Face à cette offensive, les opérateurs historiques rappellent que disposer de blocs de fréquences ne suffit pas sans une infrastructure solide.
L’autorité américaine des communications salue quant à elle une dynamique promise à dynamiser l’investissement national. Reste que l’aval final de la FCC reste indispensable pour valider officiellement le transfert de ces précieux sésames hertziens initialement cédés par T-Mobile. La bataille pour connecter les zones blanches et concurrencer les abonnements traditionnels vient de franchir un cap décisif.

articles.title: Problemas en el horizonte: las ganancias anualizadas de OpenAI se quedan 20.000 millones de dólares por debajo de lo esperado
articles.text:
A Wall Street no le gustan las sorpresas, y basta con la confirmación de que una estimación se ha desviado mínimamente para que los inversores pierdan el sueño. Esta semana le ha tocado a OpenAI, y no por una buena razón.
A finales de septiembre, Sam Altman había adelantado a sus inversores que OpenAI que las ventas anualizadas de la compañía rondarían los 70.000 millones de dólares. Las nuevas cifras se quedan bastante por debajo de esa estimación ya desatado una tormenta bajista que ha salpicado al resto de compañías tecnológicas y ha avivado una de las mayores dudas entre los inversores: ¿realmente es rentable invertir en IA?
Dos formas de contar lo mismo
A finales de septiembre, el Financial Times, Reuters y otros medios publicaron una estimación basada en fuentes de OpenIA en la que los ingresos anualizados se situaban en casi 70.000 millones de dólares. Ahora OpenAI dice a sus inversores que esa cifra finalmente se queda en unos 50.000 millones, según confirmó Reuters. Son 20.000 millones de dólares menos de lo esperado. Poca broma.
Tal y como explican en el Financial Times, esa discrepancia surge de los intentos de los inversores de OpenAI por realizar una comparación directa con los ingresos anualizados de Anthropic. El problema es que ambas empresas calculan esa cifra de forma diferente, por lo que no es posible establecer esa equivalencia de forma directa.
Anthropic incluye los ingresos por ventas a través de socios en la nube como AWS de Amazon y Google Cloud, mientras que OpenAI no. A cambio, según calculó Reuters, Anthropic paga a esos socios cerca del 16% de cada dólar que entra por esa vía.
Según fuentes del Financial Times, los esfuerzos de los inversores por inflar los ingresos anualizados de OpenAI provocaron informes que indicaban que los ingresos de la compañía rondaban los 40.000 millones de dólares en julio. Posteriormente, la compañía comunicó a sus inversores que sus ingresos anuales se habían incrementado más del 70% desde julio, lo que cual dejaba unas estimaciones que coincidían con los 70.000 millones de dólares que se habían barajado. Una cifra que la compañía no negó.
UN VISTAZO A...
Sin embargo, la nueva presentación para inversores de OpenAI muestra que los ingresos anualizados de julio no fueron de 40.000 millones, sino que estaban más cercanos a los 30.000 millones de dólares. Esa diferencia en la estimación es la que ahora ha pillado por sorpresa a los inversores.
Wall Street se pone nerviosa
La reacción de los mercados al ajuste de ingresos anualizados de OpenAI fue inmediata. De acuerdo a lo publicado por The Guardian, el Nasdaq 100 cerró ayer con una caída del 1,4%. Nvidia cedió un 2,9%, Oracle un 5,5% y Micron se dejó un 4,8%.
El efecto dominó que azotó los índices tecnológicos tiene su lógica. OpenAI es un cliente gigante para muchas de esas compañías. Si los de Altman no ingresan lo suficiente, toda la cadena de financiación que se ha generado en el desarrollo de la IA se viene abajo.
Oracle, por ejemplo, firmó un contrato de 300.000 millones de dólares con la empresa de Sam Altman. Si OpenAI no incrementa su volumen de negocio, esos pedidos pierden su base. Lo mismo sucede con Nvidia o Micron, que dependen del crecimiento de OpenAI para suministrar los chips comprometidos.
El primer obstáculo de OpenAI para aumentar lo encontramos en sus planes de precios: la mayoría de usuarios de ChatGPT no paga, y OpenAI asume el coste de cada respuesta. El dinero de verdad está hoy en las empresas, no en las suscripciones individuales de 20 dólares, sino en las licencias empresariales. Y ahí Anthropic se está moviendo más rápido.
Como recordaba Reuters, la creadora de Claude ya superó a OpenAI en ingresos trimestrales con 11.500 millones dólares frente a 6.700 millones de OpenAI. En abril, el Wall Street Journal reveló que OpenAI había perdido terreno en programación y en clientes corporativos. Además, comparte el 20% de sus ingresos con Microsoft hasta 2030.
Además, a Sam Altman lo que mejor se le está dando es gastar. Sus planes apuntan a unas inversiones por valor de 121.000 millones en cómputo para 2028. Aun duplicando ingresos, las pérdidas rondarían los 85.000 millones. Para acabar de rematar la foto, la compañía ha aplazado su salida a bolsa alegando que "Ahora sería un momento poco sensato para salir a bolsa", lo que le ha obligado a negociar una nueva ronda de inversión que la valore en 1,4 billones. Eso sí, de las diez mayores startups que están liderando el desarrollo de la IA, ninguna gana dinero.

articles.title: Midnight Mimosa infecte des smartphones Android avant même leur première utilisation
articles.text:
Le logiciel malveillant Midnight Mimosa est installé dans le firmware de certains smartphones Android à bas prix avant même leur mise en vente. Ses opérateurs en tirent des revenus publicitaires frauduleux et revendent la connexion des appareils à d’autres pirates, sans que leurs propriétaires puissent le supprimer.
Les chercheurs de Bitdefender ont repéré le paquet com.android.system.lite sur des téléphones équipés de puces MediaTek. L’utilisateur n’en voit qu’un libellé « System », sans icône. Ce composant dispose pourtant des privilèges du système. Ses opérateurs peuvent ainsi installer ou supprimer des applications en silence et charger du code envoyé depuis leurs serveurs. Ils transforment aussi certains appareils en proxys résidentiels, et d’autres pirates font alors passer leur trafic par l’adresse IP de la victime.
En deux ans environ, des milliers d’appareils ont été touchés dans plus de 150 pays. La France fait partie des trois pays les plus exposés, avec le Mexique et l’Italie. Les pirates atteignent donc leurs victimes par deux chemins : des téléphones contrefaits, mais aussi des applications du Play Store reliées aux serveurs de la campagne.
La solution tout-en-un pour protéger votre entreprise
Votre petite entreprise a de grandes ambitions. Protégez-là contre les pirates. Et développez sereinement votre activité !
Des faux Galaxy S25 Ultra vendus à petit prix
Les pirates derrière BADBOX 2.0 avaient infecté un million d’appareils Android bas de gamme en 2025.
Avec Midnight Mimosa, le matériel est tout aussi bon marché, mais il est vendu sous des noms prestigieux. Dans les relevés de Bitdefender, les téléphones infectés sont enregistrés sous les noms « S25 Ultra » ou « i17 Pro Max ». Il s’agit en réalité de combinés MediaTek d’entrée de gamme, sans aucun lien avec Samsung ou Apple. Les faussaires vont jusqu’à copier la référence SM-S938B du véritable Galaxy S25 Ultra.
Les deux modèles les plus fréquents viennent en revanche de marques bien réelles : le S200 X de Doogee et le KINGKONG X de Cubot. Des propriétaires de ces téléphones renforcés avaient d’ailleurs signalé un paquet caché com.Android.sys.* sur le forum XDA. Après chaque suppression, ce paquet revenait sous un nouveau nom. Une partie des firmwares analysés est signée avec des certificats au nom du fabricant de tablettes Shenzhen Zediel. Les chercheurs n’ont toutefois aucune preuve de son implication. Ils ignorent aussi à quelle étape le code malveillant est intégré, chez un intégrateur de firmware ou chez un logisticien.
Une fois le téléphone déballé, son propriétaire ne peut pas supprimer ce module par les menus d’Android, puisqu’il est installé dans la partition système. Il faudrait nettoyer le firmware ou désactiver le module par ADB, et la plupart des acheteurs en sont incapables. Pour Bitdefender, seuls les fabricants et les plateformes qui vendent ces téléphones peuvent régler le problème durablement. Les auteurs de la campagne ont en outre donné à ce module un accès aux services d’accessibilité et aux SMS, de quoi lire l’écran ou intercepter un code à usage unique envoyé par texto. Les chercheurs n’ont observé aucune utilisation de ces autorisations, mais les opérateurs peuvent les activer à distance, au moment de leur choix.
Play Protect désactivé, treize applications sur le Play Store
Le module système n’affiche aucune publicité. Ses opérateurs installent en arrière-plan de fausses applications de météo ou de verrouillage, chacune équipée d’un kit publicitaire légitime. Les régies rémunèrent ensuite ces applications pour des impressions et des clics simulés, sans que le propriétaire touche son écran. D’après Bitdefender, il en existe au moins 32. Elles sont installées puis désinstallées à tour de rôle, pour rester le moins longtemps possible visibles dans la liste des applications. Les pirates appliquent même à leur surface publicitaire le marqueur de sécurité conçu pour les écrans bancaires, et le propriétaire ne peut ni la capturer ni la filmer.
Avant chaque installation, ils désactivent le Play Store, qui héberge l’analyseur de Play Protect, puis le réactivent dès la fin de l’opération. Ils falsifient aussi la source déclarée de l’application. Dans les paramètres, l’utilisateur trouve alors une fausse mention d’installation depuis Google Play.
Les chercheurs ont par ailleurs identifié sur le Play Store treize applications de météo ou de lecture de QR codes qui portent les marqueurs de fraude de la campagne. Google les a validées puis distribuées à des utilisateurs à la recherche de ce type d’outil, sans aucun téléphone contrefait en jeu. Une partie a été publiée par les comptes de développeur fivedev et CPS Developer, et chacune des treize est signée avec un certificat différent. Ces applications affichent des publicités hors de leur interface, parfois même quand personne n’utilise le téléphone. Les opérateurs exploitent leurs serveurs avec ces deux canaux à la fois. Google peut retirer ces applications du Play Store, mais cela ne change rien pour les téléphones contrefaits déjà vendus.
Le firmware regroupe les composants logiciels fournis avec le téléphone (dont Android et des modules préinstallés), et une partie est stockée dans la partition système, conçue pour être en lecture seule en usage normal. Un code malveillant placé à cet endroit bénéficie souvent de privilèges élevés et survit aux désinstallations classiques, voire à certaines réinitialisations. Le supprimer proprement suppose en général de remplacer l’image système (reflash) ou d’intervenir avec des outils avancés, ce qui n’est pas accessible à la plupart des utilisateurs. Tant que la chaîne de production ou d’intégration du firmware reste compromise, de nouveaux appareils peuvent sortir avec le même implant.
Un composant avec privilèges système (application système/privileged) peut accéder à des API et autorisations interdites aux applications ordinaires, car il est considéré comme faisant partie du système d’exploitation. Cela peut permettre d’installer ou désinstaller des applications sans interaction visible, de modifier des réglages sensibles ou de charger du code additionnel à distance. Dans ce modèle, l’interface utilisateur peut rester quasi inchangée, ce qui réduit les signaux d’alerte. Le risque augmente si le module dispose en plus d’accès à des données sensibles (SMS, accessibilité), car ces droits ouvrent la voie à l’interception de codes ou à l’automatisation d’actions à l’écran.
Un proxy résidentiel est un relais de trafic internet qui utilise l’adresse IP d’un particulier, ce qui fait apparaître les connexions comme provenant d’un foyer et non d’un datacenter. Des attaquants s’en servent pour contourner des contrôles anti-fraude, masquer l’origine d’activités illicites ou automatiser des actions en ligne avec une IP jugée plus “crédible”. Si un smartphone est enrôlé comme proxy à l’insu de son propriétaire, une partie du trafic d’autres acteurs peut transiter par sa connexion, avec des impacts possibles sur la consommation de données, les performances et la réputation de l’adresse IP. En cas d’abus, des services peuvent associer l’activité au titulaire de la connexion, même s’il n’est pas l’auteur des actions.

articles.title: Jev: Warum dieses KI-Modell Entwickler begeistert – und welche offenen Alternativen es gibt
articles.text:
Support-Anfragen in 70 Millisekunden sortiert: Was das KI-Modell Jev von Claude und GPT unterscheidet
Mit Jev sorgt seit Kurzem ein KI-Modell für Aufregung in Entwickler:innen-Kreisen, das ausnahmsweise weder von einer der großen KI-Firmen aus den USA noch von einer aus China kommt. Entwickelt wurde Jev von dem US-Startup Typesafe, das bis zum Release Mitte September 2026 noch im Stealth-Modus operiert hat. Auch das Modell selbst arbeitet nicht so, wie wir es von Claude, GPT, Deepseek oder anderen großen Sprachmodellen kennen.
Während die Platzhirsche vor allem Texte erzeugen, ist Jev auf etwas ganz anderes trainiert: das Treffen von Entscheidungen. Als Beispiel nennt Hersteller Typesafe etwa eine Support-Anfrage. Natürlich könnte man auch ein großes Sprachmodell entscheiden lassen, ob die Anfrage eine Lieferung betrifft, eine Nachfrage zu einer Rechnung darstellt oder eine Beschwerde. Aber das wäre weder sonderlich kosteneffizient noch besonders schnell. Zumal die Antwort dann auch wieder eine mehr oder minder lange Erklärung in Textform wäre, die es bei Automationen überhaupt nicht braucht.
Genau da setzt Jev an. In diesem Beispiel würde das Modell die Kundenanfrage abhängig vom Inhalt einer der drei Optionen zuordnen. Und zwar innerhalb von nur 70 bis 500 Millisekunden. Ideal also für automatisierte Prozesse. Denn Software interessiert sich herzlich wenig für lange Erklärungen darüber, warum oder weshalb eine Entscheidung ausfällt, wie sie ausfällt.
Typesafe wirbt entsprechend auch damit, dass ihr Modell für den Einsatz durch Maschinen gedacht sei. Während der Output großer Sprachmodelle für Menschen optimiert sei. „Jev verleiht der KI die Eigenschaften von Code“, so das Herstellerversprechen.
Was wir über die Funktionsweise von Jev wissen – und was nicht
Jev kann nicht nur Entscheidungen treffen, sondern gibt auch in einem Prozentwert an, wie sicher sich das Modell ist, dass die Antwort korrekt ist. Der Vorteil: Gibt Jev nur eine Antwort mit geringem Prozentwert aus, könnte die Support-Anfrage aus dem obigen Beispiel gezielt einem menschlichen Mitarbeiter zur Prüfung vorgelegt werden.
Laut Typesafe soll ein spezieller Trainingsprozess, den das Unternehmen Reinforcement Learning for Calibrated Decisions (RLCD) nennt, dafür sorgen, dass die Wahrscheinlichkeitsangaben möglichst nah an der realen Trefferquote liegen. Zwar könnten wir auch ein normales Sprachmodell fragen, wie hoch es die Wahrscheinlichkeit einschätzt, dass die getroffene Entscheidung korrekt ist. Nur ist das kein Beweis dafür, dass die Angabe auch stimmt.
Das Problem: Typesafe hat weder in einem Paper öffentlich gemacht, wie Jev das alles praktisch anstellt, noch wurden die Modellgewichte veröffentlicht. Wir können daher nur mutmaßen, wie das Ganze wirklich aufgebaut ist.
Der 21-jährige Entwickler und Startup-Gründer Archer Hume liefert in einer online veröffentlichten Analyse aber immerhin Ansatzpunkte, wie Jev vermutlich funktioniert. Dazu hat der Australier 100.000 Anfragen an die Jev-API gesendet und anschließend ausgewertet.
Hume hat dazu die Anfragen immer leicht verändert. Also mal längere Texte geschickt und mal mehr und mal weniger Antwortmöglichkeiten an Jev übertragen. Anschließend wertete er aus, wann das Modell langsamer wurde und wann nicht, um so Rückschlüsse auf den Aufbau zu erhalten.
Er vermutet, dass im Kern von Jev ein herkömmliches Sprachmodell steckt. Genau so eins, wie wir es von Chatbots kennen. So kann Jev auf das notwendige Wissen und Sprachverständnis zugreifen, mutmaßt Hume.
Der große Unterschied: Jev hört im Gegensatz zu anderen Modellen dieser Art nach dem Lesen auf. Da nicht aufwendig Text generiert werden muss, ist es für das Modell auch weitestgehend egal, ob es zwischen 2 oder 100 Möglichkeiten entscheiden muss.
Hume geht außerdem davon aus, dass Jev alle Fragen getrennt voneinander beantwortet. So könne verhindert werden, dass die eine Antwort die andere beeinflusst.
Aber wie steht es um die Behauptung des Herstellers, dass Jev die Wahrscheinlichkeiten tatsächlich bestimmt und nicht etwa von einer KI behaupten lässt? Hume hält das für wahrscheinlich und stützt sich dabei auf zwei Indizien. Zum einen lässt die Anzahl der berechneten Token darauf schließen, dass Jev eben wirklich keinen Text generiert. Das wäre ein Indiz dafür, dass auch der Prozentwert nicht generiert wurde – sondern auf eine andere Art und Weise ermittelt wurde.
Zudem komme die Entscheidung auf eine Frage mit 200 Antwortmöglichkeiten genauso schnell zurück wie eine mit nur zwei. Würde Jev die Antwort wie ein herkömmliches Sprachmodell generieren, müsste das in der Variante mit den 200 Antwortmöglichkeiten auch länger dauern, denn die Token-Anzahl ist deutlich höher in diesem Fall.
Die Angaben dürften entsprechend irgendwo in dem Modell selbst abgelesen werden. Und das macht Jev offenbar auch recht gut. Zumindest bei den von Hume durchgeführten Proben lag die reale Trefferquote meist sehr nahe an dem vom Modell angegebenen Wert.
Mittlerweile gibt es auch ein eigens für Jev und ähnliche Modelle erdachtes Benchmark namens Jevbench der Plattform Benchmark Heaven. Auch hier liegt Jev zum jetzigen Zeitpunkt vor der Konkurrenz. Eine Konkurrenz, die sich zumindest in Teilen auf Humes Analyse von Jev bezieht.
Kev und mehr: Diese Open-Weight-Alternativen gibt es
Typesafe selbst mag die technischen Details seines Modells zurückhalten, das hindert die KI-Community aber offensichtlich nicht daran, offene Alternativen vorzustellen. Mit Projekten wie Kev, Semlf oder Reflex gibt es bereits eine Reihe von offenen Alternativen.
Sie alle beziehen sich explizit auf die Analyse und Schlussfolgerungen von Hume über die Funktionsweise von Jev. Als Basismodell kommen Varianten des Open-Weight-Modells Qwen von dem chinesischen E-Commerce-Konzern Alibaba zum Einsatz.
Im Benchmark mögen die Modelle noch nicht ganz an Jev herankommen. Allerdings wurde Humes Analyse auch erst am 17. September 2026 veröffentlicht. Also zwei Tage nach der Veröffentlichung von Jev selbst.
Da die Jev-Nachahmer alle auf kompakte Qwen-Varianten setzen, braucht es nicht mal besonders leistungsfähige Hardware, um sie lokal auszuführen. Selbst auf einem sechs Jahre alten Macbook Air mit M1-Prozessor erreichten wir etwa mit Kev Antwortzeiten von weit unter einer Sekunde.
Die offenen Entscheidungsmodelle eignen sich damit hervorragend, um sie als Teil eigener Automatisierungsworkflows selbst zu hosten, statt auf die Cloud angewiesen zu sein.
Von Ollama bis Ollaya: So führt ihr Jev-ähnliche Modelle direkt auf eurem Rechner aus
Mit Ollama und LM Studio unterstützen bereits zwei der beliebtesten Werkzeuge zur Ausführung lokaler KI die neuen Entscheidungsmodelle. Bei Ollama benötigt ihr mindestens Version 0.35. Bei LM Studio wurde die Unterstützung mit Version 0.4.26 integriert.
Alternativ dazu gibt es mittlerweile auch eine Reihe von Tools, die ausschließlich für den Einsatz mit Jev-ähnlichen Modellen konzipiert wurden. Dazu gehört etwa das quelloffene Tool Ollaya, das wie Ollama über die Kommandozeile gesteuert wird, und den direkten Download passender Modelle erlaubt.
Wer hingegen nur ein bisschen mit der Technologie experimentieren möchte, ohne gleich das Terminal bemühen zu müssen, der kann einen Blick auf die Open-Source-App Kevmac werfen. Die nimmt euch den Installationsaufwand ab und erlaubt euch, in einer grafischen Nutzer:innen-Oberfläche selbst Fragen und mögliche Antworten zu definieren, und dann lokal mit einem Kev-Modell auszuführen.

articles.title: Lagos Life maker Vatar raises $500,000 one week after launch
articles.text:
Vatar Inc., the company behind the viral Nigerian browser game Lagos Life, has closed a $500,000 angel round at a $10 million valuation three days after incorporation, according to a company statement.
“We built something people love that is growing very fast, so a lot of investors wanted to be involved,” Shalom Rayhamen, co-founder and CEO of Vatar Inc., told TechCabal in an interview. “We got the opportunity to connect and hear their offers, and because we are growing so fast, we closed it quickly so we could focus on the product.”
Olugbenga “GB” Agboola, Flutterwave’s CEO, invested through his fund, Resilience17. Oo Nwoye, Nathan Nwachuku, Terra Industries CEO, and Abdulhamid Hassan, Mono’s CEO, also participated in the round, which the company says closed in a day.
Lagos Life is part of a wave of Nigerian-made browser games sparked by Lagos Run, Opeyemi Adeniran’s game about driving a danfo, the iconic yellow bus, through Lagos, which drew more than 140,000 players in its first week. Rayhamen built Lagos Life days after seeing Lagos Run on X, and copycats soon followed.
The developers are building fast with AI, and the games spread through links shared on social media. In a fortnight, the shift shows that a game made by Nigerians, about Nigeria, can reach a mass audience almost immediately.
Lagos Life hit 4.3 million users on Thursday evening, with users from 15 countries. More than 100,000 were playing on Thursday evening, Rayhamen said, and the game has peaked at more than 200,000 players at once. After Nigeria, most users come from the US, UK, Ghana, Canada and the Netherlands, she added.
“Just signing up, setting up your character. That makes you registered,” Rayhamen said.
Rayhamen co-founded Vatar Inc. with Owen Rayhamen, the chief product officer, and Anderson Oriahi, the chief business development officer, on October 6. The funding will go to product, marketing, and hiring.
“We can still reach more people,” she said, adding that four million players is still a small share of Nigeria’s population.
How the game works
Lagos Life is a free life-simulation game that runs in a web browser. Players create a character, get a job, earn virtual naira, pay rent, and meet other players in a shared city. They buy generators to deal with power cuts, ride danfo buses, and live under a virtual governor and commissioners. Players pick who holds office, Rayhamen said, because a world where people earn money needs people in charge.
The in-game clock runs on real Lagos time. Real locations such as the Quilox nightclub and the Amala Shitta food spot appear in the city so players recognise them.
“It’s intentional,” Rayhamen said.
Each new player starts as either “Nepo,” with money and connections, or “Lapo,” a reference to microfinance loans and a hard start. Rayhamen said players asked for the feature. Some now say it promotes classism, which she said “wasn’t what I had in mind.”
“You release features, and some people will say ‘yay’ and some people say ‘nah’,” she said.
She expected players to want to socialise, but was surprised by how much. Recent requests include cooking, starting a family and sending children to school. “It’s almost blurring the line between the physical and the simulation,” she said.
The game’s virality and users’ ability to message each other have raised questions around content moderation and user protection. Rayhamen said Vatar has added an age check and tools to help users protect themselves.
“We screen and censor messages,” she said. “We have put mechanisms in place to keep users safe. Users can report other users, and they can block anyone they do not want to talk to.”
How it makes money
Selling games to Nigerians has long been hard. Credit card penetration in Nigeria is about 3.5%, making paid downloads and in-app purchases hard. Lagos Life is free to play and has charged brands since it launched.
Businesses rent billboards and plots inside the virtual city, while musicians pay to have their songs played in its clubs. Chowdeck, a food delivery company, appears as an app on every character’s phone and has partnered with Vatar Inc.
Rayhamen told TechCabal the game currently has five revenue streams, including advertising, music promotion, company deals, and football streaming. Players can also pay real money to top up their in-game cash.
“People want to have like an edge in games,” she said.
Vatar says it has earned and contracted more than $170,000 since launch. That is up from about $46,900 in its first four days, a figure Rayhamen posted on X. Payments run through Flutterwave, she said.
“This is actually a business,” she said, adding that “the infrastructure is expensive.” She declined to say how much the game costs to run and did not say whether Vatar is profitable.
Built in one night
Rayhamen started building the game at 9 p.m. on Wednesday, September 30. After working until 5 a.m., she took a nap and released it at 7 a.m. on October 1, Nigeria’s Independence Day.
“The first thing I worked on was the world itself, then the avatars, meaning the people,” she said.
“I started by researching the places I wanted to put in and placed them to create the world. The avatars take a lot of time because you have to think about everything an avatar should be able to do. It should be able to walk, sit down, sleep, and dance,” she added.
She used AI for research and coding through Anthropic’s API. “I’m pro AI,” she said. “I know how to use AI to my advantage.”
Rayhamen is a software developer with nearly a decade of experience, mostly in JavaScript for web and mobile. She holds a UK Global Talent visa, according to the company’s statement.
She built the game while caring for her four-month-old baby. “I’m a mom, so I’m proud of that,” she said, hoping her story encourages other nursing mothers and challenges the idea that marriage and children end a woman’s ambitions.
The idea came from The Sims 3, which she played as a child, and from Lagos Run, a browser game in which players drive a danfo bus through Lagos.
“I didn’t know it was going to grow so fast,” she said. Since launch, she has been rebuilding the game’s systems to handle the traffic. She uses AI agents to collect player requests from social media and sort them into bugs, urgent fixes, and new features. The agents are expensive, she said, but they help her decide what to build next.
Rayhamen said she has released products for years, and Lagos Life is her first big hit. “I’ve finally built something that people love,” she said.
What’s next
Port Harcourt, Nigeria’s oil hub in the Niger Delta, went live in the game around October 6, Rayhamen said. She declined to name the countries or cities Vatar plans to feature next. “I want people to anticipate,” she said.
Copycats have already appeared, including PH Lifestyle, a Port Harcourt Life game, and London Red Bus, a version of Lagos Run. Rayhamen said developers with AI tools should build something original.
“I feel like that is not creativity,” she said. “You have that opportunity, and all you can do is copy.”
Rayhamen said the moment Lagos Life stops feeling new will help Vatar, because the team can then build features players have not asked for. “When they get used to it, then we blow their minds,” she said.
Editor’s note: An earlier version of this article described Vatar’s $500,000 raise as a pre-seed round. Vatar has since clarified that it was an angel round. The article has been updated.

articles.title: Unpatched AhsayCBS Vulnerabilities Exploited in the Wild
articles.text:
Hackers have been exploiting two unpatched vulnerabilities in the AhsayCBS backup solution for remote code execution (RCE), cybersecurity firm Huntress warns.
A centralized cloud backup server management console developed by Ahsay Systems, AhsayCBS provides backup policy, storage, and user management and is popular among MSPs and system integrators.
Tracked as CVE-2026-105133 and CVE-2026-105134, the exploited security defects allow attackers to manipulate arguments in certain functions of the tool to bypass authentication and inject OS commands.
They were disclosed on October 4, when NIST warned that exploit code targeting them had been released, and that all AhsayCBS versions up to 10.3.2 were affected.
On Thursday, Huntress warned that attackers have exploited the two flaws in the wild and that the latest AhsayCBS version, 10.3.4, is also affected.
“Until a patch is available, we recommend restricting access to the management interface and investigating for signs of compromise,” Huntress says.
According to Huntress, threat actors are chaining the two bugs to access vulnerable systems and execute arbitrary code on them. As of October 8, at least five organizations had been targeted.
“Huntress observed threat actors exploiting the vulnerabilities to gain unauthenticated remote code execution and deploy webshells on exposed systems,” the cybersecurity firm notes.
It also warns that CVE-2026-105134 can be exploited for unauthenticated RCE with System privileges through an API of the Replication Receiver component.
“The API contains an authentication bypass that could allow for a random token to substitute valid credentials. After exploitation, a threat actor configured a malicious receiver and dropped a Java Server Page (JSP) webshell into the application directory served by the CBS application,” Huntress explains.
After gaining initial access, the attackers conducted reconnaissance and deployed XMRig cryptominers disguised as Microsoft Edge. They also planted an AI-assisted PowerShell script to monitor Task Manager and terminate it if it remains open for too long.
They also achieved persistence by creating a Windows service masquerading as Microsoft Edge Update to execute a modified copy of the legitimate NSSM utility named msedge.exe with System privileges.
“NSSM can support other programs to ensure they stay running and restart after a crash or reboot, and threat actors in this incident likely used it to maintain persistence for edge.exe, while disguising the service-related binary as a legitimate-looking file,” Huntress notes.
In one attack, the hackers deployed WinRing0x64.sys, a legitimate but vulnerable kernel driver that enabled the cryptocurrency miner to operate with kernel-level access.
“Organizations should restrict AhsayCBS management interface web access, as the exploit targets the externally accessible web app service on the host. Access should be limited to trusted IP addresses only or require VPN,” Huntress recommends.

articles.title: Former CIA chief says AI could begin directing battlefield weapons by 2030
articles.text:
Looking ahead: AI could begin directing networks of battlefield sensors and weapons by 2030, according to retired US Gen. David Petraeus, who expects military use of the technology to expand from analyzing data to making decisions with little or no human input. The former CIA director's forecast centers on AI staff officers and autonomous command systems that could coordinate multiple machines. Rather than operating drones independently, militaries would connect them through a command network able to gather information and direct operations.
"Just four years from now, we will have autonomous systems, and I think we will have the beginning of autonomous systems of autonomous systems; we will have AI agents, so you'll have agentic AI staff officers," Petraeus told investor Finn Murphy on the Forecast2050 podcast.
Petraeus outlined how such a network could operate during a CNBC interview in May. Autonomous sensors would collect battlefield data and relay it to a central command system, which would then direct weapons with little or no human involvement.
That would give AI a broader role than controlling a single drone or sorting information for a human commander. The software would help run operations across groups of machines. Petraeus has previously said autonomous systems could soon work together in platoon- or battalion-sized units, sharing information and coordinating without human intervention.
He described the prospective AI staff officers as "generic artificial intelligence staff officers who will never sleep, never eat, never take a break."
Petraeus also cited recursive learning, in which an AI model uses its own data and processes to improve itself. He expects that capability to contribute to the changes ahead, although the account provided no details about how military systems would implement or test it.
Petraeus expects Ukraine to see increasing use of autonomous unmanned systems by the end of 2026. For drones, one immediate consequence would be a reduced need for pilots, allowing more aircraft to operate without a corresponding increase in personnel.
The US military's stated approach still leaves decisions about using weapons to human operators. Admiral Brad Cooper, the head of US Central Command, has confirmed that AI is being used to sift through large amounts of data, but has not detailed the applications.
Human operatives will "always make final decisions on what to shoot and what not to shoot, and when to shoot," Cooper said.
Petraeus said adopting autonomous warfare would also require changes within military institutions. He argued that the UK could be positioned to lead because it has a smaller force, a more centralized defense ministry and a budget with greater emphasis on unmanned systems, despite its smaller economy.
The US, he said, still lacks some of the institutional changes needed for the transition. His forecast leaves militaries facing two tasks: building systems that can coordinate battlefield operations and deciding how much authority to give them.

articles.title: HashiCorp Relased Terraform Google Cloud Provider 8.0 in General Availability
articles.text:
HashiCorp has announced the general availability of version 8.0 of the Terraform provider for Google Cloud. The major release updates the default load balancing for two Compute Engine resources. It also removes resources linked to retired Google Cloud services. Additionally, it changes several order-insensitive attributes from lists to sets. This prevents ongoing plan differences. Because it is a breaking release, HashiCorp recommends moving to the latest 7.x release first and clearing deprecation warnings before upgrading.
The most visible behavioral change affects google_compute_backend_service and google_compute_global_forwarding_rule. Their default load-balancing_scheme now shifts from EXTERNAL to EXTERNAL_MANAGED. This means configurations that don't set the field will use the new external Application Load Balancer instead of the Classic one. Teams that depend on Classic behavior must set load_balancing_scheme = "EXTERNAL" explicitly, or a plan may propose changes to existing load balancers.
The release also removes resources and data sources. This is because their backing services have been shut down or replaced. Removed resources include google_iap_brand and google_iap_client (after the IAP OAuth Admin APIs shutdown), the three google_notebooks_* resources (users should move to google_workbench_instance), google_ml_engine_model, and the BeyondCorp app connection, connector, and gateway resources, with Security Gateway resources as the replacement. google_vertex_ai_schedule is replaced by google_colab_schedule. Configurations referencing any of these must be updated before upgrading.
On schema behavior, attributes where ordering carries no meaning have changed from lists to sets. These include fields in Compute Service Attachments, GKE logging and monitoring configuration, and Cloud Security Compliance Frameworks. HashiCorp says this prevents perpetual diffs when an API returns values in a different order than the configuration. Validation is stricter for some Google Cloud APIs. For example, source_contents is now required for google_workflows_workflow. Also, claim_mapping is needed when creating Workforce Identity Pool Provider SCIM tenants. Some state changes, like some integer-to-string conversions, migrate automatically. But others need configuration edits.
The announcement also summarizes 7.x-era capabilities that 8.0 builds on. The provider now supports Terraform list resources. These resources work with the terraform query workflow. You can search for existing infrastructure outside of the state and optionally create resource and import configurations. Coverage spans Compute Engine, IAM, BigQuery, Pub/Sub, Secret Manager, Migration Center, and Network Services. Resource Identity support grew. It now offers providers a clear way to represent a remote object. This can be used for import, along with traditional IDs. Write-only attributes send sensitive values to APIs without saving them. They now include certificate private keys, AlloyDB passwords, and IAP credentials.
The provider is developed jointly by the Google Cloud engineering team, HashiCorp, and the Terraform community, and 8.0 is available in the Terraform Registry. The post does not include benchmarks or adoption figures, and it does not list every removed resource, so the upgrade guide and GitHub changelog are the authoritative references.
A possible upgrade plan could be:
- Pin the provider and upgrade to the latest 7.x release first. Resolve deprecation warnings, then move to 8.0 in a non-production environment.
- Search your code for the removed resources listed above, and for load balancer resources that omit load_balancing_scheme. Set it explicitly to avoid unintended migration to EXTERNAL_MANAGED.
- Check the terraform plan carefully. Focus on resources marked for destroy or replace. Pay special attention to list-to-set conversions and any write-only version attributes that changed type or became required.
Teams running OpenTofu can adopt most of the release, but not all of it. The provider's breaking changes include the EXTERNAL_MANAGED default, removed resources, and list-to-set conversions. These changes are in the provider and apply no matter the CLI. Write-only attributes need OpenTofu 1.11 or later, which is the version that introduced them.
The discovery workflow using Terraform to query and list resources has no equivalent in OpenTofu. A feature request for a tofu query (issue #3787) is still pending. So, those teams will continue using import blocks and generated configuration for their current infrastructure.
OpenTofu's support for Resource Identity was not confirmed at the time of writing, so teams that plan to use identity-based import should check the OpenTofu changelog first. Teams should also verify that the 8.0 provider build is available in the OpenTofu registry before pinning it.

articles.title: Kubernetes on cgroup v1 is dead. Here’s what comes next.
articles.text:
Kubernetes on cgroup v1 is dead. Here’s what comes next.
Welcome back to another edition of Road to KubeCon, where we’re tracking the latest movements in the cloud-native ecosystem as we prepare for KubeCon + CloudNativeCon North America 2026, happening November 9-12 in Salt Lake City, Utah.
In this edition, we consider what happens when compute workloads need to run AI on the edge. Underlying Kubernetes mechanics change, as do observability practices and security decisions. We take a look at the emerging tactics and how a couple of key projects are responding to these changes.
Check out the story below on opening up Kubernetes capacity, HPE’s advances in purpose-built compute for AI, a reminder to evolve a deprecated Linux kernel interface, and what to expect at this year’s Kubernetes on Edge Day and Cilium co-located events.
HPE’s case for purpose-built edge compute
Using edge compute for AI inference makes sense for many reasons — you reduce unnecessary server calls, cut data egress fees, and keep data away from the cloud for compliance. As a result, many enterprises are turning to edge AI for these reasons and more.
Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) is a presenting sponsor of Road to KubeCon. HPE Software helps IT organizations modernize infrastructure, streamline operations, and accelerate AI initiatives across hybrid, multi-vendor environments.
However, as HPE’s Aaron Lamond notes in a recent HPE blog post, organizations often try to fit a square peg in a round hole when using unoptimized servers. “As intelligence becomes more distributed, purpose-built compute becomes increasingly critical to operational success,” he writes.
For Lamond, “purpose-built compute” should consider how hardware, software, security, and operations fit together. He says ProLiant edge servers are fit for the task because they are edge-optimized for resource-constrained environments that require high-grade security.
Edge knowledge returns to Kubernetes on Edge Day
Edge deployment on Kubernetes has been gaining steam for years, with CNCF projects like KubeEdge and many vendor platforms emerging to support Kubernetes at the edge. This year’s KubeCon + CloudNativeCon will host a dedicated, co-located Kubernetes on Edge Day to explore this intersection of cloud-native and edge computing.
As Mars Toktonaliev and Katerina Arzhayev write on the CNCF blog, “The event was created to address the gap between traditional, data-center-centric cloud native approaches and the operational realities of edge computing.” They mention observability and security as particularly relevant themes.
The Kubernetes on Edge Day schedule will showcase a broad spectrum of case studies and operational guidance—helpful for engineers running Kubernetes across distributed, resource-constrained environments.
Node swap brings Kubernetes density gains up to 3x
Bursty agentic AI workloads can require significant upfront memory unexpectedly. After this, memory often sits idle. But idle RAM is expensive, and this allocation caps Kubernetes cluster density.
On Monday, Ocean Xie and Yuan Wang dive into this issue on the Kubernetes blog. “Memory is often the first hard limit a Kubernetes cluster hits,” they write. “Nodes run out of RAM long before they run out of CPU, and the new wave of agentic AI workloads makes this worse.”
They propose running Kubernetes nodes with node swap, a feature that reached general availability in Kubernetes v1.34 and can act as a “shock absorber” during traffic spikes.
In their benchmarking, the authors report density gains of up to three times when node swap is backed by fast NVMe SSDs in certain scenarios. The analysis contributes to emerging methods to mitigate the high computational overhead and costs of agentic AI in practice.
Self-hosted platform deployments need prep before install
This week, Fairwinds, a managed cloud-native infrastructure provider, shares helpful guidance for those selling self-hosted AI platforms. According to Munib Ali, director of engineering, the installation is only the beginning.
Ali argues a working installer isn’t enough. Too often, platform vendors ship and don’t consider the surrounding mechanics required on the customer end—like establishing team responsibilities upfront, setting up IAM, ongoing maintenance, compatibility with customer private clouds, supported DNS configurations, and more.
“Self-hosted Kubernetes deployments for AI platforms often stall when customer prerequisites, environment restrictions, and cross-team handoffs are incomplete,” says Ali. Without this in place, the installation date can slip, or the project may never start.
Some cloud-native vendors offer customer-hosted delivery for privacy, sovereignty, or control reasons. But to make this seamless and avoid bottlenecks, teams need to figure out a lot before “go-live,” which should arguably be a shared responsibility.
As Kubernetes evolves, so do the demands on the teams running it. Presenting sponsor HPE helps teams address that complexity with software spanning virtualization, cloud management, observability, and automation.
Kubernetes shifts toward Linux cgroup v2
On Tuesday, Paco Xu, open source team lead at DaoCloud, a cloud-native software company, shares thoughts on cgroup v2, a kernel feature for managing resources like CPU and memory. According to him, cgroup v1 has many limitations.
“Compared with cgroup v1, cgroup v2 provides a single unified hierarchy, a more consistent interface, and a stronger foundation for resource isolation and modern resource-management features,” writes Xu. Depending on the Kubernetes version and configuration, cgroup v2 supports memory quality of service updates, container-aware OOM handling, rootless support, and other features.
Since v1.35, the kubelet refuses to start on cgroup v1 nodes by default. If you’re on an older release, Xu recommends migrating every Linux node to v2 before upgrading. Operators should consider responding to reap the benefits and avoid a stale architecture.
Spotlight on recent Cilium community updates
Cilium, the CNCF-graduated project for eBPF-based networking, observability, and security, will host another co-located event in Salt Lake on November 9 this year. Attendees can expect sessions to focus on cloud-native AI and security.
As Joe Stringer, Isovalent at Cisco, and Google’s Jordan Rife write on the CNCF blog, “this year’s agenda goes straight at the problems that show up when AI and GPU workloads push Kubernetes networking past what it was built for.”
The community continues to respond to new GPU demands and AI-driven observability requirements, as well as new vulnerabilities. Plenty of additional interesting case studies have also emerged recently, showing how Cilium, and eBPF for that matter, are getting more production use.
“Cilium’s recent case studies with Splunk, Celonis, and Preferred Networks talk about how eBPF is being used for security and AI use cases, and I think are a good indicator of where things are heading,” Bill Mulligan, Cilium and eBPF community pollinator, tells The New Stack.
He also points to BpfJailer, an open-source eBPF security tool from Meta. It’s an experimental open-source rewrite of Meta’s internal closed-source eBPF security tool.
Hiveminders into Cilium, Tetragon, or eBPF should know: Isovalent is also hosting its epic Hive Mind Mingle in Salt Lake… but sign up soon; attendance is limited.
Follow the Road to KubeCon
Road to KubeCon is an eight-part series presented by HPE at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon North America in Salt Lake City. Before you go, explore how HPE Software helps IT teams do more with less complexity.
If you haven’t bought your ticket yet, The New Stack readers get a special discount courtesy of the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF). Use the code KCNA26MED10 when you register at this link for 10% off your ticket.
Until the main event, we’ll be here every Friday covering what you need to know on the road to KubeCon.
In the meantime, you can catch up on past editions covering Kubernetes v1.37, inference costs, OpenTelemetry updates, and cloud-native AI harnesses. Or read the full archive.
The writer for this series, Bill Doerrfeld, is open to pitches. Send PRs, updates, projects, quotes, or hot takes via his personal contact page.

articles.title: Waymo cerró un préstamo de USD 5.000 millones para expandir su servicio de robotaxis
articles.text:
Waymo, la empresa de autos autónomos de Alphabet, cerró un préstamo de USD 5.000 millones con un grupo de bancos y fondos de inversión. Es la primera vez que la compañía recurre a deuda en lugar de vender participación accionaria para financiar su expansión.
El anuncio lo hizo el director financiero de Waymo, Steve Fieler, a través de un comunicado publicado en el blog oficial de la empresa. PIMCO, Blackstone y Sixth Street actuaron como prestamistas principales del acuerdo.
También participaron como prestamistas relevantes Capital Group, Loomis Sayles y T. Rowe Price. La lista se completa con Apollo, Blue Owl, Diameter Capital Partners, Franklin Templeton, Fidelity Management & Research Company, HPS Investment Partners y Oaktree. Goldman Sachs fue el único banco organizador de la operación.
De una ronda de capital a un préstamo
A comienzos de este año, Waymo ya había cerrado una inversión de capital de USD 16.000 millones destinada a expandir el despliegue de su tecnología de manejo autónomo, según precisó la empresa en el mismo comunicado.
Fieler explicó que el nuevo financiamiento complementa esa ronda de capital y le da a la compañía “flexibilidad financiera adicional para fortalecer su balance” de cara a las oportunidades comerciales que identifica por delante.
A diferencia de una ronda de capital, un préstamo no diluye la participación de Alphabet ni de los demás accionistas de Waymo. A cambio, la empresa deberá devolver el monto con intereses en los plazos pactados.
Una red que sigue sumando ciudades
Waymo informó que el mes pasado comenzó a operar en su decimoquinta ciudad en Estados Unidos y que anunció nuevos destinos internacionales, en momentos en que la compañía describe un crecimiento comercial a “un ritmo récord”.
La empresa ya presta servicio en ciudades como Los Ángeles, San Francisco, San Diego, Austin, Dallas, Houston, Miami, Orlando y Tampa, de acuerdo con el repaso que hizo TechCrunch del historial de expansión de la compañía.
El medio citado agregó que Waymo realiza pruebas en Londres y Tokio, con planes de lanzar su servicio comercial en ambas ciudades, aunque la empresa no precisó fechas concretas para esos mercados en su comunicado.
Para qué se usará el dinero
Según el comunicado oficial, el capital obtenido con el préstamo se destinará a “acelerar la expansión continua” del servicio de viajes totalmente autónomos de la empresa, tanto dentro de Estados Unidos como en el resto del mundo.
Fieler afirmó que contar con el respaldo de “socios financieros de primer nivel” le permite a la empresa “ejecutar con velocidad, escalar de manera responsable y seguir liderando la industria de los vehículos autónomos”.
El movimiento ocurre mientras Waymo compite con otras compañías de manejo autónomo, como la china Apollo Go de Baidu y el proyecto de robotaxis que Tesla despliega en Austin, por quedarse con una porción mayor del mercado de viajes sin conductor.
Cómo funciona el Waymo Driver
El sistema de conducción autónoma de Waymo, llamado Waymo Driver, se clasifica como tecnología de nivel 4 de automatización según la escala de la SAE (Society of Automotive Engineers). Esto implica que el vehículo puede circular sin conductor humano al volante, aunque limitado a las zonas geográficas que la compañía ha mapeado previamente como áreas de servicio.
Para percibir su entorno, los vehículos integran varios tipos de sensores que funcionan de manera redundante y se complementan entre sí. Entre ellos se encuentran los LiDAR de alta resolución, que generan mapas tridimensionales mediante pulsos de láser, y permiten detectar objetos a más de 300 metros de distancia.
A esto se suma una red de decenas de cámaras que ofrece visión panorámica de 360 grados alrededor del automóvil, junto con radares capaces de operar en condiciones climáticas adversas como lluvia o niebla. El sistema incorpora, además, receptores de audio externos que identifican la procedencia de sirenas de vehículos de emergencia, un dato relevante para anticipar maniobras de cesión de paso.
Toda la información recogida por estos sensores es procesada por una supercomputadora instalada a bordo, que aplica inteligencia artificial combinada con cartografía de alta definición desarrollada por la propia empresa.
Ese procesamiento incluye modelos de predicción de comportamiento, con los que el vehículo estima de antemano los movimientos de peatones, ciclistas y otros automóviles, además de responder a situaciones imprevistas en cuestión de milisegundos.
La arquitectura del vehículo también contempla sistemas de respaldo en sus componentes críticos: dirección, frenado, suministro de energía y computación secundaria. Esta redundancia busca garantizar que, si uno de los sistemas principales falla, el automóvil mantenga el control de forma segura hasta completar la maniobra o detenerse.
.

articles.title: Ghent-based SpectaCell launches with €6 million to advance its cell analysis platform for immunotherapy development | EU-Startups
articles.text:
SpectaCell, a new Ghent-based startup specialising in next-generation cell therapy analytics, has announced its official launch with €6 million in Seed funding. The company has spun out of imec, VIB and Ghent University.
The round was led by imec.xpand, with participation from PMV’s Flanders Future Tech Fund, InnovationQuarter Capital, Qbic and VIB.
Tony Montoye, CEO and co-founder of SpectaCell, said, “Breakthrough medicines need breakthrough tools. Researchers need to know much earlier which candidates deserve further investment and why. We are building a new standard in cell analysis: detailed insight, results within hours and a simple workflow that connects research with manufacturing.
“Together with our biopharma partners, we will turn that vision into a platform for developing better treatments more efficiently. And ultimately, that is what we want to make possible for patients: better medicines, sooner.”
Founded in 2026 by Mathieu Rabaey, Veronique De Vroey, Jan Van de Velde, and Tony Montoye, SpectaCell is a Belgian life sciences company developing a next-generation cell analysis platform for drug development and manufacturing.
Its proprietary technology combines digital imaging and data analysis to measure how treatments affect individual cells.
According to the company, immunotherapies are opening new ways to treat cancer and diseases of the immune system. Yet predicting which candidates will work in patients and producing them consistently remain major challenges. It notes that developers need a clearer view of what a treatment actually does, earlier in the process. Slow, fragmented testing can leave critical gaps in that understanding and delay decisions while patients wait.
SpectaCell claims to tackle these testing bottlenecks with a next-generation cell analysis platform that measures how treatments affect individual cells. Applications include cell therapies and T-cell engagers that help immune cells recognise and attack cancer cells.
“Developers of new immune therapies need to understand what happens when a treatment meets its target: does it kill a cancer cell, for example, and how do individual cells respond? Many existing tests provide only part of that picture because they measure indirect signals or averages across a sample. Important differences between cells can disappear in those averages,” the company mentioned in the press release.
SpectaCell highlighted that it combines chip-based imaging with data analysis to track large numbers of individual cells and their interactions directly, at high resolution and over time. The technology does not require fluorescent labels that can interfere with cell behaviour. The company is developing an easy-to-use, cartridge-based instrument designed to deliver these insights in hours rather than days.
It is targeting pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies and specialist manufacturers worldwide. The company is developing a single platform for use from early research and process development through to routine manufacturing quality checks. The Belgian company says it will enable researchers to compare drug candidates, development teams to improve production processes, and manufacturers to assess whether each batch meets required performance standards.
Benoit Devogelaere, Partner at imec.xpand, said, “SpectaCell brings together disruptive semiconductor technology, an experienced team and a major commercial opportunity in drug development and manufacturing.
“We are convinced that SpectaCell can become essential to how new medicines are selected, developed and produced. With applications across cell therapies, T-cell engagers and other advanced treatments, we see the potential to set a new industry standard and build a globally competitive life-sciences business. We are proud to lead this round and back that ambition.”
The company plans to use this capital to fund further development and commercialisation of the platform with pharmaceutical and biotechnology partners.

articles.title: Exclusive: Automattic loses its interim CFO just weeks after boardroom shakeup
articles.text:
Automattic’s interim chief financial officer Jeremy Klaperman has left his position after less than a month, TechCrunch has learned. Klaperman had been elevated to the new job last month after the governance crisis at the WordPress.com parent company, which saw its entire board either quit or be fired.
The company confirmed the departure with the following statement, shared by Automattic’s director of communications Megan Fox: “Automattic will always be grateful for Jeremy Klaperman’s leadership. We wish him the best of luck on his next endeavor.”
Before serving as the organization’s interim finance chief, Klaperman had served as the CFO of Automattic’s VIP Enterprise business unit.
He was meant to replace the former CFO, Mark Davies, who had briefly become Automattic’s CFO after the company’s board members voted to put CEO Matt Mullenweg on leave in September. Within 33 hours of the board’s decision, Mullenweg retook the CEO role, and the board was wiped clean.
Automattic’s chief legal officer Andy Missan had also left the company alongside Davies. Both executives had signed reciprocal severance deals during Mullenweg’s short leave of absence, TechCrunch previously reported. Automattic’s new board of directors was announced in late September, and includes best-selling science-fiction author Hugh Howey; two co-founders of the now-defunct social app IRL, Henry Khachatryan and Krutal Desai; plus author Amy Chan.
A source at Automattic told TechCrunch that Klaperman was upset the board was considering external candidates for the CFO role. Though he was announced internally as interim CFO, the board never legally approved his title, the source said. In addition, there was a disagreement with Mullenweg over a work project related to employee performance reviews, which led to Mullenweg’s demotion of Klaperman back to his former position at VIP. Klaperman resigned shortly thereafter.
Automattic’s spokesperson did not comment on the reason for Klaperman’s departure. The company is still performing an external search for a qualified CFO candidate, we understand.
After publication, the company issued a statement via X post, which implies that Klaperman was offended by the board’s search for external CFO candidates.
It read, “At Automattic, we consider it best practice to evaluate external candidates for critical roles alongside internal people stepping up. We are always talking to and recruiting the best talent. Sometimes people are offended or surprised by this and they resign, sometimes it has led to amazing mentoring or advising situations. We won’t comment on any specific person, but as a company we’re always trying to optimize and redefine ourselves to serve our customers better and promote the ideals we aspire to around Open Source, freedom, liberty, autonomy, and hackers.”
When the company originally announced Klaperman’s new role as interim CFO internally on Automattic’s Slack, Mullenweg reiterated that he had “100% confidence” in the company’s cash and financial position.
Updated after publication with more information about Klaperman’s departure.

articles.title: Kioxia unveils E1.L SSDs for hyperscalers with up to 122.88TB capacity — extreme density meets compact form factor
articles.text:
Kioxia unveils E1.L SSDs for hyperscalers with up to 122.88TB capacity — extreme density meets compact form factor
When compactness weds density.
Kioxia introduced its LD4-series solid-state drives (SSDs) in an E1.L form factor with capacities up to 122.88TB designed for high-density storage deployments in hyperscale data centers on Friday. The new drives use proven BiCS8 3D QLC NAND and are aimed at read-intensive workloads like AI data repositories and object storage, according to the manufacturer.
Kioxia's LD4-series SSDs rely on the company's proprietary platform complying with the NVMe 2.0e specification and featuring a single-port configuration along with select requirements of the Open Compute Project Datacenter NVMe SSD specification 2.6. Although Kioxia lists PCIe 5.0 compliance, the drives operate at PCIe 4.0 x4 speeds of up to 16 GT/s per lane, which provides a theoretical maximum bandwidth of approximately 7.88 GB/s in each direction. While the company currently offers capacities of up to 30.72 TB, it has validated an architecture capable of supporting 122.88 TB drives, though it never revealed when such drives are set to be available, something not surprising in a world where 3D NAND memory is sold in advance.
Interestingly, Kioxia did not disclose any actual performance characteristics of its LD4-series SSDs, including sequential read and write speeds, random read and write IOPS, or latency. The company also did not reveal their endurance ratings in drive writes per day (DWPD) or total bytes written (TBW), nor did it specify their power consumption. These characteristics are particularly important for hyperscale operators evaluating the cost, performance, and longevity of storage infrastructure.
The key selling point of Kioxia's LD4-series and its E1.L form factor — 318.75 mm length × 38.4 mm height × 9.5 mm thick — is its ability to house numerous 3D NAND flash packages on an elongated printed circuit board, thus enabling multiple drives to be installed in a thin 1U server, offering vast capacities. This enables system manufacturers among those who build OCP-compliant servers to maximize storage capacity without increasing rack space requirements, which is particularly important for large-scale storage deployments.
Kioxia is currently sampling 15.36 TB and 30.72 TB LD4 drives to select customers. The company has not disclosed when 122.88 TB configurations will become available or when the series will enter mass production. The drives will be demonstrated at the OCP Global Summit in San Jose in mid-October.
