articles.title: ‘I think that's a fight worth having’ — award-winning illustrator Rob Biddulph on why the big AI companies haven’t won the war against human creativity yet
articles.text:
‘I don't think this is a fight that artists can afford to walk away from’ — award-winning illustrator Rob Biddulph says human creativity is worth defending against AI
Rob Biddulph says the problem with AI art isn't quality — it's personality
“There's a sort of soullessness to them, and I find it sad that we appear to be increasingly happy to settle for that.”
I'm talking to Rob Biddulph, the children’s book illustrator and author who rose to prominence during the Covid pandemic when his #DrawWithRob YouTube channel racked up millions of views from children and parents needing an outlet for their creativity, about a very different kind of pandemic: the proliferation of AI-generated art.
Biddulph was named Illustrator of the Year 2025 at the British Book Awards, but today he’s talking about the troubling increase he's seeing in shops and cafes and other venues displaying posters that are clearly designed by AI.
“I think they're really depressing, to be honest," he tells me. "One of the things I love about illustration is that it's an expression of somebody's individual personality. Human beings can't help but put a bit of their own personality into a drawing or a design.
"Often, you can look at a piece of artwork and recognize the person who made it — see their quirks, their imperfections, their sense of humor and the decisions they've made along the way. To me, that's what makes it interesting.
“And I also think there's something particularly ironic about using AI to advertise a local event. Surely the whole point of a local event is that it's about people and community?”
AI is doing more than cluttering the high street
Biddulph has a point. Personally, I’d rather see a wonky poster created by a real person than another technically polished but utterly generic piece of AI artwork. But AI is doing much more than cluttering up the high street with slop art. It’s taking paid work away from human designers and illustrators — the irony being that those AIs have all been trained on the work of human artists, with no compensation paid to those artists.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
“The thing to always remember is that these AI systems haven't appeared out of thin air,” explains Biddulph. “They've been trained on enormous quantities of existing creative work produced by artists, illustrators, photographers and writers who were never asked for permission for their work to be used and haven't been paid for it.
“And now those same systems are being used to produce work that competes directly with the people whose work helped train them in the first place! That's the bit I find particularly difficult to accept.”
Buddulph thinks there needs to be more of a reality check when it comes to talking about the creative industries in general. “I also think there's a tendency to talk about the creative industries as though they're made up entirely of wealthy, successful people," he says. "They're not. They're made up of thousands upon thousands of freelancers, small studios, illustrators, photographers, designers and writers, many of whom are already working in incredibly precarious circumstances.
"For an established artist, the impact might be a reduction in commissions, but for somebody just starting out, it could mean that the opportunities to build a career simply aren't there in the first place”.
They haven’t won
A few years ago there was a lot of talk about regulating AI companies' use of artists' work to train their models for free; these days I don't hear so much about the subject. I asked Biddulph if the AI companies had effectively won, or if there was still a fight to be had.
“I certainly don't think they've won”, he responds, “although I can understand why it sometimes feels that way. The technology has moved so quickly, and the companies behind it have such enormous financial resources, that it can feel as though the horse has already bolted and the rest of us are constantly playing catch-up. But I don't think the argument has gone away. If anything, I think we're entering a really important phase of it.
“In the UK”, he explains, “there was a huge amount of opposition from the creative industries to the Government's original proposal, which would effectively have allowed AI companies to train on copyrighted work unless individual creators specifically opted out.
“The problem with that approach was obvious. It placed the responsibility on millions of individual creators to protect their own work, rather than requiring companies to seek permission in the first place. The Government subsequently stepped back. So I think it's important that we recognize that artists, writers, publishers and other creative organizations have made their voices heard, and have had an impact.”
Biddulph is in favor of an opt-in system. “My own feeling is that the principle should be fairly straightforward: if you want to use somebody else's creative work to build a commercial product, you should have to ask permission and pay for it. I don't see why artists and illustrators should be expected to accept a different set of rules simply because the technology is new. I'd like to see a proper opt-in licensing system, rather than an opt-out system.”
A fight worth having
“If an artist wants to make their work available for AI training, that's absolutely their choice," he adds. "They should be able to do so, and be paid accordingly. But that choice should belong to the artist. I also think we have to be careful not to confuse the inevitability of the technology with the inevitability of the way it's being developed and used.”
So does Buddulph think AI is here to stay, and that illustrators need to keep fighting for better rights?
“Yes, AI is here to stay”, says Biddulph. “That doesn't mean we have to accept every aspect of the business model behind it. Personally, I don't think this is a fight that artists can afford to walk away from, even if, at times, it feels hopeless. It's about more than protecting individual livelihoods. It's about establishing what we value as a society, and whether we believe that human creativity has an intrinsic value that deserves to be protected. And I think that's a fight worth having.”

articles.title: Tesla muda nome do sistema de direção assistida na Europa
articles.text:
A Tesla mudou o nome de seu sistema avançado de assistência ao motorista na Europa após críticas do Ministério dos Transportes da Alemanha. A tecnologia, antes chamada de Full Self-Driving (Supervised), agora se chama Tesla Assisted Driving (direção assistida da Tesla, em tradução livre). A alteração busca evitar interpretações equivocadas sobre as capacidades do software e pode ajudar a empresa a ampliar a disponibilidade do recurso no continente.
O ministro dos Transportes alemão, Steffen Bilger, afirmou no início de outubro que a denominação anterior poderia induzir os consumidores ao erro, já que o sistema não realiza todas as tarefas de condução de forma independente. Segundo comunicado oficial do ministério, a própria Tesla sugeriu a mudança após conversas com o governo alemão no mês passado.
Com a alteração, Bilger pretende defender a aprovação do Tesla Assisted Driving em outros países europeus antes de uma possível votação em toda a União Europeia, que pode ocorrer ainda neste ano. O CEO da companhia, Elon Musk, agradeceu ao ministro na rede social X nesta semana. O executivo vinha pressionando há anos pela liberação do recurso na região.
Em março de 2026, a Holanda se tornou o primeiro país europeu a aprovar o Full Self-Driving (Supervised). Na quarta-feira (7), a Reuters publicou uma reportagem segundo a qual a campanha da Tesla pela aprovação europeia se apoiou em pesquisas de segurança consideradas problemáticas e estudos com falhas. A agência também relatou que a autoridade holandesa de segurança veicular, RDW, sofreu forte pressão da empresa e de seus apoiadores na internet.
Apesar dos avanços do software, o sistema continua exigindo que o motorista preste atenção à estrada e assuma o controle quando necessário. A tecnologia consegue manobrar para entrar e sair de vagas e navegar por ruas e rodovias.
Entretanto, o Full Self-Driving está no centro de investigações nos EUA e processos civis relacionados a acidentes nos quais teria sido utilizado. O sistema Autopilot, menos avançado, também foi associado a dezenas de mortes. A Tesla descontinuou o recurso no início deste ano, depois que um juiz concluiu que a empresa havia adotado práticas de marketing enganosas sobre suas capacidades.
Ana Figueiredo é editora de tecnologia do Olhar Digital. É formada em Jornalismo pela Universidade Federal de Uberlândia (UFU).

articles.title: The Download: AI’s refusal problem and weight-loss drug side effects
articles.text:
The Download: AI’s refusal problem and weight-loss drug side effects
Plus: The US has frozen green cards for Microsoft and other IT firms.
This is today's edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what's going on in the world of technology.
We’re putting too much faith in AI’s ability to say no
Today’s AI models are trained to refuse a vast number of prompts. If you ask your chatbot how to poison a colleague or how to tie a noose, chances are it’ll turn you down. But refusal fails, sometimes horrifically.
Some people are attempting to use AI to hone biological pathogens and build autonomous drone swarms. Sooner or later, failed refusals may result in global calamity. What’s more, relying on refusal means drawing a line between what a model should obey and what it must disobey.
Governments will also get to draw their own lines, potentially restricting free speech. At the same time, the capabilities that make AI useful could also make it dangerous. If we want it to help cure cancer, AI needs genetics expertise that could also produce bioweapons.
Read the full story on the formidable tradeoffs of AI refusal.
—Arthur Holland Michel
This story is from the next issue of our print magazine. Subscribe now to get your hands on a copy as soon as it lands on Wednesday 21 October!
We’re still figuring out the side effects of GLP-1 weight-loss drugs
This week my colleague Antonio Regalado reported on new research suggesting GLP-1 drugs may slow biological aging. It’s the latest in a raft of potential benefits associated with these drugs. But there are also some weird side effects.
The most common are gastrointestinal, but researchers are also investigating possible links to hair loss, nail disorders and damage to the nerves behind the eye.
Here’s what we know so far about the side effects of weight-loss drugs.
—Jessica Hamzelou
This story is from The Checkup, our weekly biotech newsletter. Sign up to receive it in your inbox every Thursday.
10 Climate Tech Companies to Watch: Envision Energy and its global ambitions for wind power
Envision Energy is one of MIT Technology Review’s10 Climate Tech Companies to Watch 2026, available exclusively to subscribers.
China is installing wind turbines faster than any other country. One of its leading manufacturers, Envision Energy, is integrating renewable energy into data centers, using wind turbines to generate power and batteries to store it on-site.
Recently, it became the first company to directly power a data center entirely with renewable energy. An AI-powered system optimizes the power output so the facility can receive a steady supply, regardless of whether the wind is blowing. Now, it wants to bring that approach to data centers in deserts around the world.

articles.title: Microsoft bloquea el último truco para instalar Windows 11 sin una cuenta en línea
articles.text:
Uno de los más recientes trucos para instalar Windows 11 sin tener que iniciar sesión con una cuenta de Microsoft ha sido bloqueado. La empresa de Redmond se ha encargado de parchear un loophole que permitía configurar el sistema operativo sin tener que depender de una cuenta en línea y una conexión a Internet.
Según reporta Neowin, ya no es posible saltearse el requerimiento de una cuenta de Microsoft al pulsar el botón "Saber más" en el inicio de sesión del configurador de Windows 11. Esta peculiar alternativa se descubrió en septiembre y es evidente que se trataba de un bug.
La compañía ha introducido un parche silencioso que elimina esta posibilidad. Todavía se puede instalar Windows 11 con una cuenta 100 % local, pero es un proceso que requiere de algo más de trabajo. Con el más reciente cambio de Microsoft, se vuelve imposible evadir el requisito directamente desde las pantallas del configurador.
No es la primera vez que la firma estadounidense toma una medida de este tipo. En el pasado, los de Redmond fueron eliminando otros métodos que permitían saltear el uso de una cuenta de Microsoft en la instalación de Windows 11. Sin embargo, siempre aparecía un fallo o una brecha desconocida que facilitaban el proceso por al menos un tiempo más. Claro que con cada parche que se añade al software se va cerrando más esa puerta.
Instalar Windows 11 sin una cuenta de Microsoft todavía es posible
Pese a que Microsoft está cerrando todas las brechas que permiten instalar Windows 11 sin una cuenta online, todavía quedan alternativas. La más efectiva es modificar el instalador del sistema operativo desde Rufus, una aplicación para crear discos de arranque usando memorias USB.
Como ya explicamos en este tutorial al detalle, solo tienes que descargar la imagen ISO de Windows 11, que está disponible gratis en la web de Microsoft, y ejecutar Rufus para crear la unidad de instalación con un pendrive. Antes de que el proceso de grabación se inicie, te permite eliminar el requisito de una cuenta en línea y establecer una cuenta local. Asimismo, puedes eliminar otros requisitos indeseados como la instalación automática de Copilot y otras aplicaciones de la compañía.
Es un paso extra, sin dudas, y puede resultar algo molesto si no un poco de conocimientos técnicos. Pero al menos así te garantizas poder seguir instalando Windows 11 sin estar forzado a iniciar sesión con una cuenta de Microsoft o a estar conectado a Internet.

articles.title: Anthropic’s AI gave Philadelphia police a fake tip about an unsolved homicide
articles.text:
An Anthropic AI model provided false information about an unsolved homicide to a Philadelphia Police Department (PPD) tipline, according to a report from 6abc. In a statement released on Friday, the PPD said the AI model sent the tip through PhillyUnsolvedMurders.com on July 18th, but the investigators never reviewed it because it was marked as spam.
Anthropic’s AI gave Philadelphia police a fake tip about an unsolved homicide
The false tip ‘purported to come from someone who might have information about the case.’
Anthropic learned its AI model sent the false tip on September 28th and notified the PPD on October 7th. The company said that during testing, its AI model was interacting with “randomly selected websites” and submitted false information through the PPD’s tipline, according to the PPD’s statement. The submission “purported to come from someone who might have information about the case,” the PPD said.
After discovering the submission, Anthropic halted the testing process that led to the false tip. Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google have been the subject of increased scrutiny after disclosing that their AI models escaped testing environments and hacked third-party companies. Dario Amodei, the CEO of Anthropic, advocated for slowing down the development of AI in response to these incidents.
“The company [Anthropic] must strengthen its safeguards to prevent similar incidents from impacting city systems without the city’s knowledge,” the PPD added. “The two-month delay in detecting and reporting the incident to the City is unacceptable.”
Anthropic didn’t immediately respond to The Verge’s request for comment. The company is planning to publish a report about this incident, as well as other “instances of unintended model behavior” on Friday, according to the PPD’s statement.

articles.title: Essential Tools and Checks Every Content Creator Should Use - Tech Guide
articles.text:
You must have seen some popular content creators becoming irrelevent behind because of a few pieces of low-quality content or delay in publishing a new content.
Undoubtedly, the content creation industry has become a tremendously saturated sector.
No matter how innovative or creative your ideas are, you may lag behind other creators or writers if you do not publish regularly. Nor can you post random content just to increase the numbers.
So, if you are a newbie in the content industry or an aspiring content creator, you must keep in mind that this is quite a competitive place. And you must work smarter to stay ahead.
So, you cannot help but use different tools, technologies, and AI assistance to ensure both high-quality and regular content delivery to stay relevant.
Here are seven fundamental tools you should use, whether you are working on written or visual content.
AI Detector
The content industry has become more complicated these days, as creators have to worry about the huge amount of AI-generated content as well.
They have to make sure that their content does not resemble them, while making the effective use of AI tools.
So, the very first thing you should ensure is that there is a solid way of AI detection in the content generation workflow.
So, for that, you can use a Pro AI detector that can identify even the tiny portions in content that look automated, synthetic, or unnatural.
The AI checker will flag all portions that appear AI-generated or odd. So, you will only have to work on those portions, humanize them in totality, and improve the quality.
The more natural your content looks, the better it is supposed to perform and engage with the audience. So, before finally wrapping up, always run an AI check for the best result.
Moreover, detection tools will not only help your own content look better, but also help you identify AI-created content and find better ones for reference that you can go through to get ideas.
Writing Tool
If you are into written content, an AI writing tool is a must for you to improve and scale the content.
You can use these writing tools in multiple ways. You can either use it to write a whole blog, post, or an article with a detailed and nuanced prompt. Then add your own personal insights or make a few edits to vocabulary and syntactic structure.
Or you can write the whole content on your own and improve it with the tool by fixing grammar errors, bringing clarity, and integrating brand voice. Also, you can paraphrase, compress, and expand writing with these tools.
So, if you have a huge pile of content to submit within a day or two, you can still manage to submit decent-quality content by making impactful use of these writing tools.
Chatbots And Research
Sometimes, you are out of topics and ideas for creating a trendy video or writing a relevant topic. You may want to find and create new ideas for that.
In these kinds of cases, AI chatbots and research tools may be extremely helpful. The chatbots are really helpful for researching certain trends and ongoing topics on social media and Google SERPs.
Moreover, you can keep digging and converse with the chatbots and research tools, go deeper, use your own experiences and ideas, and find interesting topics that may be relevant but have not been covered by other creators yet.
So, whether you are making funny visual content for social media and YouTube, or writing a short promotional post and long-form blogs, these chatbots are great tools for doing the research work.
Visual Creator And Editor
If you are a video content maker, you cannot go without video editing tools. But these tools are also essential for content creators who are writing content, as they often need to attach images and icons to their blogs and articles.
Therefore, a visual content tool is a must-have in your bucket no matter what type of content creator you are.
Some AI visual tools can turn a simple prompt into a whole piece of video or image. So, you can create an innovative visual with them from scratch. In a way, it is more effective, as you can make any type of content according to your or your clients’ requirements.
But there are some video editors that you can use to improve the quality of the content. You can also add different stuff like audio, text, icons, links, and other miscellaneous things that are needed for a social media or YouTube video using these tools.
Also, you might need to edit visuals and images as well to resize and fix the color grading of the existing images you want to publish.
Moreover, you need editors to work on the visuals you create through AI tools to make them more humanized and natural and remove all the odd stuff.
So, always prioritize good-quality video and image creation or editing tools to keep in your list.
SEO Tool
In the present online scenario, you cannot expect content to perform well and be visible enough without SEO optimization.
But it includes a lot of tasks to be done for the best result. So, an SEO tool is another must-have thing for a content creator.
SEO tools help users with keyword research and finding trending queries online. Also, they can automatically integrate them into your content.
The SEO platforms also guide you with the latest SEO patterns and search algorithms, and provide you with strategies on how to get mentioned in AI overviews and chatbots for more visibility.
Also, these tools can check if your site is optimized enough or not, and provide a percentage or probability of how well it is going to perform. Considering the probability, you can work on the content further for better SEO.
Content Moderator And Performance Tracker
Influencers, writers, or video creators must use an automated content moderator to ensure that the pieces they are posting align with the community guidelines, safety policy, legal requirements, and other necessary compliance requirements.
Not only that, but this kind of software also ensures content quality by reviewing the writing style, language, vocabulary, and elements present in an image or video.
You can also use the automated moderators as a performance tracker, as they can review the comments and reactions of the audience and viewers of your content.
However, you can also keep track of the performance of your content through a separate app. The apps measure analytics of traffic, reach, engagement with viewers, SEO performance, ranking of the content, and conversions, if you are working for a brand.
The performance tracker and moderation tool keep you aware of the impact of your writing, videos, and images on your audiences and drive you to improve them. So, always use them in your content creation workflow.
Note-taker And Scheduling
Many of the new content creators might ignore this, but note-taking or scheduling tools might be very useful for them. Especially if you are working on your own.
Being a content creator, you will surely have a lot on your plate to accomplish every day. From creating and reviewing to publishing content, you have to work on a lot of things.
It is very likely that some of the points slip your mind that you wanted to add to your content, and you can even forget to accomplish a task or post something on a super busy day.
If you keep a note-taking tool and a scheduling app, they can help you organize all your small and important tasks. They can even set reminders for you to post something, submit a blog for your clients, or attend a meeting.
Some of them have an automated system where the app automatically publishes content on the set schedule.
So, with these tools, you can work more effectively in an organized way, following a proper timetable without forgetting anything.
Final Thought
The above-mentioned seven tools are the most essential ones that you should keep to produce and create better content and work in a more composed way.
The more you grow as an online content creator, the more advanced tools to polish your work and bring perfection.
However, while using these tools, always remember that there is enough human supervision to keep an eye on how these tools are processing all the tasks and to ensure quality checks.

articles.title: Cyberattaque sur l'iPhone : le malware DarkSword est de retour sous une nouvelle forme
articles.text:
En mars 2026, le monde apprenait l’existence de DarkSword, un outil de piratage d’iPhone qui peut tout voler à l’intérieur. Depuis, il fait régulièrement parler de lui, notamment après s’être retrouvé en ligne, disponible pour tout le monde. Cette fois-ci, c’est une nouvelle version qui fait parler d’elle.
P7 DarkSword, une nouvelle version encore plus perfectionnée
La société de cybersécurité mobile iVerify a publié ce 8 octobre un rapport sur P7, une variante de DarkSword qu’elle dit avoir découverte. Elle explique que le nom P7 « provient de l’utilisation par l’attaquant du préfixe variable lors de modifications apportées au code source original de DarkSword. » P7 a été découverte en août dernier, alors qu’iVerify recevait une alerte concernant une infection par DarkSword sur l’iPhone de l’un de ses clients. Problème, « la détection différait légèrement des détections habituelles de DarkSword » déjà observées.
Les employés d’iVerify écrivent que comparée aux versions précédentes, P7 « réduit son empreinte sur l’appareil, permet le vol de clés et de portefeuilles de cryptomonnaies ». Elle peut aussi établir une communication bidirectionnelle entre le serveur de l’attaquant et l’appareil ciblé. Habituellement, les variantes sont développées à l’aide d’outils d’intelligence artificielle, mais ce n’est pas le cas de P7. La cyberattaque se déroule de la même manière : il suffit de se rendre sur un site web vérolé, et le piège se referme sur votre iPhone.
Au contraire, pour iVerify, elle a été développée avec « des efforts considérables pour la modifier ». Elle est plus discrète en éliminant ses traces dans le journal de débogage, elle est plus stable en utilisant le stockage local du navigateur, et elle propose davantage de fonctionnalités. Par exemple, les données du trousseau d’iCloud sont extraites au format JSON, ce qui faciliterait leur exfiltration. Pour la société de cybersécurité, « P7 DarkSword démontre que les opérateurs de DarkSword améliorent constamment le dispositif. »
Comment protéger son iPhone de cet outil de piratage ?
On ignore qui se cache derrière DarkSword, mais l’on sait que plusieurs opérateurs distincts sont à l’origine de cyberattaques avec cet outil. Il semble que ce dernier soit vendu ou partagé entre plusieurs acteurs : groupe russe, entreprise turque, FBI, etc. Les probabilités que vous soyez ciblé par P7 DarkSword restent minimes, l’outil vise surtout les salariés d’entreprises sensibles, les détenteurs de cryptomonnaies, ou encore les personnes travaillant sur des sujets politiques.
Mais le mieux à faire reste toujours de se protéger et dans ce cas-ci, ce n’est pas très compliqué. Il suffit de mettre à jour son iPhone, comme l’a recommandé Apple : pour le moment, P7 DarkSword vise uniquement les iPhone sous iOS 18 à iOS 18.7, contre iOS 18.6 auparavant. Ainsi, si vous avez un iPhone 17, iPhone Air ou iPhone 18 Pro, pas d’inquiétude : ces modèles sont sortis sous iOS 26 et iOS 27. Quant aux autres, il est conseillé de mettre à jours votre téléphone vers la dernière version en date.

articles.title: HTC Vive Eagle : les lunettes connectées qui défient les Ray-Ban Meta avec un argument choc sur la vie privée
articles.text:
Un an après leur lancement à Taïwan, les lunettes connectées de HTC sont enfin disponibles en France. Néanmoins, elles arrivent dans un marché que Meta écrase pour l'instant de tout son poids. Pour se démarquer, les Vive Eagle jouent la carte de la vie privée et du libre choix de l’IA.
Il n'y a pas si longtemps, HTC était un titan de la tech, capable de rivaliser avec Apple et Samsung sur le très relevé (et lucratif) marché des smartphones. Mais demandez aujourd'hui à n'importe quel adolescent s'il connaît la marque, et il y a de grandes chances pour qu'il vous rende un regard vide. Il faut dire que le fabricant taïwanais ne pèse aujourd'hui plus grand-chose dans la tech grand public, surtout depuis le déclin de la réalité virtuelle, alors que ses casques Vive suscitaient un certain engouement.
Pour rebondir, la marque a décidé de s'attaquer à une catégorie de produits en plein essor : les lunettes connectées. Les ventes de modèles sans écran ont en effet bondi de 210 % sur un an au premier trimestre 2026, et Meta y règne presque sans partage avec 84 % de part de marché. Voilà pour le contexte.
Lancées à Taïwan il y a environ un an, les Vive Eagle arrivent enfin chez nous. Annoncées en France le 3 septembre 2026, elles sont officiellement disponibles depuis quelques jours seulement par le réseau des opticiens. Sur le papier, leur fiche technique est assez intéressante, puisqu'elles intègrent une puce Qualcomm Snapdragon AR1 Gen 1 épaulée par 4 Go de mémoire vive et 32 Go de stockage, une caméra ultra grand-angle de 12 mégapixels (Mpx) logée dans la charnière, des verres Zeiss remplaçables, quatre microphones, du wi-fi 6E et du Bluetooth 5.3.
HTC ajoute à sa recette deux arguments pensés pour se démarquer, à savoir le libre choix de l'assistant IA et une communication très appuyée sur la protection des données.
Au moment de leur sortie, les Vive Eagle sont proposées en France à partir de 469 €.
HTC propose ses lunettes en deux formats. D'un côté, la Pantos et ses verres ronds ; de l'autre, la Square et son allure wayfarer. C'est la première citée que nous testons ici, mais seul le design change entre les deux déclinaisons, le versant technique demeurant identique.
Nos Pantos affichent 48,8 g sur la balance, verres compris, quand les Square grimpent à 51,5 g. Dans les deux cas, cela reste très raisonnable pour un accessoire qui embarque puce, caméra, batterie et haut-parleurs dans ses branches.
La monture abrite par ailleurs deux boutons physiques. Celui de la branche gauche gère l'allumage et le déclenchement de l'assistant IA, tandis que celui de droite pilote la caméra. Une surface tactile prend place sur la branche droite pour la navigation. Signalons que l'ensemble est certifié IP54, de quoi encaisser les projections d'eau et la poussière, mais certainement pas une immersion.
Bon point, l'utilisateur peut remplacer lui-même les verres Zeiss et y intégrer une correction optique. Une déclinaison AdaptiveSun à verres adaptatifs existe aussi, mais pas pour le marché français à notre connaissance.
Un mot sur le système de recharge et l'étui. Chez Meta, il s'agit de la même chose, ce dernier servant à la fois de système de recharge et de batterie externe pouvant recharger plusieurs fois la monture. Hélas, ce n'est pas le cas ici.
HTC se fend d'un système certes fonctionnel, mais assez décevant. L'étui des Vive Eagle est tout à fait classique, à cela près qu'il dispose d'une petite poche supplémentaire pour avoir toujours avec soi le câble de recharge. Nous y reviendrons plus bas.
Un module photo ultra grand-angle avec capteur de 12 Mpx se niche dans la charnière gauche, une led blanche témoin prenant place dans la charnière opposée. Ce module permet de capturer des photos de 3024 x 4032 pixels avec HDR et des vidéos verticales en 1512 x 2016 pixels à 30 images par seconde (i/s), auxquelles s'ajoute un mode ralenti à 120 (i/s) en 960 x 1280. Les clips sont plafonnés à 10 min, et les 32 Go de stockage absorbent environ 3000 photos ou une cinquantaine de vidéos.
Force est de constater que cette fiche technique est en retrait de la référence actuelle du marché, les Ray-Ban Meta de seconde génération filmant jusqu'en 3K (2384 x 3168 pixels). Autre bémol, le rapatriement des images ne se fait pas tout seul. Il faut ouvrir l'app Vive, se connecter au réseau wifi généré par les lunettes elles-mêmes et importer manuellement ses fichiers. Une gymnastique qui lasse vite quand on multiplie les captures. Toutefois, de ce point de vue, les Meta ne font pas mieux.
Le rendu des photos et vidéos capturées par les Vive Eagle est correct, sans plus. En outre, cela ne concerne que la captation avec des conditions de luminosité idéales. Quand la lumière vient à manquer, la production de ces lunettes s'avère difficilement exploitable.
Deux haut-parleurs stéréo ouverts diffusent le son vers les oreilles sans les obstruer, format oblige. HTC les présente comme dotés de basses renforcées, une promesse maison formulée sans plus de détails techniques, ni puissance ni réponse en fréquence.
La partie captation paraît plus travaillée avec quatre microphones au total, dont un module directionnel placé au niveau du pont nasal pour isoler la voix du porteur, les trois autres étant omnidirectionnels. Un attelage qui sert autant les appels (le Bluetooth 5.3 est de la partie) que les interactions vocales avec l'assistant.
Un “Hey Vive” suffit à réveiller l'assistant. C'est ici que HTC se distingue, puisque l'utilisateur choisit le modèle qui lui répond : Gemini de Google, ChatGPT d'OpenAI ou l'assistant natif de son téléphone. Les commandes de base (déclencher une photo, lancer la musique, gérer un appel) sont traitées en local, directement sur les lunettes, tandis que les requêtes plus complexes sont anonymisées avant d'être transmises au modèle retenu.
La fonction Vive AI Notes complète le tableau en transcrivant les conversations, en distinguant les interlocuteurs et en générant des résumés, le tout chiffré en AES-256 et stocké localement, selon HTC. L'accès à l'IA passe toutefois par un abonnement Vive AI décliné en deux formules, Plus et Pro, toutes deux plafonnées par un quota mensuel de requêtes, sans aucune option illimitée. Heureusement, un essai conséquent de 24 mois à la formule Plus est inclus avec les lunettes, de quoi se faire une idée sur la durée.
HTC a bâti sa communication sur la protection des données et avance des gages concrets, à commencer par sa conformité aux normes ISO 27001 pour la sécurité de l'information et ISO 27701 pour la gestion des données personnelles. Les requêtes envoyées à Gemini ou ChatGPT sont donc dépersonnalisées avant transmission.
Côté captation, la led blanche s'allume pendant l'enregistrement et un capteur surveille sa visibilité. L'enregistrement s'interrompt si la diode est masquée ou si une personne à portée de micro prononce la commande “stop recording”. Au moment de notre test, le produit refusait tout bonnement les commandes en français, ce qui est particulièrement dommage pour un accessoire officiellement distribué dans notre verte contrée.
HTC se dit convaincu qu'il est impossible de filmer quelqu'un sans que la led reste visible en permanence. La réalité est moins flatteuse. Un simple morceau de carton noir correctement positionné suffit à masquer la diode sans interrompre la capture. Le dispositif a au moins le mérite d'exister, mais il n'est pas infaillible.
Avec leur batterie de 235 mAh, les Vive Eagle promettent 4,5 h d'écoute musicale, 3 h d'appels et 36 h en veille. C'est évidemment le nerf de la guerre sur ce type de produit, mais ces chiffres font pâle figure face aux Ray-Ban Meta, créditées de 8 h d'utilisation et livrées avec un étui de recharge offrant jusqu'à 40 h supplémentaires. Comme vu plus haut, l'étui ne permet pas la recharge ici. À l'usage, en écoutant de la musique, des podcasts et en passant quelques appels, les lunettes peinent à dépasser la demi-journée d'autonomie.
Le constructeur compense en partie par la recharge rapide, revendiquant 50 % de batterie récupérée en 10 min et 80 % en 23 min, des valeurs qu'il annonce sans en détailler la méthode de mesure.
Dommage que cette recharge passe par un connecteur magnétique propriétaire relié à un câble USB-C qu'il faudra veiller à ne pas égarer. Pour tenir la journée, HTC propose enfin le PowerBoost, une batterie d'appoint de 120 mAh qui se clipse magnétiquement sur la monture, en option (évidemment).
Les Vive Eagle ont quelques arguments en leur faveur pour qui place la confidentialité et la liberté logicielle en tête de ses priorités. Le choix entre plusieurs IA, le traitement local des commandes de base, le chiffrement des transcriptions et les certifications ISO composent un dossier irréprochable sur le papier, bien meilleur que la concurrence. Néanmoins, si ces préoccupations ne sont pas tout en haut de votre liste et que vous cherchez avant tout des lunettes pour capturer vos souvenirs ou écouter de la musique du matin au soir, les Ray-Ban Meta gardent l'avantage avec une définition vidéo supérieure, une autonomie nettement plus généreuse et un tarif de départ plus doux.
Difficile de comparer ces Vive Eagle à autre chose qu'à des Meta Ray-Ban à l'heure actuelle, tant l'étasunien écrase de sa présence ce marché. L'affrontement tourne court tant Meta a accumulé d'expérience sur ce segment des lunettes connectées. À date, son offre comporte une multitude de montures aux styles très différents et qui profitent pour la majorité de marques reconnues dans le monde de l'optique, telles que Ray-Ban ou Oakley. Les lunettes de HTC gardent en revanche l'avantage pour tout ce qui touche à la confidentialité et aux performances de l'assistant d'IA.

articles.text:
Lidl suele tener muchísimos productos en su sección Bazar, y lo bueno es que dicha sección se va renovando semanalmente, lo que nos deja con muchísimas novedades cada poco tiempo. Ahora mismo en su tienda online tenemos un espumador de leche que destaca sobre todo por dos cosas: su color pastel en verde (también lo hay en rosa) y su precio de 17,99 euros.
Si se acaba agotando (el color negro ya se ha agotado), y como alternativa, Amazon tiene de oferta el espumador de leche Philips Senseo por 66,29 euros. Es bastante más caro que el de Lidl, pero es el que tengo en casa y funciona muy bien. Los resultados son muy cremosos y funciona con leche de soja.

Este espumador ofrece una potencia de 500W para poder conseguir buenos resultados y el interior cuenta con un revestimiento antiadherente para evitar que se queden pegados los restos de leche. articles.title: Près de 80 % des Français ont des données en vente sur le darknet
articles.text:
Environ 80 % des Français ont une partie de leurs informations personnelles en vente sur le darknet, a prévenu hier à Toulon le général André Petillot, major général de la gendarmerie. Des escrocs peuvent ensuite acheter ces fichiers pour monter de faux dossiers de prêt ou des arnaques.
Lors des Rencontres stratégiques de la Méditerranée, organisées par la fondation FMES, le général a précisé que certains Français sont bien plus exposés que d’autres. « Il y a des gens pour lesquels il y a tout », a-t-il ajouté, avant d’énumérer les coordonnées postales et électroniques en vente, jusqu’aux données de santé. D’après une étude publiée en juillet, 43,4 millions de comptes français ont été compromis entre janvier et juin 2026. Sur six mois, la hausse est de plus de 62 %. Pour Karim Hamia, expert en cybersécurité chez Check Point Software Technologies, interrogé en août par l’AFP, la France est le deuxième pays le plus touché par les fuites d’informations, derrière les États-Unis. Et une fois les fichiers vendus, leurs acquéreurs peuvent aussi exploiter ces informations hors ligne, jusqu’à la porte des victimes.
Des données volées exploitées jusque chez les victimes
On a documenté sur Clubic la cyberattaque menée contre le fisc. Des pirates lui ont dérobé, fin juin puis fin juillet, les données de 678 000 particuliers et professionnels. Le groupe ZeroBytes, dont un membre présumé de 18 ans a été mis en examen et écroué début septembre, avait affirmé mi-août à l’AFP avoir vendu ces fichiers à deux acheteurs contre plusieurs milliers d’euros. Impossible de vérifier cette vente, mais la DGFiP a prévenu un par un les usagers concernés contre de possibles escroqueries ciblées.
Pour les tireurs sportifs, le risque est physique. Des pirates ont pénétré en octobre 2025 dans le logiciel de gestion des licences de la Fédération française de tir, et des criminels auraient ensuite exploité ces fichiers pour localiser des licenciés et cambrioler leur logement à la recherche de leurs armes, rapporte l’AFP.
Pour Hugues Foulon, directeur général d’Orange Cyberdéfense, présent à Toulon aux côtés du général Petillot, « un certain nombre d’infrastructures publiques ne sont pas à la hauteur » du niveau de protection exigé aujourd’hui.

articles.title: Volkswagen ID. Tiguan : on a vu le SUV qui veut faire oublier l'ID.4 - Numerama
articles.text:
Volkswagen est en grand ménage de printemps dans sa gamme électrique. Il va être l’heure de faire ses adieux aux ID.4 et ID.5. Les deux modèles vont être remplacés par l’ID. Tiguan, dont on vous a déjà dévoilé quelques éléments le 28 septembre.
Un changement de nom qui n’est pas anodin : le constructeur capitalise sur l’aura de son SUV star (vendu à plus de 8,3 millions d’exemplaires depuis 2007) pour rassurer et séduire les familles en quête d’un véhicule électrique spacieux, sérieux et abouti. Voici tout ce qu’il faut retenir de cette nouveauté.
Un design à la sauce « True Volkswagen »
Le design de l’ID.4 a souvent été pointé du doigt pour ses rondeurs qui juraient avec le reste de la gamme du constructeur. Avec l’ID. Tiguan, Volkswagen corrige le tir. Ce nouveau modèle inaugure la philosophie stylistique de la marque, baptisée Pure Positive, que l’on retrouve aussi sur les nouveautés électriques de 2026. L’objectif est au passage de gommer la différenciation stylistique de la gamme ID, pour en faire un SUV plus statutaire et robuste, comme l’est le Tiguan thermique actuel.
Ce changement de cap est particulièrement visible sur la face avant. L’ID. Tiguan adopte un capot plus plat et haut, et surtout une calandre plus expressive. Le tout est souligné par une signature lumineuse inédite : un bandeau LED horizontal transparent que les designers surnomment « l’aquarium » (en espérant que cela n’en devienne pas un vrai au fil des ans). Il intègre le logo VW illuminé et surplombe les projecteurs IQ.LIGHT.
De profil, les proportions évoluent avec une longueur de 4,61 mètres (3 cm de plus que l’ID.4) et un empattement généreux de 2,76 mètres (similaire à l’ancienne version). Volkswagen réintroduit d’ailleurs de « vraies » poignées de porte creusées, nettement plus pratiques et ergonomiques que les anciens systèmes affleurants de la gamme ID.
À l’arrière, on retrouve un large bandeau lumineux 3D très soigné, qui assoit visuellement la voiture sur la route. C’est classique, très Volkswagen dans l’esprit, mais le bond en termes de prestance est indéniable. Et ce, même dans ce coloris « Bronze olive métallisé » un peu particulier à mon goût.
Un habitacle transfiguré et l’arrivée du troisième écran
C’est à l’intérieur que la comparaison est la plus rude pour l’ID.4. L’ID. Tiguan balaie l’ancienne planche de bord austère pour proposer un environnement plus cohérent avec la tendance du moment. Les matériaux et les finitions montent d’un cran, avec l’utilisation de similicuir moussé et de tissus recyclés (Seaqual) sur la planche de bord et les contreportes. C’est plus cohérent.
Mais c’est surtout la débauche d’écrans qui interpelle. Outre un affichage tête haute à réalité augmentée et une dalle centrale XXL de 15 pouces placée au cœur de la planche de bord, le passager a désormais droit à son propre écran tactile de 12 pouces. C’est évidemment une option, mais c’est habituellement réservé aux véhicules plus haut de gamme. Précisons qu’un filtre de confidentialité l’empêche bien sûr d’être vu par le conducteur, permettant au passager de regarder un film ou de jouer en toute tranquillité, avec le son diffusé dans des écouteurs Bluetooth indépendamment.
Avec le renouvellement de la gamme cette année, on ne cesse de radoter la même chose : Volkswagen a appris de ses erreurs ergonomiques passées. Le constructeur réintroduit de vrais boutons physiques (notamment sur le nouveau volant) et a placé une barre de commandes pour la climatisation et un bouton rotatif au centre pour le volume audio. Et à l’usage, c’est vraiment un grand « oui » de notre part.
Le nouveau gimmick du skin rétro chez Volkswagen
Pour apporter un brin de folie à cet habitacle très/trop sérieux, Volkswagen a intégré un mode « Retro » aux deux écrans. Mais la petite subtilité sur l’ID. Tiguan, c’est qu’il ne s’agit pas du même que sur l’ID. Polo, l’ID. Cross et l’ID.3 Neo.
D’une pression sur le volant, vous pouvez transformer les compteurs numériques pour reproduire fidèlement l’affichage iconique (bleu et rouge) de la Golf IV. Et pour aller plus loin, l’écran central peut même afficher les graphismes d’anciens systèmes multimédias ou les silhouettes de la Golf 1, de la Coccinelle ou du premier Tiguan. C’est gadget, mais cool, surtout pour les plus nostalgiques. J’ai quand même une préférence pour le mode rétro de l’ID. Polo. L’écran façon Golf IV (et autres modèles de cette époque), ça m’embarque moins.
Une familiale taillée pour la route
Derrière son changement stylistique, l’ID. Tiguan repose sur une évolution de la plateforme électrique du groupe, rebaptisée MEB+. Néanmoins, l’esprit reste similaire à ce que propose l’ID.4. Il n’y a pas de grosse révolution.
La gamme s’articule autour de trois niveaux de puissance et deux tailles de batterie, couvrant tous les besoins des familles :
| Caractéristiques | Entrée de gamme | Cœur de gamme | 4MOTION | 
| Puissance & Transmission | 140 kW / 190 ch (Propulsion) | 210 kW / 286 ch (Propulsion) | 220 kW / 299 ch (Intégrale) | 
| Batterie (chimie) | 58 kWh (LFP) | 77 kWh (NMC) | 77 kWh (NMC) | 
| Autonomie WLTP (estimée) | Jusqu’à 450 km | Jusqu’à 600 km | Jusqu’à 560 km | 
| Performances (0 à 100 km/h) | 8,5 s | 6,6 s | 6,3 s | 
| Vitesse maximale | 160 km/h | 180 km/h | 180 km/h | 
| Recharge rapide DC (10 à 80 %) | 105 kW (env. 26 min) | 165 kW (env. 29 min) | 165 kW (env. 29 min) | 
| Capacité de remorquage | 1 800 kg | 2 000 kg | 2 000 kg | 
Par rapport à l’ID.4 actuel, le futur ID. Tiguan ne révolutionne pas la fiche technique : il reprend les batteries de 58 et 77 kWh ainsi que les motorisations de 190 à 299 ch. Il se distingue surtout par une capacité de remorquage portée jusqu’à 2 000 kg et par une autonomie maximale annoncée à 600 km, tandis que sa puissance de recharge de 165 kW reste légèrement inférieure à celle de l’ID.4 équipé de la batterie de 77 kWh.
L’ID. Tiguan offre 534 litres de coffre et, nouveauté très attendue pour éviter de vider la malle en cours de route, un « frunk » sous le capot avant pour ranger les câbles de recharge, mais c’est à peu près tout ce qui tiendra dans cet espace. Ajoutez à cela une capacité de remorquage allant jusqu’à 2 tonnes sur les versions les plus puissantes, et vous obtenez un véhicule polyvalent.
L’ID. Tiguan n’est peut-être pas le véhicule le plus exubérant du marché, mais il coche consciencieusement toutes les cases de la familiale accomplie. Son arrivée sur le marché européen est prévue pour le début de l’année prochaine. En attendant, vous pourrez le découvrir au Mondial de l’Auto de Paris du 12 au 18 octobre 2026.
L’ID. Tiguan sera vendu en France à partir de 43 990 €. Les préventes seront ouvertes dès le 13 octobre 2026.

articles.title: Laut Harvard-Studie kann KI die Produktivität in der Software-Entwicklung steigern: Warum der Effekt trotzdem verpufft
articles.text:
Laut Harvard-Studie: Warum Software-Entwickler durch KI nicht wirklich produktiver sind
KI kann die Produktivität beim Programmieren zwar steigern, aber die Gewinne schlagen sich weder im Ergebnis noch im Arbeitsaufwand nieder. Der Grund: Entwickler:innen müssen mehr Zeit für die manuelle Prüfung von KI-generiertem Code aufwenden. Zu diesem Ergebnis kommen Fiona Chen und James Stratton von der Universität Harvard in ihrer Studie, die den Titel Künstliche Intelligenz im Unternehmen: Engpässe in der Software-Produktion trägt. Für ihre Analyse nutzten die beiden Co-Autor:innen einen neuartigen Datensatz, der auf 300 Millionen Arbeitsergebnissen der Engineering-Analytics-Plattform Jellyfish basiert.
KI-Tools sparen beim Coding (ein bisschen) Zeit
Ziel der Studie war es, herauszufinden, wie sich der Einsatz von Coding-Tools und KI-Agenten konkret auf die Arbeit von Entwickler:innen auswirkt. Der Datensatz deckt den Zeitraum von Januar 2021 bis März 2026 ab und umfasst Informationen zur Arbeit von über 700.000 Beschäftigten aus 718 Unternehmen. Um die Auswirkungen generativer KI-Tools auf die Produktivität zu untersuchen, betrachteten die Autor:innen drei zentrale Kennzahlen: die erstellten Codezeilen, Commits und Pull-Requests. Dadurch ließ sich überprüfen, ob Entwickler:innen mit der Hilfe von KI tatsächlich in der Lage sind, in kürzerer Zeit mehr funktionierenden Code zu schreiben.
Reaktive KI-Assistenten führten zu einem leichten Anstieg des Code-Outputs. Entwickler:innen schrieben mit ihnen zwölf Prozent mehr Codezeilen, die Commits stiegen um neun und die Pull-Requests um fünf Prozent. Laut den Forscher:innen sei allerdings nur der Effekt auf die Commits statistisch signifikant. Teilautonome KI-Agenten hingegen konnten alle drei Kennzahlen signifikant anheben: Die generierten Codezeilen stiegen um 30 Prozent, die Commits um 20 Prozent und die Pull-Requests um 23 Prozent. Damit decke sich die Analyse mit den Ergebnissen anderer Studien, liege allerdings am unteren Ende der Bandbreite.
Die Überprüfung von KI-Code dauert länger
Diese Steigerungen hätten laut den Forscher:innen allerdings keinen Effekt auf den Output. Auch bei der Gesamtbeschäftigung zeige sich kein signifikanter Effekt. „Wir sehen Anzeichen für einen Engpass im Überprüfungsprozess des Codes”, heißt es in der Studie. „Die durchschnittliche Zeit für die Überprüfung eines Pull-Requests steigt um 49 Prozent, der Anteil der Pull-Requests, bei denen Änderungen verlangt werden, verdoppelt sich fast und die Anzahl der Kommentare pro Pull-Request steigt um 35 Prozent.“ Unternehmen würden die Kapazität ihrer Mitarbeiter:innen deshalb zunehmend in Richtung Überprüfungsaktivitäten verlagern. Der Anteil derer, die Code-Reviews durchführen, sei um 14 Prozent gestiegen. Dieser Engpass bleibe auch nach der Einführung von KI-Tools für Code-Reviews bestehen. Menschliche Prüfer:innen würden also weiterhin eine zentrale Rolle spielen.
Um die Validität ihrer quantitativen Analyse zu überprüfen, führten die beiden Harvard-Forscher:innen zusätzlich qualitative Interviews durch. Sie befragten 21 Personen aus verschiedenen Unternehmen, darunter Entwicklungsleiter:innen, Software-Entwickler:innen und Produktmanager:innen. Ein:e leitende: Entwickler:in berichtete, dass KI-Tools für Routineaufgaben bereits gut trainiert seien. „Mit Claude Code kann ich in zwei Sekunden einen Entwurf schreiben, der in 90 Prozent der Fälle korrekt ist“, heißt es in der Studie. „Bei anspruchsvolleren technischen Aufgaben spart es nicht so viel Zeit – es macht häufig Fehler und man verbringt letztendlich mehr Zeit mit der Überprüfung.“ Ein:e Junior-Software-Entwickler:in bestätigte, dass KI rund 95 Prozent der Aufgabe erledigen könne und die Arbeit dadurch deutlich beschleunigt werde. „Die restlichen fünf Prozent bestehen darin, herauszufinden, was es falsch gemacht hat, und es zu korrigieren.“

articles.title: Microsoft: Outdated Windows devices will stop receiving security updates
articles.text:
Microsoft says devices running unsupported versions of Windows will stop receiving security updates after next year's Windows Update certificate rotation.
To ensure devices keep receiving updates, admins and users must upgrade to a supported version of Windows before the Windows Update certificates expire in May and June 2027.
"As a standard security practice, these certificates have an expiration date. This means that they eventually need to be rotated (that is, replaced by new certificates). A set of these certificates will expire on May 17, 2027 and June 19, 2027," Microsoft said on Thursday.
It also added that devices on unsupported versions of Windows "will lose access to Windows Update services and won't receive any updates as a result" and recommended "upgrading to a supported version of Windows client or server."
In a separate Microsoft 365 Message Center update, it also noted that replacement certificates have already been delivered to systems running a supported Windows version and don't require additional action if they're up to date.
Microsoft shared the following detailed guidance on the required actions by Windows version:
- Windows 11, version 25H2 and later: No action is required.
- Windows 11, version 24H2 and Windows Server 2025: Install the September 2025 security update or later before June 19, 2027.
- Other supported versions of Windows 11, Windows Server 2022, and Windows 10: Install the July 2026 security update or later before June 19, 2027.
- Windows 10 Enterprise 2019 LTSC, Windows Server 2019, and Windows Server 2016: Install the July 2026 security update or later before May 17, 2027.
- Other Windows versions: Upgrade to a supported version of Windows client or Windows Server.
Microsoft advised IT administrators to identify all devices running older or unsupported Windows versions before the Windows Update certificate rotation in 2027.
They should also deploy monthly Windows updates on all supported devices to keep them up to date and create an upgrade plan for unsupported devices before May and June 2027.
"And if you do need to act on older device populations, there's still time! Review, update, and plan upgrades for unsupported versions before the May 2027 or June 2027 certificate expiration dates," it added.
However, this doesn't apply to devices that receive updates from Windows Server Update Services (WSUS), which downloads updates and distributes them across enterprise networks.
Last month, Microsoft released Windows 11, version 26H2 (also known as the Windows 11 2026 Update), which is now generally available for eligible Windows 11 24H2 and 25H2 systems as a small enablement package (instead of a full OS replacement) in a phased rollout that will expand over the next few months.

articles.title: La 5G est-elle devenue la norme en France ? Ce que révèlent les derniers chiffres
articles.text:
À votre avis, est-ce que les forfaits 5G sont aujourd’hui majoritaires en France ? La réponse est non, mais on s’en rapproche. Dans son observatoire des marchés publié ce jeudi 8 octobre, l’Arcep indique qu’au deuxième trimestre 2026, 37,5 millions de cartes SIM étaient actives sur les réseaux 5G dans le pays. Elles représentent 44 % des 84,7 millions de cartes SIM en service, contre 34 % un an plus tôt.
Sur un an, le nombre de cartes actives en 5G bondit pourtant de 32 %, soit 9,1 millions de plus. Comme le parc total n’a gagné que 580 000 cartes SIM sur la même période, il s’agit surtout d’abonnés existants qui sont passés à la 5G. Quant à la 4G, elle n’a pas dit son dernier mot avec une augmentation de 2 % du nombre de cartes actives en 4G sur la même période. Nous sommes tout de même loin de la période 2018-2021, où la hausse oscillait entre 10 et 13 % par an : avec 91 % des cartes SIM déjà actives en 4G, il ne reste plus grand monde à convertir.
De plus en plus de cartes SIM 5G pour toujours plus de données
Si la 5G a le vent en poupe, c’est d’une part parce que la couverture 5G du pays continue de s’étendre, d’autre part parce que de plus en plus de clients ont à la fois un smartphone compatible et un forfait qui inclut la 5G, explique l’Arcep.
Passer à la 5G ne fait pourtant pas grimper la consommation de chacun. Dans le détail des chiffres de l’Arcep, une carte SIM active en 5G consomme en moyenne 27,8 gigaoctets par mois au deuxième trimestre 2026, contre 27,9 gigaoctets un an plus tôt. Les utilisateurs 5G restent de plus gros consommateurs, avec 46 % de données en plus que les clients actifs en 4G, mais l’arrivée de 9 millions de nouveaux utilisateurs n’a pas fait bouger leur moyenne.
Sur le 2e trimestre 2026, 4,6 exaoctets de données ont été consommés via les réseaux mobiles. Pour vous donner une idée, ça fait 4,6 milliards de gigaoctets. Un chiffre en hausse, +9,4 %, mais qui ralentit puisque l’on était habitué à +13 % ces deux dernières années.
Ramené à l’échelle d’un seul client, cela fait 19,3 gigaoctets de données par mois, toujours sur le second trimestre de cette année. Soit 1,5 gigaoctet de plus sur un an (+8,5 %). L’Arcep note que l’augmentation est plus forte quand on s’intéresse aux clients des opérateurs français qui utilisent leurs forfaits à l’étranger : +24 % sur un an.
Pour les abonnés, cette consommation en hausse va de pair avec une facture en baisse. D’après l’Arcep, la facture mensuelle moyenne par carte SIM tombe à 13,70 euros HT au deuxième trimestre 2026, soit 70 centimes de moins qu’un an plus tôt ; pour un forfait, elle passe de 15,20 à 14,40 euros HT. Le revenu des opérateurs sur les services mobiles recule ainsi de 4 % sur un an, notamment sous l’effet des baisses de prix intervenues en 2024.

articles.title: Why Moove is leaving the Nigerian market it was built in
articles.text:
Six years after Moove put 76 cars on Lagos roads and asked Uber drivers to pay for them out of their earnings, the mobility company is leaving Nigeria, its founding market, and handing many of those drivers their cars.
In a statement on Thursday, Moove said it will hand over eligible vehicles worth about ₦35 billion ($26.3 million) to the drivers, with no further payment due from October 1. Every Moove employee will also get a free car. The announcement came five weeks after Uber, Moove’s investor and its only ride-hailing partner in Nigeria, exited the country.
“Nigeria will always be where Moove started,” the company said in its statement, describing the handover as its way of thanking the customers and staff who built the business.
Moove’s exit is a knock-on effect of Uber leaving Nigeria. If you think of Moove’s Nigerian business as a lending business, then it relied on Uber earnings data to decide who got a car and ensure they kept paying. When Uber left Nigeria, that data went with it, and Moove lost its way to price and collect those loans.
With Moove’s future in robotaxi depots in the United States, its Nigerian business, which faced many challenges, no longer represents a solid business opportunity.
How we got here
When the International Finance Corporation (IFC), the World Bank’s private-sector lender, invested in Moove in 2021, it described a product that financed up to 95% of a car over two to four years, with drivers repaying a share of their weekly platform earnings. Uber was picked as the platform.
That same year, Ladi Delano, Moove’s co-founder and co-CEO, told Bloomberg that the company used ride-hailing earnings and performance data to make its credit decisions. Moove shared offices with Uber in Lagos, Johannesburg and Accra and said it had no plans to work with any of Uber’s rivals, including Bolt.
The exclusivity was essential to the business model. Moove kept its Nigerian drivers on Uber Go, Uber’s budget category, and in 2022 said it couldn’t generate the data it needed to underwrite loans if drivers used several ride-hailing apps.
The model depended on two things Moove did not control: Uber’s demand and the naira.
Moove funded part of its Nigerian fleet with dollar-denominated debt while its drivers earned in naira. When the naira fell, it hit Moove’s pricing. In February 2023, TechCabal reported that drivers paid ₦9,400 ($14.57) daily for Suzuki SUVs priced at ₦11.7 million ($18,134). Suzuki’s Nigerian retail price was ₦9.9 million ($15,344).
By 2025, Moove’s weekly remittance had doubled, going from ₦56,400 ($87) to ₦112,200 ($74). At 2025’s average exchange rate, ₦112,200 came to about $74 a week. That is less than the roughly $87 that ₦56,400 was worth at 2023’s rate.
While the naira was in freefall, drivers saw a lender squeezing them. They went on strike, and by November the Lagos State chapter of the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC), the country’s largest trade union, was planning a protest at Moove’s office.
Demand on UberGo was also thinning. In January 2025, Moove drivers told Technext that ride requests had dried up and some were missing their targets. Some drivers said Moove sent agents posing as riders to catch them working on inDrive. Despite Uber losing market share to Bolt and inDrive, Moove kept its drivers tied to Uber.
Uber and Moove’s deep relationship
Uber called Moove its preferred fleet partner in sub-Saharan Africa. In March 2024, the ride-hailing giant led Moove’s $100 million Series B at a $750 million valuation, its first investment in an African startup, owning more than 10%.
When Nigerian drivers protested unfair working arrangements in 2023, Uber kept its distance, saying it had been made aware of concerns from a small group of drivers.
Hours after Uber’s exit on September 2, Moove dropped the Uber-only rule drivers had demanded for years. That solved the drivers’ problem but ended the single data stream Moove’s lending relied on. By then, Nigeria was already a small part of Moove.
In December 2024, Waymo, Alphabet’s self-driving car unit, hired Moove to run fleet operations, depots and charging in Phoenix and Miami. In August, Moove raised $250 million at a $2.1 billion valuation, reporting about 42,000 vehicles in 29 cities across 13 countries and $420 million in annual recurring revenue. The new funding will finance self-driving fleets and robot-run depots the company calls Nests. Nigeria is not a destination for any Nest, because the country cannot support the self-driving technology at scale.
Today’s handover looks like Moove’s cheapest way out. Without Uber’s data, Moove would have to collect repayments from drivers now working for Bolt and inDrive, in naira, for a company that no longer has Nigeria in its focus.
Giving drivers ownership ends a years-long fight and buys goodwill. Whether it is also generous depends on a number Moove has not shared: how much those drivers still owed on October 1.
Moove started in Lagos by putting cars in drivers’ hands on credit. Delano once said Nigeria taught Moove how to finance and run a fleet, and many of the drivers who paid for that lesson now keep the cars.
True scale demands moving beyond surface-level integrations to robust execution. We’ve filtered the noise out of Moonshot 2026, optimising the conference strictly for high-calibre connections between startup founders, global financial operators, enterprise leaders and individuals rewiring Africa’s technical frameworks. articles.title: Cloudflare acquires Node.js creator’s startup that copied its serverless playbook
articles.text:
Cloudflare acquires Node.js creator’s startup that copied its serverless playbook
Cloudflare is buying the startup co-founded by Node.js creator Ryan Dahl, a longtime competitor that recently built its own open-source version of Cloudflare’s serverless computing platform.
The company announced on Friday that the entire team behind Deno, the JavaScript and TypeScript runtime, is joining Cloudflare. Deno’s standalone runtime and cloud hosting service will be wound down, with its engineers turning their attention to Cloudflare Workers, the serverless computing platform unveiled in 2017 that allows developers to run applications without managing the underlying infrastructure.
Terms of the deal were not disclosed.
Deno’s Cloudflare-inspired project
Deno emerged in 2018 as Dahl’s attempt to address shortcomings in Node.js, particularly around security and dependency management. The startup, which raised around $26 million in funding across two rounds, later launched Deno Deploy, putting it in direct competition with Cloudflare Workers.
The companies have also experienced more than a little friction through the years. In 2021, Cloudflare mistakenly blocked Deno’s website and module registry after incorrectly identifying TypeScript files as video content, forcing Deno to move infrastructure elsewhere.
“Celld is a love letter to their idea; a primitive this good deserves to run anywhere.”
Then back in August, Deno introduced Celld, an open-source project that recreated Cloudflare’s Workers and Durable Objects programming model, for developers wanting to run distributed applications on their own infrastructure.
Deno made no secret of the inspiration. On the Celld website, the company explicitly credited Cloudflare distinguished engineer Kenton Varda and the Workers team for the underlying design, describing its project as a tribute to their work.
“Celld is a love letter to their idea; a primitive this good deserves to run anywhere,” the website states.
The admiration, it seems, was mutual. In a joint blog post published on Friday, Varda praised Deno’s expertise in an area where Cloudflare had perhaps struggled.
“The Deno team understands how to create a good developer experience around a self-hosted runtime — something we never quite cracked with workerd,” Varda writes.
Moreover, he also acknowledges that Cloudflare has struggled to make its open-source Workers runtime practical for developers operating outside its network.
“Frankly, we haven’t done a great job of building out the ecosystem of adjacent services and tooling to make it really work.”
“Frankly, we haven’t done a great job of building out the ecosystem of adjacent services and tooling to make it really work,” Varda continues. “We’d released the runtime, and then we sort of just hoped the community would step in and start adapting it to every possible environment.”
What’s next for Workers and Deno
Cloudflare now plans to merge Celld with Workerd, its existing open-source runtime, with Dahl and Deno co-founder Bert Belder leading the effort. The aim, ultimately, is to make it easier to build and operate distributed applications using Cloudflare’s programming model on independently managed infrastructure.
In an email Q&A, Dahl says the combined project is expected to remain open source, likely under the Apache 2.0 license already used by Celld. He also outlines how developers would be able to operate it without relying on Cloudflare’s infrastructure.
“Running a fleet of workerd instances will require only an industry-standard object storage bucket for coordination and storage,” Dahl tells The New Stack. “The API will be the same as Cloudflare’s own platform — which is a good thing.”
Asked what guarantees developers would have against vendor lock-in, Dahl argues that the project’s licensing and the team’s intentions were central to its independence.
“We believe only the open version wins here, because anything this fundamental to the future of how developers build on the web needs to be inspectable, portable, and usable outside a single vendor’s platform,” he continues. “We wouldn’t be trying this any other way but open, as there’d be no point.”
“We believe only the open version wins here, because anything this fundamental to the future of how developers build on the web needs to be inspectable, portable, and usable outside a single vendor’s platform.”
This decision also means Deno will stop developing its standalone runtime and hosting service, with the team instead focusing its efforts on the combined platform. The Deno runtime will receive monthly maintenance and security updates for another year, while Deno Deploy will shut down in six months, with migration assistance for paying customers. The JSR package registry will continue under Cloudflare.
Asked how much competition with Cloudflare Workers had influenced the move, Dahl points to the similarities between the two platforms and Deno’s increasing compatibility with Node.js.
“Deno Deploy was built towards the same ideals as Workers, this is why joining forces made so much sense,” he explains.
As for the runtime itself, Dahl says its growing compatibility with Node.js had effectively left Deno maintaining another implementation of the same technology.
“Many love the Deno runtime, and it remains MIT-licensed, but there are bigger problems that can be solved with a distributed programming model,” he adds.
JavaScript runtimes find a new home in AI
For what it’s worth, the acquisition follows Anthropic’s purchase of Bun in December 2025, which brought another prominent Node.js alternative under the ownership of a larger technology company. There is a key difference, however: Anthropic committed to continuing Bun’s development as an open-source JavaScript runtime, whereas Deno’s runtime development will end with its transition to Cloudflare.
In a separate blog post published on Friday, Dahl also highlights AI agents as an important application for the technology, particularly as developers look for simpler ways to manage the infrastructure underpinning them.
“The need for better abstractions is especially acute with AI,” Dahl writes. “Durable Objects bring together capabilities that are particularly useful for agent harnesses: inexpensive, serverless execution, persistent state, WebSockets, and a high-level JavaScript interface.”
For Cloudflare, the acquisition brings in an experienced engineering team and technology that addresses a longstanding gap in its Workers platform. For Deno, it marks the end of its independent runtime ambitions, even as the Cloudflare-inspired project it launched just two months ago becomes central to its future.

articles.title: Cloudflare K2 Builds Event Streams on R2 Object Storage, at a Second of Produce Latency
Being mean to AI could get you banned as Anthropic introduces new rules against abusing Claude
articles.text:
WTF?! You might have heard the one about being nice to chatbots in case they remember you once the machines take over. It seems Anthropic is heeding this warning, barring users from being excessively abusive or cruel toward its AI models.
Anthropic's first changes to its usage policy in over a year include new restrictions on abusive behavior. The updated policy prohibits "sustained and needless abusive or cruel behavior" toward its models.
Don't worry if you're a Claude user who occasionally gets annoyed at the chatbot and throws a few expletives its way. The policy update only applies in extreme cases, in which users repeatedly act cruelly toward the models for no discernible reason.
Anthropic also writes that the policy does not apply to common expressions of user frustration, pushback, dark creative themes, or model testing and research.
This change is an extension of a feature it introduced in August 2025. Anthropic said at the time that Claude would be allowed to end conversations with users in rare, extreme cases of persistently harmful or abusive interactions.
The company said the feature was developed primarily as part of its exploratory work on potential AI welfare, though it has broader relevance to model alignment and safeguards.
Anthropic says Claude's ability to end abusive interactions will remain the primary enforcement mechanism. Its wider policy allows warnings, restrictions, suspensions, or termination of access, so bans are a possibility.
In addition to its new rules against being mean to Claude, Anthropic is clarifying rules covering fake accounts and propaganda campaigns, weapons software, and surveillance.
The deceptive activity section brings together existing restrictions on political and commercial manipulation, including networks of fake accounts and fabricated news sites. Claude also cannot recommend who police should investigate or arrest.
The company is also dropping its blanket ban on personalized voter and campaign targeting, allowing legitimate civic work while keeping restrictions on deception and voter suppression.
There are clearer requirements for human oversight in areas such as health and finance, plus new safeguards for Claude controlling potentially dangerous hardware. A qualified operator must be able to monitor and stop the equipment, which must remain safe if Claude disconnects.
Other changes address non-consensual intimate imagery and clarify access restrictions involving unsupported regions, including companies majority-owned or controlled by people or entities based in those regions.
The updated policy takes effect on November 12, giving users a little time to work on their chatbot manners.

articles.title: Pre-Baked Firmware Malware Hits Budget Android Devices in 150+ Countries
articles.text:
There is a large global market for low-cost Android devices. Bad actors are aware and are servicing the demand through devices built on MediaTek platforms – but with malware preinstalled in the device firmware.
When the recipient of such an affected device switches it on, the malware is present, unseen, and available to any bad actor who can control it remotely from its C2. It is a persistent, pre-installed firmware system app that cannot be removed by normal uninstall procedures.
The campaign, dubbed Midnight Mimosa, was discovered and analyzed by Bitdefender.
The potential for this type of malware infection controlled via the actor’s C2 is massive. “The malware runs with system-level privileges that allow it to silently install and remove apps, grant permissions, and load arbitrary code supplied remotely. This essentially means its operators could install and delete apps at will, tuning each device to their needs, including making them part of large botnets,” writes the Bitdefender report.
Midnight Mimosa is focused on ad fraud, automated click fraud, and turning the device into a single component of a much larger botnet. This makes sense for a campaign seeking to fly under the radar with an army of soldiers. Many thousands of click frauds over a period of time would provide a healthy ROI for any bad actor. And botnets are described as a hot commodity that can be rented out to other bad actors. The bigger the botnet, the better the bounty.
Over the last two years, Bitdefender has observed thousands of unique affected devices in more than 150 countries. No single country or region dominates distribution. Mexico and France lead, followed by Italy, US, Germany, Brazil and Spain. Regionally, Western Europe and the Americas stand out. The report gives no indication of the actual monetary gain achieved by the Midnight Mimosa operators but does provide an extensive list of IoCs to help prevent it.
Bitdefender also found 13 apps on Google Play with separate signing certificates under two developer accounts and containing the same Midnight Mimosa ad-fraud code. “The campaign is not confined to preinstalled firmware. Thirteen applications published on Google Play were found carrying the same family markers as the dropped cover apps, in builds distributed by Play itself,” note the researchers.
These Play Store apps do not have the same privileged access as the preinstalled malware, but are considered associated with the broader ecosystem, giving the attackers an additional distribution channel.
Whether the malware is preinstalled or loaded from Play Store, it has been seen disabling the Play Store before installing additional payload applications and then re-enabling it afterward – probably to avoid detection by Play Protect. “Beyond suppressing the install prompt, the plugins blind Google Play Protect for the duration of the install,” note the researchers. “The malicious install happens in a window where Google’s scanner is switched off.”
Midnight Mimosa is best considered as a supply-chain threat where malware is largely integrated into the Android device prior to sale. The campaign is characterized by preinstalled persistence, system-level control, ad-fraud activity, proxy-network abuse and remote payload management. Attackers have extensive control over affected devices from the get-go.

articles.title: London’s Sava raises €32.08 million and partners with Ascensia to bring its glucose microsensor to Europe | EU-Startups
articles.text:
Sava Technologies, a London-based HealthTech company developing a wearable biosensor platform that detects molecules just beneath the skin, today announced a €32.08 million ($36 million) Series B round to fund manufacturing scale-up and commercial readiness.
The round was led by Ascensia, with participation from institutional investors Balderton Capital, Norrsken VC, Simplyhealth Ventures, JamJar Investments, Pentland Ventures and others. In July 2025, the company announced a €16.6 million Series A funding round led by Balderton Capital and Pentland Ventures.
This funding brings the company’s total funding to €60.6 million ($68 million). The UK startup also announced an agreement appointing Ascensia, a subsidiary of PHC Holdings Corporation (TYO 6523), as its commercialisation and distribution partner, initially in Europe.
Renato Circi, co-founder and Co-CEO of Sava, said, “For decades, continuous monitoring has been held back by the same legacy technology. This is about to change. We’re thrilled to be partnering with Ascensia, a global powerhouse in the space, to deliver, as a first step, something radically better to millions of people with diabetes.”
Founded in 2019 by Imperial College London bioengineers Renato Circi and Rafaël Michali, Sava is a venture-backed consumer and medical device company behind a next-generation glucose microsensor. After five years in stealth, it emerged in June 2024 and announced that it had raised more than €7.4 million in a Seed funding round led by Balderton Capital and Exor Ventures.
The company says it has developed a wearable built on its proprietary microsensor technology that measures molecules just beneath the skin, painlessly and continuously. While the platform starts with glucose, it is also designed to track other biomarkers, opening the door to continuous sensing far beyond diabetes.
According to Sava, its microsensors are about ten times shorter than the filament in traditional continuous glucose monitors (CGMs), reducing disruption to the skin while still reaching interstitial fluid.
The company notes that since the technology was designed from the outset for high-volume manufacture, it is built to reach people at scale. It is now focusing on commercialisation and has therefore partnered with Ascensia to get there at scale.
Basel-based Ascensia is a member of PHC Group and was established in 2016 through the acquisition of Bayer Diabetes Care by PHC Holdings Corporation. Ascensia sells its products in more than 90 countries, with direct commercial organisations in 29 markets. Its portfolio includes the CONTOUR range of blood glucose monitoring systems.
Peter Bodlund, Chief Executive Officer of Ascensia, commented, “Microsensor technology has the potential to transform the day-to-day monitoring experience for people with diabetes. By bringing together Sava’s innovative technology with Ascensia’s deep diabetes expertise, strong reputation and commercial capabilities, we have an exciting opportunity to address important unmet needs in diabetes care. This is an exciting step for Ascensia as we continue to broaden our portfolio and pursue our ambition to simplify and improve life for people with diabetes.”
Sava is also planning a pivotal clinical study this year and is targeting CE approval for non-adjunctive use. This means the device could be used to make insulin dosing decisions without routine fingerstick confirmation—the standard required for a CGM to replace, rather than supplement, blood glucose testing. Subject to CE approval, Ascensia will lead the commercial launch, starting in Europe.
The company plans to use this capital to fund manufacturing scale-up and commercial readiness.
