articles.title: Microsoft reveals the Surface Laptop Ultra - the most powerful product it has ever built - Tech Guide
articles.text:
Microsoft has released the Surface Laptop Ultra – the most powerful product the company has ever created – which has been engineered for next-level performance and AI.
The Microsoft Surface Laptop Ultra is powered by the new NVIDIA RTX Spark Superchip which includes NVIDIA AI, Blackwell RTX graphics, up to 20-core NVIDIA Grace CPU and up to 128GB of unified memory. It can also be configured with up to 2TB of storage.
It has a 15-inch MiniLED Ultra 120Hz touchscreen display with up to 2000 nits of peak HDR brightness.
The display offers Dolby Vision IQ and 100 per cent DCI-P3 colour gamut for incredible colour accuracy.
And it is all housed in an aluminium chassis that is just 18mm thick and weighs 2kg.
The Microsoft Surface Laptop Ultra is already drawing comparisons with Apple’s MacBook Pro.
Microsoft says when compared to a MacBook Pro with an M5 Pro chip, the Microsoft Surface Laptop Ultra offers 6.2x faster video generation and 4.3x faster image creation.
The Surface Laptop Ultra also has the largest thermal system Microsoft has ever included on a laptop it can cope with demanding workloads and still maintain peak performance.
The Surface Laptop Ultra user is designed for someone who will be video editing, CAD and 3D modelling and using professional technical applications.
And it’s also an impressive gaming computer with a screen that makes your games look amazing and a processor to make them responsive and immersive.
Naturally the Microsoft Surface Laptop Ultra is a Copilot+ PC with powerful AI capabilities.
It also includes CUDA support – part of the NVIDIA platform for accelerated computing – so it can handle demanding local AI workflows.
On the connectivity side the Surface Laptop Ultra has three USB-C, USB-A, HDMI, headphone jack and an SD card reader.
But it is also introducing a new port called Magnetic Connect – the world’s first magnetic USB-C charging port with the convenience of magnetic charging and a standard connection.
The Microsoft Surface Laptop Ultra is available to pre-order and starts at $4,399.
Is available in two colours – Nightfall and Platinum.
It goes on sale in the coming weeks.

articles.title: “Don’t use ‘open weight’ and ‘open source’ interchangeably”: Percona CEO on why AI terminology matters
articles.text:
“Don’t use ‘open weight’ and ‘open source’ interchangeably”: Percona CEO on why AI terminology matters
The AI industry has enthusiastically embraced the language of open source, even as some of its most prominent “open” models offer developers only a fraction of what that term has traditionally promised.
Speaking at Open Source Summit Europe in Prague on Wednesday, Peter Farkas, co-creator of the open source MongoDB alternative FerretDB and now CEO of open source database services company Percona, has a simple request: “Don’t use ‘open weight’ and ‘open source’ interchangeably,” he says.
“’Open source’ is only going to remain ‘open source’ as long as we preserve the actual meaning and the freedoms that are behind open source, and open weights are not providing that,” Farkas continues.
“’Open source’ is only going to remain ‘open source’ as long as we preserve the actual meaning and the freedoms.”
The distinction matters as open-weight models become a major part of production AI. In August, they accounted for 56% of tokens processed through Vercel’s AI Gateway and 60% of US-originating token consumption on OpenRouter, with Chinese-developed models accounting for the majority
An AI model’s weights are the numerical parameters produced during training that encode the patterns the model has learned. Making them available lets developers download and run a model on their own infrastructure, even when its creator hasn’t released the ingredients or process used to produce it.
“You don’t have the source code, you don’t have the training data, you only have the output of these two,” Farkas says. “So why would we call this open source in the first place?”
James Landay, director of Stanford’s Institute for Human-Centered AI (HAI), has drawn a similar distinction, arguing in an August HAI article that access to model weights alone falls short of what developers and researchers need from genuinely open-source AI.
“Open weights answer ‘can I run this?’” Landay said. “Open source answers ‘can I trust this, improve it, and build the next thing on top of it?’”
For now, Landay argues, the major AI labs are largely answering the first question while falling well short of the second.
“Open weights answer ‘can I run this?’ Open source answers ‘can I trust this, improve it, and build the next thing on top of it?’”
If “open washing wins”
Some companies are already going beyond releasing the weights. Xiaomi, for example, recently launched its MiMo-V2.6 models and livestreamed nearly a week of reinforcement-learning training through a public dashboard. The company also released more than 7,000 reinforcement-learning task environments, along with its RL training code and technical documentation, offering more transparency into how the models were fine-tuned.
Whether that’s enough for MiMo-V2.6 to qualify as “open source AI” is a separate question. Xiaomi’s release, however, illustrates the spectrum Farkas describes: “open” AI releases can reveal vastly different amounts of what went into building a model.
Farkas points to China’s DeepSeek as an example of the confusion, with its models widely described as open source despite the company releasing model weights rather than everything required to reproduce the models from scratch.
However, he stresses that the ability to download and run those models remains valuable in its own right.
“Are open weights a bad thing? No, open weights are great.”
“Are open weights a bad thing? No, open weights are great,” Farkas says. “You can run your models in your own environment, you can experiment with them, and if you understand the risks, you can also use it in production. The problem is when open weights are positioned as, ‘hey, this is as good as open source‘.”
Without a commonly understood boundary, Farkas argues, “open washing wins.” And he worries that accepting a looser meaning of open source for AI could ultimately weaken the definition for software more broadly.
“Companies are going to get away with calling something Apache 2.0 that [for example] you can’t use in the European Union,” Farkas says. “Open source AI is one thing, but if we talk about open source, and we let this happen to the core definition itself, that is going to go way beyond AI.”
A definition still under discussion
The Open Source Initiative (OSI) published its first Open Source AI Definition in 2024, establishing criteria around the freedoms to use, study, modify, and share AI systems. But the definition remains contested, particularly over what information about training data an AI system must disclose to qualify as open source.
Responding to Farkas from the audience, Duane O’Brien, who became the OSI’s new executive director in April, acknowledged the criticisms of its original definition and made clear that OSI is reopening the discussion.
“We did have a conversation two years ago — it was an important conversation, and two years is a long time in this space,” O’Brien says. “We are in the process of reopening and having another set of conversations.”
The OSI recently launched an Open Source AI Fellowship, appointing Gabriel Toscano as its first fellow to help build consensus around what constitutes open source AI. The two-year program will explore potential revisions to the definition, while OSI also plans a series of community discussions, or “open source salons,” over the next two years.
O’Brien encouraged Farkas and others to participate, while acknowledging the criticisms already leveled at the original definition.
“The criticisms that have been lodged against open source AI definition ‘one’ are valid,” O’Brien says. “We have to continue that conversation.”

articles.title: Anthropic Fast-Tracks AI Bug Reports to OSS Maintainers, Taps 11 Firms for OT Security
articles.text:
Anthropic on Thursday announced two new cybersecurity initiatives: one gives open source maintainers faster access to AI-generated vulnerability reports, and the other targets companies that help secure operational technology (OT).
The programs build on lessons from Project Glasswing. Anthropic said Glasswing partners uncovered many vulnerabilities, but admitted that it has not yet cut cyber risk enough.
According to the company, finding vulnerabilities has never been easier, but verifying, prioritizing and patching them remains hard. Flaws found through Glasswing often took months to get fixed.
Scanner reports reach maintainers without human review
Inspired by Google’s OSS-Fuzz, OSS Scanner is a free service that uses Anthropic’s most capable models to periodically scan open source projects. Maintainers have to opt in to have their projects scanned.
Each report explains the potential vulnerability, includes a PoC showing how it could be exploited and, when one is available, suggests a fix.
Anthropic launched the service after some OSS maintainers who can triage vulnerabilities at scale asked for everything its AI models had found in their projects, including unreviewed findings.
“The reports are model-generated and sent without human review,” the AI giant said.
Skipping review gets reports to maintainers faster, but Anthropic warned that some will contain inaccuracies, such as wrong severity ratings. It expects a true-positive rate above 90% and aims to improve it over time.
The service is meant for projects with the capacity to keep up with the findings. Other projects will continue to receive human-verified disclosures through Anthropic’s coordinated vulnerability disclosure process.
Critical infrastructure program targets OT providers
The Critical Infrastructure Defense Program (CIDP) brings frontier Claude models, on-site engineers and Anthropic’s threat research to the providers that power, water, manufacturing and transportation operators rely on for OT security.
The founding partners are Accenture, Booz Allen, CrowdStrike, Deloitte, Dragos, Hitachi, Insane Cyber, Nozomi Networks, Palo Alto Networks, PwC, and Rockwell Automation. They include consulting and technology firms, security vendors, and the manufacturers that build and patch industrial equipment.
Anthropic noted that OT systems often cannot be taken offline for patching, so known vulnerabilities can remain unresolved for years. In rare cases, it said, a patch could take decades to apply safely.
According to the company, several partners are already working with Claude to fix vulnerabilities and help customers do the same.
Anthropic is starting with a small group of providers to learn which strategies are most effective and practical. It plans to bring the program to more partners and sectors in the coming months.
Related: Anthropic Introduces 3-Tier Cyber Verification Program for AI Access
Related: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei Says AI Industry Needs to Give Safety Measures Time to Catch Up

articles.title: Bern-based Besso raises €4.29 million to scale its AI-powered trade regulation intelligence platform | EU-Startups
articles.text:
Besso, a Bern-based startup that helps companies manage the complexity of international trade regulations, has secured €4.29 million (CHF 4 million) in funding.
The funding came from a single large European family office, which opted to remain anonymous. This is a departure from traditional early-stage funding rounds, which have multiple backers, and the company says the funding raised from a single long-term investor was deliberate.
“We have always been very deliberate about building Besso around real customer demand rather than funding milestones. The traction we are seeing now tells us that the time is right to invest more aggressively in growth. Having one long-term investor take the entire round gives us both the resources and the focus to do exactly that,” said Philip Sieber-Gasser, founder and CEO of Besso.
Founded and headquartered in Bern, Switzerland, Besso helps multinational corporations turn the growing complexity of international trade regulation into a source of competitive advantage. It has built an AI platform that continuously monitors over 1,250 trade regulations and tariff schedules across global corridors, automatically identifying where companies are overpaying on duties and offering them opportunities to recover costs through preferential tariff rates and free trade agreement (FTA) eligibility.
According to the company, global tariff teams miss out on preferential tariff rates on around 30% of eligible shipments. This reportedly costs mid-size importers between $2 million and $15 million annually. In addition to cost, these trade teams are also grappling with more than 7,000 regulatory changes every week across major trade corridors, a figure that has grown due to geopolitics and tariff volatility.
Besso’s AI platform replaces the manual, error-prone processes reliant on spreadsheets, PDFs, and consultancy dependency that most companies currently use to manage their requirements. Besso has already built a strong roster of global clients, including Danone, Unilever, AB-InBev, BASF, Coca-Cola, Heineken, Philip Morris International and Syngenta. The company says additional Fortune 500 companies recently joined the platform.
Alongside its strong client base, the company has built a team with expertise in legal research and is supported by academic partners including the Geneva Graduate Institute, the World Trade Institute, and ETH Zurich. Its advisory board includes Jean-Daniel Gerber, a former Swiss Secretary of State for Economic Affairs, along with other leading trade law academics and AI specialists.
The company, a Venture Leaders alumnus, plans to use the funding to increase its headcount, scale capacity to serve a rapidly growing multinational customer base, and advance its technology platform through continued investment in product development and R&D.
“This is an important milestone for us, but the funding itself is not the destination. What matters is what it enables us to build from here,” added Sieber-Gasser.
With geopolitical uncertainty and shifting tariff regimes reordering the global supply chains, the demand for intelligent trade compliance tools is surging with NMSC forecasting the AI trade compliance market to reach €9.84 billion ($11.05 billion) by 2035, expanding at a 21.07% CAGR. Besso is positioning itself as the platform of record for multinationals looking to reduce trade-related costs and build more resilient supply chains.

articles.title: Calgary philanthropist donates $30 million to fund drone facility at SAIT | BetaKit
articles.text:
A Calgary philanthropist has donated $30 million to the Southern Alberta Institute of Technology (SAIT) to develop a training facility for autonomous and remotely piloted aircraft, also known as drones.
The news: On Thursday, SAIT announced plans to develop the Bissett Autonomous Aviation Park at its campus. Named after David Bissett, a long-time supporter of the technical institute whose donation made the facility possible, the park will be dedicated to training, testing, and certifying both remotely piloted aircraft systems (RPAS) and autonomous aerial vehicle systems.
From the source: “Autonomous flight is a new industry taking shape in real time. I want young Albertans to be building it, not watching it happen somewhere else,” Bissett said in a statement on Thursday. “A province’s prosperity depends on whether its people have the skills the global economy is asking for.”
The context: The Bissett Autonomous Aviation Park will serve a growing cohort of drone-focused programming at SAIT, which has a long history of aviation-based education. In 2023, it launched Western Canada’s first professional RPAS certificate program, and this fall launched the first RPAS diploma program.
The drone industry is growing at a feverish pace in Canada as the federal government looks to build out domestic drone manufacturing capacity and defence capabilities. It’s also been spurred on by deals between Canadian startups like Sentinel R&D and Ukraine’s Airlogix, the latter of which has helped build out an expansive drone development industry in Ukraine’s fight against Russia.
Final thought: In Canada, the drone market is expected to hit a $10-billion valuation by 2030. In Alberta, Calgary Economic Development identified autonomous aviation as an emerging driver within the city’s broader aerospace ecosystem, which itself is expected to grow to more than $4 billion by 2030. SAIT’s facility places the school in a position to train the professionals needed to meet that growing demand.
BetaKit’s Prairies reporting is funded in part by YEGAF, a not-for-profit dedicated to amplifying business stories in Alberta.

articles.title: Starlink Mobile just acquired additional spectrum, which could set it on the path to becoming a ‘major’ US carrier — but there are still some big obstacles
articles.text:
Starlink confirms plans to become ‘the world’s most advanced mobile network’ and a ‘major’ US carrier
New spectrum for improved coverage
- SpaceX has announced that it's acquired some low-band 800MHz spectrum for Starlink Mobile
- This is ideal for providing coverage indoors, and along with the launch of new satellites, it could pave the way for Starlink Mobile to become a 'major' carrier
- However, it's likely to still need both additional spectrum and significant investment in ground-based infrastructure
Only a week ago, AT&T’s CEO claimed that SpaceX’s Starlink Mobile plans weren’t viable, but perhaps he’ll be rethinking that claim now, as SpaceX has just announced that it's purchased 14Mhz of spectrum in the 800MHz band.
As explained in the company’s announcement, this is an ideal band for helping a signal penetrate obstacles like walls, ensuring that Starlink Mobile’s signal can be delivered inside buildings, and complementing the company’s existing mid-band spectrum, which is high-bandwidth and good for high-speed connections.
SpaceX claims that, as a result, it’s now positioned to build “the world’s most advanced mobile network” and to become “a major mobile carrier in the US,” by deploying this spectrum through a combination of its satellites and “an advanced terrestrial deployment” — meaning masts or other infrastructure on the ground.
Additionally, the FCC (Federal Communications Commission) has also approved Starlink Mobile’s Gen2 constellation application, allowing the company to launch 15,000 new satellites, which can apparently deliver more than 100 times the bandwidth of the current generation, for high-speed mobile service anywhere in the world.
Just the first step
So, this certainly sounds promising for the company, but it’s unlikely to mean the imminent launch of a major mobile service.
As Tim Farrar, an industry expert at TMF Associates, explained to CNBC, “This adds fuel to the fire in the battle between SpaceX and the mobile operators, but it’s still a very limited amount of spectrum, and to get reliable building penetration in urban areas, SpaceX would have to deploy towers on the ground.”
So, it’s likely that SpaceX will need both more spectrum and substantial ground-based infrastructure before the likes of AT&T, T-Mobile, and Verizon really need to worry. Still, this latest move suggests that SpaceX is serious about its Starlink Mobile ambitions — and that the major carriers might need to start looking to space if they want to remain top dogs in the long run.

articles.title: Xona's commercial GPS alternative is about to go live | TechCrunch
articles.text:
The first precision commercial alternative to GPS is preparing to go live when six satellites designed by the startup Xona Space Systems launch into orbit this month.
A service that competes with free signals provided by governments around the world may seem foolhardy, but Xona is hoping to add navigation and timing to the list of de facto government space monopolies disrupted by venture-backed startups.
Xona was founded in 2019 by a team of five engineers who originally met at Stanford University’s aerospace engineering graduate program. One, Tyler Reid, went on to earn a PhD, writing his thesis on the possibilities of using satellites in low-earth orbit to improve navigation.
GPS and analog satellite networks built by Europe, China, and Russia provide huge value, but are also easy to jam and aren’t precise enough to be used alone for applications like farming robots or self-driving cars. Over “pizza and beer chats,” the friends mulled whether fixing those problems could be a business.
“My knee jerk was like, this is dumb,” Xona CEO Brian Manning told TechCrunch during a recent visit to the company’s headquarters. “Why would anybody replace GPS? It’s free, right? And I started digging into it. People think of GPS as a free service, but the market isn’t the service. The market’s the hardware, and you have billions of devices being sold every year; those things aren’t being given away for free. There’s an immense market that is desperately looking for better performance.”
That didn’t mean the road to delivering such a service was simple. Improving GPS with a stronger signal that offers more precise timing and location data remained a technical challenge. The company needed to develop a unique architecture that would allow its satellites to keep time without expensive atomic clocks onboard, taking advantage of the spacecraft’s proximity to Earth and close communication with ground-based sources of truth.
The other technical challenge the company solved was making sure its signals could be received by existing GPS receivers with a relatively simple software modification. That gives Xona immediate access to the market and smoothes the way through the regulations for broadcasting navigation signals.
Later this month, a SpaceX rocket is scheduled to launch six satellites for Xona. Four are similar to a prototype the company launched last year that proved its technology; those satellites are built around a satellite platform from Aerospace Labs. The other two satellites were built entirely by Xona at its Burlingame, California, headquarters, and are intended to be the foundation of the company’s 258-satellite operational constellation, called Pulsar.
Pulsar will offer centimeter-level precision for geolocation, instead of the meter-level precision provided by GPS, and its signal is strong enough to be detected inside buildings and in urban environments. Manning also believes its signal is powerful enough to deter would-be jammers and spoofers, too.
Xona can begin beta-testing Pulsar with real customers once its satellites are in orbit and passing overhead the mid-latitudes about eight times a day.
Ian Gough, the CEO of TimeBeat, a company that specializes in electronic timing, says the initial pilot will allow his engineers to check and correct the timing provided by its devices around the world. By 2028, Xona hopes to offer full coverage in the U.S., Europe, Japan, and South Korea.
Xona has raised just over $300 million from venture investors since its founding, including $20 million from the U.S. Space Force. While the company is focused on offering a commercial service, the U.S. government is clearly interested in the technology, as jamming and spoofing of satellite navigation services become increasingly common in conflicts.
While there are literally billions of potential users for a new precision timing signal, Xona is also looking ahead to a world of growing autonomy. Reid, whose thesis inspired the company and who now serves as its CTO, worked on self-driving cars at Ford and saw that a service like Pulsar would be needed to realize the potential of autonomous vehicles of all stripes.
Xona’s headquarters boasts an incredible view of planes landing at San Francisco International Airport. Watching the jets come in, Manning points out that among “all the forms of mass transportation, the gold standard for safety is civil aviation. We see Xona and what we’re building being able to play a big part in that … to provide the service to a car, so you can feel as safe taking your hands off the wheel as you are laying back in an airliner.”

articles.title: No sólo potencia: los nuevos cargadores UGREEN Nexode Pro incorporan pantalla, cable retráctil y posibilidad de carga en remoto
articles.text:
Ahora que estamos en verano, preparar la maleta para los viajes requiere meter dentro todos los cargadores y cables que necesitamos. Cargadores para uno o dos teléfonos, para el portátil, para el reloj… Al final una maleta pequeña acaba llena de cables que se enrollan entre ellos. UGREEN pone fin a este problema con su nueva serie de cargadores Nexode Pro: cargadores muy potentes, versátiles y que simplifican todo al máximo.
UGREEN se ha especializado en este tipo de complementos, y la evolución que ha supuesto en algo tan sencillo como un cargador, es digno de valorar. No sólo por hacer cargadores con una gran potencia de carga, sino que también incluye algunas características como un display con información relacionada, la gestión de carga remota o el cable retráctil para hacer más sencilla y limpia la tarea de carga para el usuario.
Pero eso no es todo porque entre las características de estos nuevos cargadores también se encuentra potencias que van desde los 160W en cargadores de viaje hasta los 300W en los cargadores de escritorio, capacidad de cargar hasta 7 dispositivos a la vez y la tecnología GaNInfinity que permite mayor densidad de potencia con un rendimiento mejorado de eficiencia que evita que se sobrecaliente.
Vamos a ver en detalle cómo son los tres nuevos cargadores de UGREEN porque son una auténtica maravilla.
El primer cargador de 160W con cable retráctil
De los tres que acaba de presentar, el primero es el UGREEN Nexode Pro 160W. La mejor carta de presentación es que se trata del primer cargador de 160W con un cable retráctil que queda escondido cuando no lo estamos utilizando. De esa manera, queda todo mucho más limpio. La longitud del cable es de hasta 70 cm. Y no te preocupes por la durabilidad del sistema porque ha sido testado con más de 25.000 tirones para comprobar su resistencia.
Tiene una potencia de carga para ordenadores de 140W pero llega hasta los 160W de potencia total para todo tipo de dispositivos, como tablets, teléfonos o auriculares. Su sistema de carga inteligente es capaz de detectar de manera automática el tipo de dispositivo que hemos conectado para que de esta manera ajuste la potencia de carga.
También incorpora un cómodo display con el que podremos ver tanto la potencia de carga, el voltaje o la temperatura durante todo el proceso. Desde la aplicación de UGREEN también se puede personalizar y monitorizar todo lo relacionado con el proceso de carga.
Por último, es capaz de cargar de manera simultánea hasta 4 dispositivos. Tiene un precio de 129 euros pero lo puedes encontrar durante las próximas semanas por sólo 99,99 euros.
Lo más bestia en el mundo de los cargadores, para usuarios exigentes
Este cargador Nexode Pro 300W está pensado para todos aquellos usuarios que necesitan mucha potencia de carga en varios dispositivos, y destinado para ser utilizado en escritorios de trabajo. Con una increíble potencia de hasta 300W, no te faltará de nada.
Entre sus especificaciones, tiene 3 puertos USB-C de 140W. Puedes cargar tu portátil sin problema y dejar dos puertos libres para cargar cualquier otro dispositivo. Al igual que el modelo anterior, también cuenta con una pantalla inteligente donde ver todo lo relacionado con el proceso de carga y al mismo tiempo que desde la aplicación Ugreen Connect podemos incluso gestionar la carga de manera remota. También tiene cinco modos de carga inteligente en función del dispositivo que conectemos, de esa manera contribuimos a proteger la salud de la batería.
Con cargadores de tanta potencia, es sencillo preocuparse por la temperatura y los sobrecalentamientos. Para ello UGREEN incorpora su tecnología GaNInfinity que aumenta la eficiencia de carga al mismo tiempo que reduce el calor. Por otro lado, el sistema Thermal Guard es capaz de monitorizar la temperatura hasta 200 veces por segundo por lo que nuestros dispositivos estarán siempre controlados y protegidos.
En cuanto a uso, puedes cargar hasta siete dispositivos de manera simultánea. Es el cargador más polivalente que hay ahora mismo en el mercado. Tiene un precio de 165 euros pero lo puedes encontrar por poco tiempo por sólo 125,99 euros.
Un cargador compacto con cuatro puertos y 100W
Pequeño, compacto, potente y capaz de cargar cuatro dispositivos a la vez. El Nexode Pro Charger de 100W de UGREEN es el típico dispositivo que todo el mundo debería tener encima. Lo tiene todo en un tamaño muy pequeño: cuatro puertos (3 USB C y 1 USB A) con un sistema inteligente que ajusta el proceso y soporta prácticamente todos los estándares de carga.
Tiene también la tecnología GaNInfinity y el sistema de protección Thermal Guard por lo que no tienes que preocuparte por la salud ni del cargador ni de los dispositivos que conectes. Su precio habitual es de 59,99 euros pero lo podrás encontrar por sólo 45,99 euros durante algunos días de septiembre.
En resumen, UGREEN sigue innovando muchísimo en el terreno de los cargadores, llevando a los usuarios la mejor experiencia posible al mismo tiempo que cuida de la salud y la batería de nuestros equipos.

articles.title: Nikon microscopic video competition winner disqualified for using generative AI
articles.text:
Nikon says the video that originally won first place in its Small World in Motion contest “did not comply with the competition rules regarding generative AI.” BBC reports that the original first place video from Dr. Ning Xu claimed to show “tiny, hair-like structures called cilia moving in the airway of a child with the respiratory condition PCD.” Nikon said last week that it was reviewing the video following skepticism online about its authenticity.
Nikon microscopic video competition winner disqualified for using generative AI
Nikon says it’s revisiting its competition rules after the original winner’s video was too good to be true.
In a comment on LinkedIn, Dr. Xu admitted to using AI for the video: “An unsupervised neural-network method was subsequently used for AI-assisted post-processing to distinguish and visualize features in the reconstructed grayscale images from the super-resolution optical imaging.”
Dr. Xu’s video has now been disqualified and appears to have been removed from Nikon’s website. A video from Nguyen Nam Nhat now holds first place, according to the contest’s updated rankings. Following the incident, Nikon says it plans to “revisit rules and evaluation procedures for future competition entries.” It also noted in its statement on the contest that the decision to disqualify Dr. Xu’s video “should not be interpreted as a judgment of the entrant’s professional reputation, scientific contributions, or intent.”

articles.title: Furieux contre Adobe, il recrée Photoshop et six autres logiciels avec l'IA
articles.text:
La série s’appelle ArtCraft et aligne sept logiciels calqués sur les piliers de la Creative Cloud, dont PhotoCraft, réplique de Photoshop publiée la semaine dernière sur GitHub. Derrière le projet, un seul homme : Brandon Thomas, un développeur d’Atlanta passé par les systèmes de paiement, « vétéran de quinze ans dans l’industrie » comme il se présente. L’intéressé assume des logiciels en version alpha, « loin d’être prêts », et promet des primes à qui l’aidera à corriger les bugs.
Sept clones, zéro abonnement
Le catalogue recouvre l’essentiel de la suite d’Adobe : PhotoCraft pour Photoshop, VectorCraft pour Illustrator, FilmCraft pour Premiere Pro, LightCraft pour Lightroom, EffectCraft pour After Effects, DesignCraft pour InDesign et PrintCraft pour Acrobat. Le tout est écrit en Rust, sans une ligne de code d’Adobe, et tourne en natif sur macOS, Windows, Linux et FreeBSD, ainsi que dans le navigateur. PhotoCraft ouvre et réenregistre les fichiers PSD, gère calques, masques et styles, et expose plus de 500 commandes pilotables par script ou par un agent IA : tout ce qui se clique peut aussi s’automatiser.
L’usage est gratuit, sans abonnement ; seuls les crédits de génération d’images par IA se paient. Vibe coding oblige, les bugs sont bien là : la transformation libre s’annule parfois toute seule, et la stabilité reste celle d’une alpha précoce. Lui qui se décrit comme tout sauf « un simple amateur occasionnel du vibe coding » en convient sans détour.
Pourquoi Adobe est la cible idéale
Adobe a soldé cette année, pour 150 millions de dollars, des poursuites fédérales engagées en 2024 qui l’accusaient de piéger ses clients dans leurs abonnements. Ce ras-le-bol nourrit une tendance de longue date avec le géant du logiciel créatif : plutôt que de payer chaque mois, certains développeurs font écrire leurs propres outils par l’IA, et ArtCraft en est la vitrine la plus ambitieuse.
Thomas a codé ses clones avec Claude Opus 5.5, le modèle d’Anthropic, dont Adobe est précisément partenaire : depuis fin avril, un connecteur officiel permet à Claude de piloter plus de 50 outils de la Creative Cloud. L’IA que l’éditeur met en avant pour enrichir Photoshop sert donc aussi, ailleurs, à le cloner gratuitement (quand ce n’est pas directement dans Claude que le clone arrive).
Pour l’abonné Creative Cloud, rien ne change ce matin : les clones plantent trop pour remplacer quoi que ce soit, et Adobe conserve des années d’avance fonctionnelle. Les alternatives gratuites à la suite Adobe ne sont pas pléthoriques, mais Affinity reste une référence solide pour remplacer le triptyque Photoshop, InDesign, Publisher.

articles.title: Hace un millón de años, los humanos venían a este lugar de Tarragona como quien va al supermercado. Los arqueólogos siguen encontrando cosas
articles.text:
En La Canonja, a pocos kilómetros de Tarragona, hay un yacimiento que lleva dos décadas dando que hablar: el Barranc de la Boella. El IPHES-CERCA lo excava de forma sistemática desde 2007. Resulta interesante por varios motivos. Para empezar, por su antigüedad: sus herramientas de piedra y sus restos de fauna rondan el millón de años. En segundo lugar, porque el equipo defiende que ahí aparece por primera vez en Europa el Achelense, la tecnología de las hachas de mano. Todo eso ya da para un buen documental. Sin embargo, los investigadores insisten en un matiz todavía más potente: los homininos que dejaron esas piezas no vivían allí.
Qué han encontrado. El yacimiento se divide en Cala 1 y La Mina. Ambos tienen una cronología cercana al millón de años. El yacimiento se divide en Cala 1 y La Mina (y según el investigador Josep Vallverdú, el barranco era una rambla que desembocaba en las marismas del río Francolí). Ambos tienen una cronología cercana al millón de años. La vigésima campaña sacó unas 300 piezas de fauna y herramientas.
Y hay dos novedades: en Cala 1 aparecen indicios de un hueso de rinoceronte. En La Mina, un posible diente de hipopótamo. Se suman a hallazgos anteriores: un mamut desollado por homininos, en 2007 y 2018, y un fragmento de cráneo de oso, en 2024.
Un supermercado, no un hogar. Al parecer, aquí no vivía absolutamente nadie. La directora de las excavaciones, Palmira Saladié, compara el barranco con un supermercado donde los homininos buscaban comida y materias primas. El proceso era sencillo. En un paisaje similar a la sabana africana, lo primero que se buscaba era el agua. ¿Lo segundo? El agua atraía herbívoros. Tercero, los herbívoros atraían depredadores: hienas, dientes de sable y leones. Y ahí es cuando algunos animales quedaban atrapados en el fango y los homininos aprovechaban su carne.
Hachas de mano. Y estos homínidos no iban al Brico Depot ni al Leroy Merlín: se lo fabricaban todo. El Achelense es una tecnología de piedra más compleja que la de las primeras herramientas. Según el investigador Andreu Ollé, la mayoría de los yacimientos achelenses europeos tienen poco más de 500.000 años. La fecha en La Boella, según un estudio de 2014, la sitúa entre hace 0,96 y 0,78 millones de años. Por eso se habla de "alrededor de un millón". La hipótesis es la famosa dispersión desde África. El equipo la sitúa hace unos 1,4 millones de años.
UN VISTAZO A...
Qué pasa después de excavar. La campaña terminó el 30 de septiembre. Ahora las piezas se consolidarán, se identificarán herramientas y especies y se buscarán marcas. Hay que saber si las hizo un hominino o un carnívoro y el proceso puede durar meses. Por eso los resultados probablemente se irán a 2027. Desde 2008, este yacimiento acumula más de treinta publicaciones.
Antiguos y modernos. La Boella no es, en todo caso, el lugar de los primeros europeos. Hay restos humanos más antiguos. En Atapuerca, un fragmento de cara de entre 1,4 y 1,1 millones de años. En Orce, fósiles de 1,4 millones. Lo que aporta La Boella es una tecnología avanzada para su época. No hay un solo resto humano y no se sabe qué especie fabricó las herramientas, aunque el equipo no descarta que aparezcan en próximas campañas.
Pueblo con museo. Este municipio, que cuenta con más de 6.000 habitantes y se sitúa a solo 6km de Tarragona, apostó desde el primer momento por el yacimiento paleontológico del Barranco de la Boella. Hasta aquí han venido especialistas de toda Europa a datar restos de caballos y herramientas de sílex. Y eso se nota en los resultados. En junio de 2025 inauguró el Espai Mammuthus, un centro interactivo muy atractivo para cualquier ciudadano. Reúne restos originales de 29 especies y herramientas de piedra. Superó los 1.500 visitantes en sus primeras semanas.
Por qué siguen apareciendo cosas. La razón es el método, está claro. Los hallazgos llegan "gota a gota", campaña a campaña. Solo se ha excavado una pequeña parte del barranco. Saladié cree que queda trabajo para otra generación de arqueólogos. Además, el equipo ya ha apuntado que quiere sondear capas más profundas en La Mina. Si aparecen, podrían superar el millón de años. Como suele decirse, la historia es algo que siempre está pendiente de ser reescrita.

articles.title: One Piece OP17 : où acheter les nouvelles Mini Tins Luffy, Shanks et Boa Hancock TS-03 ?
articles.text:
Bandai sort une troisième série de mini-boîtes pour son jeu de cartes à collectionner (JCC) One Piece Card Game. Les Mini Tins TS-03 arrivent en France le vendredi 30 octobre 2026, avec trois personnages très populaires de l’univers d’Eiichiro Oda : Monkey D. Luffy, Shanks le Roux et Boa Hancock.
Ces Mini Tins ne sont pas tout à fait inédites. Bandai a lancé le 8 mai 2026 une version réservée aux marchés asiatiques (hors Japon), avec les mêmes personnages et six boîtes, mais quatre boosters OP-13 au lieu de deux boosters OP-17. La version qui arrive en France le 30 octobre a donc un contenu différent.
Où acheter les nouvelles Mini Tins TS-03 de One Piece ?
La sortie officielle est prévue le vendredi 30 octobre 2026. Pour tenter de les acheter au prix conseillé, voici les principaux marchands à surveiller :
Ces petites boîtes métalliques s’adressent autant aux joueuses et joueurs qu’aux collectionneurs. Chaque Mini Tin renferme deux boosters de l’extension OP-17 « Les Guerriers les Plus Puissants au Monde » ainsi qu’une carte promotionnelle exclusive. Il existe six designs différents à collectionner, répartis entre Luffy, Shanks et Boa Hancock.
L’extension OP-17, « Les Guerriers les Plus Puissants au Monde », est sortie en France le 28 août 2026. Ses boosters se trouvent donc déjà à l’unité : la Mini Tin intéresse surtout pour sa boîte et sa carte promotionnelle.
Pour les collectionneurs, la difficulté sera double : acheter les boîtes au prix conseillé et réunir les six modèles. En ligne, le design est souvent envoyé au hasard, et commander six Mini Tins ne garantit pas d’obtenir les six illustrations. Certaines boutiques vendent toutefois chaque modèle séparément : vérifiez la fiche produit avant de commander.
Le prix conseillé d’une Mini Tin One Piece Card Game TS-03 est de 11,99 €. Certaines enseignes pourront toutefois l’afficher quelques euros plus cher, notamment lorsque les stocks commencent à se raréfier.
Que contiennent les Mini Tins One Piece Card Game TS-03 ?
Avec cette troisième série, six illustrations différentes sont disponibles. La carte promotionnelle existe elle aussi en six versions.
Chaque Mini Tin française contient :
- Deux boosters de l’extension OP-17 « Les Guerriers les Plus Puissants au Monde »
- Une carte promotionnelle parmi les six modèles disponibles
- Une mini-boîte métallique parmi les six designs disponibles
Avec ses six illustrations, le TS-03 mêle ouverture de boosters et objet de collection. Bandai a choisi trois des personnages les plus populaires de One Piece, et les six boîtes forment une série à exposer.
Pourquoi les Mini Tins TS-03 pourraient encore une fois être rapidement être en rupture ?
Les Mini Tins attirent les collectionneurs, avec six boîtes à réunir, comme les joueurs, avec leurs boosters OP-17, le tout pour un prix conseillé d’une douzaine d’euros.
La difficulté sera surtout de trouver les boîtes au prix conseillé le 30 octobre et après. Pour réunir les six illustrations, mieux vaut repérer les revendeurs qui vendent les modèles à l’unité ou par lot complet. À l’approche du vendredi 30 octobre 2026, le plus judicieux est de surveiller régulièrement les différentes enseignes plutôt que d’attendre le jour de la sortie pour commencer ses recherches.
Attention aussi aux boutiques inconnues qui promettent du stock ou des précommandes sur des produits introuvables ailleurs. La forte demande autour des cartes à collectionner attire les arnaqueurs, comme l’illustre la multiplication des fausses boutiques Pokémon. Certaines affichent des sites très soignés et des prix crédibles, mais encaissent les commandes sans jamais les honorer. Avant de payer, vérifiez l’identité du vendeur et cherchez des retours d’acheteurs indépendants : les avis affichés sur la boutique et sa présence dans Google ne suffisent pas à garantir sa fiabilité.

articles.title: Noch zu teuer für den Massenmarkt: Doch diese Batterie aus China will den Lithium-Ionen-Akku beerben
articles.text:
Dreimal so viel Energie: Dieser Batterie-Prototyp soll Lithium-Ionen in den Schatten stellen
Sichere und bessere Batterien sind das Ziel von Welion New Energy. Das will das Unternehmen mit Semi-Solid-State-Zellen erreichen. Damit sollen Brandgefahren gemildert werden und gleichzeitig eine höhere Energiedichte als Lithium-Ionen-Batterien zur Verfügung stehen, um Elektroautos, Boote oder Drohnen anzutreiben. Der Bedarf ist groß: Von Elektrofahrzeugen, die Pendler nach Hause bringen, bis zu Schiffen, die Güter über Landesgrenzen hinweg transportieren – immer mehr Fahrzeuge um uns herum arbeiten mit Batterien. Lithium-Ionen-Akkus sind hier Standard. Da der Bedarf an Batterien stark steigt, wächst aber auch die Nachfrage nach Zellen, die mit einer einzigen Ladung mehr Energie speichern können als die ältere Technik.

articles.title: Passer d’un iPhone à un Samsung Galaxy devient beaucoup plus simple chez Free (transfert eSIM) — Frandroid
articles.text:
Les abonnés Free qui passent d’un iPhone à un Galaxy n’ont plus besoin de commander une nouvelle eSIM (la carte SIM intégrée au téléphone, sans puce à insérer). Ce vendredi 9 octobre, le compte X Free 1337, l’un des comptes officiels de l’opérateur, a annoncé la compatibilité des smartphones Samsung sous One UI 8.5 avec son « Quick Transfert xOS ». Ce-nom-désigne le transfert d’une ligne d’un système d’exploitation à l’autre. La ligne passe alors directement de l’ancien téléphone au nouveau, sans frais si elle est déjà en eSIM.
Free avait commencé par les Google Pixel le 2 octobre, dans les deux sens. Le Pixel propose de récupérer une SIM depuis un « iPhone ou iPad ». L’iPhone, lui, affiche une option « Transférer à partir d’Android », à côté du transfert habituel depuis un autre iPhone.
Avant ces annonces, changer de camp obligeait à demander une nouvelle eSIM depuis l’espace abonné. Free facture cette opération 10 € sur la fiche tarifaire de ses forfaits.
    Pour aller plus loin
Comment passer d’Android à un iPhone ? Transférez vos comptes, photos, contacts et applications
            
Samsung rejoint Google, d’autres marques attendues
One UI 8.5, la surcouche Android de Samsung, est arrivée avec les Galaxy S26 en début d’année. Elle a ensuite été déployée au printemps sur une large partie des Galaxy récents, des S23 aux S25, en passant par les pliants Z Fold et Z Flip 5, 6 et 7. Les Galaxy S22, Z Fold 4 et Z Flip 4 n’y ont pas eu droit. Côté Google, les Pixel 9 et 10 récupèrent une eSIM d’iPhone depuis leur mise à jour de mars 2026. Lors de l’Android Show du 12 mai, Google a ensuite annoncé une refonte du passage de l’iPhone à Android, eSIM comprise, en commençant par les Galaxy et les Pixel.
Encore faut-il que l’opérateur active ce transfert de son côté. En France, SFR avait été le premier à le faire, uniquement avec les Pixel 9 et 10 à l’époque. Free promet d’autres marques Android « prochainement », sans donner de liste ni de date.
Orange propose aussi ce transfert : la fiche d’assistance d’Apple le cite parmi les opérateurs français compatibles, avec SFR et Free. Bouygues Telecom n’apparaît pas dans cette liste. Chez lui, passer d’un iPhone à Android oblige encore à générer une nouvelle eSIM depuis l’espace client.
Avec une carte SIM physique, il faut d’abord convertir
La gratuité ne vaut que pour les lignes déjà en eSIM. Avec une carte physique, il faut d’abord convertir sa SIM en eSIM, et ce sont alors les 10 € habituels. L’opération suppose aussi un Galaxy compatible eSIM.
Côté iPhone, Apple réclame au minimum un iPhone 11 sous iOS 26. Le smartphone Android doit tourner sous Android 16 ou une version plus récente. Les deux téléphones doivent être connectés au Wi-Fi, avec le Bluetooth activé.
Un transfert d’eSIM peut aussi coincer, même entre deux appareils du même fabricant. Chez Bouygues Telecom, passer une eSIM d’un iPhone à l’autre sous iOS 27 a bloqué l’un de nos journalistes pendant 24 heures. Avant de vous lancer, lisez les pièges à éviter lors d’un transfert d’eSIM. Vérifiez aussi la version de One UI de votre Galaxy, dans Paramètres, puis À propos du téléphone et Informations sur le logiciel.

articles.title: Citrix Urges Immediate Patching of Critical NetScaler Vulnerability
articles.text:
Citrix on Thursday warned users of a critical-severity NetScaler vulnerability that requires immediate patching.
Tracked as CVE-2026-107406 (CVSS score of 9.5), the flaw is described as a memory overflow that could lead to remote code execution (RCE) or denial-of-service (DoS).
According to Citrix, the security defect impacts NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway appliances configured as a SAML SP or SAML IdP, under specific configuration conditions.
The bug also affects Secure Private Access Hybrid deployments that use NetScaler. Customers need to update these NetScaler instances as well.
Patches were included in NetScaler ADC and Gateway versions 14.1-73.46, 13.1-64.29, 14.1-73.46 FIPS, and 13.1.37.283 (of 13.1-FIPS and 13.1-NDcPP).
“As of the publication of the bulletin, Citrix is not aware of any unmitigated exploits of this vulnerability,” Citrix notes, urging customers to upgrade their instances as soon as possible.
Citrix’s fresh warning comes days after the company sounded the alarm on CVE-2026-88779, a zero-day in NetScaler leading to DoS.
A week before, two other NetScaler zero-days were patched: CVE-2026-88771 (leading to RCE), and CVE-2026-88772 (leading to RCE or DoS). They have been exploited in attacks against government, financial services, education, legal, and professional services organizations.

articles.title: Edmonton Startup Week panelists say AgTech could power the next tech boom | BetaKit
articles.text:
Founders looking to ride the wave of the next tech boom should look to AgTech, according to a group of panellists at Edmonton Startup Week.
Douglas Mills, the vice-president of external relations at the Canadian Agri-food Automation and Intelligence Network (CAAIN), told audiences during a panel discussion on opportunities within AgTech that the space was uniquely positioned to experience a boom in innovation, citing its tendency toward early adoption, lower regulatory thresholds, and hands-on validation.
“Whether you’re interested in AI, data, biotech, sustainability, advanced manufacturing, AgTech presents real-world problems that need innovative solutions.”
Douglas Mills, CAAIN
“[It’s] a sector rich with opportunity,” Mills said. “When we’re talking about agriculture, think broadly. We’re not just talking about a farm, tractor, or cows in a field. Think of opportunities across the whole value chain: animal health, logistics, transportation, solar, processing, value-add tools, machinery, analytics, robotics, computer vision, AI research, and biotech.
“It’s a massive sector when you’re looking at all the opportunities out there. Whether you’re interested in AI, data, biotech, sustainability, advanced manufacturing, AgTech presents real-world problems that need innovative solutions,” he added.
Mills was joined on stage by three others, including Colin Coros, the COO at precision diagnostics and medtech company Nanostics, BJ Fuchs, a cattle rancher and AgTech supporter, and David Bressler, the vice-president of international innovation and enterprise at the University of Alberta.
“One of the exciting things about Ag … is they’re leading technology. They’re early adopters,” said Coros. Prior to his role at Nanostics, he was the CEO of Delta Genomics, where he worked on livestock biobanking. Biobanking is the process of freezing and storing biological or genetic material to preserve agricultural diversity, or reconstitute livestock breeds.
“We think autonomous vehicles are coming one day, but they’ve already been in the agriculture sector for over a decade. There’s not a combine in Alberta that isn’t self-driven.
“It’s an industry where if there’s a solution, and they can increase productivity with it, they’ll adopt it, and they’ll adopt it faster than almost any other sector,” Coros added.
That makes the field particularly attractive to entrepreneurs, especially those looking to validate technology, or who are struggling to navigate complex regulatory requirements in a field like medtech or biotech. Coros said AgTech can be a useful stepping stone for both.
RELATED: Edmonton mayor hints at upcoming support for entrepreneurs as city’s Startup Week kicks off
“I talk to a lot of deep tech healthcare people … and you’re talking about going through a 15-year journey before you even get anything into the medical space,” he said. “If you really want to provide your technology, have you thought about livestock where maybe you can get this to market in five years, work out your kinks, and then maybe the next market is healthcare?”
That rule applies for tech startups who might not be in the traditional AgTech space. Fuchs, whose company Business Wide View has been involved in trialling innovations in real-world settings, said agricultural producers should be the first point of contact for anyone looking to see if their tech might have a dual-use purpose in the agricultural space.
“Sky’s the limit. Drones, water-trough monitors: there’s so much out there, and every operation is different,” Fuchs said. “If you have a great idea, talk to a producer; talk to more than one. It will give you answers around what the challenge is.”

articles.title: New AKG headphones?! Not quite, but they may live again through Samsung's rumored 'Galaxy Studio' cans
articles.text:
Samsung may finally be putting all of its Harman, AKG, JBL and B&W juice in a blender for its first headphones in 10 years
They're said to be called the Galaxy Studio
- The rumored name for Samsung's first over-ears in a decade was spotted
- They may be called Galaxy Studio, according to a leak and a trademark
- And also, they'll give Samsung's various audio brands something to do
For almost a decade, Samsung has been the proud owner of a who's-who of legacy audio brands, and it finally looks like it's ready to do something with them. A potential AirPods Max 2 rival, possibly called the Galaxy Studio, is rumored to be on the way.
That Samsung has some over-ears in the works has been leaked before, but people are finally taking the rumors seriously now because of the mention of an actual name. These fresh leads stem from a leaker on Twitter called @evowizz, who also successfully leaked the Pixel 11 Pro Fold. It is they who gave us the Galaxy Studio moniker.
Now, the title 'Studio' might suggest professional uses for these headphones. Maybe they're made for music mixing and/or critical listening? This is Samsung though, a tech giant that typically sticks to the consumer product realm to support its ecosystem, so perhaps the name was simply chosen because it makes them sound premium.
In fact, Samsung trademarked this name a whole decade ago, and re-filed it in mid-September. So the Galaxy Studio is sounding increasingly likely. And with the brand's recent push into new audio form factors, including the Galaxy Buds On, it makes the new cans seem increasingly likely.
There's no indication of price, feature set or release date just yet. Some fans are hoping for a 2027 release date, so maybe they'll come alongside the Galaxy S27, Galaxy Z Fold 9s or another release that year. But it's impossible to say for sure.
It's an audio party and everyone's invited
Samsung bought Harman International in November 2016, which means the likes of Harman Kardon, JBL and AKG are all in its trophy cabinet. A later acquisition of Masimo's audio brands in late 2025 means that Bowers & Wilkins, Denon and Marantz are also on its roster.
Despite all that knowledge and R&D on its shelves, the brand has been content releasing in-ears only, including the Galaxy Buds 4 and Galaxy Buds 4 Pro. We haven't seen any over-ears since the likes of the Samsung Level On Pro, back when ANC was a new novelty, rather than a mandatory feature for any new wireless over-ears.

The shame is that some of the Harman International brands have languished recently. JBL and Bowers & Wilkins still push out glorious over-ears regularly, but Harman Kardon now seems to exist solely as a brand which tunes others' headphones, and when was the last time we saw a major AKG release? These are legacy audiophile brands, seemingly going to waste.
Hi-fi fans have been begging for an proper AKG revival for a long time, and the Samsung Galaxy Studio won't be that — they won't be designed and honed for audiophiles in the same way that AKG's cans might be.
But if there's even a small splash of juice from all of its well-known names, the Studio could turn out to be a pretty tasty smoothie. For now, we wait…

articles.title: Terremoto de magnitude 7,6 atinge Panamá e provoca alerta de tsunami
articles.text:
Um terremoto de magnitude 7,6 atingiu a costa sul do Panamá nesta sexta-feira (9), provocando evacuações de edifícios e levando à emissão de alertas de tsunami para áreas do Oceano Pacífico. O tremor ocorreu a cerca de 10 km de profundidade, segundo o Serviço Geológico dos Estados Unidos (USGS), e foi sentido na capital panamenha e em San José (Costa Rica).
O epicentro foi localizado nas proximidades de Pitaloza Arriba, no sul do Panamá. Inicialmente, o USGS estimou a magnitude do terremoto em 8,0, mas revisou o número para 7,6 após analisar os dados do evento.
Na Cidade do Panamá, imagens de emissoras locais mostraram pessoas deixando edifícios após o tremor. Até as primeiras informações divulgadas, não havia relatos imediatos de danos confirmados, e as autoridades locais avaliavam possíveis impactos.
Alerta de tsunami abrange países das Américas
- O Sistema de Alerta de Tsunamis dos Estados Unidos emitiu avisos sobre a possibilidade de ondas perigosas em áreas costeiras de diferentes países;
- O alerta incluiu trechos do litoral do Panamá, da Colômbia, da Costa Rica, do Equador, do Peru, da Nicarágua, da Guatemala, de El Salvador e do México;
- O sistema também indicou risco para o Havaí. Segundo as informações divulgadas, a possibilidade de ondas perigosas nas áreas costeiras foi avaliada para as horas seguintes ao terremoto;
- A extensão do alerta levou autoridades a acompanhar os possíveis efeitos do tremor em diferentes regiões do Pacífico. A situação ainda estava em atualização nos relatos iniciais.
Leia mais:
- Testes nucleares da Coreia do Norte podem ter provocado milhares de terremotos nos anos seguintes
- Terremoto acorda vulcão adormecido há 500 anos na Rússia e NASA grava erupção do espaço
- O terremoto que revelou uma camada desconhecida da Terra e mudou o que se sabia sobre o interior do planeta
Terremoto foi sentido em países vizinhos
Além do Panamá, o tremor foi percebido em San José, capital da Costa Rica. Testemunhas relataram à Reuters que sentiram o abalo nas duas capitais.
Na região de Herrera, próxima ao local do terremoto, moradores relataram objetos derrubados dentro de residências. O episódio provocou apreensão entre a população, enquanto equipes de proteção civil avaliavam possíveis danos.
O USGS ainda poderia revisar os parâmetros do terremoto à medida que novos dados fossem analisados.
Rodrigo Mozelli é jornalista formado pela Universidade Metodista de São Paulo (UMESP) e, atualmente, é redator do Olhar Digital.

articles.title: Marvel anuncia su nueva serie live-action para Disney+: ya sabemos su título y cuándo se estrena
articles.text:
Aunque hace unos meses se confirmó que Marvel tenía intención de pisar el freno con sus series para Disney+, la compañía acaba de anunciar otra más. La Casa de las Ideas está a punto de estrenar VisionQuest, que llegará a la plataforma de streaming en apenas unos días. A esta le seguirá la temporada 3 de Daredevil: Born Again en la primera mitad del próximo año. Y, con ello, todas las series marvelitas live-action que han visto la luz hasta ahora habrán terminado. Por ello, el estudio ya tiene nuevos planes.
Durante el panel de Marvel Television en la New York Comic Con, el estudio anunció oficialmente su nueva serie: Zodiac. Será, tal y como revelaron, una serie de espías. Además, también se confirmó que su estreno está previsto para 2028. El rodaje comenzará en Londres en primavera y se espera que el casting arranque en las próximas semanas.
Porque, a pesar de que Marvel ha anunciado ya el desarrollo de Zodiac, lo cierto es que esta nueva serie aún no cuenta con reparto confirmado. No sabemos exactamente qué personajes aparecerán en ella. De hecho, ni siquiera se ha desvelado si lo que se presentarán serán nuevos héroes y villanos o si sus protagonistas serán rostros ya conocidos del UCM.
Lo único que podemos hacer a día de hoy es aventurarnos con algunas teorías. Por ejemplo, gracias al logo de Zodiac que Marvel presentó, parece que la letra "A" hace algún tipo de referencia a S.H.I.E.L.D. Así, ya se rumorea que este proyecto podría ser una suerte de reboot o revival de Agentes de S.H.I.E.L.D. adaptado a la situación del UCM después de Avengers: Secret Wars. De hecho, el actor Clark Gregg, quien diera vida al agente Phil Coulson, ha compartido el anuncio de la serie en su Instagram.
De qué podría ir Zodiac, nueva serie de Marvel
Si atendemos a los cómics de Marvel, sin embargo, la historia de la serie podría llevarnos por un camino diferente. Y es que en las viñetas existe una organización criminal de asesinos en la que sus miembros adoptan los nombres de sus signos del zodiaco.
El primero en debutar fue un villano llamado Escorpio, que quiso asesinar a Nick Furia. Todos ellos acaban asumiendo no solo el nombre sino también trajes y apariencia de sus signos zodiacales. Es posible que Marvel quiera llevar Zodiac por ese camino. Por el momento, tendremos que estar atentos a las novedades que lleguen en los próximos meses.

articles.title: Google teases Fitbit Edge launch next week
articles.text:
It looks like Google is getting ready to take the wraps off its rumored Fitbit Edge next Monday. In a post on X, Google posted a picture of what appears to be the side of the fitness tracker, with the caption: “Get an Edge on your health. 10.12.26.”
Google teases Fitbit Edge launch next week
The Fitbit Edge will launch on October 12th.
The Fitbit Edge will launch on October 12th.
A trove of Fitbit Edge leaks has surfaced over the past couple of weeks. So far, details shared by Dealabs and Android Headlines suggest that the upcoming device could feature a 1.34-inch always-on OLED touchscreen, built-in GPS, and several other sensors, including an accelerometer, barometer, altimeter, and gyroscope. It may also come with optical sensors for measuring heart rate and blood oxygen saturation (SpO2) and electrical sensors for capturing ECGs.
As reported by Dealabs, the tracker may also be able to notify wearers about potential atrial fibrillation and irregular heart rhythms. The Fitbit Edge is rumored to come with a replaceable lithium-ion battery with up to seven days of battery life. Rumors suggest that it could cost around $180 in the US when it launches next week.

articles.title: Hopper cuts staff shortly after co-founder departs | BetaKit
articles.text:
Travel technology company Hopper appears to have laid off staff on its enterprise side, following the departure of the company’s co-founder last month.
The news: On Sept. 28, Hopper co-founder Dakota Smith announced on LinkedIn that he was leaving the company after leading its enterprise division, Hopper Technology Solutions, as CEO for the past three years. Shortly after, more than half a dozen employees posted on LinkedIn indicating their roles had been eliminated.
BetaKit reached out to Hopper for more details but has not yet received a response. In a LinkedIn message, Smith told BetaKit that he had nothing further to share on his departure and that he didn’t have insight into restructuring as his last day was in mid-September.
From the source: “Scaling an org from [less than] 200 employees to 1,200+ distributed across 37+ countries while keeping the bar as high as ours has been pure madness to say the least,” Kamil Eladas, a former technical recruitment manager who had worked at the company for nearly seven years, wrote in an Oct. 2 post. Eladas didn’t directly state whether his departure was due to the layoffs, but said that leaving the company was “bittersweet.”
The context: It’s unclear how the job cuts were distributed across the company, and whether Smith’s departure was related. HTS is Hopper’s B2B division that provides data, e-commerce, and financial technology services; it accounts for the majority of the company’s revenue.
Hopper has made multiple rounds of layoffs over the past few years as it has navigated changes to its partnerships. Earlier this year, Hopper client and US financial services giant Capital One brought the platform Hopper was developing, and the employees behind it, in-house. Hopper also inked significant deals this year, landing a partnership with Royal Bank of Canada to power its travel rewards program.
Final thought: The travel industry publication Skift reported that Hopper may be facing pressure from increased competition in Asia, due to travel company Booking Holdings’ upcoming consolidation of its brands Agoda, Priceline, and Booking.com.
Feature image courtesy Hopper.

articles.title: The Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra is down to $950 after Prime Day
articles.text:
Amazon has the Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra in black with 256GB of storage discounted to $949.99, a healthy discount from its usual price of $1,399.99. This phone’s standout feature is the adjustable privacy display, which can hide your entire screen, or just portions of it, from onlookers and strangers. It doesn’t meaningfully hurt the screen’s performance otherwise, and it’s only noticeable at steep angles, and it includes a built-in stylus for writing or drawing.
The Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra is down to $950 after Prime Day
The S26 Ultra’s privacy display is the headlining feature.
Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra
Samsung’s 6.9-inch S26 Ultra is the only model in the lineup with the new privacy display, designed to limit what people around you can see on your screen. It also includes the S Pen and upgrades the camera hardware, adding dual telephoto lenses alongside a 200-megapixel main sensor. Read our review.
Even beyond the privacy display, the S26 Ultra is an impressive flagship phone for mobile enthusiasts. The upgraded camera hardware makes a big difference when it comes to photo quality, particularly in low lighting conditions. For better or worse, it’s still a sizable phone, with a 6.9-inch AMOLED display, but it’s slimmer and more comfortable than the S25 Ultra.

articles.title: Chip Industry Week In Review
articles.text:
Chip Industry Week In Review
                    
    
    
                            
						
$2B foundry pact; hyper-NA EUV; TSMC, Samsung financials; Canon readies nanoimprint; AI chips under scrutiny; $10T data center buildout; $1.5B SiC boost; chip smuggling; 800V power gains traction; quantum HW scales up; wireless EV road charging; sub-nm gate dielectrics; mobile fab.
					
				 
				
				
					
Top of the Week
- TSMC and GF inked a $2B manufacturing agreement, under which GF will manufacture silicon interposers for TSMC’s CoWoS advanced-packaging ecosystem at its Malta, New York fab. Volume production is expected to ramp in the first half of 2028.
- Applied Materials and Intel are expanding their R&D collaboration to develop next-gen transistors, interconnects, and advanced packaging technologies, combining work at Applied’s EPIC Center in Silicon Valley with Intel’s R&D operations in Hillsboro, Oregon.
- Rapidus launched Rapidus CORE, a global ecosystem framework intended to support customers from chip design through manufacturing for its planned 2nm foundry business. The first phase includes 17 design-service partners.
- Xanadu and GF formed a multi-year manufacturing partnership to move ultra-low-loss silicon nitride photonics and superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors onto GF’s 300mm production line in Malta, New York.
Big hauls
- Wolfspeed received a conditional commitment for up to $1.5B in 30-year U.S. government financing to expand domestic SiC materials and wide-bandgap power-device production.
- Vinci raised $250M in Series B funding at a $1.5B valuation to expand its AI-powered physics simulation platform. The platform models thermal, thermo-mechanical, and fluid behavior during design, with simulations reportedly running in minutes rather than hours or days.
- Oratomic raised $475M for its neutral-atom quantum computing hardware.
- VEIR raised $110M for superconducting power delivery technology for AI data centers.
- Atomic Machines launched with $250M for its Matter Compiler system that builds micro-machines from code, including an electromechanical micro-relay to cut power in 800VDC data centers during a fault.
Financials
Analysis
- Global semiconductor sales reached $159.7B in August, up 8% from July, with year-to-date sales topping $1T, reports SIA/WSTS.
- McKinsey expects inference to account for about 60% of AI compute by 2030, driving demand for custom accelerators, HBM, chiplets, advanced packaging, and silicon photonics.
- Silicon photonics, CPO, and optical networking are emerging as the next U.S.–China semiconductor battleground as AI data centers outgrow electrical interconnects, says Wilson Center, which estimates China accounts for 56% of global optical-transceiver manufacturing capacity.
- Brookings estimates the U.S. AI buildout could require $10.3T through 2032 for data centers, power, networking and specialized chips, but it warned that increasingly complex financing could obscure financial risks.
Lithography
- ASML and Carl Zeiss researchers outlined a hyper-NA EUV lithography architecture with a numerical aperture of at least 0.75, potentially enabling features as small as 5nm, more than one-third smaller than current high-NA systems. The technology could be ready in about a decade, although commercial production remains uncommitted.
- Canon says its nanoimprint lithography technology is entering the final stage toward full-scale mass production.
- DUV immersion lithography is the strongest remaining chokepoint on China’s AI-chip production, contends think tank Center for Technology & Statecraft. It estimates Chinese-owned fabs had accumulated more than 330 DUVi systems by 1Q26 and says continued imports could significantly narrow the U.S.-allied AI-chip manufacturing advantage. The report calls for a China-wide ban on DUVi exports, servicing restrictions and tighter controls on critical components.
Memory
Security and export controls
- Arteris won an additional $3.3M through the U.S. government’s Trusted and Assured Microelectronics initiative to expand its third-party IP (3PIP) security assurance program in collaboration with BAE and SiFive.
- The U.S. DOJ charged the owner of California-based Earthmade Computer with allegedly smuggling more than $300M in export-controlled computer servers to China. Prosecutors allege the servers contained high-end U.S.-manufactured GPUs and were routed through Malaysia and Singapore using false end-user and destination information to evade U.S. export controls.
- Meanwhile, CSET researchers modeled more than 10 million scenarios for detecting diverted AI chips and found ping-based location verification to be the most cost-effective approach. However, they cautioned that implementation costs and complexity could limit its usefulness, and said that combining PLV with targeted physical inspections could improve enforcement.

Americas
- Nvidia, AMD, Micron, and eight other companies committed a combined $2.4B in AI tools and compute credits to the U.S. government’s Genesis Mission.
- CSIS examines the trade-offs between restricting exports of U.S. AI technology and expanding global adoption of American chips and models, recommending targeted export controls and faster domestic innovation.
- Draper broke ground on a 111,000 square-foot design, manufacturing, and advanced packaging facility in Massachusetts.
- San Francisco enacted a 45-day moratorium on building or expanding data centers while the board looks at energy, water, air quality, land use, and community impacts, per NBC.
Reports and Deals
Patent agreement
M&A
- Microchip acquired Vorago Technologies, maker of rad-hard, rad-tolerant MCUs and MPUs.
- Skyworks completed its combination with Qorvo.
- Navitas Semiconductor completed its acquisition of IVR maker Claros.
- Cirrus Logic acquired INVENTVM, an Italian fabless chip company specializing in mixed-signal power-management and audio ICs.
- Infineon completed its acquisition of C2i Semiconductors, adding software-defined multiphase controllers, smart power stages and vertical power-delivery expertise for AI data centers while expanding its power-systems R&D presence in India.
Reports and opinions
New Technologies
EDA
- Keysight added agentic AI to its design software, enabling engineers to connect AI agents to RF tools for circuit generation, verification, and optimization. ADS 2027 converts graphical RF designs into machine-readable representations and lets agents learn repeatable engineering workflows, addressing the inconsistent way LLMs interpret schematics and layouts.
- Silicon Labs expanded its edge AI developer platform with SDKs and design intelligence.
Test
- Teradyne added burn-in capabilities to its Titan HP system-level test platform, allowing high-power AI and other reliability-sensitive devices to be stressed under realistic workloads while controlling junction temperature and power at each device rather than using conventional burn-in ovens.
- Keysight and research institutions developed a new measurement approach for continuous on-wafer characterization of sub-THz semiconductor devices. The company also introduced its Velocity 4900 Series aimed at test lab modernization for AI, enabling engineers to integrate physical test environments into automated CI/CD workflows.
Data center
Research
A Cornell-led team developed silicon-doped α-(AlxGa1−x)₂O₃ with a bandgap exceeding 7 eV while maintaining n-type conductivity, and fabricated both a Schottky diode and transistor using the ultra-wide-bandgap material. “Our achievement breaks the trend of increasing synthesis difficulty, cost and small size of ever-wider-bandgap semiconductors, for example, diamond and cubic boron nitride,” the researchers wrote.
UIUC, DOE’s NETL, and collaborators integrated a high-k oxide with 2D semiconductors using a carbon-dot monolayer as a van der Waals interface. The approach produced a smooth, stable gate dielectric with an equivalent oxide thickness of about 0.6 nm, low leakage and a high breakdown field, addressing a key challenge in scaling 2D transistors.
The U.S. DOE awarded $159M to 12 AI-driven scientific research projects, including a Fermilab-led effort to accelerate the design of microchips for extreme environments and a Harvard-led project combining AI and quantum hardware to advance quantum error correction.
More academic papers
Security
Hardware security releases
- Lattice is collaborating with Arm and AMI on secure AI data-center infrastructure that combines Arm’s AGI CPU server platforms with Lattice FPGAs and AMI firmware.
- Nuvoton and AMI launched a secure OpenBMC server-management platform built around Nuvoton’s Arbel BMC and AMI firmware.
Alerts and vulnerabilities
- MediaTek disclosed 31 vulnerabilities across its chipsets, including two critical out-of-bounds-write flaws in modem components and high-severity issues affecting NeuroPilot, APU, and other subsystems.
- Qualcomm detailed several high-severity chipset vulnerabilities, including a boot flaw that can bypass cryptographic-signature checks for certain partitions and a core-security issue involving page-table changes before secure-memory initialization.
- CrowdStrike linked an AI attack of major South Korean financial institutions to a recently released open-source agentic penetration testing tool developed in China.
Government security news
- The NSA released new Zero Trust guidance for securing critical operational-technology environments.
- The GAO warned that federal agencies are not fully prepared for the transition to PQC, with many agencies still lacking complete inventories of vulnerable systems and adequate migration testing.
- President Trump and executives from OpenAI, Anthropic, Nvidia, and other AI companies signed a voluntary AI safety accord, committing to internal safeguards, independent evaluations, and board-level oversight. However, the agreement carries no regulatory penalties for noncompliance.
Security technical papers
Vehicles, Batteries
Infineon debuted its new TRAVEO CYT4EN automotive MCU for high-performance instrument clusters and advanced cockpit graphics that could also be used in motorcycles.
Samsung’s System LSI division is reportedly halting its development of new automotive application processors amid cost pressures, Munhwa reported.
EVs
- Honda and collaborators developed underlying technology for a wireless charging road system that could charge EVs, including heavy-duty trucks, while driving. The system uses power transmitters embedded in roadways and receivers installed in vehicles.
- BMW debuted its new iX4 luxury electric SUV, with the vehicle reportedly offering fast charging and up to 514 miles in WLTP range.
Government Regulations

Quantum
QC hardware
- Infineon and Swiss quantum computing company ZuriQ AG expanded their quantum computing hardware collaboration to further scale quantum processing units for future commercial systems.
- Infleqtion, Honeywell Aerospace, and UCSB collaborated on a new integrated optical cavity, built on silicon nitride, that reduces the space needed to keep lasers stable inside quantum systems, paving the way for miniaturization of quantum hardware.
- IonQ demonstrated a photonic quantum interconnect linking a trapped-ion qubit with silicon-vacancy quantum memory at more than 1,000 entanglement events per second, over four times the previous reported trapped-ion record.
Investment, government initiatives
- DARPA selected four companies to advance to the final stage of its Quantum Benchmarking Initiative: Atom Computing for scalable arrays of neutral atoms; Diraq for Si CMOS spin qubits; IBM for modular superconducting processors; and IonQ for trapped-ion quantum computing.
- PsiQuantum received a conditional loan commitment of up to $150M from the U.S. Department of War to expand its manufacturing and prototyping capabilities at the hub in Milpitas, California.
- Universal Quantum raised over $100M to commercialize its modular technology with a path to fault-tolerant quantum computing.

Workforce, Education
Purdue University launched a mobile semiconductor fabrication lab that brings hands-on lithography, deposition, and etching training directly to students and aspiring technicians without requiring access to a full cleanroom.
Cadence announced new Digital Badges, verified credentials issued through Credly, aimed at PCB and package design.
Government intervention
- The NSF launched a program to create accelerated bachelor’s-to-Ph.D. pathways and interdisciplinary graduate training aimed at moving STEM graduates more quickly into critical technology fields.
